_meta.title: Emit Templates — every HTML output shape the converter produces
_meta.purpose: The single home of the converter's HTML forms: element families, callout classes, image/video/audio embeds, the red-flag form, the interactive placeholder, and the page-skeleton fragments keyed by Style_Anchor_Registry field VALUES. ContentConverter.js and SkeletonBuilder.js read THIS file. Changing what any output looks like is an edit here — never a code change.
_meta.grounding: Forms taken from the finished corpus (OSAH401, ANZH205, ARFUN01 …) and Style_Anchor_Registry_Examples.json. Where the corpus varies, the dominant/most-recent form is used and noted.
_meta.placeholders: {curly} tokens are filled by the engine. {content} is the gathered learner content; {classes} is a space-joined class list.
_meta.extension_rule: New style / class / menu shape / footer arrangement = a data edit here. If a change seems to need engine code, stop — design error.
_meta.comment_policy: Only TWO comment uses are permitted converter-wide: Mode P's commented image reference (below) and the ACK-TODO supplement (Acks_Formats.json). The acks lesson-label comments are mandated by the acks spec itself. No other comments are ever emitted.

red_flag.form: Red Flag: {text}
red_flag.cs_form: Writers Note: {text}
red_flag.todo_form: Designer/Developer To Do: {text}

black_developer_note._inside_widget_doc: false: a black line inside a widget's capture (the nearest tag before it, over black lines only, is a widget tag) is left as the widget's own content — the un-built hand-off box keeps the writer's lines as typed (XOTPB09 / XOTPB13's carousel boxes keep their «CS: …» line).
black_developer_note._doc: THE BLACK DEVELOPER NOTE IS A WRITERS NOTE. A line the writer addressed to the developer but typed in BLACK ('Note to CS – Please use Sassoon font.', 'Note to developer – …', 'DEV: Colour code for phase 2:', 'Cs: can these two images …', 'Can we make something like this please?') would ship as learner text; the human build drops these lines. A black item whose text matches `pattern` — or a heading tag (heading_tags) whose whole payload does — is read as the writer-instruction item the normaliser already makes of that text (Parse → class instruction, no tag), so the instruction path prints the red Writers Note in its place. A parse that is not a pure instruction is left alone. The 'Insert / Add image …' form is NOT listed: it mixes learner instructions ('Add photos of your work to your journal'). Env BLACKDEVNOTE_OFF reverts.

todo_lead._doc: A red line that already OPENS with the ledger's To Do prefix is a designer To Do, not a writer's instruction: it renders with todo_form ('Designer/Developer To Do: …') instead of cs_form ('Writers Note: Designer/Developer To Do: …'). It serves converter-generated To Do notes that travel the red-text path, such as the XOTP adapter's overview note (Input_Doc_Rules adapter overview_link_only_todo). Env TODOLEAD_OFF restores the Writers Note form.

ledger_note_scheme.note: The design team's SOURCE-SPECIFIC red-note prefix scheme (KB CL-0010 + CL-0013): a WRITER'S own note / CS instruction (kind 'cs') → 'Writers Note:'; a CONVERTER-detected issue (kind 'diagnostic', the default — ambiguity / missing info / unbuildable structure) → 'Red Flag:'; a DEFERRED piece of a known, correctly-built pattern (kind 'todo' — an asset/URL/setup the developer supplies in production; matches Subject_Global_Parameters._meta.red_note_format byte-for-byte) → 'Designer/Developer To Do:'; a whitelisted Word comment → 'Note from {author}:' (Comment_Authors.render.form). ALL render red AND BOLD ('color: red; font-weight: bold;' — the bold weight is CL-0010's), always visible, never a hidden comment. The cv2-note / cv2-comment marker classes keep every note out of structural comparisons. The human gold strips ALL developer notes, and these prefixes are design-authority decisions the gold predates — recorded in Subject_Global_Parameters._universal_conventions (overrides_gold:true) so the wording is never chased back toward the gold. Env NOTESCHEME_OFF (or enabled:false) renders every note in the legacy forms (legacy_form / legacy_cs_form here + Comment_Authors.render.legacy_form).

phrases: insert appropriate introductory video to pique student interest
in this section outline any connections this module has with other learning in ara ako, or in fundamentals
outline any relevant information relating to assessment for learning in this module
depending on the size and complexity of your
insert the content for your fundamental here
omit_placeholders.note: OMIT a writer instruction that is verbatim WT TEMPLATE-PLACEHOLDER text the writer never replaced. These are the template's default prompts ('Insert brief introductory text.' / 'Insert appropriate introductory video to pique student interest [max. 3 minutes].' / 'Start with a whakatauki' in [MODULE INTRODUCTION]; 'In this section outline any connections…' in [Connections]; 'Outline any relevant information relating to assessment…'; and the per-lesson [Lesson Overview] prompt 'Depending on the size and complexity of your module, it may or may not be relevant for you to add additional Learning Intentions and Success Criteria…'). Leaving them means the writer supplied NO content, so the human OMITS them entirely — they are NOT surfaced as a CS note. The Lesson Overview prompt is stored as the SHARED PREFIX 'depending on the size and complexity of your' because the Fundamentals subjects (HPFUN*/XFUN01) carry a variant ('…your FUNDAMENTAL, …frame THE LEARNING') of the standard ('…your MODULE, …frame EACH LESSON'); the prefix covers both. The #redFlag emitter (kind 'cs' only) folds the note text (Utils.Fold: lowercase, accents stripped, dashes→hyphen, whitespace collapsed) and, when match=='prefix', drops it if the folded text EQUALS or STARTS WITH any phrase (so the '[max. 3 minutes].' tail and trailing whitespace variants match); no red-flag is counted. These phrases are template boilerplate, never a unique writer note, and the human build never keeps them. Diagnostics (kind 'diagnostic': 'Empty [tag]…', missing URL) are never omitted. Env PLACEHOLDER_OFF surfaces every placeholder as a CS note.

note_tidy._prefixes_note: The CL-0010/CL-0013 ledger prefixes ('Writers Note:' / 'Red Flag:' / 'Designer/Developer To Do:') are in the coalesce list; the legacy 'CS:' / 'RED FLAG:' stay so a NOTESCHEME_OFF (legacy-form) output tidies identically. Matching is case-sensitive startswith, longest-first.
note_tidy.bare_cue_pattern: ^(dev|developer|dev team|cs|creative services|note to dev(eloper)?|note to cs|note for creative services)$
note_tidy._doc:
Post-pass over the FULL assembled page (PageAssembler calls NotesAndComments.TidyDeveloperNotes after OmitPlaceholderResidue, before Indent). THREE behaviours, all on cv2-note

s (cv2-note is excluded from every structural comparison): (5a MENU RELOCATE, env MENUNOTE_OFF) a developer comment rendered INSIDE the module menu (a cv2-note before the

boundary — the menu is #header-scoped) is HELD and re-emitted as the FIRST element inside the body, so the developer sees it — comments are never left inside a menu, where the developer may miss them. (5b COALESCE + BARE-CUE FOLD, env COALESCE_OFF) a RUN of consecutive cv2-notes (nothing but whitespace between) sharing the same prefix collapses to ONE note — only the first line keeps the prefix ('CS:' / 'RED FLAG:' etc.); the following lines drop it and join with
. A note whose body is a bare/bracketed addressee cue ([Dev], [CS], Dev team, 'note to developer') with NO real content is DROPPED (folds forward — the run's prefix carries to the next real line; a standalone bare cue is dropped, e.g. a '[Dev]' in its own coloured span that would otherwise give a contentless 'CS: [Dev]'). The human developer deletes these comments in the final build, so the target here is the developer hand-off rule, not the gold; no documented instruction is silently stripped (the comment is kept, just relocated + tidied). Env NOTETIDY_OFF turns off the whole post-pass.
note_tidy.note: cv2-comment (whitelisted Word comments) are NOT coalesced or relocated by this pass — only cv2-note (the CS / RED FLAG retained writer instructions).

cs_relabel.note: Split retained red notes by SOURCE. A writer→Creative-Services note (the retained instruction: the Instruction_Cues vocabulary + developer-directed questions, plus the undocumented container-positional note) renders with the CS: prefix via cs_form; a converter-emitted TECHNICAL diagnostic (the hardcoded #redFlag messages: empty/malformed tag, missing URL, orphan sub-tag, un-built widget, unmatched menu/container) keeps RED FLAG: via form. The #redFlag emitter picks cs_form only when called with kind='cs'. Greppability per §4.1: 'RED FLAG:' finds exactly the converter issues, 'CS:' finds the writer notes. enabled:false OR env CSRELABEL_OFF renders every note as RED FLAG.

cs_dedupe.note: DEDUPE the doubled CS prefix ('CS: CS Note: for the image…'). When cs_form is about to add the canonical 'CS:' prefix AND the writer's retained note ALREADY opens with a Creative-Services-family cue, that leading cue is folded away so the note reads 'CS: <body>' not 'CS: CS Note: <body>'. The engine builds one case-insensitive regex from cues (longest-first, \b-anchored so 'CSV'/'csc' are safe), an optional ' note'/' notes' suffix, and a trailing run of :,.–- delimiters. SCOPE: only the cs_form path — under CSRELABEL_OFF the prefix is 'RED FLAG:', where a leading 'CS Note:' is NOT a duplicate, so the cue is preserved. RED FLAG diagnostics never begin with a CS cue. NOTE:/answers:/alert-note/activity-note labels are deliberately NOT CS cues and are left intact. The DEV family + addressed 'note to/for <addressee>' forms are folded SEPARATELY by addressee_fold. Never strips a note down to empty (keeps the original if it would). enabled:false OR env CSDEDUPE_OFF keeps the doubled form.

addressee_fold.note: Extends the CS-prefix fold to the remaining redundant ADDRESSEE leads, so a note whose audience the 'CS:' prefix already implies doesn't repeat it. Two branches, both requiring an explicit delimiter: (1) a BARE dev-family cue — 'Dev:', 'Dev team –', 'Developer note:' (bare_cues + optional_suffix); (2) an ADDRESSED form — 'Note to developer:', 'Note to dev team:', 'Note to CS:', 'Note for Creative Services.' (addressed_by + optional 'the' + addressed_cues + optional_suffix). Delimiters folded: : , . – (en-dash) - (hyphen). bare_cues are DEV-ONLY so this never strips a bare CS cue — that stays cs_dedupe's job, independently reversible. \b-anchored so 'development'/'device' are safe. NOTE:/designer/'general note to the designers'/answers/image/video/source are NOT folded (not an audience the CS: prefix subsumes, or content). Never strips to empty. enabled:false OR env ADDRFOLD_OFF turns it off.

red_flag.note:
Ground-truthed canonical form (Tag_Interpretation_Rules.md §4.1): always a block

, inline style with no trailing semicolon (the sanctioned inline-CSS exception), fixed greppable prefix. The writer's own DEV: cue stays inside {text}; a leading CS-family cue is folded into the prefix by cs_dedupe to avoid a doubled 'CS: CS …'. Styling is identical across form/cs_form — only the prefix word differs (still BOLD RED on the front-end).

dual_language._doc: Bilingual reoTranslate body unfold: a reoTranslate module's English|Māori content table -> interleaved <tag reo>{Māori}</tag><tag eng>{English}</tag> in ONE row>col-md-8 wrapper; media (image/audio/video) emitted ONCE, un-paired. Env REOTRANSLATE_OFF.
dual_language._use_mtk_flag_doc: false (default) = the 'MTK WRITERS TEMPLATE' house header does NOT put a module in reoMode (almost every WT carries it — it is the house template NAME, not a bilingual marker, and no genuine bilingual module relies on it alone). Genuine bilingual = reoTranslate body_class OR a code_prefixes match. true (or env MTKREO_OFF=1) = the flag is honoured and puts the module in reoMode.

mtk_leak_guard._doc: Leak guard: on a module whose mtkFlag is set but not honoured (see _use_mtk_flag_doc), a NORMAL-path kept free-body table whose rendered HTML still shows a resolved [tag] falls back to the reoMode placeholder form (cv2-interactive bilingual-unbuilt) that hides it — this covers the kept-table class (OS-family [Click drop], ENG-family [image], [body] tables as in ENGS202/TWHA901). Env MTKGUARD_OFF disables just the guard.

reo_layout_table_grid._note_layout_grid: In reoMode (a bilingual module OR any module the broad mtkFlag flags), a free-body table that ALL the bilingual handlers decline falls through to a cv2-interactive 'bilingual-unbuilt' placeholder that keeps the raw WT [tag] text BY DESIGN. That is right for an un-built widget/spec table, but a CLEAN STRUCTURAL LAYOUT table (a side-by-side image|body panel, every cell led by a structural [tag]) is NOT a widget — the human renders it as a row>col GRID (as in ENGS201's 'Origin stories' image|body table), and the placeholder would leak [body]/[image] as visible text. So before the placeholder, TablesAndGrids.layoutTableGrid is tried (the SAME detector the normal path uses — single-row or all-cells-tagged only, and it BAILS on any widget-member cell tag). A grid is emitted for a clean layout table; a widget/spec/data table still returns null and keeps the placeholder, so no [tag] is newly exposed. env REOLTABLE_OFF = always the placeholder.

proverb_box._doc:
KB 07B §7 'Whakatauki / Proverb' ('Uses a dedicated component:

…

…

', the author optional, TRR107's h3 variation named). Bilingual Writers Templates write the proverb as a bilingual table row `[H1] Proverb ║ [H1] Whakataukī | Whakatauākī:` + `[Body] ║ [Body] `; the human build renders it as a div.whakatauki with the heading row dropped (bilingualContainer fires only on a leading [Whakatauki] TAG, so this row form needs its own rule). BilingualBuilder.bilingualRows: a row whose folded English cell matches eng_head_pattern and Māori cell reo_head_pattern (tags, bold, red markers stripped) is dropped and the NEXT row renders as ONE box in the table's own column — the proverb paragraph(s) joined while a quote is open, bold / italic stripped; a trailing short line (<= author_max_words, no terminal punctuation) = the author (both cells → p > span reo + span eng, the TRR102 gold form; one cell → a plain p); a heading-led cell keeps its heading + paragraphs inside, reo block then eng block (TRR107); any other paragraph is commentary AFTER the box (reo / eng interleaved; TRR114); media after that. Env PROVERBBOX_OFF turns it off.

act_label_box._exclude_doc: TRR102's own gold keeps the intro FREE on most of its label tables, contradicting KB 07B's form, so TRR102 is excluded and keeps the unboxed output (§2 (c)); TRR116 and most of TRR106 / TRR103 are boxed.
act_label_box._intro_h2_level_doc: KB 07B's box holds the title as <h3 reo> / <h3 eng> (the gold agrees); the writer's [H2] in the intro renders h2 inside the box (the free intro is relevelled to h3 by the page's heading pass, which does not reach inside div.activity) — an h2 from the intro table is emitted at this level.
act_label_box._data_rows_handoff_doc: The [Activity: Embedded] table's rows after its marker / [H#] / [Body] / blank rows are the widget's DATA (the nested sentence ║ word ║ picture ║ audio grids, word lists, Note-to-CS lines) → ONE cv2-interactive bilingual-unbuilt hand-off (TablesAndGrids.contentTable, every column kept) inside the activity box, so the picture / audio cells are not lost (a loose-paragraph unfold reads only the first TWO cells). Env ACTDATA_OFF turns off just this hand-off (ACTLABELBOX_OFF turns off both).
act_label_box._doc: KB 07B §7 'Activity Structure' (`| Activity 1A: | Ngohe 1A: |` + `[H2]` title + `[Body]` → ONE div.activity number= holding the reo / eng title + prose; `interactive` when it holds a widget), a §1d FAMILY dialect (code_prefixes). TRR116 / TRR106 write each activity as TWO tables — the bilingual intro (`English ║ Te Reo Māori` / `Activity 4E: ║ Ngohe 4E:` / `[H2] title` / `[Body] …`) and the red `[Activity: Embedded] <type>` table (instructions + the widget's data, often a NESTED table); the human build boxes them TOGETHER, with the title inside div.activity. (A) ContentConverter's reoMode dispatch, BEFORE bilingualTable: a bilingual table whose first content row is a label pair matching label_pattern (bold / red / tags stripped) gathers itself + a following [Activity: Embedded] marker table + its spec tables (the existing gather's stops) into bilingualActivity (label rows skipped, the number read through the bold). (B) data_rows_handoff: in bilingualActivity a MARKER table's rows after its leading marker / heading / body / blank rows are the widget's DATA → ONE cv2-interactive bilingual-unbuilt hand-off (TablesAndGrids.contentTable, every column kept). Env ACTLABELBOX_OFF turns it off.

media_in_place._doc: The human puts each media embed (images, audio, video, audio-image units) in a bilingual cell where the writer typed it, between the paragraphs, not after every paragraph of the row. BilingualBuilder.bilingualSplit records each embed's position (the count of text elements before it in its cell) and bilingualRows' per-element reo/eng interleave emits it before the paragraph pair at that position (counted on the stream the media came from, after the same Activity-label / section-id strip). Only the interleave branch (section_grouping ON) is affected; the plain unfold keeps its order. Env REOMEDIAPOS_OFF.

audio_image_tag._doc:
KB 01E / 04B 'Audio Image': `
`. In a bilingual cell (BilingualBuilder.bilingualSplit) the writer's `[Audio Image]` / `[Audio Image Hover]` / `[AudioImage]` tag line followed by its `[Item N] [Image] desc` and `[Item N] [Audio] name` lines is ONE audio-image unit (id = the audio name, the img = the cell image the converter already builds), rather than the lexicon's `audioimage` alias of `audio` giving an empty audio player + an image + a second audio player. Units the source runs together (no text between them) share one `div.row`, each unit in the `group_cols` column for the run's size (the gold: 2 → col-md-6 offset-md-0 col-12, 4 → col-md-3 col-6); a lone unit stands bare. A broken shape (no image, or no audio after it) emits the plain embeds. Env AUDIOIMGTAG_OFF.

audio_image._status: Default-off. The build matches the human's `row>col paddingR>audioImage>audioImageOption>img` byte-for-byte, BUT the human NESTS the audioImage grid inside the section's `col-md-8` / `div.activity` (with the lesson heading), while this build emits a BARE top-level `<div class="row">` — the rich structure in the WRONG nesting fits the human page worse than a single cv2 widget placeholder. The bilingual page is richly NESTED (section -> activity -> widget), so a piece built in isolation lands in the wrong place. The audioImage build (`ContentConverter.#bilingualAudioImage`) + flag stay here as the base; enabling it needs a HOLISTIC bilingual structural build (row-group the section's heading + grid + widget under one col-md-8 / div.activity). TRR112-style grids (embedded in content tables, not separate 2-row tables) also need the prose+widget split first. env AUDIOIMG_OFF.
audio_image._note_phonics_grid:
The audioImage PHONICS GRID, the most frequent bilingual widget (spec §5b). A reoMode table laid out as a column-aligned IMAGE row (`[Item N] [Image] {desc}`) over an AUDIO row (`[Item N] [Audio] {name}`) is built as the human's `
…` per column (image id = the audio name the JS plays; NO

content_table_guard._note_pairing: Default-on, and it must run WITH section_grouping: the released content tables unfold reo/eng inside the human's div.activity nest, and the embedded-widget marker is re-emitted inside the box. On its own (without the selective boxing + the per-paragraph interleave) unfolding a content table that embeds a widget reference puts the prose in the wrong order and nesting. env REOTABLE_OFF turns it off independently of REONEST_OFF.
content_table_guard._status: The guard stops the scanner over-capturing a bilingual `English|Māori` content table as a widget (so the intro unfolds + the activity box wraps the REAL widget). Unfolding a content table that EMBEDS a widget must still emit the widget in the human's structure (its own row>col / the audioImage grid / etc.) — a bare cv2 placeholder is not enough on modules with no activity box (as in TRR113). The guard + `#bilingualContentTable` + the `#bilingualTable` placeholder + the `#bilingualSplit` consecutive-tag strip are flag-gated here; they run together with section_grouping and REOACT to produce the boxes.
content_table_guard._note_overcapture: The activity-box prerequisite. Writers embed a widget reference (`[Interactive] [Flipcard]`/`[Carousel]`) INSIDE the intro `[Body]` cell of a bilingual `English|Māori` content table (as in TRR102); without this guard `InteractiveScanner.#interactiveInTable` OVER-CAPTURES the WHOLE content table (Activity NX: + [H2] heading + [Body] prose) as a flipCard widget, so the reo/eng intro prose never renders and the activity box lands on the WRONG content. So in reoMode, `#interactiveInTable` is skipped for a table whose row-0 header is `English|Māori` (`#bilingualContentTable`, mirrors `#bilingualHeader`) — the table falls through to `#bilingualTable` and unfolds as reo/eng. A real widget table ([Activity Embedded] [X] opener, flipCard [Item N] data, quiz) has NO English|Māori header → still captured. env REOTABLE_OFF.

bundle_handoff._doc: A widget bundle the bilingual section consumes gets the STANDARD hand-off box (#interactivePlaceholder, hand-off only — InteractiveBuilder.Build is NOT tried for a bilingual widget), the same box every bundle outside a section gets, with its data-cv2-index matching {CODE}_interactives.txt. Otherwise the section would render one bare `cv2-interactive bilingual-unbuilt` box holding only the bundle's FIRST member — an EMPTY <table> when that member is the writer's `[Activity: Embedded] …` tag line — and every later member (the reo/eng heading + instruction table, the data table) would render nothing. env BILHANDOFF_OFF.

section_grouping._note_selective_boxing: Default-on. The human boxes SELECTIVELY: only lesson rows that are true interactive activities are `div.activity`; prose / intro / audioImage-grid sections sit in a BARE `col-md-8` (others are callouts or side columns). So #bilingualSection boxes a real-widget section -> div.activity[number] and leaves a prose/audioImage-grid section as a bare col-md-8, and #bilingualRows interleaves reo/eng PER PARAGRAPH (reo,eng,reo,eng — spec §9b balance) and strips the `Activity NX:`/`Ngohe NX:` label (the human omits it / lifts it to the box's number= attr). The `[H1] N.M` discriminator finds every section, the scanner's #bilingualSectionOpener terminator releases each from an over-capturing bundle, and the nesting renders as the human's `row > col-md-8 > div.activity > row > col-12`. See spec §9e. env REONEST_OFF.
section_grouping._note_section_nesting: Holistic bilingual SECTION nesting. The human wraps every Te Reo lesson SECTION in `#body > div.row > col-md-8 col-12 > div.activity > div.row > col-12 > {heading + reo/eng prose + audioImage grid + the widget}` — ONE nested box per `[H1] N.M` decimal section. Without it each bilingual table would be its own FLAT top-level row + cv2 placeholders, and every nested piece (audioImage / content_table_guard / reo_bundle_activity) would land at the wrong depth. reoMode-scoped (env REONEST_OFF): `ContentConverter.#bilingualSection` triggers on a `[H1] N.M` section-opener table, GATHERS the section's items (bilingual content tables -> reo/eng unfold via #bilingualRows; audioImage grids; a consumed widget bundle -> ONE cv2 marker with bundle._emitted suppressed; black prose) up to the next `[H1] N.M` opener / a non-section callout / page boundary, and wraps the FLAT inner content in the human's `row > col-md-8 > div.activity > row > col-12`. A section that contains a widget -> `div.activity interactive`; a prose-only section -> grouped under a bare `col-md-8` (the standard row-grouping mechanism, reoMode-scoped). Standard modules carry no reoMode and are unaffected. Pairs with content_table_guard (so the prose unfolds rather than cv2-capturing).

pin_title._doc:
KB 07D's MTK lesson skeleton (`

{MAORI_LESSON_HEADING}

`) and the gold put bilingual lesson titles at h2. bilingualLessonTitleHtml forces title_level, but ContentConverter.#relevelHeadings would otherwise rank the title as the page's shallowest free heading and map it to h3. So the title's tags carry the transient writer-digit marker data-wd=title_level; the re-level pass pins it (and still counts it in the rank pool — the page's other headings keep their levels) and strips the marker. Env LESSONPIN_OFF turns the pin off.

lesson_heading._note_lesson_form: Extends the section box to the `[H2] Lesson N` lesson form (the TRR108/114/203/301 family). The section box (`_note_section_nesting`) groups a `[H1] N.M` decimal section; `ContentConverter.#bilingualSection` ALSO opens on a `[H2] (Lesson|Hei Mahi|Ngohe) N` first-content-row table (via `#bilingualLessonNum`, this pattern) when there is no `[H1] N.M`, with TWO differences: (1) the lesson TITLE renders as a BARE `row>col-md-8><h2 reo/eng>` OUTSIDE the box (the human keeps the lesson title at h2, ungrouped), and the activity content gathers into the box from the row AFTER the title; (2) the box `number=` is RESEQUENCED to `{lessonNum}{letter}` with the letter A,B,C,D assigned sequentially within each lesson — the human DISCARDS the writer's irregular letters (TRR203 WT 1A/1E/1H -> human 1A/1B/1C). Everything else is shared: the gather stops at the next `[H2] Lesson N` (a new activity) AND at `#isCalloutTable`, so the `[Alert]`/`Finished` tail falls OUTSIDE the box (the human never puts those alerts inside a box); SELECTIVE boxing keeps a shell lesson with no widget (TRR107) as a bare col-md-8. Disjoint from the `[H1] N.M` family by the marker + reoMode-gated, so standard modules are unaffected. env REOLESSON_OFF (independent of REONEST_OFF). The later 'dipthong-tail' pages of TRR114 / TRR107 ('Oro tōpū', 'Kete Kupu', 'Silly Sentences') are developer-authored shells with no WT source (spec §7), so they are not generated (Framework C).

section_id_number._doc:
KB 07B_MTK_CONTENT_PATTERNS 'Activity Structure'. The bilingual writer's BARE SECTION-ID heading — `| [H1] 1.1 | [H1] 1.1 |`, a numbered section label with no words — is the section's activity NUMBER in decimal form (`
`; the KB: 'Preferred approach: use decimal format (1.1, 1.2, 1.3)'), never a heading: the gold never keeps a bare-id heading and numbers the boxed section with the writer's own id (PNR101/102/104, TRR109/110/111; TRR112/113 re-letter it 1A/1B — the human's letter form, which the KB's preference overrides). The tagged `[H1] N.M` form lives ONLY in Bilingual WTs; an untagged bare `N.M` cell in a Standard WT is a maths decimal, not the signal. TWO seams, both in BilingualBuilder: (1) `bilingualRows`' interleave strip (the same seam that drops the `Activity NX:` label line) also drops a rendered heading whose whole text is a bare section id (`strip_heading`), so no phantom `

1.1

1.1

` pair appears; (2) `bilingualSection`, when the section was opened by `[H1] N.M`, is boxed (has a widget) and found no `Activity NX:` label, numbers the box with the section id as written (`number_from_section`; the label keeps priority). An un-boxed prose section simply loses the phantom heading (the gold leaves it un-boxed and un-numbered). Env REOSECID_OFF turns it off; REONEST_OFF turns off everything above it.

course_code_heading._doc: The bilingual writer's COURSE-CODE heading row — `| [H1] TRR900 | [H1] TRR900 |`, a heading whose whole text is a course / module code — at the head of the MTK Module Introduction table (TRR1 / TRR2 / TRR3, PMT101) and of every PNR activity table is dropped: the gold never renders a bare-code h2-h6 on a Bilingual page (TRR108_0.0 keeps an h1 pair — the one named override). A named override of the KB 07D skeleton comment 'Typically: course code h1'. Stripped in bilingualRows at the section-id seam; the module-code chip (h1 in the header) is untouched. code_pattern = the heading's whole text.

boxed_heading_level._doc:
KB 07B_MTK_CONTENT_PATTERNS 'Activity Structure' + 05B activities. Inside a bilingual SECTION BOX the writer's `[H2]` heading renders at the KB's activity level h3 (`

…

…

`), not at the writer's h2: the heading re-leveller excludes activity-anchored headings from its pool (right for the Standard template, whose `[Activity]` box title is the writer's `[H3]`), but the bilingual section box opens on `[H1] N.M` with the writer's `[H2]` section title INSIDE it. The gold renders these in-box headings at h3 (the label-form family TRR102/108/114/203/301 already uses h3/h4). The PNR family (PNR101/102/104 — the newer 'Te Aka Taumatua' MTK template, whose `[H1] Lesson Title:` section row the gold keeps at h2; 07B does not describe that dialect, so its own gold governs) is excluded via `exclude_code_prefixes`. Mechanism: `BilingualBuilder.bilingualSection`, when the section is boxed, re-levels every `` open/close tag in the gathered inner HTML to `to_level`; h1 and h3+ untouched (the gold keeps the writer's `[H3]` at h3). Env REOBOXH_OFF turns it off.

lesson_table_boundary._note_lesson_row_split: Convention 2: a `[H2] Lesson N` / `[H2] Ngohe N` TABLE-ROW heading opens a lesson page when the lesson number INCREMENTS. The TRR107/108/114/115/203/301/304 family carries no `[LESSON N CONTENT]` tag — it marks each lesson with a `[H2] Lesson N` table-row heading, REPEATED at the top of each sub-activity (TRR114: Lesson 1 ×3, 2 ×3, 3 ×3), so splitting on every marker would over-paginate. The human splits ONLY on a NEW (higher) number (TRR114 → pages 1.0/2.0/3.0). `PageSplitter.Split` (reoMode-scoped) scans a table's first rows for `[H2] (Lesson|Ngohe) N` and opens page N.0 when N > the running lessonOrdinal. Self-discriminating (overview headings are Overview/Key Objectives/… never Lesson N) + reoMode-gated → standard modules untouched. The dipthong-tail lessons (no `[H2] Lesson N`, e.g. TRR114 pp 4-5) + PNR `Hei Mahi` are not covered. env REOPAGE2_OFF (independent of REOPAGE_OFF).

page_split._note_lesson_tag_split: The bilingual PAGE-SPLIT, convention 1. A reoTranslate module's WT marks each lesson with a `[LESSON N CONTENT]` marker that the normaliser resolves to a SECTION_MARKER (NOT a PAGE_BOUNDARY); the overview body is trimmed upstream, so the stream STARTS at `[LESSON 1 CONTENT]`, and without this rule the implicit overview would swallow lesson 1 and shift every later lesson by one. reoMode-scoped (env REOPAGE_OFF): (1) a numbered `[LESSON N CONTENT]` opens lesson page N.0 (mirrors the `lesson` PAGE_BOUNDARY path); (2) a MID-doc `[Title Bar]` is kept on the current lesson page as its title, NOT treated as a sub-document twin (TRR102 lesson 4 uses `[Title Bar]` for its heading); (3) RR-4 KEEPS an empty overview (the bilingual menu page 0.0, body intentionally empty). Convention-1 family = TRR102/103/106/109/111/112/113; the `[H2] Lesson N` TABLE-ROW convention is lesson_table_boundary. reoMode = bilingual only (TRR/PNR prefix / reoTranslate body / mtkFlag), so standard modules are unaffected.

dropdown_menu._doc: The MTK 'Te Aka Taumatua' bilingual Writers Template (the PNR101/102/104 family) opens with a [Content for DROP DOWN MENU] section: ONE English|Maori two-column table holding the whole module menu ([TITLE BAR] row, [H2][TABn] tab-label rows, [H1]/[H2] pane headings, [Body] content), closed by [END OF DROP-DOWN MENU] (PNR102 types it WITHOUT the hyphen), then a [MODULE CONTENT: PAGE 1] marker whose table is the overview body, then [LESSON N CONTENT] lessons. Unless these markers are recognised as content-start, DocxExtractor.TrimFrontMatter would cut EVERYTHING before [LESSON 1 CONTENT] as front matter and the whole overview (menu + title + intro) would vanish. This config drives five coupled pieces: (1) content-start recognition (Input_Doc_Rules content_start_fragments_dropdown); (2) PageSplitter keeps the [MODULE CONTENT: PAGE n] marker's content ON the overview page (module_content_pattern below — the human's 0.0 = menu + module content); (3) InteractiveScanner never opens a widget bundle for the opener (it parses as a 'dropdown' INTERACTIVE invocation — it is a menu marker, not a widget); (4) ContentConverter.#partitionItems routes the opener..closer region's table to the MENU side (flagged _reoDropdown); (5) MenuBuilder.#reoDropdownTabs composes the human's bilingual tabs menu (nav <span reo>/<span eng> labels; per-pane reo/eng element pairs; h4span section heads / h5 lead-ins; the Information pane splits at a 'Connections'-family heading into paddingR|paddingL columns, as in all three human builds). The module title comes from the front-matter metadata table's 'Module Name' row ('Nga tau: 1 | Numbers: 1' — pipe-split, payload order = reo first, the CEDW501 positional-slot precedent; see front_matter_metadata.table_row_fields). The marker family is exactly PNR101/102/104. Env REODROPMENU_OFF turns off ALL five pieces (the overview page is then empty).
dropdown_menu._doc_module_content_all_tables: PageSplitter flags EVERY table in the [MODULE CONTENT: PAGE n] region (until the next structural red marker — [END OF PAGE]/[LESSON N CONTENT]) as _reoModuleContent, not just the FIRST. A writer may split the module intro into several tables (PNR104: a whakatauki table with its own English|Maori header + a 'Module Introduction | Kowae Ako Whakataki' table); an unflagged later table would be declined by bilingualTable (no header) and the module introduction would render as a raw cv2 bilingual-unbuilt dump. The marker modules are exactly PNR101/102/104 (TRR304's opener-less form never enters this branch). false (or env REOMODCONTENT_OFF) flags only the first table.

activity_marker_red._doc_wrap_number: A box opened by the red-wrapped marker (and only such a box — BilingualBuilder.isRedOnlyActivityMarker; every other activity path is untouched) takes the KB 07D lesson wrapper row > col-md-8 col-12 (wrap) and, with no id of its own, the KB 07B decimal number '<lesson>.<k>' — k = its position among the page's activity boxes (number; consecutive). Without them the bare box would sit directly in #body with no number.
activity_marker_red._doc: BilingualBuilder.activityMarkerRe is anchored at the cell start, but the MTK writer types [Activity: Embedded] in the template's red style — the raw cell reads '🔴[RED TEXT] [Activity: Embedded] Word select [/RED TEXT]🔴' — so the red-run markers are stripped before the marker test; otherwise isActivityMarker never matches, the bilingual activity gather (ContentConverter → BilingualBuilder.bilingualActivity, KB 07B 'Activity Structure': div.activity.interactive[number] > row > col-12) never runs, and the instruction table and its data tables render as top-level bilingual-unbuilt dumps. The marker row renders as the writer's own note (NotesAndComments.redFlag kind cs — a cv2-note) instead of a stray widget-type paragraph. Env ACTMARKRED_OFF turns it off.

overview_table_tabs._doc: KB 07A §4 'Module Menu Tabs' + the 07D §19.1 / §19.2 skeletons (the TRR family). With Input_Doc_Rules.content_start.table_title_bar_opener keeping the table-cell [TITLE BAR], an MTK overview page holds the writer's overview TABLES: the title-bar table ([H2] Overview), then one table per menu role ([H1] Strand / Dispositions / Key objectives / Critical Point / Learning Intentions — or the [H2] Key objectives / Information dialect of TRR109–113), then the [H1] TRR900 / Module Introduction table, which is BODY (KB: 'Body content of overview page'). ContentConverter.#partitionItems captures the title-bar table and every following table whose first heading row matches a role (untagged black lines between them stay body; a tag item or a non-role table ends the run); MenuBuilder.#reoOverviewTabs composes one tab per role on the reo_tabs shell: the role heading is the nav label (the KB label below when given, else the writer's heading) and is not repeated in the pane (render_heading: the Learning Intentions <h4><span>); the KB 5-TAB DEFAULT merges a Critical Point table into the Key objectives pane before it ('When in doubt: default to 5 tabs'; the WT offers no discriminator — TRR107 / TRR304's six-tab golds are named overrides); heading rows → reo/eng pairs (section_heading_match → <h4><span>, else <h5>; the Overview pane keeps the writer's bold, KB 'h5 with b'); body rows → BilingualBuilder.bilingualSplit pairs; a pane with a two_column_match heading is the KB's two-column Learning Intentions layout, split at the first column_split_match heading once the left column has content (KB: right column = Planning / What do I need / Connections). Env REOOVTABS_OFF renders the tables as body.
overview_table_tabs._doc_untagged_roles: A table whose first content row carries NO [H] tag may still open a role pane when its text names one of these roles (TRR304: 'Ngā Whenu Ngā Toi Mokopuna Ngā Whāinga Matua / Strands Dispositions', typed untagged); the row is the label only. Overview / Information / Learning Intentions are never matched untagged — those words open ordinary prose too.
overview_table_tabs._doc_intro_match: The table that ends the menu run is the overview's BODY introduction (KB 07A §2 'Module Introduction … Body content of overview page'); when its first heading row is the course code alone ([H1] TRR900) it has no English|Māori header row, so it is flagged _reoModuleContent and takes the header-less bilingual unfold (BilingualBuilder.bilingualTable forceNoHeader, as for the dropdown-menu modules) instead of the raw bilingual-unbuilt table dump with its literal [H1] / [Body] tags.
overview_table_tabs.two_column_match: ^(learning intentions|success criteria|planning your time|what do i need|nga whainga ako|paeru angitu|whakamaheretia|he aha taku)
overview_table_tabs.column_split_match: ^(planning your time|what do i need to get started|whakamaheretia|he aha taku hei timata)

logical_to_element.rule: The writer's H-digit is a LOGICAL level resolved in context, never a fixed element (§5.1). In body context the digit shifts DOWN one level; page-title headings are built by the skeleton, not here; overview menu headings are CONSUMED into the menu (menu.tab_map below).
logical_to_element._relevel_headroom_note: The body emission normally clamps to h5, but when #relevelHeadings is active it RANKS the page's distinct heading levels back into h3..max_level — so the emission is allowed ONE extra intermediate level (h6) for a writer [H5]. Without it [H4]->h5 and [H5]->h5 collapse before the re-leveller sees them, so a genuine 3-level [H3]/[H4]/[H5] page (e.g. OSAI401-04: human h3 'Data, data, data' > h4 'How AI uses data' > h5 'Data collection'…) would lose its third level. With the headroom the re-leveller sees {h4,h5,h6}->{h3,h4,h5} and reproduces the human's hierarchy. The h6 is intermediate only — the re-leveller always normalises it into base..max_level; when re-levelling is disabled the ceiling stays h5 so no h6 reaches the output.
logical_to_element.lesson_first_h2: Becomes the page's body <h3> with any leading 'Lesson N' / 'Lesson N:' prefix stripped (the lesson number already lives in the header/module-code).
logical_to_element.no_span_rule: <span> wrappers appear ONLY inside header <h1> titles — never on body h2–h5.

strip_italic._note:
The human ships BODY headings PLAIN (every template, almost every subject), so a whole-heading *italic* the writer typed (a section heading like '[H3] *What is online harassment or abuse?*') is stripped rather than rendered as

…

. The exception is the ENGLISH-READING families (ENGS / ENGC / ENGR / ENGJ / ENGI), where a kept italic is a NAMED WORK (book/story title, e.g. 'The Three Billy Goats Gruff') with no derivable difference from a section heading -> excluded by subject prefix; reo/bilingual modules are excluded via MenuBuilder.isReoModule (never mtkFlag). Strips via MenuBuilder.stripTextItalic (FA icons guarded). env HEADITALIC_OFF turns it off.

header_cell_plain._doc: A TABLE HEADER CELL IS PLAIN: the human build almost never bolds a whole <th> cell, and KB 05D's form is <tr><th>Header 1</th>…, plain. The first-row-header rule promotes a writer's **bold** row to <th>, so without this the cell's own markdown would render <b> inside it. At the cell emit, free-body tables only: a header cell whose rendered content is exactly one <b>/<strong> span with no other bold inside drops the wrapper; data cells (<td>) keep theirs (the gold keeps <td><b> for a matrix's row labels).

image_row._doc: A FIRST ROW HOLDING A PICTURE IS A DATA ROW. A header cell is a column label (KB 05D); a picture is the row's content. When a kept table's first row would be the header and one of its rendered cells holds an (whatever route built it — the writer's [image] tag, a red image reference, a title-anchored image cell), the row renders with the data-cell template () instead. Where the human build keeps the picture in a table cell it writes (seven modules — ENGC401, ENGS301, ENGS401's judge tables, MXDI202, XLP01, XMES202, XMES203) and in one (CHFUN04). The cells are rendered once as the header row and re-tagged, so a header cell's bold rule stands for that row.

first_row_header._doc: A kept table's first row is the header row (<th>) — KB 05D's `<tr><th>Header 1</th>…` form, a column LABEL — UNLESS one of its cells runs to data_row_min_words words or more: a sentence is not a label, and that row renders as data (<td>; a [Body, bold] cell keeps its <b> as data cells do). In the human build a first row with a long (>= 9-word) cell is almost always <td>, while shorter first rows are mostly <th>; no other shape signal (columns, rows, bold) separates them. FREE-BODY tables only — a table inside an un-built widget's hand-off dump keeps its raw first-row form (the placeholder containment). The word count strips the red-run markers and the ** / __ emphasis. Env TBLHEADLONG_OFF = every first row th.

cell_bullets._doc:
A kept table cell whose ' / '-joined lines (the extractor's in_cell_line_break marker) include a '• ' bullet renders through ListsAndRuns.renderBlackText — the body's own paragraph + nested-list machinery: a lead line is a

, a bullet run is a

  • list (a numbered run an
      ) — instead of the raw joined string with literal '• ' text. In the human build a bullets-only cell is a bare
        in the td and a lead-text + bullets cell is

        lead

          ; a NON-bullet multi-line cell has no consistent form and is untouched. Only a FREE-BODY cell that renderCellInline declines (no structural lead tag); a hand-off dump's table keeps its raw form (the placeholder containment). Where the human keeps the writer's table, a bulleted cell is a list about twice as often as plain lines, and the whole score gain sits on those tables. Where the human rebuilds the writer's table as an accordion, prose or a widget, the writer's tag still decides the component (KB 14, Decision Framework A1): the table stays and its cell keeps the list. That costs those pages a few skeleton lines the human's rebuild does not have. No table-level cue in the writer's template separates the two (column count, header row, bullets-only or lead + bullets cells, every data cell bulleted, the host, the series), so the rule covers every free-body table. Env TBLCELLLIST_OFF = the raw joined string with literal '• ' text.

numbered._doc: A WORD-NUMBERED LIST IN A CELL IS AN <ol>. The extractor parses a cell's paragraphs without the numbering map, so every list item in a cell carries the bullet prefix '• ' (its text and the document's list counters are untouched by this rule), and it records beside the rows the text of each paragraph whose Word list is numbered (the table block's cellNumbered). On this list path such an item renders as a numbered item, so the cell's run becomes an <ol>. Where the human keeps a cell's list, the writer's Word format decides its kind: a numbered Word list is an <ol> about 20 times in 21 and a bulleted one a <ul> about 96 times in 97. Elsewhere the writer's cell numbering stays as it was: across the corpus the human rarely shows it, so it is never restored into the cell text. Env TBLCELLOL_OFF = every cell list item a <ul> item.

grid._doc: The same in a LAYOUT-GRID cell (a table rebuilt as a row of columns, renderCellParts — an activity box, a column of text beside a picture): a cell list item whose Word list is numbered renders as a numbered item, so the run is an <ol> (the gold's form in activity boxes 35 of 35, in body columns 26 of 31). Matched by the item's own text against the cell's cellNumbered record, as on the kept-table path. Env GRIDCELLOL_OFF = a grid cell's list items stay <ul> items.

cell_paragraphs._doc:
A TABLE CELL'S PARAGRAPHS ARE LINES, NOT SLASHES. The extractor joins a Word cell's paragraphs with the in-cell marker « / » and records the paragraphs themselves beside the rows (cellParas); a free-body data cell of two or more paragraphs renders them as lines joined by joiner, so the learner reads «Tīkina o tino pene…» and «Kautehia ia kara…» on two lines instead of one line broken by a slash. A writer's own « / » inside one paragraph («Whenu / Strand») is never split — the paragraphs come from the side-channel, not from the marker — and a cell a caller rewrote keeps its single-line form. The human build writes these lines with
more than any other form (CBI, CEDK, XGF, MXDB, CEDW almost always). Hand-off boxes keep the raw marker (a developer reference).

cell_image_reference._doc: THE WRITER'S IMAGE REFERENCE IN A TABLE CELL IS THE CELL'S IMAGE. A writer often types the picture a cell should hold as a red label with no bracket — «Image: iStock: symbol on speech bubble:», «Image RHS: iStock: board walk along the lake waihola:», «Image on RHS of text: istock: Lake Wanaka New Zealand:» — followed by the stock or source address. A kept table cell prints red text as cell text, so the learner read the label and a raw link. In a FREE-BODY table cell, a red span that holds no bracket, opens with an image word and reads as a label (label_pattern: the image word, then a colon within a few words), together with its web address — inside the span, typed right after it, on the cell's next line, or (with no address typed) the table link whose words sit inside the span — renders through the cell's own image emitter (TablesAndGrids.cellImage: the run's Mode P / D image, the iStock id giving the file name) in the place the writer put it; the cell's other words stay. Text after the address on the same line stays as the cell's text. A span with a bracket, a label with no resolvable address, and hand-off boxes are left exactly as they were. The human build carries the picture on about two thirds of these (its stock id in an ), in the cell or beside the table. The layout-grid cell (a table rebuilt as a row of columns) has its own switch, grid.
cell_image_reference._trailing_note_doc: The cell's next line, wholly red with no bracket, straight after the reference («(image needs to be flipped vertically as above)») is the writer's note on that picture: it renders as a Writers Note beside the image (the layout cell's red-note form) instead of cell text. false = it stays cell text.

grid._doc: The same reference in a LAYOUT-GRID cell (renderCellParts): the part renders as the image (cellImage) in place, before the red-note rule that would otherwise print a wholly red reference as a Writers Note, and instead of the learner paragraph a red label with a black address printed.

semicolon_label._doc: The label's colon may be a semicolon («Image; iStock; organic waste; https://…» — CEDK401, CEDT501): some writers separate the label's parts that way. When on, this label_pattern replaces the block's own.

cell_red_request._doc: THE WRITER'S RED REQUEST IN A TABLE CELL IS A WRITERS NOTE. A kept table cell prints red text as cell text, because a red span in a cell is usually a data label the learner should read. A red span that is a request to the developer («Please insert the image on page 6», «Can we split this picture please», «(Please use a diagram that looks like this: )») was printed to the learner the same way. In a FREE-BODY kept-table cell, a red run (consecutive red spans read as one) with no bracket, at least min_words words and an instruction cue (Instruction_Cues.cue_patterns — the same test that makes an un-bracketed red span in the free body a Writers Note) renders as a Writers Note (NotesAndComments.redFlag kind cs) where the writer put it; the cell's other words stay. A red run with no cue — a data label, a header label, red answer or learner text — stays visible as before. Runs the image-reference rule has taken are not seen here. The layout-grid cell has its own red-note rule (layout_table_grid.red_part_note). Hand-off boxes keep the raw form.

cell_audio_word._doc:
THE WRITER'S RED [word] BESIDE ITS WORD IS THE WORD'S AUDIO BUTTON. A te reo dictionary table puts, in each row, the writer's red «[kuia]» (the audio request) in the first cell and the word «kuia» in the next, then its meaning; the page printed «[kuia]» to the learner. The human build makes every such cell the word's audio button, `
` (BLL271 / 273 / 274 / 275 / 276: 58 of 58 rows), named from the VISIBLE word in the next cell (BLL271's «[teketeko]» beside «tekoteko» → tekoteko): folded (no macrons, lower case), its other characters dropped, its words joined by name_joiner («Ngāti Porou» → ngati-porou, «Auē!» → aue). In a FREE-BODY kept table, a cell that is wholly red and only «[w]» (at most max_words words) whose next cell is plain text (no red, no bracket, at most max_words words) folding to w within max_edit letters renders as `form`; a first row led by such a cell is a data row, not the header (a header label carries no audio request). Any other bracketed red cell stays as before. Hand-off boxes keep the raw form.

rows._doc: The vertical half: a cell merged down rows (w:vMerge restart + its continuation cells) renders with rowspan and its EMPTY continuation cells are omitted. Measured over the whole corpus it moves 25 pages / 21 modules, 10 up / 9 down, net positive, every gate held. The dips are tables the human rebuilt in another form (ENGC301's quiz «Options» column as a widget, AGH1007's shared description repeated in each row) or whose header row differs (ENGS401's judge tables — the gold's own rowspan, a <td> first row); the human build uses rowspan where it keeps the merge (ENGI405, ENGJ201, ENGS202, ENGS401, CEDK501, MXDI301, MXFUN01). When off, a vertically merged cell renders as before (the origin cell, then empty cells below it).

merged_cells._doc: THE WRITER'S MERGED TABLE CELL IS A MERGED CELL. A Word table cell merged across columns (w:gridSpan) renders with colspan, so a merged header such as «Income (weekly)» spans the whole table instead of leaving a short, ragged row. The vertical half (rowspan) is the `rows` block below. The extractor records each cell's Word facts (span width, vertical-merge state, grid column) beside the table's rows; the text form, the widget builders and the hand-off dumps read nothing new. Applied to FREE-BODY tables only (a hand-off dump keeps the writer's raw grid) and only when the recorded facts line up with the rows the renderer receives (a caller that re-cut the rows keeps the plain form). A continuation cell that carries text stays a visible cell. The human build uses colspan on most plain tables where the writer merged across columns, and where it does not it moved the merged row out of the table or rebuilt the grid — never a short row; where the writer merged down rows it uses rowspan or drops the merged column, almost never a column of empty cells.

comparison._note_enabled: Enabled (borders AND equal columns): a TRUE two-column comparison table (every row two cells, the header row an opposite pair from this lexicon) renders as table table-bordered tableFixed — borders kept, a NAMED override of KB 05D l.239. The lexicon excludes non-comparison pairs (input/output, question/answer, English/te reo, English/Maori) and relations that are not opposites (cause/effect, causes/effects, problem/solution); a sideways-typed comparison (as in AGH1003) is not detected. Env TBLCOMPARE_OFF gives the plain bordered class (table table-bordered).
comparison.note: The human build's two-column contrast-header tables use no consistent class (plain table / table-bordered / bordered+tableFixed / tableFixed), so the lexicon above follows the KB's comparison-table rule rather than the corpus; the hook is data-driven so the KB can refine it.

kb_class_form.rule: KB 05D level 1: every content table is emitted as <table class="table table-bordered"> inside the table-responsive wrapper (the human build borders most tables in all four templates; on the Standard plain-table pages this is a NAMED override of the gold). 05D's optional noHover / center-text are not emitted. Env TBLBORDER_OFF gives the bare table class.

table.note: Standalone content tables only — a table inside an interactive block is captured data, not rendered here. The <table> is wrapped in <div class="table-responsive"> to match the human convention (e.g. AGH1008, BLL233, MXDB202 wrap every table) — Bootstrap's horizontal-scroll wrapper for narrow screens.

inline_format.info_trigger_note: INLINE info-trigger annotation (a hover/rollover definition the writer dropped INLINE as 'term [hovertrigger: DEFINITION] continuation'). The scanner (InteractiveScanner standalone-marker handling) re-stitches the split fragments and encodes the DEFINITION in a private-use sentinel right after the anchor term; #inlineMarkup turns 'anchorDEF' into this template ({info} = the definition → the human's info= attribute; {anchor} = the bolded/italicised term). Built ONLY when the anchor is a clear bold/italic run (the human's 1,645 inline infoTrigger spans; ENGC201-00 whakatauki / ENGC201-01 universal expressions / ENGC201-02 contractions); a non-derivable anchor (e.g. a plain unbolded word) drops the sentinel to plain text (the definition deferred — never a leaked inline string). Edit this string to restyle with no code change.
inline_format.convention_note:
The Te Kura house convention is PRESENTATIONAL inline markup — /, NOT semantic / (the human build uses / far more often). Read by ContentConverter.#inlineMarkup (**bold** → , *italic* → ). ( and
are also used by the human but have no source marker in the writer's ** / * markdown, so are not derivable here.)

external_link_button_standalone.note:
A STANDALONE [external link] (NOT 'external link button') whose item content is ONLY a bare URL — no descriptive label text and no [LINK:] hyperlinked phrase — is the human's external-resource BUTTON, exactly like the [external link button] tag. #inline emits buttons['external link button'].form (
LABEL
) with the default label ('Go to website', or 'Go to video' for a video host) — the exact wording (e.g. 'Be internet awesome', 'Netsafe') is the human's editorial coinage, not in the WT. The human renders the URL-only form as an externalButton (OSBY201/OSBY101, OSAH401, ENFUN01, ENGC201, OSGM101, …), while a TRAILING labelled / [LINK:]-phrase form stays an inline link — so the discriminator is 'item text is the bare URL alone'. Fires only on the external-link tag with empty label text + a URL. A LEADING [external link]+phrase is also a button — see external_link_button_labelled. Env EXTBTN_OFF renders the bare URL as

URL

.

external_link_video_embed._doc: A STANDALONE [link]-FAMILY PARAGRAPH WHOSE TEXT IS NOTHING BUT A VIDEO URL IS THE EMBEDDED VIDEO. The writer types '[Link] https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=…' on its own line, under an '[embed video with image and play button]' instruction or after 'Watch the following video…'; the human EMBEDS it (videoSection + iframe) rather than showing a 'Go to video' button. A link with several visible words (a titled link) stays the inline anchor / button. TWO SEAMS: (A) the [external link] inline branch — a url-only item whose url is a VIDEO url renders MediaBuilder.media (the standard [video] embed) instead of the button; (B) MediaBuilder.media's following-link source — a [video]/[embed] element with no own url whose next unconsumed item is such a url-only external-link TAG item takes that url and consumes the item (the black-line rule extended to the tagged line). host_match falls back to buttons.video_destination.host_match. Env LINKVID_OFF turns off both seams.

external_link_button_labelled.note:
A LEADING [external link] tag (governs the paragraph — '[external link] __The Story of Mauao__ [LINK:url]', the tag FIRST, the linked resource title as the whole rest) is the human's external-resource BUTTON, not the inline

weave. DISCRIMINATOR = tag POSITION: a LEADING [external link]+phrase -> externalButton (as in ENGI302, ENGI303, ENGJ201); a TRAILING [external link] (appended after a phrase in a bullet/sentence — OSBY201 '...Complete an online contact form [LINK] [external link]', OSAH401) stays the inline weave, which the human never renders as a button. Trailing forms reach #inline's !text early-return; only a leading tag (the phrase in blackAfter) reaches this branch. The human's class is 'button externalButton'; the standalone-bare-URL form keeps its own 'externalButton'. The href is the WT [LINK:] URL (the human re-hosts PDFs / coins copy-doc links — non-derivable editorial). Guarded: primary.tag==='external link' (leading) + a short label (<=label_max_words, no end-punctuation) so a leading ext-link governing a prose sentence can never become a giant button. Env EXTBTNLABEL_OFF renders the inline

link.

all_external_links_videos.note:
A writer '[all external links]' instruction governing a 'Videos:' block converts the FOLLOWING [video] items in that section to external-link BUTTONS (the human renders them as
TITLE
, NOT embeds — the instruction declares these videos are external links, as in OSBY201). The button LABEL is the [video] item's italic title (e.g. '*Why be kind*' → 'Why be kind'); the URL is the video link. A section pre-pass marks each governed [video] (governance resets at the next heading/page boundary); the [video] branch reads the flag. The rule is keyed on the INSTRUCTION, not a module code. Env ALLEXTVID_OFF renders standard video embeds.

stopwatch_build._exclude_note: A `[designer note]` / `[dev note]` span DESCRIBES a widget the writer requested elsewhere (BLL262: `[designer note] Please follow the design below… The stopwatch/timer should be displayed alongside the mats…` after its own `[interactive stopwatch]`) — it never builds a second stopwatch.
stopwatch_build._doc: THE WRITER'S STOPWATCH. A writer's RED request (`[Insert timer on the side that shows minutes and seconds]`, `Can we insert a stopwatch on the RHS…`, `[Interactive Stop Watch] Placed over on the right side of the activity…`, `[Please add a stopwatch]`) is built as the stopwatch the human build adds, not left as a red Writers Note, a table-dump line or visible learner text. On the whole-span instruction path a red span naming a stopwatch / timer (cue_pattern, minus exclude_pattern: CS image notes, pictures, URLs) builds KB 04C's `stopWatch` in an `alertActivity` box (04C: 'commonly placed inside alertActivity sidebars'), HELD as the side column of the row it sits in (the pendingSideAlert pairing — the human's col-md-4 beside the activity, usually in alertActivity), inline when a side box is already pending; an adjacent second cue span is absorbed. Variant: KB 14.7 for BLL (`noMilliSeconds noHours`), else `noMilliSeconds noHours` when the request names minutes / seconds, else the 04C base. Env STOPWATCH_OFF turns it off.

table_cells.exclude_pattern_note: A visible text ending in a file extension (`Tukutuku.jpg`) passes the address shape but is a file name, never woven. Web-page endings (.html / .php) and every domain ending stay addresses.
table_cells.anchor_pattern_note: Only a link whose VISIBLE text is itself a web address or an email address is woven into a cell (`www.youthline.co.nz`, `help@netsafe.org.nz`): a table block's link list also carries its image / file / video asset references (iStock titles, SharePoint files, YouTube clips, a single hyperlinked letter) and descriptive phrases whose text recurs elsewhere in the table, which the human mostly does not link — only the address shape is the writer's unambiguous learner-facing link.

phrase_links._doc: THE WRITER'S PHRASE LINK IN A TABLE CELL KEEPS ITS ADDRESS. Beside the address-shaped links above, a cell also weaves a link whose visible words are a phrase of at least min_words words («online contact form» → netsafe.org.nz/report) when its target is an ordinary web page: not a stock-image, video, file-share, drive or LMS host (asset_host_pattern — those links are the writer's asset references, a picture's title, a clip, a file; an image-search or mail-safelink address is a source, not a page) and not a file. The gold links these phrases (the OS series' Netsafe «online contact form», the TWHK volunteering pages). Env CELLPHRASELINK_OFF = address-shaped links only.

table_cells.note: THE WRITER'S HYPERLINK IN A TABLE CELL. The weave below also runs in the three table-cell renderers (TablesAndGrids.renderCellInline's segments, the data-table cell fallback, renderCellParts' text flush + heading), which receive the table block's own links, so a writer's cell hyperlink renders as a link as the human keeps it (OSBY401 2.0 `Email help@netsafe.org.nz` / `online contact form`, CEDW501 / CEDT501 `www.youthline.co.nz`, CEDK501 `www.sorted.org.nz`). Free-body cells only — a table inside an un-built widget's hand-off box stays the raw dump. Env CELLLINKWEAVE_OFF turns it off.

hyperlink_weave.note:
A run HYPERLINKED in the Writers Template (a real w:hyperlink, captured by DocxExtractor as block.links {text,target}) is woven onto its DESCRIPTIVE phrase as phrase, the human convention (the human links descriptive phrases, not bare URLs). The writer's [external link] tag is an 'opens externally' MODIFIER on the phrase, not its own element, so it emits no separate bare-URL

when the block already carries a descriptive-phrase hyperlink (#inline suppress). Conservative: exact phrase text, first occurrence per line, skipped if already inside an or if the link text IS the URL (the bare-URL rule links those). Env LINKWEAVE_OFF turns off BOTH the weave and the [external link] suppress (plain phrase + separate bare URL).

info_trigger_punct_anchor._whole_line_doc: When the line is ONLY a short term (≤ whole_line_max_words words) + its punctuation + the marker — `setting.` as a list item (ARFUN05), `Ka rawe tō mahi!` as a paragraph (BLL272–276), `WIE HEIßT DU? WIE HEIßEN SIE?` (GENO901) — the whole line, punctuation INSIDE, is the anchor: the human's own form (`setting.`), rather than a last-word span.
info_trigger_punct_anchor._last_word_upper_doc: The last-word anchor needs a CAPITALISED definition: on the 32 last-word candidates the anchor was the gold's term for 17 of 22 capitalised definitions (`Looking at the whole picture…` → holistically) but 4 of 10 lower-case ones — a lower-case def mostly glosses a term named EARLIER in the sentence (HIS1006 `the belief that certain groups…` = stereotype, HIS1002 `atolls in Mā’ohi Nui` = Moruroa) or is a note (TEFUN08 `the single sign on?`). The bold and quoted anchors need neither.
info_trigger_punct_anchor._doc: THE HOVER DEFINITION AFTER THE FULL STOP. ListsAndRuns.inlineMarkup wraps the word right before a woven hover sentinel; a writer who typed the marker after the sentence's punctuation (`…organic matter. [hover definition: material that has come from…]`, AGH1002; `…wellbeing holistically. [Hover: Looking at the whole picture…]`, CEDW501) leaves no such word, and the definition would be dropped. So before the drop, the bold / italic run, the quoted “phrase”, or — for a definition of min_def_words+ words (a one-word def is a translation whose word sits elsewhere: ANZH205's `Sovereignty`) — the last word right before 1–2 punct_class marks becomes the anchor; the punctuation stays after the span. note_pattern keeps a writer NOTE on the drop path: `on ‘Fibre’` (HES1002), `over Māori boy`, `colour 3`, `(`, `Blue text:`, `production – the process…` (a term – def the writer anchors elsewhere), a file name, `with image`. Env HOVERPUNCT_OFF.

info_trigger_inline.note: A SELF-CLOSED inline trigger marker ('anchor [audio trigger DEF]' / '[hover trigger DEF]', the DEFINITION carried INSIDE the marker's own red span so there is NO separate ']' closer) is woven onto its preceding anchor word as anchor (using the inline_format.info_trigger template), instead of breaking the paragraph and dropping the def. The DEF is recovered in ORIGINAL case from the marker text after 'trigger' (parse.remainders is lowercased/mangled). InteractiveScanner inserts the U+E000 sentinel right after the anchor; ContentConverter.#inlineMarkup builds the span. Conservative: fires ONLY on the self-closed form with a non-empty def AND a preceding anchor word; the SPLIT-bracket form ('[hover trigger DEF' + a separate ']' item, as in ENGJ302/MXDI301) is a distinct tokenisation handled by the hasCloser path. Env INFOTRIG_OFF keeps the paragraph-break behaviour.
info_trigger_inline._closer_host_skip_empty_doc:
THE BACK-TO-BACK SPLIT TRIGGER. The split-bracket form (`[HInfo trigger: ] def ]`, the def in black between a red opener and a red `]` closer) anchors on the preceding item; when two triggers follow each other (`…such as who [HInfo trigger: ] asks about a character ] , what [HInfo trigger: ] asks about a thing or idea ] , where …`, BLL243) that item is the closer the first trigger emptied, so the second one's sentinel would start a bare line — its definition dropped and the sentence broken into `

, where

` paragraphs. The host is therefore the nearest preceding item of the same paragraph that still carries text — the self-closed branch's and the hover weave's own rule. Env TRIGHOST_OFF.

named_anchor._doc: THE UNQUOTED NAMED ANCHOR. The writer names the hovered word in the marker head WITHOUT quotes: `[Rollover definition for supreme: Ultimate or final.]` (HIS1005 — typed on its own line after the paragraph), `[Hover on identities: Who we are.]` (ARFUN01 — inline, after the word), `[roll over definition mamae: painful, sore, hurt]` (HIS1006). Appending these after the host's LAST word would fail when the host ends a sentence (no word there), and the definition would be dropped. So the TERM (patterns[] group 1; a leading the / a / an stripped) is searched — whole word, case-insensitive, never inside an earlier woven definition, never a word that already carries one — in the nearest `lookback` text-carrying items when the marker stands on its own line, and ONLY in its own paragraph when it is inline (the nearest text shares its source paragraph: ARFUN05's 'setting. [hover on time: Where is the story taking place?]' — a writer typo — keeps the placement on 'setting' instead of reaching back into the 'time' bullet); the sentinel lands after its FIRST occurrence when the marker stands on its own line (a different source paragraph — the gold's HIS1005 'supreme'), after its LAST when the marker is inline in the same paragraph (the word just before it); after any closing ** / * markup so a bold anchor wraps whole. A marker with a lifted leading anchor (A3) or a quoted anchor keeps its own path; no TERM, or no match in the lookback → the plain last-word append. A standalone marker's own trailing text stays its own paragraph (never glued onto a foreign one). Env HOVERNAMED_OFF turns it off.

pre_anchor_paren._doc: Form (A6) of InteractiveScanner.#weaveHoverDefinition: THE MARKER BEFORE ITS ANCHOR, THE DEFINITION IN PARENTHESES. A bare hover head typed in front of the hovered words with the definition in parentheses after them — black parentheses (`[Rollover Definition] features (Parts of the product.) are…` TEFUN01; `[Hover Trigger] **digits** (definition: Any of the symbols…)` MXDI301, the `definition:` / `definition when hovered:` lead stripped) or a red `(` + a black definition + a red `)` (`In [Roll over definition] ancient Mesoamerica ( where countries like Mexico are today ), they made…` TEFUN03, ENGR202, CHFUN07). The human's span sits on those anchor words; without this the first would show a literal parenthesis and the second would split the sentence into three paragraphs. The anchor (≤ max_anchor_words) + the sentinel definition + the rest of the sentence join the nearest preceding text of the SAME source paragraph (or become the item's own text when the marker opens the paragraph). Runs before the `trigger` skip; a marker resolving to a real non-infoTrigger widget is left alone. Env HOVERPREANCHOR_OFF turns it off.

paren_def._doc: THE PAREN DEF: a CLOSED bare `[hover]` whose definition the writer typed in parentheses right after it, black — `Hoa ako [hover] (learning partner) could find a class or a book to follow` (XDLS902, the learning-support family's standard idiom; XDLS502 / 902 / 903 / 905 / 906). Without it the weave finds no definition and the tag and THE REST OF THE SENTENCE go into a red Writers Note. The human's infoTrigger carries exactly the parenthesised text, so that text is the def (it weaves onto the preceding word like every other hover form), and the sentence continues after it. The other bare forms are unchanged (the def inside the red span after the bracket is form C; a bare tag followed by an unbracketed sentence — CEDK401 — has no consistent human form). Env HOVERPAREN_OFF.

split_bracket.leading_anchor_note: The ANCHOR-BEFORE-BRACKET shape: after DocxExtractor merges the writer's adjacent red runs the marker span reads 'ANCHOR [hover|rollover|mouseover SEP DEF]' — the hovered WORD sits INSIDE the red span, before the bracket, so head_pattern (^\[) fails and the whole span would leak as a 'CS:' note (breaking the paragraph / fragmenting a [whakataukī] box). WT: CEDW501 'He kākano ahau i ruia mai i 🔴Rangiātea [Hover: 🔴🔴Represents a place of origin… for all Māori.]🔴', and the body 'proud of your 🔴whānau🔴🔴 [Hover: People linked…]🔴'. When the merged span does NOT start with '[' but matches ' [hover…]', the anchor text is lifted out and appended to the preceding host with its LAST word woven as word (the same U+E000 sentinel), and the DEF is recovered after the COLON inside the bracket ('Hover: DEF'). The human renders these terms as infoTriggers (CEDW501 whānau/iwi/Rangiātea, CEDT501 perspective/pātai/clarification, CEDR501 accurate, …). The 'trigger'-keyword + widget guards still exclude MXDB301 '[Hover Triggers…]' / SSOG101. SCOPE: only the COLON 'Hover:' form is woven here. The SPACED-DASH form ('Hover - DEF' / 'Hover – DEF', CEDT501 kaupapa/mana/erase) keeps its own behaviour: when the dash marker is a SEPARATE red span (anchor not merged) it goes through the split-bracket path, where the A2 'def-in-next-item' can mis-grab a following bullet. Env HOVERANCHOR_OFF turns it off (independent of HOVERSPLIT_OFF/HOVERDEF_OFF).
split_bracket.note: TWO split/orphaned bracket shapes, both reversible via env HOVERSPLIT_OFF (independent of HOVERDEF_OFF). (A1) lead_orphan: the marker's opening '[' sits in the preceding BLACK run, so the resolved item text begins 'hover definition] DEF' with NO leading '[' and head_pattern (^\[) fails (AGH1004-01 '…specific areas or **regions** [🔴hover definition] a distinct…'). The '[' is restored before the head test (gated: a head keyword at the very start + a ']' present) and the orphaned '[' is stripped off the host so it never leaks as 'regions ['. (A2) unclosed_next_item: the marker carries NO usable def of its own — an UNCLOSED '[hover definition:' (no closing ']') OR a closed-but-empty '[hover definition]' — and its blackAfter is empty; the def is the FOLLOWING red/black item (DocxExtractor merges the writer's fragmented red runs into ONE item: 'DEF…]' with the paragraph continuation in ITS blackAfter), e.g. AGH1004-02 '…beautiful topographies 🔴[hover definition:🔴 🔴the shape and features…🔴 on planet Earth…'. That item is consumed as the def (a stray late ']' trimmed) rather than rendered as a 'CS:' note. SAFETY: the def-in-BLACK form (no red def item; the next item is plain black text, e.g. AGH1007 'plant materia]') is NOT touched; the consumed next item must be a non-interactive instruction/noise/black span, never a real widget tag.
split_bracket._def_black_tail_doc: THE DEF-IN-OWN-BLACK-TAIL SHAPE — ENGJ403's standard hover idiom: a red '[hover info ‘pitch’:' span with NO closing bracket, the DEFINITION as the span's own black tail, then a bare ']' red span whose black tail continues the sentence. (A2) requires an EMPTY own tail, so without this shape the marker would leak as a Writers Note and the paragraph would fragment. Here: def = the marker's own black tail; the ']' closer span is consumed and its tail rejoins the sentence; a QUOTED anchor in the head ('pitch') weaves the sentinel onto that word's LAST occurrence in the host prose, falling back to the last-word append when absent/not found. The human renders all of these as class=infoTrigger spans. Env HOVERTAIL_OFF turns off just this shape.
split_bracket._def_black_tail_head_doc: THE HOVER DEFINITION'S RED FIRST LETTER. When the writer's red marker run carries the definition's first letter(s) — `[roll over definition: T` red, `o move to or find a place.` black (SSFUN03), `[roll over definition: A` + ` large part of a continent.`, TEFUN05 `H` + `ow you expect…` — the unclosed marker takes the def_black_tail path, which reads the black tail; the text after the unclosed marker's colon is the def's head, joined exactly as the source joins it (a space only when the black tail opens with one), so the tooltip keeps its first letter(s). Env HOVERTAILHEAD_OFF.

hover_definition_inline.note: A hover/rollover/mouseover DEFINITION marker whose def is NOT carried after a 'trigger' keyword (so info_trigger_inline does not weave it). TWO shapes: (A) COLON self-closed '[hover: DEF]' / '[hover definition: DEF]' / '[rollover definition: DEF]' / '[mouseover definition: DEF]' — the def is inside the bracket after the first colon; without this, '[Hover: …]' would resolve to plain [body] (paragraph SPLIT) and '[hover definition: …]' would hit the bare-marker guard (def DROPPED). (B) MARKER-THEN-DEF '[hover text] DEF' — the bracket closes and the def follows it inside the SAME red span (ENGC101 'Using **adjectives** [hover text] Describing words. can make…'). Both are woven onto the nearest preceding word as anchor in ONE paragraph (the same U+E000 sentinel + ContentConverter.#inlineMarkup machinery as info_trigger_inline). SCOPE/SAFETY: the head must start with hover/rollover/mouseover (head_pattern); a marker that resolves to a NON-infoTrigger interactive widget (shapeHover, a hover audio player, etc.) is skipped; a marker carrying 'trigger' (skip_if_tag_keyword) is left to info_trigger_inline; a marker with NO recoverable def is left untouched (never a leaked literal). Env HOVERDEF_OFF turns off both shapes.

def_clean._weave_separators_doc: weave_separators: the scanner weave's form (A) also takes `=`, a spaced dash and a quoted payload after the head words (head_words_pattern), and form (C) needs a letter or digit after the bracket, so a `[hover – DEF]` / `[hover = DEF]` / quoted marker is woven instead of splitting its sentence around a Writers Note. Env WEAVESEP_OFF turns off just this part (HOVERDEFCLEAN_OFF turns off all of def_clean).
def_clean._separator_note: The plain hyphen is NOT a weave separator: `[hover - what the word means]` (ENGI101) is woven by the render stitch, and consuming it at item level would move the next drag-and-drop's activity number (a stray 2H box).
def_clean._tight_after_span_note: ListsAndRuns.inlineMarkup drops the whitespace between a built infoTrigger span and a following , . ; : ! ? ) — the removed marker's padding space, which the human build never keeps. Env HOVERTIGHT_OFF keeps the space.
def_clean._tight_note: A continuation that opens with , . ; : ! ? ) joins the woven span with no space (XWHA02 `ākonga, kaimahi`).
def_clean._doc: THE HOVER DEFINITION'S OWN TEXT. The human's infoTrigger definitions carry the bare definition (AGH1009 `Lake`, TWHK903 `wellbeing`), almost never a leading separator. Without cleaning, a definition can keep the writer's separator (`info=": the number of seeds that germinate"` AGH1003, `"– prayer/chant/incantation"` MXFL401) or be a lone `.` / `,` / `:` — InteractiveScanner.#weaveHoverDefinition form (C) would read the sentence's full stop after the `]` as the definition whenever the bracket held no COLON (`[hover = wellbeing].` TWHK903, `[hover – a phrase…].` EXBP901, `[hover “anticipating what to do next”].` XLP06). (1) ListsAndRuns.inlineMarkup strips a leading lead_pattern run from every sentinel definition and drops a sentinel with no letter or digit left (the word renders plain, never a `.` tooltip); (2) weave_separators (see _weave_separators_doc). Env HOVERDEFCLEAN_OFF turns it off.

table_cell_release._doc_fence: The fence: a table whose own first row, or one of the cue_lookback text-bearing items before it, matches interaction_cue_pattern is the DATA of an interaction the writer announced (DAN1004 1.0 `Match the verbs with their corresponding photos above` — the human's drag-and-drop; AGH1007 3.0 / 6.0 `[Interactive: Image with click on points for information]` — the human's clickDrop image): it stays captured as that widget.
table_cell_release._doc: THE INLINE HOVER IN A TABLE CELL. InteractiveScanner.#interactiveInTable takes the FIRST red span in a table's cells that parses as an INTERACTIVE invocation as the table's widget, so an inline hover definition typed after its anchor word in a cell (`herbicide [🔴hover definition🔴: a spray designed to kill plants]`, AGH1003 6.0) would make the whole table — mostly the writer's LAYOUT table (`[body] text ║ [image] url`) — an un-built infoTrigger hand-off box. The human renders the table (or un-tables the layout) with the <span class="infoTrigger"> woven in the cell (AGH1003_06.0 `herbicide`). So a red span that ListsAndRuns.hoverStitch WOULD weave onto an anchor (the same marker test the free-body cell renderer applies — its head words, separators, decline rules and anchor resolution) is not a widget invocation: the scan moves on, so the table takes its ordinary path or the widget a LATER invocation names. The `trigger`-worded forms hoverStitch declines stay captured. Env TABLEHOVER_OFF turns it off.

trigger_heads._doc_master: Also off under TABLEHOVER_OFF (the table_cell_release master toggle).
trigger_heads._doc: Works with table_cell_release: the `trigger`-worded head WITH a separator (`nouns [hovertrigger: Person, place or thing.]`, `intern [hover trigger: An intern is…]`) is woven by this render stitch like any hover head; 'hover trigger' also matches 'hovertrigger' / 'hover-trigger'. The paragraph path weaves it in InteractiveScanner (the single-bracket inline trigger); a table cell reaches only this pass, so without it the released layout tables would show the marker as text. A trigger marker with NO separator right after the head is still declined. Env HOVERTRIGSTITCH_OFF.
