bold_anchor._doc: The render stitch's last-word anchor fallback also takes a closing **bold** / *italic* run right before the marker (`**visual storytelling** [hovertrigger: Telling a story…]`, ENGI303 1.0): the sentinel goes after the run and ListsAndRuns.inlineMarkup wraps the whole run as the infoTrigger anchor — the form the paragraph path builds — instead of the marker keeping its literal text. Also off under TABLEHOVER_OFF (the table_cell_release master toggle).

render_stitch.note:
RENDER-LEVEL re-stitch of any hover/rollover/definition marker that reaches the FINAL visible text as a LITERAL. The scanner weave only reaches clean red TAG items; the residue arrives as a BLACK item (HIS1002/HIS1005 'for TERM'), a 'definition'-head data-marker tag (ENGJ301), or a table cell (CEDO501). ListsAndRuns.hoverStitch runs at the TOP of inlineMarkup (every visible-text path:

/

  • /) AND on the FULL multi-line text in renderBlackText (cross-line 'for TERM'), inserting the U+E000…U+E001 sentinel that #inlineMarkup converts to anchor. CONTAINMENT-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: cv2 placeholder dumps render RAW (never via inlineMarkup/renderBlackText — their bare URLs stay unlinked), so markers inside un-built widgets are untouched. ANCHOR: a 'for/on TERM' marker weaves onto the LAST whole-word occurrence of TERM in the preceding text; otherwise the single word immediately before the marker. Uses the same hygiene as the scanner weave (instruction-def + URL-tail decline) and the 'trigger' exclusion (those belong to info_trigger_inline). A marker with no clean anchor/def is LEFT as the literal — never a wrong weave, never a NEW leak. Env INFOSPLIT_OFF turns it off.
render_stitch._head_words_note: 'hover info' (first, longest-wins) admits both the spaced '[hover info ‘X’:' AND the glued '[hoverinfo ‘X’:' cell forms (head_words internal spaces compile to [-\s]?) — as in ENGJ403's activity-structure table cells. The quoted-anchor weave in hoverStitch pairs with it.

hover_definition_inline._head_pattern_note: 'hover(?:\s*info(?:rmation)?)?' admits the GLUED '[hoverinfo ...' form (as ENGJ403 types it) — the spaced '[hover info ...' matches via the bare 'hover' + \b.

define_heads._doc: The bare [define: DEF] head weaves like [hover define:] (as in SCCH302-03 'boiling point', SCFUN01): head_pattern here REPLACES the base pattern (adding 'define' to the alternation) in the scanner weave, and stitch_heads joins the render-stitch head_words. Def-less forms (PES1007 '[define this:]') are declined by the guards. 'definition' is deliberately NOT a scanner head: [definition…] spans are mostly data-marker SUBTAGS inside widget bundles (MXDB302 matching pairs, ANZH203, CEDT104 flipcard hovers), and weaving them would break widget capture; the render stitch carries 'definition' for render-level literals. All existing instruction/URL/trigger guards apply. Env DEFINEHEAD_OFF uses the base head_pattern + head_words.

orphan_definition_weave._paren_tail_note: A CLOSED empty [definition] bracket whose black tail opens with a parenthesised phrase and then continues — `aroha [definition] (Love, concern, compassion.) is important.` — takes the parenthesis as the definition (parens dropped, the human's info= form, XDLS905-7.0 `info="amount needed"`) and lets the prose after it resume the sentence; a full-tail `(def)` keeps the standing form. These markers reach the weave via the near-red tag rule (Input_Doc_Rules.red_runs.near_red_tag_runs, XDLS904/905's c00000 markers). Env DEFPAREN_OFF turns off this shape alone; DEFWEAVE_OFF turns off the whole pre-pass.
orphan_definition_weave._doc: THE GLOSSARY DEFINITION WEAVE. A writer's inline hover definition ([definition: …]) resolves to the canonical `data marker`, whose directive is SUBTAG, so in open prose it would reach the ORPHAN branch: a red flag, and — because Word routinely splits the bracket across coloured runs — the writer's ONE sentence broken into three or four paragraphs with the flag wedged in the middle and the anchor word cut in half (ENGR302-1.0 'holds a hierarchical' / flag / 'rranged according to level of importance.'). This is a ROUTING rule: a PRE-PASS (ContentConverter.#definitionWeavePrepass, beside the other pre-passes) re-joins the sentence and inserts the SAME U+E000…U+E001 sentinel that ListsAndRuns.inlineMarkup turns into <span class="infoTrigger" info="DEF">. The sentinel is used rather than a re-written bracket literal because an unanchored sentinel is DROPPED to plain text by inlineMarkup's own last rule — so the pre-pass can never turn a red flag into a NEW visible leak. SHAPE A (the marker interrupts a sentence, so the anchor is the LAST WORD behind — the human's own dominant convention) and SHAPE B (the writer NAMES the anchor, '[Definition] culture: Refers to…', and that word IS in the text behind). FIVE writer shapes: an OPEN bracket split mid-word ('[definition: A' + 'rranged…' -> 'Arranged…', joined with NO space because the black tail carries no leading one) or split at a space ('[definition: A ' + ' spending plan.' -> 'A spending plan.'); an OPEN bracket with an empty inner (the definition is the whole black tail); the how=exact form ('[definition' + ': The values…', a leading separator to strip); a CLOSED bracket (the definition is the inner text and the black tail is the sentence CONTINUATION — ENGC101-5.0 'techniques' + 'that we can use.'); and a CLOSED bracket with an EMPTY inner (shape B's named anchor). NOT woven: a marker that follows a COMPLETED sentence and names nothing — its anchor is recoverable only from the writer's highlight, which DocxExtractor does not carry (ENGJ301-2.0's gold anchors 'infamous' while the last word behind is 'protagonists'); and a named word that is not in the text behind (ENGI202-1.0), which would need a page-wide forward search. This does not conflict with define_heads' exclusion of `definition` from the scanner: that concerns spans INSIDE widget bundles, and bundle members never reach the orphan branch. [hover over …] markers ride the same pre-pass via hover_head_pattern + quoted_anchor_pattern; scaffold_strip removes PHE1002's '… as other word' designer scaffolding so its definitions read as the synonyms they are. A [word] + [definition] alternation (ENGI405-0.0) needs no rule of its own — the definition's anchor IS the preceding [word]'s tail — and suppress_paired_word_flag drops the now-structural [word] flag; a [word]+[answer] run (ENGI405-1.0, a drag-and-drop in the human build) is untouched BY CONSTRUCTION (an [answer] is not a definition head). Env DEFWEAVE_OFF turns off the whole pre-pass; DEFANCHORNAMED_OFF turns off shape B alone; DEFWORDFLAG_OFF turns off the paired-[word] flag suppression alone.

hover_weave_hygiene.note: HYGIENE guards shared by BOTH sentinel-weave paths (info_trigger_inline + hover_definition_inline). (1) instruction_def_guard — a recovered 'def' matching instruction_cue_pattern is a writer NOTE, not a definition ('For each concept, please have the rollover definitions below. Ngā mihi' HIS1002-16; '…Please embed these images and have drop-down boxes…' AGH1004-01): DECLINE the weave so the marker falls to the CS-note handling — the human strips both. (2) url_host_skip — the anchor-host walk never selects a candidate whose trailing text is a bare URL or media FILENAME (+']'/')' residue; media_tail_pattern): the URL machinery would read straight through the private-use sentinel ('…Pounamu_0.jpg⟨IT0⟩For' becoming part of the URL and orphaning ⟨IT1⟩ into the output), or weave info onto URL fragments such as 'png' (MXFU201's '[hover] enlarge graph' hints). With only media adjacent the anchor is non-derivable → the no-anchor fallback (def dropped, marker consumed — as the human drops the text at MXFU201). Named-anchor selection (HIS1001 '[Rollover for moratorium: …]') belongs to the split-bracket and render-stitch rules, not here. Both guards only DECLINE mis-weaves; clean weaves are untouched by construction. Env HOVERHYG_OFF turns off all 4 sites.

video_embed_title_drop.note:
A [video] whose embed was built (a YouTube id OR a generic iframe URL) DROPS its OWN title line (the [video] element's blackAfter) from the body — that text is the video's NAME, which the AcksBuilder ships as the acknowledgement, so the human renders ONLY the embed (ENGC102 overview '[video] Nonfiction Text Features' and the 'Red Pandas | …' / 'PANDA PANTS …' titles are in the human ACKS, never the body; the human build never shows a video-title

). SAFETY: only the element's OWN blackAfter is dropped — genuinely-FOLLOWING separate prose (a later [body]-less paragraph the #gatherFollowing also pulled in, e.g. ENGJ402 'Here is an alternative video…') is KEPT, and AUDIO text is always kept (MXFL301 [audio clip] dialogue 'Hi, I'm John Atkins…' has no external embed → kept). Env VIDTITLE_OFF renders the title as a body

.

media_url_paren_strip.note:
After a media-reference URL is stripped from a [video]/[audio]/[image] caption, the now-EMPTY '()' / '( )' wrapper and any orphan single ')' / '(' left behind are removed — the human never ships these (e.g. ENGC102 '

)

', XDLS908 'Stop sign ( )'). Conservative: only EMPTY parens and isolated single parens are removed; '(real text)' inside genuine prose is preserved (the regex requires whitespace/boundary on both sides of a lone paren). Shared by #media and #image via #stripMediaResidue. Env MEDIAPAREN_OFF leaves the paren residue.

media_timestamp_note.note: A RED parenthetical that is WHOLLY a clock timestamp / time-range — '(to 1:00)', '(0:10-1:48)', '(1:45-2:27)', with an optional timing lead/trail word (to/from/at/clip/…/onwards/only) — is a writer's MEDIA-USAGE instruction to Creative Services (how to trim the video/audio it sits beside), NOT noise. Without this, TagNormaliser classifies it 'noise' (it is <3 words, carries no instruction cue, has no bracket) and ContentConverter silently DROPS it (ENGI302-00 '(to 1:00)' after the intro-video URL). When the free text matches this pattern, the span is reclassified 'instruction' so the retained-instruction path keeps it as a 'CS:' note immediately after the media element. TIGHT by construction: requires the parenthesis boundary AND a \d:\d\d / \d.\d\d time, so it can never grab labels like (front)/(Back)/(Gold)/(middle image)/(trigger engagement), nor money ($58.20) / decimals / time-of-day (10:00 AM) which are not parenthesised timestamps. The longer '… only' / 'clip …' forms are already kept as >=3-word instructions. Env TIMESTAMPNOTE_OFF drops it as noise.

caption_not_media.note: A writer's CAPTION marker that embeds a media word — '[Insert caption with video]', '[caption with image]', '[Caption text for image]' — resolves to the embedded media tag (video/image) via the longest-suffix embedded match, so without this rule ContentConverter would build/red-flag a media element from a caption (ENGS302-00 'RED FLAG: [video] with no URL found' on '[Insert caption with video] Watch this clever Lord of the Rings…'). When a media-resolved tag's RAW text contains the word 'caption', it is a CAPTION: its following text renders as ordinary body, never an embed/red-flag. The bare [Caption]/[Insert caption] (data-marker SUBTAG, image-caption widget) never reaches a media branch, so it is untouched. Env CAPTIONMEDIA_OFF builds the (red-flagged) media element.

media_hyperlinked_lead._note:
A hyperlink is not a red instruction span: when the BLL phonics writer hyperlinks the WHOLE line '[audio] snail, paint, trail, stain, faint, train' to its sound file, only the bracket is the tag and the words after it are the writer's CONTENT — exactly what a black run after a red '[audio 1]' is (BLL146, rendered as the caption

). So on a block the extractor marked hyperTag (Input_Doc_Rules red_runs.hyperlinked_tag_runs), MediaBuilder.media folds the element's embedded lead (RenderText of its own span) in FRONT of its black-after text and the ordinary rules apply: a built video drops it as its title (video_embed_title_drop), audio / an un-built element keep it as the caption. For the phonics lists the human usually builds per-word audioButton / word widgets (an un-derivable developer form), so the fold is scoped to the hyperlinked class ONLY, where the alternative is losing the words; the lead of a RED-span tag stays dropped, as the human mostly drops it. Env MEDIALEAD_OFF turns it off (the words are then lost). Sibling rule: buttons["audio button"].label_default (env BTNLABELDEF_OFF).

media_url_in_text.note: A [video]/[embed]/[imbed] tag whose URL the writer typed INSIDE the same red instruction span as the tag ('[Embed film] edit to start at 3 seconds https://youtu…' — the URL is part of it.text, not the black blackAfter nor a hyperlink nor a following black item) is not found by #gatherFollowing (which only scans blackAfter + following BLACK items), giving 'RED FLAG: [embed] with no URL found'. The URL search therefore ALSO scans the element's own raw it.text as a last resort, so an in-span URL is recovered and the embed builds, as the human builds it (ENGS302, ENGJ402, XDLS502/901). Env MEDIAURLTEXT_OFF uses the blackAfter/following-only search.
media_url_in_text.following_link_note: The new-era WT authors '[insert video]' on its own line with the video as a TITLE-ANCHORED hyperlink on the NEXT black line ('Pixar in a Box… - YouTube' — the URL lives in the docx hyperlink, not the visible text; as in ENGS404-00). The URL search also reads the following-black range's first hyperlink TARGET (after block-link/gathered-text, before the own-raw-text last resort). video_embed_title_drop then drops the reference line once the embed builds, exactly as for a same-line reference. Env MEDIAFOLLOWLINK_OFF turns it off.

embed_story_carousel.note: An [embed story] (also '[Embed pdf text of story]', '[Embed School Journal story]') is the writer asking to embed a decodable/journal STORY whose pages are an EXTERNAL link (SPELD/School Journal). A bare <iframe> of that site renders as a broken grey box (most story sites block framing). The HUMAN builds a CAROUSEL of the story's page images (as in BLL117), but those page images are sourced manually post-conversion and are NOT in the WT/Media List. So the human's carousel SCAFFOLD is emitted with ONE placeholder slide (the standard Mode-P/D image — the developer drops the real pages in, exactly like every other image). Keyed on the word 'story' in the tag remainder, EXCLUDING 'audio' ('[Embed audio recording of this story]' is an audio, not a visual carousel). Human ref: 01-Finalized_Modules_/BLL117/BLL117-03.html (Activity 2B). Env EMBEDSTORY_OFF emits the bare iframe.
embed_story_carousel.trigger_note: Fire when the [embed] tag's bracket contains a trigger word ('story' OR 'book' — '[embed story]'/'[embed book]'/'[Embed pdf text of story]'/'[Embed School Journal story]') and NO exclude word ('audio' — the lone '[Embed audio recording of this story]' is an audio recording, not a visual carousel). Whole-word match so 'audiobook'/'booklet' don't trip it.

link_text_display._doc: When a link points at one of the domains listed here, the FRONTEND TEXT of the link shows the domain's canonical display form while the href keeps the writer's FULL deep URL — e.g. a link to https://speldsa.org.au/pages/speld-sa-phonic-books renders as https://speldsa.org.au. The human build does exactly this in the BODY (nearly all BLL supervisor notes) while its ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS keep the full URL text — so the rewrite is applied by a full-page post-pass (ListsAndRuns.LinkTextDisplay, called from PageAssembler beside OmitPlaceholderResidue/TidyDeveloperNotes) that STOPS at the acks block. It only rewrites an anchor whose text is ITSELF a URL on the same domain (a writer's descriptive phrase link like 'SPELD SA website' is never touched), so it can never destroy meaningful text. Applies to EVERY module and every emitter whenever this type of link is used. Add a domain by adding a key; env LINKTEXT_OFF keeps the raw full-URL text.

widen.head: ^\[\s*caption\s*\d*\s*\]\s*$
widen._doc:
Three widenings of the caption_text branch: (A) 'head' accepts the writer's NUMBER — [caption 2], as in SCFUN01; (C) 'inspan' takes the caption words riding the span itself (original case from the raw span text) — HIS1007, HIS1008; (B) a bare head with an empty tail takes the NEXT black item WHOLE as the caption (the human ships the whole item as ONE captionText — HIS1005-4.0/-9.0 verbatim, newlines as
) and consumes it — SSFUN05, HIS1005, HIS1006, HIS1007, HIS1008. Deliberately NOT captions (the head pattern fails them BY CONSTRUCTION): [Caption:] + [Caption for the map] (HIS1001 — the human ships a PLAIN

/

, not captionText) and [caption hover] (OSOH101 — the human builds a carousel caption). Env CAPTIONWIDE_OFF turns off the widening alone (the exact-bracket + blackAfter path unchanged); CAPTIONTEXT_OFF turns off the whole branch.

caption_text._doc:
A FREE-BODY [caption] (outside any interactive) is the writer's image caption; the human ships

…

(as in SCCH302-02). 'caption' stays an alias of the data-marker SUBTAG, so inside widget bundles nothing changes (carousel/flipCard captions etc — most [caption] tags are widget members); this rule fires ONLY at the orphan-sub-tag branch (which by definition is outside every interactive), replacing the 'Orphan sub-tag [data marker]' red flag + plain

with the captionText paragraph. The match is the EXACT bare bracket ([caption] and nothing else in the span) so a caption marker carrying extra instruction text still surfaces as a flag. Env CAPTIONTEXT_OFF turns it off.

cs_video_marker._doc: KB constraint 64 / CL-0037, 05A 'Creative Services Videos (Vimeo)': 'any video produced by Creative Services … e.g. an animated intro …' is the Vimeo videoSection scaffold with the ID PENDING and a visible Designer/Developer To Do note; the scaffold is emitted exactly as the design team supplies it, its two time-placeholder comments included — the KB's narrow comment exception. The generic `[Audiovisual item N]` marker is mostly audio and is not covered; the writers' `[Insert animated character]` marker (the BLL blended-literacy family) asks for an in-house animation, and the human page carries a Vimeo player for it. Its red span becomes the To Do + scaffold (the writer's request in the same span rides in the note); the `Animation Script` link line that follows joins the To Do (the human page never shows it). Env CSVIDEO_OFF.
cs_video_marker.note: add vimeo embed for the animated character

asset_todo_notes._doc: THE THREE NOTE FAMILIES (item / merge / audiovisual). Each points at an asset that is OUTSIDE the writer's document: a numbered Media-List slot, a page of a legacy D2L course, a sound not yet recorded. Nothing is built here (see decline_evidence below); what this sets is the NOTE: 'Designer/Developer To Do: Media List item 7 goes here' tells the developer exactly what to fetch, where a generic 'Red Flag: Orphan sub-tag [data marker] outside an interactive' would tell them nothing. Kind 'todo' = the ledger scheme's Designer/Developer To Do prefix (red + bold, class cv2-note). At the orphan branch only the item's blackAfter renders, so the marker's OWN residue would otherwise be discarded (MXFUN01 'MXO302 Parts of a Whole: Lesson 1.0 Decimals - use all content on page' beside a D2L URL); the note carries that residue, so the writer's content is kept.

decline_evidence.item: Not built: this is a Media-List asset-resolution case, not a data-marker one. The asset is outside the document, and the item number never determines the container — the neighbouring red tag does ([Please create a carousel], [Create Flip cards], as in CEDT104 and ARFUN02).
decline_evidence.merge: Not built: every named source course (MXO301/302/313/323/331/333/341/414/432/442/443/521, HEO1005, HPO1091, HTO1101/1103) is a legacy D2L course outside this corpus, and the human mostly leaves these markers as empty panels. There is no shared-asset mechanism in the HTML at all.
decline_evidence.audiovisual: Not built without the recordings: the audioButton needs an audioName of the form {CODE}_{ACTIVITY}_{N} and THE ACTIVITY CODE IS NOWHERE IN THE MARKER; the Media List (as in BLL270) has no item numbers or Audio rows for these; and the human's own answer differs by module (BLLR201 ships no audio at all, SSCI205 uses audioImage tiles). A silent button is worse than an honest note.

families.head: ^\[?\s*(?:insert\s+)?items?\s*(?:no\.?|number)?\s*#?\s*(\d+)?\s*[:.\]]*\s*
families.note_nonum: A Media List item goes here.
families.note_nonum_rest: A Media List item goes here — {rest}

families.head: ^\[?\s*(?:insert\s+)?(?:audio\s*visual|audiovisual|av)\s*items?\s*#?\s*(\d+)?\s*[:.\]]*\s*
families.note: Audiovisual item {n} — the recording is to come.
families.note_rest: Audiovisual item {n} — the recording is to come. {rest}
families.note_nonum: An audiovisual item — the recording is to come.
families.note_nonum_rest: An audiovisual item — the recording is to come. {rest}
families.note_contains: {rest} — the audiovisual recording is to come.

black_line._doc:
THE BLACK-LINE RIDER. A writer can make the bracket the ANCHOR TEXT of a hyperlink to the asset (BLLR201 '[Audiovisual item 1]', '[audiovisual item 4]'), so the block carries NO red span at all — it is a BLACK item, never reaches the orphan branch, and would print as a visible

[Audiovisual item 1]

. This rule catches it: a BLACK item whose ENTIRE text is one of the three families' brackets becomes the same todo note, with any hyperlink target carried in the note text. [Item N] markers inside BILINGUAL TABLE CELLS (TRR102/TRR106/TRR109) are rendered by the table path and are not touched. Env TODOBLACK_OFF turns off the rider alone.

orphan_instruction_reclass._doc: THE MIS-CLASSIFICATION GUARD. Some writer spans that reach the orphan sub-tag branch are not structural markers at all: they are INSTRUCTIONS TO THE DESIGN TEAM whose bracket happens to contain a `data marker` alias buried in the prose ("[Please put the Maths Minute activities in a box in the right column]" matches on `column`; "[This recording has all 5 sounds please snip …]" on `word`). Rather than "Red Flag: Orphan sub-tag [data marker] outside an interactive", which is wrong and useless, they print the ledger scheme's "Writers Note:" (kind "cs") carrying the writer's own raw span text verbatim — the SAME form used for every span the resolver classifies as an instruction in the first place. The content below the marker is unchanged. NOTHING IS BUILT and no writer word is lost; only the prefix and the body change.
orphan_instruction_reclass._scope_tags_doc: THE SCOPE_TAGS. The same predicate applies to the other orphan labels in scope_tags (shape n, answer, correct, question, option, drop), each with its own env toggle in scope_tags_env. Every span it reaches is an instruction to a person: '[Please create a tick box where akonga can earn a star]', '[Blocks for the type of learning it supports - please randomise. Correct match in brackets]', '[The options below can be presented as click-drops]', '[Can you put this Maths moment in a box with a coloured background...]'. min_words 3 applies unchanged; the floor makes no difference in this population.

_judgement_calls.answer_keys_with_instructions: A span that carries an ANSWER VALUE and a CS instruction in ONE red span (SSEA203 '[Answer = $70.00 or $70] CS ensure $ symbol is out of the box') is relabelled: an answer key must never become learner-visible content, but a cv2-note is designer-facing, in the same channel the structural flag already occupies, and deleted by the developer — so the relabel keeps the writer's instruction instead of silently stripping it (§6). PURE answer keys are excluded BY CONSTRUCTION: '[answers] seven, 65, 15, 24 ...' (MXFU201 7.0) and '[Answers: 1= C, 2 = D, 3 = A, 4. = B]' (TWHT903 2.0) fire no instruction cue, so the guard cannot reach a key that stands alone.
_judgement_calls.leading_question: When the writer's learner-facing question and the instruction are one red span (CEDW303 0.0 'What did you learn? [Use the same box please]'), the note carries both; only blackAfter would otherwise reach the page, so the relabel keeps the writer's words rather than exposing anything new.
_judgement_calls.per_span_scope: The scope applies per span: on a module where a `shape n` / `correct` / `answer` span is relabelled (ANZH205, CEDT104, ENGI201, XGF9004), a `data marker` span that fails the fence (how !== 'embedded', or no cue) still prints the structural flag.

orphan_instruction_reclass._predicate: TagNormaliser.IsInstructionDominant, reused unchanged: parse.class === "tag" AND every tag how === "embedded" (the clean_hows fence) AND an Instruction_Cues cue fires AND >= min_words words. No new vocabulary is introduced. min_words is 3 here rather than the scanner's 8 because the span has ALREADY failed to be a usable structural marker (it is an orphan by definition), so a short instruction fragment is safer to relabel than to leave under a structural flag; the short spans it reaches are genuine instructions (BLLR201, CEDW501, SSFUN02).
orphan_instruction_reclass._fence_doc: The fence keeps real markers out: the how==="embedded" test excludes every [Item N]/[item #N] Media-List shape and every exact-form single-word marker — [definition], [word], [Label], [Incorrect], [Insert thumbnail], [embedded webpage] — BY CONSTRUCTION; the cue and min_words requirements leave only one-off design instructions. A [word highlighting] instruction with no [definition] partner (BLLR201 6.0 "[word highlighting] Two colours as outlined below") is relabelled and does not affect the [word] + [definition] pairing in orphan_definition_weave.

_limits.no_cue_keeps_flag: A layout request that fires no Instruction_Cues cue keeps the structural flag: XGF9006 "[Three tiles across the page]", "[Make word green/red/blue]" (CEDK501), "[insert arrow down]" (XTAS103), "[One basket with the label 'Fair' and one with 'Unfair']" (XGF9004), "[Insert links to the 4 individual phases – side by side across screen]" (ARFUN01), "[allow them to be able to move the words between boxes …]" (BLL147), "[Displayed as links to lessons …]" (XDLS902). There is no general structural discriminator between those and a genuine content marker of the same shape — "[Definition of inaccuracies = something that is not correct]" (ANZH203) is also a whole-span, multi-word, how=embedded bracket. The separation is SEMANTIC, and semantics lives in Instruction_Cues; a local verb list fitted to these strings would be a curve fit (§6).
_limits.can_we_is_not_a_cue: Instruction_Cues.cue_patterns carries "can you", "could you", "could we", "can this", "can there" but deliberately NOT "can we" (so ART1006's "[Can we have a side bar …]" keeps its flag): many real widget tags carry a 'can we' request ("[drop and drag] Can we make something like this please …" across the BLL phonics family, "[Rolling banner] Can we have something like this please …", "[audio] can we attach the audio …"). cue_patterns is SHARED: it feeds IsInstructionDominant, which InteractiveScanner uses to decide whether a span is swallowed as an instruction MEMBER, and the PageSplitter lesson-boundary guard, so adding the phrase would change widget capture widely.
_limits.not_instructions_at_all: Two kinds of span are not design instructions and must never be relabelled: a QUIZ DISTRACTOR fragment (SSOG301 8.0 "Party B can govern alone (incorrect)]"), which belongs with the orphaned [correct] / [answer] gathering class; and the "[Item N]"-with-a-prose-lead records (CEDT104/ARFUN02/MXDI201), a Media-List asset-resolution class, excluded BY CONSTRUCTION because their tags resolve how="denumbered"/"denumbered_head", not "embedded".
_limits.auto_feedback: [Auto-feedback] markers (TEDC401/TEDC402) are out of scope: the framework has no feedback slot, and a note for them would be a DIFFERENT family with a different prefix (todo, not cs) and its own wording, fenced by its own head pattern.

orphan_instruction_reclass._env: ORPHANCS_OFF turns off the whole guard — every relabelled span prints the structural orphan flag.

widget_alt_postpass._doc: KB constraint 52's POSITIVE half on EVERY image: an iStock image's alt is its iStock / Getty title. The widget-internal #assetImage seam sees only the filename, so iStock images inside widgets (flipCard, carousel, activity, speechBubble, accordion …) would otherwise keep alt="" although a title is recoverable; the human build fills most iStock alts. MediaBuilder.FillWidgetAlts runs LAST on every finished page: an naming iStock- (the Mode-P placeholder, the commented reference, a Mode-D image) takes the verified *_istock-acks.txt title, else the Title-Cased slug of that id's URL anywhere in the module (Media List items, Writers Template blocks); no URL and no verified title → alt stays "" (never invent); non-iStock images untouched; 'stock photo' stripped (c52's negative half). Env WIDGETALT_OFF turns it off.

image_attrs.note: Applied as a post-fill (MediaBuilder.FinishImg) on free-body + table-cell content images. alt authority: verified iStock API title (run.istockAcks, the *_istock-acks.txt map) > URL-slug Title-Case (the verified 98% slug-is-title rule) > empty. loading=lazy is a forward rule — gold era-mixed 24%; overrides-gold capture Subject_Global_Parameters._universal_conventions.img_alt_lazy. Env IMGATTRS_OFF reverts both.
image_attrs.widget_internal_note: Widget-INTERNAL images (InteractiveBuilder.#assetImage) follow the same rule. Title authority = the VERIFIED map only (id read from the filename; no URL at that seam, so the slug fallback never fires — the widget_alt_postpass fills the rest); loading=lazy completes flipCard's Mode-P visible template (shapeHover's style-first Mode-P template is not matched by the finisher's regex). Env WIDGETIMG_OFF turns off the widget-internal part ALONE (IMGATTRS_OFF turns off both), so it can be toggled independently of the body-path rule.

bare_url_heading._doc:
THE BARE URL AS A HEADING: the bare-URL passes (bare_stock_url_image, bare_video_url_embed, bare_link_url_note) read a block whose whole content is one URL; with this flag they read a HEADING of these tags the same way as the

form. A heading whose whole text is a URL (D2L pages, iStock pictures, a YouTube link, Google docs — reached via a merged-item line, an [activity N image] co-tag whose title is the URL, a heading co-tag on an [Image], an instruction naming a heading) is never shown as a heading in the human build. Env HEADURL_OFF (the three passes read

only).

redundant_bold._doc:
THE REDUNDANT BOLD IN A HEADER CELL OR HEADING. A header cell and a heading already render bold; the writer's bold over the WHOLE text (`Livestock Group`, `

Rumen

`) is redundant, and the human build almost always renders these plain (the few exceptions — some MXFU / JPFUN header cells, some TRR headings — have no derivable signal). An element of a listed tag whose whole content (whitespace aside) is ONE bare run loses the ; the words stay. A partly-bold cell or heading is untouched. Env REDUNDANTBOLD_OFF.

visible_tag_lift._doc:
THE WRITER TAG LEFT IN LEARNER TEXT (KB constraint 5 + the red-note family c37). tag_only_paragraph_note handles paragraphs that are ONLY writer tags; this handles tags that sit beside learner words: `… lived _______ [options for drop-down: in urban areas, by the ocean, rurally].` (ANZH301 / 302), `[Item: 4] Paptuanuku,` (TRR115), `He [dropdown: tākuta/kuki/…] ia.` (TRR304), `[LESSON 2] THE WORLD COURT` (HIS1002), `[Journal] 3E: Dig deeper` (PWY1001), `… in detail [Hover definition] it is important …` (DAN1003), `[Click information] Cows feed requirements …` (AGH1007 cells). In a

/

  • / / /

    –

    outside a cv2-interactive hand-off box and outside a note, every bracket token matching visible_tag_pattern (the elements.tag_only_paragraph_note.tag_pattern vocabulary) that is not inside an and carries no URL is lifted out of the text, and the lifted tags ship as ONE red Writers Note — after the

    / heading, inside the

  • / cell (a note inside a list item or a cell is valid HTML). A block that is left with no words becomes the note. A developer-question tag (`question_tag`: `[?]`, `[dev …]`) takes the rest of its text run with it into the note — `[?] Creative Services we would like your input on how best to display this…` (EXPFUN03) is the writer's question to Creative Services, not learner text. Env TAGLIFT_OFF.

empty_list_item_drop._doc:
THE EMPTY BULLET. A list item left with no content would show as a lone bullet dot: `
` after a bullet's image / video / answer was hoisted out of it (HES1006 1_0, ENGJ202 0_0, ENGI102 2_0), the media-list preamble residue (ANZH103 1_0), the audio / checkbox bullets (BLL110 / BLL130, ENGI103). An
  • whose content is only whitespace (no text, no element), outside a cv2-interactive hand-off box, is dropped; a
      /
        left with no item goes with it. Env EMPTYLI_OFF.

tag_only_paragraph_note._doc:
THE WRITER TAG ALONE ON ITS LINE SHIPS AS A WRITERS NOTE (KB constraint 5 + the red-note family c37). The converter reads [tags] in RED text only, so a writer tag typed in black, or a red tag no emitter knows, that stands ALONE on its line would otherwise show as learner text: `

[audio]

`, `

[insert audio 1]

`, `

[LESSON 2]

`, `

[Clickdrop 1 Image]

`, `

[Video https://…]

`, `

[Insert accordion]

`. A

(not a cv2-note / cv2-comment / cv2-omit / ackTodo, not inside a cv2-interactive hand-off box) whose visible text is only bracket tokens (plus spaces and ` - – : . ,`), at least one of them matching `tag_pattern`, ships as NotesAndComments.redFlag(text, run, "cs") — the red `Writers Note:` the developer acts on. A paragraph with learner words beside the tag is untouched. Env TAGONLYNOTE_OFF.
tag_only_paragraph_note._skip_when_url_note: A tag-only line that carries a URL (`[Video https://…]` XDLS902, `[Image https://unsplash…]` DTC1005) is a MEDIA REQUEST with a usable link the human builds as the embed / image, so it is skipped here rather than turned into a note.

lone_punct_unwrap._doc: THE LONE STYLED PUNCTUATION MARK. A Word run that styled only the mark after a word would render as its own element — `eagles.`, `elements of:`, `pin ,`, `confidently –`; the human build leaves a lone sentence mark or dash plain. Math operators, blanks, arrows and a mark alone in a cell are not touched. A bare / holding only sentence punctuation or a dash (spaces allowed), directly after a word character, a closing quote or bracket (at most one space between), is unwrapped — the mark stays. Runs after merge_split_runs. Env LONEPUNCT_OFF.

merge_split_runs._doc: THE SPLIT SAME-STYLE RUN. A writer's two bold (or italic) Word runs with an UNSTYLED space between would render as two elements — `write the word helmet`, `Rainbow Warrior`; where the human keeps the style it carries ONE run. In the page body a bare closing tag, a whitespace-only gap (or none) and the same bare opening tag join (the gap moves inside the run); a run carrying attributes is left alone. Env MERGERUNS_OFF.

family_quote_paragraph._doc:
THE HIS UNTAGGED QUOTE, a family dialect (§1d exception 1). The History writers quote a source in an UNTAGGED paragraph — wholly in quotation marks (`“He wouldn’t allow his mana to sit under the mantle of a woman.” [the Queen]`, `“the great force of history is that we carry it within ourselves.” – James Baldwin`) or wholly in italics (`*New Colonists tended to look on the Treaty as an unavoidable nuisance…*`) — with its `Source:` / `Quote source:` / footnote line after it. The HIS human build styles it the KB 01F / 05D way (`p.quoteText` + `p.quoteAck`). Outside HIS an untagged quotation-mark line is usually a sample sentence (WJFUN / CEDO / HPRE), not a quote, so the rule is keyed by code prefix. In a module whose code starts with one of code_prefixes, a bare `

` outside every span whose div class matches exclude_container_pattern (and outside every table) whose content is quote_pattern (the whole text in quotation marks, an optional short dash / bracket tail) or one whole italic run of ≥ italic_min_words words becomes `p.quoteText` — a quotation-mark paragraph's `– Name` tail (≤ ack_max_words words) its own `p.quoteAck` — and a bare `

` matching ack_line_pattern DIRECTLY after a quote paragraph becomes `p.quoteAck`. Env FAMQUOTE_OFF.
family_quote_paragraph._doc_strip_italic_wrapper: The class carries the style: the gold's p.quoteText almost always holds its text plain, with no whole-paragraph <i>/<em> wrapper — so the italic paragraph's wrapper is dropped when it becomes p.quoteText.
family_quote_paragraph._doc_ack_bold_label: The HIS gold bolds the source label of its p.quoteAck (`Source:` 44, `Quote source:` 14 of ≈ 85 HIS quoteAck) — a label the writer typed plain is wrapped in (the wording untouched).
family_quote_paragraph._doc_ack_single_bullet: A one-item bulleted list directly after a quote paragraph (`• Declaration of Independence` — HIS1005_9_0 / HIS1007_3_0) is the quote's attribution: the human ships it as the p.quoteAck. 0 = off; a positive value = the item's word cap.

bare_link_url_note._doc: THE BARE LINK LINE IS THE DEVELOPER'S. A body paragraph whose whole content is one URL that is neither a stock photo (bare_stock_url_image) nor a video (bare_video_url_embed) — a D2L / Te Kura page, a source site, a Google doc — is not shown to the learner in the human build (occasionally the link is woven onto nearby prose, but which words is not derivable). Outside the un-built hand-off boxes the paragraph becomes the house To Do note (NotesAndComments.redFlag) — no URL for the learner, the link kept for the developer. Env BARELINKNOTE_OFF.
bare_link_url_note.todo_text: Designer/Developer To Do: the writer's link — {url}

escape_once._doc: The note's text is escaped by the red-note form itself (NotesAndComments.redFlag), so the link is handed over as written: an address with a query string reads «…?a=1&b=2» in the note, never «&b=2». Env TODOESC_OFF (or enabled:false) escapes it before the form does as well.

bare_video_url_embed._doc: THE BARE VIDEO URL IS THE EMBED — KB 01E ([video] → videoSection). A body paragraph whose whole content is one YouTube / Vimeo URL is embedded by the human build (the same reading as external_link_video_embed's seam A for a url-only [link] line). Outside the un-built hand-off boxes the paragraph becomes video.youtube (the group's host convention) or video.generic_iframe (Vimeo's player URL); the page's icon pass adds `icon`; when the page already embeds that video the line is dropped. Env VIDEOURLEMBED_OFF.

bare_url_link._doc: A BARE URL IS LINKED WHOLE, ITS QUERY STRING INCLUDED (KB 01C: a bare URL is a link / media reference; KB constraint 5: no stray markup in the output). ListsAndRuns.inlineMarkup turns every bare web address into a link after the text is HTML-escaped, so a query string's ampersand arrives as «&». With query_string on, the escaped ampersand stays inside the address — `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ID&ab_channel=X` is one link — and any other entity (', " …) still ends it. Off: the address stops at the first ampersand and the rest of the query shows as text. A whole-URL line also stays a whole-URL line, so the bare video / stock-photo line passes read it. Env URLQUERY_OFF.

trailing_punctuation._doc: The address ends where the URL ends: a matched address that closes with sentence punctuation («. , ; : ! ?» — never the «;» of an entity such as &) or with a «)» that has no matching «(» inside the address (a URL typed in brackets) gives that ending back to the sentence — written after the link — so the link text and the href are the address alone. Env URLTRIM_OFF (or enabled:false) keeps the ending inside the link.

title_video_line_embed._doc:
THE TITLE-ANCHORED VIDEO LINE IS THE EMBEDDED VIDEO — KB 01E ([video] → videoSection), the same reading bare_video_url_embed gives a line that is one bare video URL. A paragraph whose whole text is the words of ONE YouTube / Vimeo hyperlink («__Your guide to soil testing on a dairy farm - YouTube__ [LINK: …]», with or without a [video] tag before it) is the writer's video reference; the human build embeds the video (about 17 in 20 such lines) and drops the title. Three parts, one switch: MediaBuilder.WholeLineVideoLinks picks the video links whose words make a whole line of a text (the runs of one link joined); the body's gathered-links filter and MediaBuilder.media's gathered lines keep those links, so the line reaches the page as

Title

; #bareVideoUrlEmbed then builds the embed for a paragraph that is wholly one titled video anchor (inline b / strong / i / em / u wrappers allowed), or drops it when the page already embeds that video. A video link inside a sentence keeps the r-old reading. Env TITLEVIDEO_OFF.

labelled_video_line_embed._doc: THE LABELLED VIDEO LINE IS THE EMBEDDED VIDEO — KB 01E ([video] → videoSection). A body paragraph that is one bare YouTube / Vimeo address (the linker's anchor, its text the address itself) plus a short label — a title («Virtual eye https://…»), a lead («Video: https://…»), a note («https://… (start at 0:34)», «https://… - Gmail instructions») — is the writer's video reference with its name beside it; the gold embeds it and the label goes (it is the acknowledgement's title). Outside the un-built hand-off boxes the paragraph becomes the embed the whole-line address gets (bare_video_url_embed), or is dropped when the page already embeds that video. A label that names a start time («start at M:SS») gives the embed that start (?start=N), as the gold does. The label is 1 to max_label_words words with no other address. Env LABELVIDEO_OFF.

soft_break_lead._doc:
THE SOFT-BREAK SLASH NEVER OPENS A BLOCK (KB constraint 5: no stray markup; constraint 1: the writer's words unchanged). The parsed Writers Template writes a table cell's line break as « / ». When a builder lifts the line before it — a video address, a [caption] tag, a bold title — the marker is left opening the next block («

/ More examples of using 只 (zhī)…»), a slash the writer never typed and the gold never shows. Outside the un-built hand-off boxes a listed block whose text opens with «/ » loses the marker (repeated markers too, inside any leading inline wrapper); a block left empty is dropped. A block whose text also closes with «/» is BLL's sound notation («/ oo /») and is left alone, and so is a slash inside the text. Env SLASHLEAD_OFF.

trailing._doc: The same marker CLOSING a block: when the line after it was lifted (an image, the proverb, a second language) the block ends « /» («Insoluble /», «Whakatauki /», «Cinderella /»). The listed block loses the trailing marker (repeated markers too, inside any closing inline wrapper). A text that opens with «/» or ends «/ x /» is sound notation and is left alone, and so is a slash with no space before it («and/or»). Env SLASHTAIL_OFF (or enabled:false) keeps it.

cell_parts._doc: CONSECUTIVE markers are ONE line break where a cell is split into its lines (TablesAndGrids.cellParts). An emptied line — a token a pass dropped («[Body] / [Checklist] / ☒ Device: Tablet, laptop / …» with [Checklist] dropped), an empty paragraph — leaves «/  /» in the cell. The splitter took « /  » as the break and glued the second «/» to the next line («/ • Device…»), which then read as prose instead of the list's first item (the TRR «What do I need to get started?» menu list). A run of markers now splits once. «/ oo /» sound notation has no space outside its slashes and is not a break. Env CELLSLASH_OFF (or enabled:false) splits on single markers only.

inline_red_words._doc: THE RED RUN THAT IS PART OF THE WRITER'S TEXT STAYS IN PLACE (constraint 1: the writer's characters are never deleted). A red run with no bracket that resolves to no tag and carries no instruction word is noise to the tag classifier: it renders nothing, and the text after it starts a new paragraph. Three forms of such a run are the writer's own text; each has its own switch. The run's characters are put back in place in the black text around it (its own spaces kept, nothing added). Never a run matching exclude_pattern, never one that sits between web addresses (skip_before_pattern / skip_after_pattern), never one that belongs to an interactive's capture. Disabled, or under the env toggle, every such run renders nothing.

glued._doc: A few letters or digits typed red INSIDE a word: no space between the run and a letter on at least one side (the first letter of a word, a phonics passage's focus letters, the digit of «5s»). It can only be part of the word.

option_list._doc: The red option inside a bracketed list of options — «(hare, hear)», «[boy, girl, swimming pool]»: the run sits after an opening bracket that is not yet closed, next to a list separator. The list must show every option; with the colour gone the page no longer shows which one the writer marked. The bracket must hold at least one black option beside the run: a bracket of red runs only is a set of answers, not a list of options.

in_sentence._doc: One to a few red words inside the running text of a sentence, with black text before them that has not ended its sentence and black text after them that carries it on. Off: the form is ambiguous from the document alone — in some documents the red word is a key term of the sentence, in others it is the answer of a fill-in frame, and putting it back would print the answer.

bold_marker_residue._doc:
THE PARSED BOLD MARKER NEVER SHOWS (KB constraint 5: no stray markup). The parsed Writers Template marks bold as «**…**». When the bold run held only what a builder lifted (a flip card's image address) the block is left as the bare marker («

**

»); when a bold run crosses a soft line break each half keeps one marker («**June- Mid-July» / «LATE PREGNANCY/DRY PERIOD**», «**roue» / «vous**»). Outside the un-built hand-off boxes a listed block whose text is only asterisks is dropped, and a block with an ODD count of the two-asterisk marker loses the one at its edge (leading first, else trailing). Paired markers and longer runs («***», a censored «n*****s») are left alone. Env BOLDMARK_OFF.

media_item_video._doc: A MEDIA-ITEM REFERENCE WHOSE URL IS A VIDEO IS THE VIDEO — KB 01E ([video] → videoSection). The writer's generic reference to a Media List row («[Insert media item 9] video https://youtu.be/…», «[video, media item 5]», «[insert item 4] https://www.youtube.com/…») resolves to the image element through its alias (Tag_Lexicon), yet the row is a video and the human build embeds it (about 19 in 20 such lines). When the element's alias is one of `aliases` and its own URL — its first link, else the first web address in its own text — is a video host, it renders as the video embed (MediaBuilder.media, kind video: the group's host and icon conventions, the title-line drop); every other image element keeps the image path (an explicit «image» / «diagram» word with a video URL is often a screenshot request). Env MEDIAITEMVIDEO_OFF.

bare_stock_url_image._doc: THE BARE STOCK-PHOTO URL IS AN IMAGE. A body paragraph whose whole content is one stock-photo URL (the writer's image reference typed on its own line — after a description, after an [image] whose own line already held one, under an unknown bracket) must not show as a visible link: MediaBuilder's standing contract is that the pasted iStock URL is the asset reference, never visible text, and the human build shows that image. Outside the un-built hand-off boxes (the developer's raw copy) the paragraph becomes the image in the run's mode (image.mode_P / mode_D + MediaBuilder.FinishImg's alt and loading=lazy); when the page already shows that image (its iStock-<id> label / filename) the paragraph is dropped. Env STOCKURLIMG_OFF.
bare_stock_url_image.todo_text: Designer/Developer To Do: image goes here{label}. Link: {url}

escape_once._doc: The note's text is escaped by the red-note form itself, so the link is handed over as written («…?phrase=bed&searchscope=image», never «&searchscope»). Env TODOESC_OFF (or enabled:false) escapes it before the form does as well.

bare_stock_url_image._mode_doc: todo (default) = the house To Do note in place of the URL line (the image stays the developer's cue; no URL for the learner); image = the in-place placeholder ; drop = nothing. The human places these pictures in side columns and widgets, not at the URL's line, so an in-place usually lands in the wrong place — hence the note by default.

more_tags._doc:
media_free_note's rule for the other element tags rendered through #element: their red free text (≥ min_words, outside the brackets) that no builder shows ships as a Writers Note — `[Table] please add shading to table background` FRNO902, `Please recreate this table…` MXEX302, `[Body] Only need slides 4 and 5 for this task…` BLL212, `[Body] The poem “If” can be downloaded at:` BLL253. With it on, a span whose bracket-stripped words open with a template placeholder (red_flag.omit_placeholders — `Outline any relevant information relating to assessment…`) is never noted, for these tags and the media tags alike. `button` is NOT listed: its free text is the label, which the builders normalise (`[Button] Go to journal.` → the KB `

Go to your journal

`), so the own-output test would miss it and add false notes.

media_free_note._doc: THE WRITER'S WORDS INSIDE A MEDIA TAG'S RED SPAN. The free text a writer types inside a media tag's red span, outside its brackets (`[Interactive image] Can we have the description pop out when clicked?` AGH1003, `[Image] Carousel with management practice underneath.` AGH1001, `Please insert this map in the middle of the page of this section:` ANZH301, `The story ‘Sant the Ant’ can be found -` BLL113 [embed]) — parse.free, which no media builder renders, and which would otherwise reach no page and no hand-off file — ships as a red Writers Note after the element (KB red-note family c37 / c57 / c59 / c88). Skipped below min_words words (URLs removed), when the element's own output already shows the words, or when the span is an instruction-fragment note already.

image_reference_title_drop._doc_summary: The image's own title-form reference line never renders.
image_reference_title_drop.note:
The video_embed_title_drop rule extended to images: an OWN blackAfter line that fold-equals a non-URL hyperlink anchor of the same paragraph, or matches the iStock reference form, is the media REFERENCE, not a caption (the human never ships it as a

). Genuinely-following prose is kept. Env IMGREFTITLE_OFF. Part 2 (same flag/toggle): a whole free-body text LINE matching line_pattern is dropped at the ListsAndRuns.renderBlackText stitch seam (cv2 dumps stitch=false → untouched by construction) — catches a reference title whose [image] marker was consumed elsewhere (un-built quiz lead flushes).

bare_summary_alert._doc:
THE WRITER'S BARE [Summary] IS AN ALERT BOX TITLED 'Summary' (its own toggle, SUMMARYALERT_OFF). The bare red `[Summary]` resolves to no tag (every one is in the AGH family — AGH1002 / 1003 / 1007 / 1008), so it would show as a 'Writers Note: [Summary]' with the bullets free. The human puts every following block in `div.alert > div.row > div.col-12` headed `

Summary

` — the tag word is the title. PageAssembler re-parses the span as retag_as and makes the tag word its first content line; the ordinary strict alert path gathers the run and #alertTitleHeading lifts the short first line to the h4. A family dialect keyed on the writer's own tag (§1d exception 1).
bare_summary_alert.title: Summary

untagged_proverb._doc: THE UNTAGGED WHAKATAUKĪ. A writer who types a proverb and its translation without the [Whakatauki] tag leaves two free black paragraphs: the reo line (every word Māori-phonotactic — open syllables over the Māori alphabet, ≥ min_reo_words) and the English line right after it. The human mostly boxes the pair as div.whakatauki, and KB 07B §7 names the dedicated whakatauki component. The reo item is re-typed as the retag_as tag with the reo line as its payload, so the existing proverb-only callout (by_tag.whakatauki: reo + english, bold / italic stripped, 2 paragraphs) builds the box. Skipped: a pair the writer already tagged (the item before it is a whakatauki tag), a greeting (exclude_pattern), a reo line over max_reo_chars. The English is handed to the box as the writer's one-line `reo | english` form and its own item emptied (by emit time a later pass has merged it with the paragraphs after it, so the proverb gather would read it as commentary and leave it out); an English line over max_english_chars is commentary and stays free; a proverb right after an INTERACTIVE tag is that widget's content (ANZH301 / 302's [interactive]), and one right after an owner_tags callout with a payload or more content is that box's; a payload-free owner_tags callout whose WHOLE content is the pair is the writer's proverb box under another name and is REPLACED by the whakatauki (AGH1002 / CBI1004 / CEDT207 / CEDT301 / XDLS901's [Important] + proverb: the human ships the whakatauki alone, where the callout alone would be an 'Empty [important]' red flag); a line with a whakatauki tag within tagged_lookback short lines before it belongs to that tag (so ENGC204's four-line box stays whole); the writer's bare label line before the pair (label_pattern: Whakataukī / [Whakataukī] / Whakatauki:) and an inline label prefix (label_prefix_pattern) are dropped — the human drops both (PHE1005, CEDR203, HES1003). Env UNTAGPROVERB_OFF.

payload_forms._skip_menu_doc: The overview's module-menu region (a [TITLE BAR] section marker to the next section marker) is built by the menu builder, not the callout emitter: a proverb there stays as the writer typed it (otherwise ENGI202's Understand block menu would print the raw `reo | english` payload). Guards THIS pass only: the untagged pass does not use it, because in PWYWHA1 / XWHA01 / TWHA903 a title bar is followed straight by body text (no menu) and those proverbs are boxed in the human build.
payload_forms._doc: THE PROVERB AS A TAG'S PAYLOAD: the reo line typed on the tag's own line — [Body] *Tuku iho, he tapu te upoko.* (PHE1007, BLLR201) or a callout whose whole content is the pair, [Alert] *Kō ngā tahu ā ō tapuwai inanahi…* + the English (ANZH105 / ANZH205, SSOG101, XDLS501's [Important Statement]) — is the same proverb box; the human ships div.whakatauki on every one. The tag is re-typed as the whakatauki with `reo | english` as its payload; a whole_content_tags callout re-types only when a tag / the end follows the English. KB 07B §7.

callouts.rule: One container algorithm serves every callout — only the class differs (a lookup, not logic). Modifier keywords append their class.
callouts.side_column_backward_pair_note: A side_column callout ([Side alert] → alertActivity) is the RIGHT sibling of the immediately-preceding col-md-8 main-content column, in ONE shared <div class="row"> — the human convention across the [side alert] modules (BLL160's single own-row box is an editorial exception). ContentConverter's callout emit site detects that rowFor("section") has just closed the preceding content row (parts ends with content_row_close = close col-md-8 + close row), un-closes it, appends #sideAlertCol as the right-sibling col, and re-closes the row. The col-md-8 default content col already matches the human; the EXACT side width (col-md-4 vs col-md-3, both common) stays editorial. Falls back to the own-row form when there is no preceding content row (page-start / consecutive alerts). General + data-described: any future side_column callout pairs the same way. Env SIDEPAIR_OFF renders own-row (independent of SIDEALERT_OFF, which turns off the class entirely).
callouts.flowing_tags_note: These callouts are NOT self-contained own-row boxes (unlike alert/important) — the human renders them as classed paragraphs that FLOW into the current section row (the page-start quote opens the row and the intro flows in). ContentConverter row-groups them as 'block' (flow) and skips the after-breakRow.

rules._doc: The plain `alert` and `alert solid` boxes: when the next content is PROSE (a heading / activity / callout / widget opens a row and is not a break question), the human mostly keeps that prose INSIDE the box's column, across the Standard subjects (NCEA1 included). Bilingual is not listed (the human breaks there); `alert top` is excluded by class (exclude_class_match is tested against the box's own open tag); `side alert` (alertActivity) is its own tag and its own side-column path.

flow_after_tags._rules_doc: Each rule: tags (the callout's primary tag), templates (Module_Structure_Index module_meta template_type; empty = any), exclude_subjects (module_meta subject), exclude_class_match (a regex on the emitted box's open tag, e.g. the `top` modifier), env (an optional per-rule env toggle on top of the family env — the rule reverses alone; e.g. `ALERTFLOW_OFF`). A tag matched by any rule in scope skips the after-box breakRow; the break BEFORE the box is untouched. One env for the family.
flow_after_tags._doc: A whakataukī box OPENS its column (the break BEFORE it stands) but does NOT close it: in the human build the writer's commentary paragraph after the proverb flows on INSIDE the same col-md-8 (Online Safety, Leaving to Learn, ConnectED …). Every other box (alert, alert.solid, alert.top, alertActivity, activity) is its column's last child, so the general 'after' rule (callout_close → breakRow) stays for them. A listed tag skips the after-box breakRow at BOTH emit sites (the strict box and the CONTAINER_CLOSE of a spanning box) when the module's Module_Structure_Index template_type is listed and its subject is not excluded: NCEA1 is excluded (the HIS 'The whakataukī chosen for this module…' paragraph opens a new row in the human build), Inquiry / Bilingual are not listed (the box is the column's last child there). KB 05D gives the box form only; there is no KB rule on the row after it (authority §1b level 3 / 4). Structure-only, derivable by construction. Env WHFLOW_OFF turns it off.

containment.rule: STRICT BY DEFAULT — a callout holds ONLY its own content run: the embedded payload plus the black text following its marker, up to the NEXT tag span (the project's core marker model, §1.1: 'the marker's content is the black text that follows it, up to the next marker'). The next [body]/[video]/[image]/heading tag is NEVER inside the callout. ONE exception: when the writer placed an explicit matching [end X] further ahead, the box deliberately spans — everything until that close stays inside.
containment.evidence:
In the human pages, .whakatauki direct children are ONLY

(usually two) — never the following body/video, so the box must not swallow what comes after it. Large .alert boxes with media inside do exist (div-heavy, with few direct

) and correspond to deliberately spanned boxes — the explicit-close pathway.
containment.span_note: While spanning to an explicit [end X], only a section marker or page boundary force-closes early (the writer's close is authoritative).
containment.wrap_note: STRUCTURED-CONTENT WRAP (autoClose mode 'span-wrap'): a content callout (wrap_content — alert/important) with NO black text of its own whose content is a following TABLE spans to CONTAIN it — the strict text-gather would otherwise leave it EMPTY and lift the table out (OSGM501: [Alert] + a 2-col image|text table). Unlike an explicit-[end X] span, a wrap is BOUNDED: it ALSO closes at the next heading (rendered level <= wrap_close_heading_max) so it can never over-capture. Code: ContentConverter.#calloutWrapsStructured.

content_wrap.note:
Callouts whose by_tag def has wrap_content:true wrap their STRICT content run in this row>col-12, matching the human gold (alert content usually sits in alert>row>col-12, and the inner col is almost always col-12). whakataukī/quote keep their direct

s (no wrap).

strip_bold.note: The human strips writer **bold** landing inside an alert-family box (class alert / alert solid / alert top / alertActivity) in these subjects, consistently across every alert subclass; the bold it keeps is span-level key vocabulary (HIS 'mana'/'apartheid' definition terms) with NO derivable discriminator, so stripping is the better rule. The fragment families ANZH / ART / BLL are out of scope (the human often keeps bold there); reo/bilingual modules KEEP bold -> exclude_reo via MenuBuilder.isReoModule (never mtkFlag). class_pattern tests the by_tag def's OWN open html — whakatauki/quote/wananga/supervisor-panel defs never match, so the strip cannot reach panels, tables or widgets; nested tables/widgets render via other paths and are untouched by construction. Strips at the box's own lead/payload/content renders (#calloutOpen both modes + #sideAlertCol) via MenuBuilder.stripTextBold. A span-mode box's LATER main-loop items are not stripped. Env ALERTBOLD_OFF keeps the writer's bold.

inline_continuation.note: SAME-BLOCK button/link absorb. A STRICT wrap_content callout (alert/important) absorbs an [external link button]/[Button] (ELEMENT) or [external link] (INLINE) that sits in the SAME WT paragraph (shared source block) as the callout INTO its row>col-12 box, instead of letting it break out as a separate row below. The human renders such a same-sentence external button INSIDE the box (OSAH501/OSAH301/OSGM101/OSAH401/ANZH404/XGF9006/MXEO401). A button a PARAGRAPH later (different block) is UNTOUCHED — it stays its own row (as in the CED [alert.top] families). require_url:true gates absorption on a resolvable http(s) target (block link OR a URL in the item) so a misresolved writer instruction with the word 'button' but no link ('[please add a button to link to SSFUN07…]', SSFUN01) is NOT absorbed. The walk stops at the first different-block / non-absorbable / url-less item, so it can never over-capture. Env CALLOUTBTN_OFF renders the button as a separate row below the box.

variants._doc:
The XOTP activity-table family's Story-Questions alert holds `

` + `

` + `

    ` DIRECTLY (no inner row > col-12) in a `col-md-9 col-12` section column, as every human XOTP alert does. A variant is matched by module-code prefix (ContentConverter.#calloutVariant, the kb_form swap generalised to a family); its lead_element is FIXED against the group convention; `column` is read by the lazy row open. With ACTTABLEADAPT_OFF the module is refused, so the variant never fires without the adapter.

side alert._doc:
The writer's `[Side alert]` tip-box (as in BLL210). The human renders it as a NARROW SIDE column holding a `
` (NOT the generic `[alert]` box: no `alert` class, no inner row>col-12 wrap, no h4 lead — the content is a direct `

`); without this def the bare `alert` substring would match and emit a plain alert. `#calloutOpen` routes a def with `side_column` into `

{content}
` and SKIPS the alert wrap_content/lead. The EXACT side-column WIDTH (col-md-4 vs col-md-3, both common) is editorial; the SIDE-BY-SIDE pairing with the preceding main content is side_column_backward_pair (the `pendingSideAlert` path). General + data-described: any other writer tag with its own output shape is added here the same way. Env SIDEALERT_OFF renders the plain `[alert]`.

wananga._note_kb_form:
THE WĀNANGA / TALANOA BOX IS THE KB'S CULTURAL ALERT. The CED Phase-5 writers (CEDK501 / CEDO501 / CEDO502 / CEDR501 / CEDT501 / CEDW501) type `[Wānanga/Talanoa box]` (and `[Wananga box]`, `[Talanoa/Wananga box]`, the typos `[Wanana/…]` / `[Wananaga/…]`, CEDT501's `[Banner - Wānanga/Talanoa box]`) on its own line, then a ONE-CELL table holding the discussion prompt. The human renders every one as KB 05B's Cultural Alert `
> row > col-12 > p…` (KB 14A §14.4 ConnectED Phase 5: 'all alerts are combined unless otherwise specified'; a bulleted cell becomes a
    ; no h4). Without it the box would be an EMPTY `div.wananga` + a red flag (the strict gather finds no black text before the table) + the writer's table kept as `table.table-bordered`. kb_form: #calloutOpen swaps the def's open / close / wrap_content when on (the legacy `div.wananga` is the OFF form). table_cell_content: in STRICT mode a callout whose own gather is empty and whose NEXT item is a one-row one-cell table takes the cell as its content through TablesAndGrids.renderCellParts (a

    per ' / '-part, '• ' lines → a

      , the cell's own [H*] / [image] parts honoured) and marks the table consumed; #calloutWrapsStructured yields to it. The Banner form rides Tag_Lexicon._meta.tag_promote (carousel → wananga). ONE env WANANGA_OFF turns off all three.

proverb_normalise.note:
The writer's proverb = bold reo + SOFT line break (w:br) + English; if the soft break is lost the two lines GLUE into one

('…ana”Through perseverance…', as in XDLS905/906). The human house form for .whakatauki boxes is two+ separate PLAIN

— almost never kept , or wrapping quotes; the site CSS styles .whakatauki p, so kept double-styles. SPLITS re-derive the lost break from its visible boundary (leading **bold**/*italic* group abutting text · leading “quoted” phrase + prose · space-before pipe · full-tail '(translation)', parens dropped); STRIPS run segment-level via MenuBuilder.stripTextBold/Italic + edge-anchored quote strip. A glue with no marker at the language boundary (CEDT501-12, CEDO105) has no derivable split point and is left as it is. Engine: ContentConverter.#proverbSplit + #proverbStripSeg. Env PROVERBNORM_OFF turns off split AND strips.

proverb_split_merged._label_doc:
A leading label line in the merged item ('**Whakatauki**', FRNO902) stays out of the box — the gold keeps it as its own bold

before the box.
proverb_split_merged._pipe_doc:
The reo|english pipe / spaced-dash split (split_payload_on_pipe) runs only when the gathered content is ONE line: a proverb that already has its two lines keeps them — the English line's own spaced dash is punctuation ('Pursue excellence – should you stumble, let it be to a lofty mountain', EXBP901: the gold keeps it one

).
proverb_split_merged._doc: THE TAGGED WHAKATAUKĪ'S MERGED LINES. By emit time an earlier pass has often joined the proverb, its translation and the commentary into ONE black item ('reo\nenglish\ncommentary'); #gatherProverb's length test (proverb_max_chars) would read it as commentary, so the writer's own [Whakatauki] would come out EMPTY with an 'Empty [whakatauki]' red flag (SSEA203_0_0, EXBP901_1_0 / _4_0) or reo-only. A merged item over proverb_max_chars gives up its leading short lines, up to proverb_max_paragraphs, and keeps the rest as free body. KB 07B §7.

whakatauki.proverb_note:
A whakataukī holds ONLY the proverb (reo + english) — the leading SHORT line(s) on/after the marker. The COMMENTARY that follows (a long explanatory paragraph, no marker) is FREE body, not part of the callout: the human's whakatauki boxes almost always hold exactly the 2 proverb

s. ContentConverter.#gatherProverb stops at the first paragraph longer than proverb_max_chars (or after proverb_max_paragraphs) and leaves it un-consumed → rendered as body. split_payload_on_pipe splits reo|english on | / – / — (spaced) (as for XGF9001's en-dash proverb).
whakatauki.icon_note: No icon img: the human build renders a plain <div class="whakatauki"> (as in OSAI201-00).
whakatauki.pipe_note:
Writers give the proverb as 'reo | english' on one line; the house form is two separate

s (179/181 in the corpus).

kb_p_form._doc_extent:
THE QUOTE'S OWN EXTENT (quote_extent): the strict gather takes the whole black run after the tag, so a box can hold the quote AND the prose after it. The gold styles only the quote (SSCI104_4: the italic quote is p.quoteText, its 'Thrive means…' explanation and the question stay plain

s; PES1005_4: two quoted paragraphs then the source link as p.quoteAck). A box whose FIRST paragraph is a self-contained quote (self_contained_pattern: wholly in quotation marks, or wholly italic) ends at the first later paragraph that is not quote_like (does not open with italics or a quotation mark); that paragraph becomes the p.quoteAck when it is an attribution line (ack_line_pattern, or a bare link when ack_bare_link), and every paragraph after it stays a plain

(it flows in the same column — the quote is a flowing callout). A box that opens any other way (a poem's plain lines — ENGJ402; a quotation opened on one paragraph and closed on the next — ENGS101) keeps every paragraph as p.quoteText.
kb_p_form._doc:
KB 01F / 05D. KB 01F's normalised-tag table maps `quote` → `

"Quote"

Attribution

` (05D 'Quote Text' the same: no wrapper). The human agrees wherever it styles a tagged quote (EXBP901 / OSAI301 / 401 / 501 / ENGJ402 / OSAH401: p.quoteText (+ p.quoteAck), never a div). So: no wrapper div; every plain `

` of the box is `p.quoteText`; the attribution becomes its own `p.quoteAck` — the LAST paragraph's tail after the closing quote mark (tail_after_quote_pattern: `“…” Albert Einstein.`, `…magic.” By Arthur C Clarke…`) or after a spaced en/em dash (tail_after_dash_pattern, head ≥ dash_head_min_words words: `…ourselves. – Sir Edmund Hillary`), ≤ ack_max_words words; or a last paragraph that is itself an attribution line (ack_line_pattern: a dash / `Source:` / `By …`, ≤ ack_line_max_words words). Only a GENUINE quote tag takes the form — the primary tag's own bracket text must match genuine_tag_pattern (`quote` / `quotation` / `quotetext`, optionally `centered` / `highlighted` / `pull` / `block` before it or `by ` after it, case-insensitive); a writer INSTRUCTION the lexicon matched on the word (ART1002's `[please create three tiles … match colours with quote above …]`, ENGC403's `[insert quote from …]`) keeps the legacy box, and so does a box that OPENS with a bare link (the `[quote link] URL` instruction, HIS1005) — none of them is a quote. An untagged quote is not derivable outside the HIS family (see family_quote_paragraph). Lists, images and notes pass through untouched. Env QUOTEFORM_OFF = the legacy div box.

supervisor note.open: Supervisor note
supervisor note.note: The supervisor-note structure from the human gold standard (BLL146-0.0): a row-level super-content block. own_row = the template carries its OWN row/col wrappers, so the engine must NOT wrap it in the standard content row. The flat open/close above are the LEGACY form, used under SUPINROW_OFF; the live form is inner_row below.

text_col_by_subject._doc: The own-row supervisor panel's TEXT column (the inner row's second col) is `col-12` in most of the corpus (the BLL / MXDI majority, the template's default) but `col-12 col-md-12` in the Leaving to Learn family (as in the XDLS90x series). The module's Module_Structure_Index subject picks the class; the LAST `<div class="col-12">` of the inner_row open is rewritten. The activity-owned panel template (activity_wrapper.super_content.panel_open) is untouched (no consistent human form there).

inner_row._note: The human wraps the panel's two col-12s in an INNER row (super-content row > row > col-12 label + col-12 text) at every non-activity site (as in BLL225-0.0 and the BLL146-0.0 source). Same form as the activity-panel inner row (the reveal JS keys on the nested structure). Env SUPINROW_OFF uses the flat legacy open/close.
inner_row.open: Supervisor note

pair_with_content._note: BLL-family SIDE-BY-SIDE PAIRING: the human anchors a non-activity supervisor note to the section paragraph it annotates — ONE row.supervisor holding the note panel col FIRST + the content col (as in BLL225-0.0); every other subject ships the standalone row (MXFL101 has the IDENTICAL WT context and stays standalone). Scope: subjects prefix match, BEFORE the page's first [Activity] opener (an in-activity note belongs to the activity panel), companion = the next unconsumed [body] element. The section heading stays in its OWN row; the pre-pass swaps a note-BEFORE-heading ([supervisor note][Introduction][body], BLL225) past the heading so both writer orders ([Introduction][supervisor note][body], BLL111) reach the emit site identically. swap_heading_tags covers the mid-page [Introduction]→title-bar SECTION_MARKER alias; rendered [H1-3] headings (max_heading_level) also qualify. content_col_open_by_series: BLL2 pages mostly carry paddingR, BLL1 mostly plain. Env SUPPAIR_OFF renders the standalone form.

pair_with_heading._note: BLL1 h2-INSIDE variant: on the BLL1 single-file phonics parents (BLL130-160) each letter section opens [H1/H2] heading → [Supervisor note] → [Activity], with NO companion [body] — so pair_with_content declines. The human pairs the note with the HEADING itself: ONE row.supervisor = [panel col + col-md-8 col-12 paddingR holding ONLY the section heading]. Scope is BLL1 ONLY, not BLL-wide: BLL210 (a BLL2 parent) leaves heading-preceded notes STANDALONE, and the BLL2 h2-inside sites (BLL246/254_2.0) sit INSIDE activity boxes, which this rule does not handle. Fires only when the forward body-pair did NOT fire AND the just-emitted parts tail is a heading-only content row (row_open + <h1-3> + row_close, default col class) — the fold pops that row and re-emits the heading inside the pair's content col. Env SUPPAIRH2_OFF renders the standalone form (heading row + lone row.supervisor).

explicit_close_span._doc: A writer who CLOSES the note explicitly — `[Supervisor Button] … [End Supervisor button]` (XDLS904 / 905 / 906) or `[Supervisor note] … [end supervisor note]` (XDLS502, XDLS901) — means the whole run to the closer is the panel's content: the human's panel holds every paragraph and bullet between, where the strict gather would stop at the first tag item (a bullet's trailing inline `[link to X]`) and leave the rest as free rows. On a matching closer ahead (#explicitCloseAhead — the family set also accepts the closer of a tag_promote source, `end supervisor button`; an [Activity] opener ends the scan so an own-row span never swallows an activity) the own_row panel opens in SPAN mode (stack mode span-own): the loop renders the items between inside the panel's column, a heading never closes it (the writer's closer is authoritative; a section marker / page boundary does), the closer pops it. Every family without an explicit closer is untouched by construction. OFF = the strict panel.

fold_page_label._note: The [page N]-LABEL fold: on the BLL1 [page N]-delimited inquiry parents the writer opens a section `[page N]

supervisor note._long_payload_note:
A supervisor note whose WHOLE text the writer typed INSIDE the red span fails the ≤12-word lead rule and has no black follower, so it would render content-less + an 'Empty [supervisor note]' red flag; the human ships the prose as the panel

(with bare URLs woven). These are BLL note prose, never instructions (instructionFragment keeps the CS-note path). Rendered via renderBlackText so links weave (BLL111-01). Env SUPPAYLOAD_OFF drops the payload and shows the red flag.
supervisor note._strip_italic_note: The human strips writer *italic* landing INSIDE the supervisor super-content panel in the MXDI+XDLS families (its panels carry no <i>/<em> there, as in MXDI103). BLL is MIXED (book/story titles + letter-sound lines are KEPT) and reo/bilingual families keep reo italic → NOT in the list. Applied to the panel's lead + gathered content at #calloutOpen via MenuBuilder.stripTextItalic (Font-Awesome <i class=fa> untouched). Env PANELITALIC_OFF keeps the writer's italic.

modifier_classes._rule: Two-tier positional rule (§5.6): a positional phrase that maps to a documented class here is ACTIONED into the class; one that doesn't is rendered as a red flag at the box.

always_side._doc: 'An RHS tag always becomes the right-hand side box.' In STANDARD and FUNDAMENTALS modules (not Inquiry, whose human build rarely does this) every right-hand alert spelling becomes the side column, the box style still chosen by position (alertActivity after an activity box, alert top after content — see positional_side_alert). Two widenings: (1) extra_keywords — the writer's `[Alert box right hand side (of page)]` / `[right-hand alert]` spellings, which the rhs / rhc list does not match (BLL242 / 244 / 251 / 254–257 / 272); (2) forward_pair — a box with NO content row closed just before it (the page-top Ākonga notes, the WJFUN tile pages, a box right after a heading) is HELD and paired as the right sibling of the FOLLOWING content row (the pendingSideAlert machinery the alert-table path already uses) instead of a full-width box. Where the human uses a full-width / paragraph form instead, that is a NAMED override by this decision. Env RHSALWAYS_OFF.

tagged_content._doc: 'The box must never vanish.' A right-hand box whose writer typed its content on the FOLLOWING lines under their own tags — `[alert RHS]` + `[body] When rounding…` (MXFL301), `[Alert box RHS]` + `[H3] Extra fun` + `[Body] …` (SSFUN05), or the RHS tag typed on the heading's own line, `[Alert RHS] [H3] Key questions` + bullets (XGF9001, the heading winning the parse) — would otherwise be an EMPTY box ('Empty [alert]') or no box, its content falling into the main column. That run is the box's content: one heading as its lead (the def's lead element), then `[body]`-tagged lines (body_tags, a line carrying no other tag) and plain lines, bullets included, up to the next other tag; the side column goes beside the row just closed (the backward pairing and box-style choice) or is held for the next row (forward_pair). Env RHSTAGGED_OFF.

after_content._doc_side_column_by_subject: Optional per-subject class map for the ALERT-TOP SIDE COLUMN. The map is empty, so the #sideAlertCol hook is a no-op: the human's alert-top side-column class varies per module within a subject (MXFU301's pairs use col-md-4 col-12 paddingL, HIS1004's the col-md-4 offset-md-0 col-12 paddingL form), with no page-level discriminator, so the def's own side_column (`col-md-4 col-12`) is used everywhere; the left column stays `col-12 col-md-8`. When an entry exists #sideAlertCol resolves the class from this map by the module's module_meta subject. Env SIDECOLSUBJ_OFF ignores the map.

positional_side_alert._doc: A RIGHT-HAND ALERT IS A SIDE COLUMN; `rhs` and `summary` ARE NOT CLASSES. The writer's positional words (`[alert box rhs]`, `[alert box rhc]`, `[rhs alert]`, `[alert rhs]`, `[important info box rhs]`, `[alert.rhs]`) and label words (`[alert box lesson summary]`) would reach the page through modifier_classes as `alert rhs` and `alert summary` — tokens the human never ships and KB 05B does not define (its alert vocabulary: alert / solid / top / blank / teacher / cultural; its sidebar: col-md-4 offset-md-0 col-12 > alertActivity > h4 + p). In the human build a `summary` box is a plain `alert` (or `alert solid`) — so the token is dropped; an `rhs` box sits in a SIDE COLUMN (col-md-4 / col-4) as the RIGHT sibling of a col-md-8 content column, its class decided by what precedes it — after an ACTIVITY box the KB activity sidebar `alertActivity`, after plain content `alert top`; the writer's spelling, the subject and the box length are not discriminators. MECHANISM: at the callout emit site an `alert`/`important` whose leftover remainder words carry a keyword, in STRICT mode, with the preceding content row just closed, is spliced as that row's right sibling through the side-column pairing (#sideAlertCol, which honours a def's lead_element so an embedded payload lead is never dropped) — `after_activity` when the closed row's first block is an activity box, `after_content` otherwise; with no preceding content row, or in SPAN mode, it renders as the plain box with the token stripped. `strip_tokens` are removed from the modifier string wherever a callout opens.
