Related rules: the table-form positional alert (→ col-md-4 > alert top paired right, ENGS302), [Side alert] (→ the paired alertActivity column), and the exact spelling [right-hand alert] promoted to side alert. NAMED consensus-over-gold deltas: the rhs sites whose human build keeps a full-width plain alert; the human's editorial column padding on the alert-top sites is not followed. Env ALERTRHS_OFF turns it off (the tokens ship, no routing).

callouts.corpus_note: alert / 'alert solid' / whakatauki / wananga / quoteText counted from the finished corpus (e.g. 95× quoteText, 176× whakatauki).
callouts.lead_note:
lead_element: a short embedded title renders as this element inside the box (corpus: .alert leads are h4-dominant). Callouts without the key keep the bolded

lead.

promoted_box_empty_guard._note: NEVER HALF-BUILD THE PROMOTED SUMMARY BOX. Tag_Lexicon tag_promote rewrites a bare [summary box] into an `alert` so the existing callout machinery builds it. The callout gathers by the STRICT rule (callouts.containment): the marker payload plus the BLACK text following it, stopping at the next tag span. When the writer TAGGED the summary instead of leaving it as plain text ([Summary box:] then [body] We hope you enjoyed..., or [H4] Lesson Summary — CEDK401 2.0, XDLS912 4.0, XTAS101 1.0), the strict gather stops immediately and the box would ship EMPTY with the summary rendered underneath — a half-build. Those decline: the marker renders nothing and the content renders normally. Scoped by parse.promoted === 'summary_box', so a writer-authored [alert] can never reach this guard. Widening the gather to cross a following [body] would change containment for EVERY callout, so it is not done here. Env SUMMARYBOX_OFF turns off the whole promotion, this guard included.

drop_empty_span_wrap._doc: A span-mode callout ([alert]…[end alert]) opens its inner row>col-12 content wrapper eagerly; when the writer's whole content rode the span's own lead paragraph and the end tag follows immediately (as in SCCH302-01), the wrapper would ship EMPTY — the human never keeps the empty wrap. The CONTAINER_CLOSE site detects the untouched wrap-open as the last emitted part and drops the pair. Env EMPTYWRAP_OFF keeps it.

activity_wrapper._doc_bare: The BARE box form (no inner row > col-12): used by the clickDrop tile-grid PANEL when interactive_builders.clickDrop.tile_grid.panel_no_inner_row is on — the human's clickDropContent activity dropbox panel holds its content directly (XDLS902-906 + 909). Every other box keeps open / close.

opener_free_note._doc: THE WRITER'S WORDS INSIDE AN ACTIVITY OPENER'S RED SPAN. An [Activity …] opener whose red span carries free text outside its brackets (≥ min_words words, URLs removed) that the embedded-title rule (standalone_title_heading.embedded_free_text) did not take as the box's title ships that span as a red Writers Note right after the box opens (the plain opener) or held to the end of the lead's first prose run (the bundle-owned box — the lead_instruction_note queue): ANZH301 / 302 `[Activity 1C] Please present the following definitions in speech bubbles of different colours:`, AGH1004 `(Would be great if you could embed this somehow).`, CBI1009 `Drag and drop the colour of precipitates…`. KB red-note family; without it these lines would reach no page and no hand-off file.

uncued._doc: THE WRITER'S UN-CUED RED LINE IN AN ACTIVITY'S LEAD. lead_instruction_note without its instruction-cue test: every primary-less red span of parse class 'instruction' in the lead ships as the red Writers Note — the body path's own rule (ContentConverter's whole-span instruction branch has no cue test). This catches instructions the cue list misses (`Can we create flip cards that open for 3 seconds…` BLL1xx, `[create fill in the gap]` ARFUN04), the widget's data typed in red (`(around, inside, between)`, `Answers: 1. Fertiliser …` AGH1009) and red supervisor-style notes (BLL130), which would otherwise reach no page and no hand-off file. Off → only cued spans are noted.

lead_instruction_note._doc: THE WRITER'S INSTRUCTION IN AN ACTIVITY'S LEAD. A whole-span red instruction (no primary tag, parse class 'instruction') that carries an instruction cue (TagNormaliser.HasInstructionCue) and that the widget capture put into the activity box's LEAD (bundle.activityLeadItems — typed between the activity opener and its widget tag) renders as the red Writers Note the body path gives it (the KB red-note family, constraints 37 / 57 / 59 / 88 — a named override), in the writer's order. The lead loop otherwise renders such an item only through its primary or its black tail, so the writer's request would vanish (ARFUN04 `[CS to create tick boxes; I have highlighted the answers.]`, MXFU401 `CS: Please make these big colourful square tiles:`, BLL230 `Can we separate these into two separate lists please.`). A stopwatch request is left to the stopwatch_build hook. A cue-less red span (HIS1004's red table text) is handled by the uncued rule.

super_content._note:
A [Supervisor note] directly after an [Activity] opener has directive CONTAINER_OPEN, so container_auto_close.activity_close_before would CLOSE the activity before it — the note would be its own row supervisor block and the activity's [body]/[image] would spill into loose sibling rows BELOW the (now heading-only) box. The human instead NESTS the note as the activity's first child (as in BLL241-2 2A):
>
…note…
+
title+body
. So the [Activity] opener looks ahead for an immediately-following supervisor note; when present #activityOpen adds the super-content-button activity class, emits the nested panel (below) FIRST, then opens a fresh row>col for the title+body — matching the human two-child box exactly. Env SUPNOTE_OFF uses the auto-close + own-row form.
super_content._row_class_note: Child dictates ancestor: the TOP content row wrapping a supervisor-note activity carries '.supervisor' (every human .supervisor row contains a super-content note). The reveal JS keys off .row.supervisor — without it the note renders inline (visible) instead of the hidden icon-modal. The activity opener sets nextRowClass=row_class before its emit so body_region.content_row_open renders '<div class="row supervisor">'.
super_content.panel_open: Supervisor note
super_content._panel_note: The human's super-content panel wraps its two col-12s in an INNER <div class="row"> (super-content row > row > col-12,col-12); without it the idoc_scripts reveal JS leaves the note VISIBLE inline instead of the hidden icon-triggered modal (BLL241-2 2A/2C). Matching the human structure byte-for-byte gives the modal (the overview note uses the same super-content structure).

scan_within_activity._note: The writer also places the note MID-activity ([Activity][body][supervisor note][video][end activity]); the human STILL hoists it into the box panel as the FIRST child (as in BLL225-2.0 2E). Some human super-content boxes have no WT note at all (human-added/duplicated notes) — editorial, not generated. The opener lookahead scans forward to the activity's natural boundary (mirroring container_auto_close.activity_close_before semantics: section heading after content / next activity / any auto-close directive or tag / closer / section marker), skipping bundle-consumed members (a note after an embedded interactive still belongs to the box). The found note is consumed IN PLACE (loop index unchanged — the content between opener and note must render); the main loop skips it on arrival via its consumedBy mark. Env SUPSCAN_OFF uses the immediate-only lookahead; SUPNOTE_OFF turns off the whole super-content mechanism.

embedded_free_text._doc_guards: Guards: the `[interactive activity] type and check` / `[interactive tool] …` openers (alias `interactive` — the MXDI / MXFU / MXFL dialect names the WIDGET after the bracket) → exclude_alias_words; a Word run split mid-word (`[Activity 5A] L` + black `ooking at…`) → min_chars; a lowercase aside (`[activity 5b] wide`, `tick the pictures that show fractions.`) → require_capital (every human-titled site is capitalised); `Calculating soil type.` → strip_trailing_stop (the human's h3 carries no stop).
embedded_free_text._doc: An [Activity …] opener whose TITLE the writer typed INSIDE the red span — `[Activity 2A] Concrete poems` all red, `[Activity] Calculating soil type.`, `[Activity box:] Ka pai!` — carries it as the span's FREE text (parse.free), which neither the parent rule (blackAfter's first line) nor the owner-lead addLead reads, so without this the title would be dropped. ContentConverter.#embeddedOpenerTitle applies the rule at BOTH opener sites (the plain path via it._embeddedTitle → ActivitiesBuilder.activityOpen; the bundle-owned path as the first _ownerTitle lead item): an activity CONTAINER_OPEN opener whose bracket remainder is empty or a listed mode word, whose free text is not an instruction fragment / cue, not parenthesised, not digit-led, not colon-ended, at most max_words words, and does NOT itself resolve to a lexicon tag (`[True False Quiz]` → radio quiz, `[Drag and Drop]`, `[wordfind]`, `[Trigger Engagement]` — a widget NAME the human never uses as a title) → RenderText(free) is the box's <h{level}>; the whole blackAfter then renders as content. The human opens these boxes with that <h3> across the families (Te ara Whakapuawa, Leaving to Learn, ConnectED, Blended Literacy, Mathematics, English). Excluded: `[Activity: Embedded] <widget>` (remainder embedded), widget names, digit-led / parenthesised / colon-ended / cue text. Env EMBTITLE_OFF turns it off; ACTTITLE_OFF turns this off with the parent rule.

standalone_title_heading._note_title:
The text trailing an [Activity NX] tag is the activity TITLE; the human renders it as

as the box's first child (almost every human activity box starts with

, almost never

). The interactive-OWNED activity path promotes the lead line to

(#activityOpen renderBlack=false, the addLead title logic). On the STANDALONE path (renderBlack=true, a plain [Activity] with no captured widget — BLL233 1E), when enabled, #activityOpen promotes the FIRST LINE of blackAfter to (the title) and renders the REST as body, mirroring the owned path exactly. Env ACTTITLE_OFF renders it all as

.

number_from_tail._note_number_tail: Some writers type the activity number OUTSIDE the bracket — '[Activity] 3A' instead of '[Activity 3A]' (ANZH101/HIS family). it.parse.numbers is then EMPTY, so #activityOpen would emit a NUMBERLESS <div class="activity"> — the human gives it the number (it almost never ships a numberless box). TagNormaliser lifts a LEADING digit+letter id token from the span's free text (outside the bracket) into parse.numbers when an [Activity] CONTAINER_OPEN tag is present and no bracket number exists — so #activityOpen id, InteractiveScanner activityId, and the adjacent-merge carry all see it. Digit+LETTER only (a bare digit is skipped so prose like '5 minutes' can never be read as a number). Env ACTNUMTAIL_OFF gives the numberless box.

bare_reemphasis_merge._note_reemphasis:
A writer opens a NUMBERED activity then types a BARE [Activity] (no number) to re-emphasise where the interactive sits WITHIN it — ENGC101 2A: [Activity 2A] -> [H3] Identifying adjectives -> speech-bubble setup -> [Activity] 'Which words...Tick the describing words' -> the quiz. The human keeps ONE
with the bare [Activity]'s text as a

lead-in, rather than a SECOND, NUMBERLESS box. DISCRIMINATOR (merge vs renumber): the human MERGES only when the open numbered activity's OPENER had an EMPTY tail (ENGC101 [Activity 2A] -> title is a separate [H3]); when the opener carried its own title ([Activity 5C] Extra for Experts / [Activity 5E] Pick a task / [Activity 1D] Body rhythm) the bare activity is a NEW sibling the human RENUMBERS (Dropbox/Reflection/Pick-a-task) — so those are LEFT UNCHANGED (no merge). Rule: when a bare [Activity] opener (no number) arrives while the TOP activity is open, has content, and had an EMPTY opener tail (titledOpener=false), AND the bare lead is not an excluded standalone type (dropbox/reflection/journal/upload), its lead text flows into the open activity and the new box is suppressed. Engine: ContentConverter ConvertPage (guard before autoClose). Env REEMPH_OFF gives the split (two boxes).

owned_target._doc: The immediate merge (bare_reemphasis_merge) and the forward merge (_note_mode_merge) both look for an UNCONSUMED numbered opener after the mode opener — but when the numbered activity is the OWNER of a widget bundle (its `[Activity 1D]` + prose + table captured, the box opening on the bundle's own path) the opener is consumedBy that bundle and neither merge fires, so the mode opener (`[Activity individual]` HIS1006 / bare `[Activity]` HIS1008 / `[Activity: Embedded]` ANZH105 before a heading opener) would ship an EMPTY box followed by the owned box. The human almost never ships an empty activity box. With this on, an un-numbered content-less opener whose next non-blank item is a bundle-owned numbered opener (or a word-form heading opener) ships no box of its own — the owned box is the activity. OFF (env MODEOWNED_OFF) turns it off; ACTMODEMERGE_OFF does not cover it (a separate merge site).
owned_target._doc_past_title_headings: A writer's `[Activity individual]` → `[H3] title` → owned `[Activity 2A]` trio (SSFUN06 2A, ANZH301, HIS1003 / HIS1004, MXFUN01, CEDR204) would still leave a TITLE-ONLY unnumbered box beside the owned box when only the NEXT item is checked, because the forward merge refuses a bundle-consumed target. With this key the walk skips up to `max_intervening_headings` rendered / title-tag headings (the forward merge's predicates); on a hit the mode opener ships no box and the skipped heading(s) become the OWNED box's title (bundle._ownerTitleLines — rendered first in the owner lead stream as the <h3>; the heading item consumed as activity-mode-merge-title). The human ships ONE numbered box with the heading inside. false = check the next item only.

reverse_order._doc: The mode-opener merge family's third shape. The MXFUN family types the number on one tag and the body on a second un-numbered tag with the title between: `[Activity 2C]` → `[H3] Write the correct number` → `[Activity body] Oops! …` (MXFUN01, MXFUN02, MXFUN03, CEDK102, MXEX302, CEDR204). The adjacent-pair merge does not cover it, and the `[Activity body]` CONTAINER_OPEN would auto-close the numbered box after its title and open a second box; the human ships ONE `number=2C` box with h3 + p + table. With this block a NUMBERED content-less opener walks past up to max_intervening_headings title headings; when the next tag is an UN-numbered activity opener (unconsumed, any content) that opener is marked consumed (activity-mode-merge) — the existing handler renders its tail into the open box and it opens no second box — so the numbered opener's box holds the title and the body. false / the env turns it off.

mode_opener_merge._note_mode_merge: An un-numbered activity opener with NO content of its own — a LAYOUT/MODE annotation the writer types before the real numbered activity ([Activity individual] / [Activity embedded] / [Activity body] / [Activity box] / bare [Activity], remainder empty of a number) — is describing the SAME box as the numbered [Activity NX] that follows it, EVEN ACROSS the box's own title heading. WT shape (HIS1004): [Activity individual] -> [H3] Which rights were taken? -> [Activity 1A] -> press release + drag-drop. The human ships ONE <div class="activity" number="1A"> with the H3 as its title INSIDE; without this the mode opener would make an EMPTY-ish box (the H3 as its only child, auto-closed when the numbered opener's CONTAINER_OPEN arrives) and the numbered opener a second box (as in HIS1003 / HIS1004 / HIS1006 / ANZH301 / ANZH304 / SSFUN02/05/06/08 / CEDR204). The consecutive-opener merge (bare_reemphasis_merge) only skips BLANK lines between the two openers; this extends it to skip the box's own TITLE HEADING(s) (up to max_intervening_headings; the HIS1004 pattern is exactly one [H3]) and adopt the numbered opener's id, opening ONE box AT the mode opener's position so the heading lands inside. The numbered opener is marked consumedBy='activity-mode-merge' — it renders only its own lead into the open box, opens no second box, and does not auto-close. GENERAL (keys on 'un-numbered activity opener with empty content', NOT a per-module word list): XDLS903's [Activity] + black-text number '1A' is EXCLUDED because number_from_tail leaves the number in blackAfter (content present); a standalone mode opener with no numbered follower is left as its own box. Engine: ContentConverter ConvertPage (activity CONTAINER_OPEN branch, after the immediate merge). Env ACTMODEMERGE_OFF gives the split (two boxes).

lesson_letter_number._note_scheme: The human numbers an activity box {lessonNumber}{positional-letter} — on lesson page N the K-th activity is N+chr(64+K) (ENGI302 lesson 2: [Activity 1/2/3/4] -> 2A/2B/2C/2D; the WT activity numbers RESET per lesson, the human prepends the lesson number + converts the ordinal to a letter). The human never ships the bare WT digit. PREFIX = page.lessonNumber (PageSplitter's writer [LESSON N] / running lesson ordinal — it tracks the WT lesson structure the human uses, not the output file index). LETTER = positional order of the activity within the lesson (A,B,C…), counted across sub-pages of the same lessonNumber (the human's sub-page letters usually CONTINUE), reset per module. ONLY a BARE-DIGIT id is transformed — a tail-lifted letter id ('1A') is KEPT; overview pages (lessonNumber null) untouched; idx>=26 falls back to the bare digit. Env ACTLETTER_OFF keeps the bare WT digit.

unnumbered_positional._doc: THE UN-NUMBERED ACTIVITY OPENER TAKES THE NEXT POSITIONAL LETTER. The human numbers EVERY activity box {lesson}{letter}, including the writer's bare [Activity] / [Activity: Embedded] / [interactive] … openers with no id, which the lesson-letter rule would otherwise neither letter nor count (only an id-carrying opener or the synthetic positionalId box enters the letter counter). With this on, an opener with no writer id on a page whose lesson number is known (#pageLessonNumber != null — the same gate as the synthetic box; phase pages included) takes the next positional letter and advances the counter exactly as the synthetic box does; writer-lettered ids, bare-digit ids (the lesson-letter renumber) and pages without a lesson number are unchanged. OFF (env ACTUNNUM_OFF) turns it off.

lesson_letter_number._integer_prefix_doc: The {lessonNumber}{letter} renumber uses the INTEGER lesson part of a DOTTED page lesson number ('1.0'→'1', '5.1'→'5') as both the id prefix AND the letter-map key — the human ships '1A'/'5D', never '1.0A'/'5.1A' (ENGJ403/CEDK501/CEDT501/MXDB301/MXEO301/MXFL302), and integer map keys let a lesson split over sub-pages (2.0→2.1) CONTINUE its lettering (2A then 2B/2C). The letter-LESS dotted-id convention (number='1.1') is writer-typed ids kept verbatim — it never enters this renumber. Env ACTLNINT_OFF uses the raw dotted prefix/key.

typed_tag_title._doc:
THE WIDGET-TYPED ACTIVITY TAG'S TAIL IS THE BOX TITLE. The Mathematics MXFL / MXEO / MXFU / MXDB family (and ENGJ / ENGR) types the widget TYPE inside the activity tag — `[Activity 1B – self-marking type the answer] Fill in the blanks`, `[Activity 3A – self-marking drag and drop] Negatives on the number line`, `… – self-marking drop down quiz]`, `… – memory card game]`, `… – reorder]` — so the tag parses as the WIDGET (number 1B) and the embedded form makes it its own box's owner, with the title riding INTO the capture (or the built widget's Writers Note) as a

. The human opens `

` with `

Title

`. With this on, a tag whose raw text matches tag_pattern and whose tail is a title emits title_heading right after the box opens (as the level-pages rule does), records it._typedTitle and blanks the tail so the capture, the built widget's note and the .txt hand-off never repeat it; a trailing bracketed writer note (`(Currently in correct order – please jumble)`) is split off and stays the tail; a bracket-only tail is not a title; never on bilingual (reoMode) pages. KB 01F. OFF (env TYPEDTAG_OFF) turns it off.

embedded_interactive_activity._note_embedded: A writer tags an interactive AND its activity number in ONE bracket — '[Activity 1A drag and drop]' — so the span's primary directive is INTERACTIVE (drag and drop) while it ALSO carries the [activity] tag + the number. InteractiveScanner gives the bundle activityId='1A' but NO activityOwner (there is no separate [Activity] item to walk back to), so the activity-wrapper path (gated on activityOwner) would be skipped and the widget would render as a BARE cv2-interactive placeholder. The human wraps it: <div class="activity interactive" number="1A"> (ENGS302-01 1A, ANZH205 '[Activity: Embedded – Vertical Drag and Drop]' -> 1A, AGH1004 drag-drop activities). So when a bundle has an activityId from its OWN interactive tag's [activity] tag (no separate owner), the activity wrapper opens around the placeholder (forceInteractive per the widget type, the .interactive rule); the title/instructions/data stay INSIDE the placeholder (un-built widget). Env EMBACT_OFF renders the bare placeholder (no activity wrapper).

reo_bundle_activity._status: Default-off. It depends on content_table_guard: without the guard the InteractiveScanner OVER-CAPTURES the bilingual intro CONTENT table as a spurious flipCard (the writer embeds `[Interactive] [Flipcard]` INSIDE the intro `[Body]` cell), so the box would wrap the WHOLE intro (Activity NX: + [H2] heading + [Body]) and take its number, instead of the real widget. With the guard on the box wraps the REAL widget, but the guard on its own loses the embedded widget on box-less modules (see content_table_guard._status), so this flag and the guard are meant to be enabled together with a prose+widget split. env REOACT_OFF gives the bare placeholder.
reo_bundle_activity._note_row_number: Bilingual ACTIVITY scanner integration (as in TRR102). In a reoTranslate module the activity NUMBER is a table ROW ('Activity 1A:' / 'Ngohe 1A:') inside the bilingual English|Māori content table, NOT an [Activity N] TAG, so the InteractiveScanner opener-lookback finds no owner and the widget bundle would render as a bare cv2-interactive placeholder — the human wraps every activity widget: <div class="activity interactive" number="1A">. reoMode-scoped, reusing the bundle wrapper machinery (no parallel path): a post-scan pass in InteractiveScanner tracks the most recent 'Activity NX:'/'Ngohe NX:' row and hands its number to the FIRST following widget bundle (one number -> one box, claimed-per-row so a second bundle before the next row stays inline), setting bundle.activityId + bundle.reoActivity. ContentConverter's bundle path then opens the activity wrapper via a synthetic owner (no lead — the bilingual intro heading/body renders as its own section OUTSIDE the box, matching the human; .interactive forced per the widget-type rule). The '1.1'-positional modules (PNR / TRR103 / … with no clean row) are handled by section_id_number. SCOPE: reoMode only (standard modules carry 'Activity NX:' text too — e.g. ENGS302 — but reoMode is false for them). Env REOACT_OFF gives the bare placeholder (no wrapper, activityId unset).

title_heading_level._doc:
THE ACTIVITY BOX'S TITLE HEADING IS h3. KB 01F `activity_heading` → `

Activity heading text

` within the activity; wherever a human box's first child is a heading it is h3 (Standard, Inquiry and Fundamentals alike). A writer's [H3] typed after the [Activity] opener takes the body shift (+1 → h4; [H4] → h5) and #relevelHeadings skips activity subtrees (the anchor exclusion), so without this the in-box title would never normalise back — while the first-line title and the opener's embedded payload are already fixed at h3. MECHANISM: ActivitiesBuilder.activityTitleLevelPostpass, run in the body chain right after #relevelHeadings — for every activity box open, skip an optional super-content panel (balanced), and when the box's own row > col-12 opens with a heading, rewrite that heading's open + close tags to `level`. Nothing else in the box moves; the reoTranslate (Bilingual) family is excluded — its boxes are built by BilingualBuilder under its own heading rules (PNR keeps h2 by name). Env ACTTITLEH3_OFF turns it off.

phase_numbering._doc: On a page with NO lesson number of its own (the single-file Fundamentals modules), the human numbers every activity box {phase}{letter} — the letter sequence restarting in each phase panel (with the human's own occasional gaps / duplicates / sub-page continuations). Every phasebreak on a lesson-number-less page advances the page's activity-number prefix (generalising the level-pages ordinal, run._levelMenu), so the existing rules fire — a writer's bare-digit id renumbers to {phase}{letter} (lesson_letter_number), a writer LETTER id is kept, and the synthetic standalone-widget box takes its number (it is withheld where no number is derivable). Env PHASENUM_OFF turns it off.

lead_free_after_tag._doc: THE LEAD PROSE AFTER THE WIDGET TAG RENDERS FREE INSIDE THE BOX. A writer types the widget tag, then the instruction paragraph(s), then the widget's table — `[Interactive]` / `Drag and drop the products into the correct category.` / TABLE. The scanner walks that black run into the bundle as a MEMBER, so an un-built capture would show it inside the dashed box; the human keeps it FREE in the activity box (h3 + p + the widget) for some widget types — dragAndDrop, dropDown, reorder, typing, unclassified standalone, modal, radioQuiz — while carousel, flipCard, accordion, selfCheck, clickDrop, multiChoiceQuiz and tabs fold the lead INTO the widget. Hence the scoped sets types_standalone / types_owned below; Social Science and Arts are excluded by code prefix (the human keeps the lead inside there). With this on, ContentConverter renders the consecutive black members after the opener tag (before the first table / list / tag) as free paragraphs inside the box and removes them from bundle.memberItems before #interactivePlaceholder builds the capture; at least one non-black member must remain (require_remaining_member) or nothing moves; never on bilingual (reoMode) pages or the MTK quiz shell. OFF (env LEADFREE_OFF) turns it off.

page_number_normalise._doc: THE PAGE'S ACTIVITY NUMBERS ARE CONSECUTIVE. KB 00B_CONVERSION_PIPELINE line 187 + constraint 62: 'the first interactive keeps the writer's activity number; each subsequent interactive takes the next letter … renumber the following activities accordingly'; constraint 65 / 05D: the MTK quiz box 'carries the next consecutive activity number even where the writer assigned none'. The human's lesson pages mostly follow {page number}{A, B, C …}. The lesson-letter rule keeps every writer id that carries a letter verbatim, so a page could ship `5A, 5A` (two writer boxes with the same id — AGH1001 L5, AGH1009 L5 / L7), `1A, 1A, 1B` (ANZH301 L1) or `4A, 4B, 2A` (AGH1007 L4 — a journal-instruction box carrying the writer's stale digit) where the human ships `5A 5B`, `1A 1B 1C`, `4A 4B 4C`. MECHANISM: ContentConverter.#pageNumberNormalise, a page-level post-pass OUTERMOST in the body chain (after #cdTilePair and the dropbox / interactive post-passes): in document order, majority_digit — on a page with a lesson number a box whose digit differs from the page's MAJORITY digit (>= 2 boxes, a strict majority) takes the majority digit (a page with no lesson number is left alone: the phase panels own their digits); dedupe_letters — a (digit, letter) already used on the page, or a letter that is not a single A–Z, takes the next unused letter for that digit; a writer's gap letters stay. Never on a page carrying a decimal id (the KB 07B `1.1` family) or a bare-digit id (the single-page section form). A duplicate id can be an extra converter box as often as the writer's repeat (ENGJ102 L4: `4A 4B 4C 4C` where the first `4C` is an empty synthetic box), so on such pages the renumber can shift a box's number away from the human's; see _note_enabled. OFF (env NUMNORM_OFF) turns it off.
page_number_normalise._note_enabled: Enabled (fully consecutive everywhere): every lesson page's activity boxes are numbered in order, the KB's and the human build's convention. Pages where the human keeps a duplicate or stale id are a NAMED OVERRIDE of those pages' gold; a known side-effect: a writer's instruction that cites a number ('complete activity 4C') can point at a renumbered box. Env NUMNORM_OFF turns it off.
page_number_normalise._doc_page_digit_on_tie: KB c62 / c65, fully consecutive everywhere. majority_digit does nothing when no digit holds a strict majority, so a page would keep its writer's mixed digits — FRFUN06 2.0 `1A 3C 2C 4B 2E 2F` (human 2A–2E), 5.0 `1A 2A 5C 5D` (human 5A–5D), HIS1007 2.0 `2A 8B`. When the digits tie and the page's own lesson number ties for the most boxes, that number is the digit (the letter dedupe as before). XGF9001 2.0 is a known exception (its human build numbers 1A–1E on a 2.0 page). Env NUMTIE_OFF.

journal_instruction_box._doc:
THE JOURNAL INSTRUCTION IS ITS OWN ACTIVITY BOX. A block telling the learner to go to the journal and complete a named activity ('Go to your learning journal and complete 3A.', 'Complete activity 4A in your journal.') sits, in the human build, inside its OWN activity box numbered with that id (AGH, HES, PES, GEO, COM, CBI …), not only where the writer's own [Activity] tag puts one. Two parts. (1) bracket_sentence — the writer's red-bracket form `[Go to your learning journal and complete activity 2B]` (AGH) parses as an [Activity] OPENER, which would strip its ids into a garbled Writers Note ('…complete and' — a KB constraint-1 breach) and leave the box EMPTY or swallow the next section (AGH1002 2.0 'Soil Structure'). Right after the item stream is built (PageAssembler), such a span — an activity parse whose bracket is a journal SENTENCE (journal_pattern + verb_pattern + id_pattern, min_words..max_words, no other tag) — becomes the writer's black sentence, brackets stripped, words verbatim. (2) the page post-pass (ContentConverter, before #pageNumberNormalise): a FREE

(its column's own child, outside any activity / widget / alert) that is a journal instruction naming an id is wrapped in `div.activity[number=] > div.row > div.col-12`, together with an adjacent writer journal button (h4.goJournal or a.button — never invented); the row is split around it when the column holds other content; a row with a side column is left alone. The human's box heading is the developer's own (not in any Writers Template) — never invented. Env JOURNALINSTR_OFF turns off both (JOURNALBOX_OFF is the journal-SECTION box, a different rule).

skip_empty._doc: NO SYNTHETIC BOX AROUND A WIDGET THAT CAPTURED NOTHING. A task-type bundle whose invocation captured no content at all (a tag-only [drag and drop] / [radio quiz] / [interactive] whose title heading terminated the walk, an inline marker, a stray end tag) would otherwise render only the 'Un-built [type] marker — no content captured' red flag INSIDE a numbered activity box — a shape the human never ships, and one that also SPENDS a positional letter, so every later box on the page would be lettered one too far. With this on, saOn consults the placeholder's own content test (#bundleHasContent — headingText / instructions / tables / media / a member with words or embedded text) and a content-less bundle renders its flag alone in the section flow, consuming no letter. OFF (env SABOXEMPTY_OFF) turns it off.

inside_open_activity._doc: A SYNTHETIC WIDGET BOX NEVER OPENS INSIDE AN OPEN ACTIVITY BOX — the widget belongs to the open box. The synthetic box (saOwner) and the level-pages box (lvOwner) are decided AFTER the bundle site's isNewActivity guard, so a standalone task widget met while a writer's activity frame is still open (a bundle-owned box whose frame stayed open after its own widget, a plain writer box, a super-content box) would open its box INSIDE the open one; the human almost never nests activity boxes. Where the human does separate them it starts a sibling box (some Mathematics / English / FRFUN pages), while BLL's phonics multi-widget box keeps the widgets inside (KB CL-0030); keeping the widget inside the open box fits the human build best across every subject group. Rule: when the synthetic owner is about to open and the stack top is an activity, the synthetic box is SUPPRESSED and the widget renders inside the open box (the container_auto_close.activity_close_before keeps_inside rule); a subject listed in close_outer_subjects (the module index's subject; none listed) takes the other form — the outer closes first (the isNewActivity convention) and the widget becomes the next sibling box. Env NESTBOX_OFF allows the nested box.

standalone_widget_box._types_extra_note: box_types is an optional second type list (env SABOX367_OFF) and is deliberately EMPTY. dropDown and typing captures look boxed in the human build by a loose text match, but the converter's dropDown-typed captures are mostly the writer's `[drop down]` reveal / go-to / dropbox variants, which the human folds into the PRECEDING activity (ENGC202 lesson 1 keeps `The big reveal` inside box 1A), not dropQuiz widgets; there is no derivable discriminator between a `[drop down]` quiz and a `[drop down]` reveal. The KB c43 UPLOAD BOX (`[upload to dropbox]`, a dropDown-typed bundle through the lexicon's `dropbox` alias) always lives inside the preceding activity and never gets its own box, so the saOn branch excludes InteractiveBuilder.UploadBoxCandidate bundles.
standalone_widget_box._types_interactive_note: 'interactive' is the bare-[Interactive] generic invocation (Tag_Lexicon _meta.qualifier_alias_demote.standalone_becomes) — the scanner names the bundle after the tag, so it arrives here as type 'interactive', not 'unclassified'. The human boxes the bare-invocation class (as on AGH1001-01) and it is a task invocation by authoring intent.
standalone_widget_box._note_boundary: A TASK-type interactive the writer authored with NO [Activity] tag (AGH1001-01: '[Interactive] Drag and drop the products…' + data table) is STILL boxed by the human developer — an invented <div class="activity interactive" number="1B"> wrapping instruction + widget, numbered in the lesson's ordinary letter sequence (the human build has many more activity boxes than writer [Activity*] tags; whole families e.g. MXDI/HIS author with no [Activity] tags). The listed types are the ones the human boxes when standalone (dragAndDrop, unclassified, multiChoiceQuiz, radioQuiz, selfCheck, the bare interactive); the DISPLAY types (accordion / carousel / speechBubble / clickDrop / flipCard / tabs / modal / hintSlider / shapeHover / glossary / timeline) stay bare BY CONSTRUCTION (not listed); the ambiguous types (dropDown / selectionBox / typing / slider / reorder) need a finer discriminator and are not listed. The box takes the human's `activity interactive` form (force_interactive — the box exists BECAUSE of the widget) and the NEXT positional {lessonNumber}{letter} id (ActivitiesBuilder.activityOpen positionalId=true — the human counts its invented boxes IN SEQUENCE with the tagged ones, so the later letters on the page stay right). The human's own box TITLE heading is human-authored (in no WT) — never invented. reoMode excluded (bilingual bundles have reo_bundle_activity + their own placeholder surface). Matches on bundle.type ONLY (extraTypes-merged bundles fire via their primary type). Env toggle ACTWRAP_OFF renders the bare un-boxed placeholder/build.

prose_interactive_rows._note_rows: KB CL-0048/CL-0036 (constraint 63): inside an activity, prose sits in its OWN inner row and the interactive follows in a SEPARATE inner row at the wrapper width. The human build largely PREDATES the rule — prose+widget in ONE inner col is its dominant anatomy — so the rule is NOT applied universally (captured as overrides_gold in Subject_Global_Parameters._universal_conventions.cl0048_prose_interactive_rows; doc-14's Mode-B rule keeps gold/sibling structure authoritative for the built corpus). This registry holds the groups whose human build DOES consistently use the SEPARATED form, where the split matches the human; it is generated from the human build, never hand-typed. ENFUN|Fundamentals: the human form (ENFUN02 1D) is activity > row > col-12 [PROSE] /row + row > col-md-12 col-12 [WIDGET] /row. The prose col is NOT changed by this rule (the human's prose col for a DEFAULT-width col-md-8 wrapper is col-12, which the existing open already emits; the widened col-11/col-md-11 wrappers are not emitted — the CL-0007 widths are not applied). Fires ONLY when the activity-owned bundle emitted PROSE first (title/lead/table — the actProse flag): a widget-only box keeps the single-col form (the human's widget-only box is col-12). A box with prose AFTER the widget is rare — the split still applies and trailing prose lands in the widget row (the human sometimes uses a third row). Groups without a consistent separated form keep same_col BY CONSTRUCTION: ENGFUN|Inquiry (one module), PNR|Bilingual (the bilingual boundary rules), MXFL|Standard (its separated boxes ride wrapper widening, which is not emitted). ENFUN09 is the family's own deviant (mostly same_col in its human build); the family form is applied uniformly. Env toggle ACTROWS_OFF gives the single-col flow.

owned_activity_keeps_trailing_dropbox._note_hold: KB constraint 43, the dropbox modifier/placement class. A bundle-OWNED activity box closes at its widget's end, so a writer's dropbox marker placed AFTER the widget but still INSIDE the activity ([Activity 2D] … [clickdrop button] … [microphone, camera and video dropbox buttons] [End page] — XMES101) would escape into its own row UNDER the closed box: the marker is freed into its own dropDown bundle, the upload box builds the Upload-to-dropbox button, and the dropbox postpass (which marks `dropbox` only when the button sits INSIDE the box's own span) would not fire. The human keeps the button INSIDE the activity (BLL always). THE RULE: at the owner close site, walk forward from the bundle's opening item with the auto-close boundary semantics (scanSupNote's walk — skip the owner's own members, consumed items, blank lines; black text, tables and non-boundary tags are content; a stray non-activity CONTAINER_CLOSE is the widget's own end tag and is flagged so it cannot pop the held frame; a heading <= rendered_heading_max, an activity_close_before directive/tag, an activity closer, a page boundary, a section marker, or an item consumed by a DIFFERENT non-dropbox bundle ends the walk with NO hold); when the first foreign bundle reached is a freed upload-box bundle (InteractiveBuilder.UploadBoxCandidate — the upload box's own scan, public so scanner/builder/holder can never drift) with no activity of its own (canonTag/activityOwner/activityId all unset — the isNewActivity test), the activity frame is LEFT OPEN: the dropbox bundle then renders through the ordinary non-owner path inside the still-open box, autoClose (or the page-end drain) closes the box at the next boundary, and the dropbox postpass marks it `dropbox`. FENCES: the ENFUN prose|widget row split (prose_interactive_rows, pirKey) is excluded — its widget row is already closed at the site; the buttonD/BLL plain-box convention is untouched (the postpass's \bbutton\b test does not see buttonD — the BLL button moves inside the box, and the box stays plain as the human's BLL boxes are). max_lookahead mirrors #goJournalTail's 120. Env toggle ACTDBXINSIDE_OFF closes the box at the widget's end.

upload_box_ends_activity._seams_note: Three seams, one rule: (1) the freed upload-box BUNDLE at the inline site (XTAS101 1G — the held frame of owned_activity_keeps_trailing_dropbox); (2) the upload-box builder hands the text captured AFTER the marker back on the bundle (uploadAfterText) and the owner / inline emit sites ship it AFTER the box closes (BLL123 2E — the dropbox split is a precondition); (3) a plain [Button] whose label matches button_label_match inside an open activity frame (ENGR102 5B: '[Button] Upload to dropbox' then 'Watch the video…'); button_tag false turns seam 3 off on its own.
upload_box_ends_activity._note_ends_box: The human keeps the "Upload to dropbox" button as the activity box's LAST content child and ships whatever the writer typed after the dropbox marker with no [End activity] as FREE body rows (BLL123 2E's module-end 'Congratulations…' paragraph, XTAS101 1G's [body] + carousel, ENGR102 5B's video); without this the box would stay open to the next auto-close boundary. A few human boxes keep a tail (ENGJ403, ENGS201, XMES201 — named exceptions). Engine: at the inline (non-owner) widget site, a freed upload-box bundle (InteractiveBuilder.UploadBoxCandidate) closes the innermost activity frame right after it; a writer's own [End activity] met within max_lookahead items before the next activity opener / page boundary is flagged _dbxStrayCloser. OFF = the box closes at the next boundary.

activity_wrapper.interactive_widget_types_task_note: The SELECTION/INPUT/ORDERING task types (typing, selectionBox, dropDown, clickingOrder, crossword) are listed because the human marks activities owning them .interactive (dropDown about as often as selfCheck). The marker scan splits 'A + B' banners so every type in a multi-type marker is read (ENGS401-04 4A dropDown, ENGS401-05 5A carousel + typing). A PROSE-authored selection with no task TAG (ENGS401-01 1A: 'select the emotion that best matches how you feel', whose [modal] tags are only video pop-ups) has no tag to key off, so it stays plain; that would need a prose-selection classifier, not a blanket rule. DELIBERATELY NOT listed (the human keeps them PLAIN): modal, carousel, accordion, flipCard, clickDrop, tabs, slider, rotateBanner, speechBubble — a blanket 'any interactive -> .interactive' rule would contradict the human on thousands of boxes. Reversal: env ACTINT_OFF (the whole post-pass) or remove these entries.
activity_wrapper.interactive_widget_types_note: An activity that OWNS a widget of one of these types gets the .interactive class (the 'circle' task indicator; plain .activity is the 'triangle'). The widget TYPE is the WT signal: in the human build these types mostly carry .interactive when inside an activity (reorder, wordDrag, memoryGame, dropQuiz, radioQuiz, wordSelect, bingo, multiChoiceQuiz, dragAndDrop, selfCheck). DISPLAY widgets stay plain .activity (flipCard, carousel, accordion, clickDrop, speechBubble; typing and slider are borderline → excluded). A per-type rule, not a global 'force .interactive'.

strip_bold.note: The human strips writer **bold** landing in an ACTIVITY box's own body text (plain p/li black text) in the strong Fundamentals families (ARFUN / ENFUN / HPFUN / MXFUN / XFUN). Out of scope: TEFUN (genuinely mixed), SSFUN, SCFUN, and the non-Fundamentals templates; reo excluded via MenuBuilder.isReoModule (never mtkFlag). The bold the human keeps (ARFUN04's 'Instructions:'/'Goal:' leads + key vocab) has NO derivable discriminator (a colon lead does not separate them), so stripping is the better rule. REGION discriminator = the LIVE container stack: the mapper strips ONLY while the stack TOP is an open ACTIVITY (mode 'activity') — a span callout on top (the alert cell, which KEEPS bold in these subjects), strict callouts, kept tables, widgets, headings and media all emit via other paths/stack states and are untouched BY CONSTRUCTION. Applied at ConvertPage's main-loop black-text emit sites via #activityBoldStripper + MenuBuilder.stripTextBold. Env ACTBOLD_OFF keeps the writer's bold.

interactive_col_ceiling_note: The top-most col-* ceiling for EVERY interactive type in the human build is overwhelmingly 'col-12 col-md-8' — the body_region.content_col_class_default the converter emits (dragAndDrop mostly col-md-8, only occasionally col-md-12; even .images dragAndDrops and .interactive activities are mostly col-md-8). So a per-type WIDER ceiling (e.g. col-md-12 for dragAndDrop) is NOT supported by the human build and is NOT enforced — it would contradict the col-md-8 majority. ENGS301-1.0's col-md-12 is a NON-DERIVABLE minority (a per-instance layout choice); col-md-8 is the correct default.

mode_P.note: Mode P = visible placeholder + commented-out real reference (one of the only two permitted comment uses). The comment sits immediately after the visible placeholder.

filename_rules.label_rule: The Mode-P label is the media item number or 'image' — short, URL-safe.

istock_cdn_form._doc: THE iSTOCK IMAGE ADDRESS NAMES ITS ASSET. Writers often paste iStock's image-FILE address (https://media.istockphoto.com/id/537547686/photo/word-poetry-made-with-wooden-letters.jpg?…) rather than the asset PAGE address (…/photo/word-poetry-made-with-wooden-letters-gm537547686-…). Both carry the asset id and the title slug; the file form is rewritten to the page form so the image is named iStock-<id>.jpg (filename_rules.istock) and takes its slug title as alt, as the human build names it, instead of a generic «image» placeholder with an empty alt.

image.uniform_rule: The chosen mode applies to EVERY image in the conversion run — no mixing (brief §8.1).

video.host_note: youtube-nocookie.com is the dominant host in the human build (used more often than plain youtube.com).
video.timing_note: Writer timing notes (play from 0.18 to 5.30 …) render as red flags AT the embed — the visible note is the contract; translating to start/end params is optional and never replaces the note.

extension._doc: Series and subject|template groups mined from the human build after the base lists above, by the same rule (_note_registry: n >= 2 modules, pooled icon share >= 0.85, >= 8 human videos; a group only with no plain-majority series inside it). They join icon_series / icon_subject_template in the one group decision (MediaBuilder #videoIconGroup), so the per-embed form and the widget post-pass follow them alike. Env ICONEXT_OFF (or enabled:false) uses the base lists alone. CBI10 45/45, COM10 14/14, DAN10 42/46, DTC10 42/42, GEO10 26/27 human videos with the icon; the 1-10 Mathematics Fundamentals modules 54/56.

widget_embedded._doc: The icon rule also covers every video a WIDGET BUILDER emits (a carousel slide, an accordion / tab / clickDrop panel, the bilingual builder), which MediaBuilder.media does not see; in the icon-group modules the human puts icon on these widget-embedded videos too. MediaBuilder.videoIconPostpass(bodyHtml, run) — the last step of ContentConverter's final-body chain — adds the token to EVERY class="videoSection …" in the body that lacks it when the module is in an icon group (idempotent; one seam for every emitter). VIDEOICONWIDGET_OFF (or enabled:false) turns off the post-pass alone; VIDEOICON_OFF disables the whole rule.

icon_rule._note_registry: THE REGISTRY is mined from the human build: a series joins icon_series at n >= 2 modules AND an icon share >= 0.85 (each with >= 8 human videos). plain_series is the CARVE-OUT, consulted BEFORE the subject|template fallback: a series at n >= 2 and share <= 0.40 stays plain even inside an icon subject group (as PHE10 and HES10 inside NCEA1). NCEA1|Standard is NOT a subject group: its share is carried by HIS10 / PES10 (listed as series), and the only other series it would reach is AGH10, whose modules split icon / plain per module. Maths|Standard and ConnectED|Inquiry are not listed at subject level (too many wrong lines); their series (MXDI20, MXFU40, MXFL10) are ties and are left plain.
icon_rule._note_rule: The videoSection `icon` play-button styling. The human adds `icon` to a videoSection div as a per-SUBJECT/SERIES HOUSE STYLE, not a per-video choice: most video-carrying modules are internally PURE (all-icon or all-plain), and no per-video rule (first-video, in-carousel, in-activity, media-kind) predicts the mixed ones. The icon-vs-plain CHOICE is consistent (a SERIES with enough modules at a high icon share, else a SUBJECT|TEMPLATE group at a high share) ONLY in the listed groups; near-tie groups (1-10 Blended Literacy|Standard, 1-10 English|Standard, ConnectED|Inquiry) stay PLAIN (default). MediaBuilder.media post-replaces the class token `videoSection ` -> `videoSection icon ` (the videoHost-replace precedent) when the run's module (from Module_Structure_Index.module_meta) has its series in icon_series OR its subject|template in icon_subject_template. A few pure-plain modules inside an icon group (ANZH404, BLL171, BLL172, BLL174, EXPFUN06) get icon — the accepted cost of a group-level rule. Widget-embedded videos are covered by widget_embedded. env VIDEOICON_OFF (or enabled:false) renders all-plain.

audio.note: Corpus form. The developer drops the real file into audio/ — a missing filename stays empty exactly as the corpus does, plus the writer's sourcing note as a red flag.

label_trailing_stop._doc: KB row 55. A writer types the button label as a sentence — '[button] Learning journal.', '[button] Upload to dropbox.', '[button] Check answers.' — and the full stop would ride into the label. The KB's canonical labels (constraint 55 'Go to dropbox' / 'Go to portfolio', 14.11 'Upload to Dropbox', constraint 75 'Go to website', CL-0038 'Go to quiz') carry no terminal punctuation, and the human build's buttons almost never end in a full stop. ONE trailing full stop is stripped from the label at the generic [button]-family emit (the only seam that fills a writer's label into a button form); an ellipsis and an abbreviation (e.g. / i.e. / etc.) keep theirs; '?' '!' ':' are never touched (the human keeps them). Env BTNSTOP_OFF turns it off.

label_bracket_clean._doc: THE BRACKET FRAGMENT IN A BUTTON LABEL — KB constraint 5 (no literal tag / writer note in the output). A writer's bracket fragment can reach a button label (as in ANZH301): a split tag's tail ('Add button] Download journal', 'Button] [Download Journal', 'insert button] Download file ['), a writer note ('Upload to dropbox  [trigger engagement]', 'Lesson 5: Beyond the Basics [Not applicable]'), an unclosed note ('Download journal button] [Media item 31 -'), an orphan bracket ('Go back to [', 'go to quiz]', '] Video Mode'). The human labels are clean ('Download journal', 'Go to quiz', 'Video Mode', 'Upload to dropbox'). Complete bracket notes go (a short caps token like a video title's '[HD]' stays — keep_pattern); the text after a split tag's '…]' wins when it has letters, else the text before it without the button words (button_words_pattern); an unclosed trailing note (note_pattern) goes; any other stray bracket character goes; nothing left = the label unchanged. Text-only. Env BTNBRACKET_OFF.

canonical_labels._doc: KB constraint 55's LABEL half + CL-0038 / constraint 65 + 14.11 / 14D. A submission button keeps its full 'Go to' label: the writer's bare noun — `[Button] Portfolio`, `[Add button] Quiz button`, `[Add button] Quiz`, `[Button] Dropbox` — is the label the KB says never ships bare ('the leading Go to is never dropped to a bare Dropbox / Portfolio'; the quiz button reads 'Go to quiz'), and the human ships 'Go to quiz' / 'Go to portfolio'. The first rule whose label_match hits the resolved, trimmed label supplies the canonical label; a rule's family_labels row wins for a module whose code prefix is listed (14.11: the BLL / LS / HPE families label the dropbox button 'Upload to Dropbox'). A bare 'journal' label has no KB label rule and is untouched. Applied at the generic [button] seam after the trailing-stop trim and before the anchor wrap, so the anchor's quiz href and To Do wording key on the canonical label. Env BTNLABEL_OFF turns it off.

anchor_wrap._doc:
A call-to-action button is an ANCHOR: the KB's universal button form (05D_COMP14_BUTTONS_TABLES_COLUMNS — `
…
`; constraint 65's `href="#"` quiz button) and the human build (nearly every non-JS div.button/div.buttonD, in every template and subject) both put the button inside `` even where the developer has not wired the target yet (`href=""`/`#`). At the generic [button] seam (key === 'button' — never the engagement / supervisor / audio forms, never a widget builder's own JS button) a bare form (one that does not itself start with an anchor) is wrapped in `form` and followed by ONE Designer/Developer To Do note (cv2-note — the upload-box pattern) naming what to wire: the first `targets` row whose label_match hits the resolved label, else `default`. The href stays blank on purpose: the per-module D2L rcode / journal document / link target is in no Writers Template. Env BTNANCHOR_OFF turns it off.
anchor_wrap._doc_href: A [button] that DOES carry a URL (the writer's Word hyperlink on the label — parsed `[LINK: …]` — or a URL typed in the tag) takes button_linked.form with that URL, so the hyperlink is never lost (SSOG101 6 'How Can I Help Activity' → the human anchors the docs.google URL); the following-paragraph absorb is the other route to it. With a URL the anchor carries it and NO note is added; without one the target row's `href` (default ""; the quiz row uses constraint 65's "#") and the To Do note ship.
anchor_wrap.todo_note: Wire this button's {what} (the href is intentionally blank — {why}).
anchor_wrap._doc_exclude:
A writer's REVEAL-type [button] ('Check answers', 'Reset', 'Check answer and reset buttons', 'Reveal answer') is not a link: the human ships those as its JS reveal button `
…
` and never anchors a label of this kind, so the seam leaves them bare (without the exclusion they would gain a spurious anchor + note).

targets.why: the per-module rcode is in no Writers Template
the per-module portfolio location is in no Writers Template
the quiz's rcode is in no Writers Template

targets.what: link to the module's learning journal document
targets.why: the journal's location is in no Writers Template

targets.what: link to the file this button downloads
targets.why: the file's location is in no Writers Template

default.why: no URL was given in the Writers Template

external_destination._doc:
AN EXTERNAL DESTINATION IS THE KB'S externalButton. KB 05D 'Buttons' gives two forms — Internal `
…
` and External `
` — and the human follows it BY HOST: relative paths, `#`, drive.google.com, docs.google.com, desire2learn and the vimeo player are `button`; every outside website (youtube, youtu.be, earth.google, sparklers, teara, nzhistory, natlib …) is `externalButton`, across every template and subject family. At the plain-[button] seam only (key === 'button'), a button that carries an http(s) URL whose host is NOT in internal_hosts (exact host or a sub-domain of a listed entry) and whose resolved form is the plain `div.button` (never buttonD / downloadButton / the reveal JS buttons / an already-external form) ships `form` instead. THE LABEL HALF (constraint 75's table: 'a bare URL with no accompanying words → Go to website'): a URL-only `[Button: https://…]` / `[Button – External Link] https://…` has no writer label and would fall to journal_label_default ('Go to your journal'); the human's own labels are the resource names (TWHA905 'Go to Kiwiharvest', AGH1007 'The Amazing Cow…', ENFUN02 'Thoughtful Learning' — editorial, not derivable), so a DEFAULTED label becomes default_label, or video_label when the URL matches video_host_match (the external-link-button defaults). A writer-supplied label is never touched. NAMED exceptions: the human's `button`s on external hosts (ANZH404's 'Source A/B/C' evidence buttons, MXFL401, XGF9006 …). Env EXTDEST_OFF turns it off (class and label).
external_destination._doc_internal_hosts: Te Kura's own systems and hosted files — the LMS (desire2learn), the school's SharePoint, Google Drive / Docs / Forms (journals, worksheets, quizzes), and the vimeo player the gold treats as an embed link (6:0). www.tekura.school.nz is deliberately NOT listed: the gold ships the school's public website as externalButton 3:0. A host matches when it equals an entry or ends with '.' + entry.

video_destination._doc: A [button] WHOSE DESTINATION IS A VIDEO IS THE EMBEDDED VIDEO, NOT A LINK BUTTON. The writer's '[Button] Play video' + '[video link] URL', '[Button: youtube-url]', and the instruction brackets the normaliser reads as a button ('[embed video with image and play button]' + a bare URL line) would otherwise become an anchored button ('Go to video'); the human EMBEDS the video (only a few link buttons remain, e.g. TWHK903's iOS / Android tutorial links). The KB is silent on a button that names a video (01E's [video] → videoSection is the nearest rule; 05D's buttons are LINKS), so the human build's consensus decides (§1b level 3/4). At the plain-[button] seam only (key === 'button'; a released tile-grid lead is excluded — it keeps its own form): (A) an own URL matching host_match → MediaBuilder.media(it, …, 'video') — the standard [video] embed (host + icon conventions included; the title-drop rule drops the short label); (B) the next unconsumed item is a next_tag_families TAG carrying a video-host URL → the button renders nothing and is NOT absorbed — the video item renders itself; (C) the next unconsumed item is a bare video-host URL line → MediaBuilder.media on the button item (the gather takes the URL line). A label longer than label_max_words renders as body text before the embed (a writer's sentence is never silently stripped). Env VIDBTN_OFF turns it off.
video_destination._doc_host_match: A VIDEO url, not merely a video host: a youtube watch / shorts / embed link, a youtu.be short link, or a numbered vimeo link. A channel or user page (youtube.com/user/…) is a website — XLP05's '[button] Link' to a yoga channel stays an externalButton.
video_destination._doc_play_label_match: A label that IS the embed's play button ('Play', 'Play video', 'Watch the video', 'Go to video') — or no label at all — renders nothing beside the embed. Any other writer label keeps its own button: '[add button] Go to journal' followed by a '[video link]' item stays the journal button (no video URL absorbed) and the video embeds itself.

absorb_following_url._note_absorb:
A plain [Button] (e.g. 'Go to journal') whose URL sits on the IMMEDIATELY-FOLLOWING standalone bare-URL paragraph is the human's LINKED button — the URL is loaded onto the button as its href and the bare-URL

is dropped (human '

Download journal
'; ENGI302/ENGJ202/SSOG301/MXDI301). #element button branch: when key==='button', the button has NO url of its own, and bodyItems[i+1] is a STANDALONE bare URL (whole content is one http(s) URL, not a tag/element, not consumed), it is absorbed as the href (buttons.button_linked.form) and marked _consumed (the loop's consumed-item skip drops it). The href VALUE is the WT URL (the human re-points to a fresh copy-doc / generic Drive link — non-derivable editorial); the STRUCTURE + label match. Tight: only the bare-URL-alone next item (same discriminator as external_link_button_standalone), never prose; skipped when the dropbox-orange override fires. Env BTNURL_OFF renders the un-linked button + a separate bare-URL

.

button_download._note_download:
A [button] whose RAW in-bracket text contains 'download' (e.g. '[Download learning journal button]', as in ENGS302-01) is the human's DOWNLOAD button —
{label}
(orange), NOT a plain
'Go to your journal'
. The label is the writer's in-bracket descriptive text with the trailing 'button(s)' word stripped ('Download learning journal'). SCOPED to an explicit 'download' in the tag text: most human downloadButtons ('Download journal', 'Response sheet', 'Explore an artwork') come from a BARE [Button]/[Add button] where the label + class are the developer's editorial choice (NON-derivable); a downloadButton usually sits in a PLAIN activity, so the parent 'dropbox' class is not triggered by it. Env DLBTN_OFF.

external link button._note_external:
The human's external-link button is
LABEL
 (class externalButton, NOT button), as in OSAI201-02. The writer often drops the marker INLINE in a body sentence ('Click here to play Quick Draw [external link button] https://… then come back and do the activity.'), so the text AFTER the URL is running prose, not the button label. ContentConverter.#element: for an external link button it extracts the URL, uses a SHORT (<=label_max_words, no end-punctuation) trailing phrase as the label else a derivable DEFAULT ('Go to website', or 'Go to video' for a video URL — the human's two dominant defaults), and RE-EMITS the remaining trailing prose as body so it is neither lost nor mislabelled. (The exact editorial label e.g. 'Quick, Draw!' is the game's proper name — not derivable from the WT; the default is the safe convention.)

kb_form.label: Go to quiz
kb_form.todo_note: Wire this engagement quiz's D2L quicklink (the href is intentionally blank). Writer's quiz source: {url}{text}
kb_form._doc:
THE ENGAGEMENT QUIZ BUTTON IS THE KB'S EXTERNAL QUIZ LINK BUTTON. The writer's [Engagement quiz button] (the OS family + ARFUN01/02 + HPFUN401) would otherwise ship the legacy `form` above — a bare div with a class the human never uses, no anchor, and a label that falls to the journal default (`Go to your journal`) or the quiz document's FILENAME. KB 01F `engagement_quiz_button` → "External quiz link button" (the `button` form `
`); constraint 65 / CL-0038 fix the quiz button's label `Go to quiz` and its blank publish-time href. The human ships `
Go to quiz
` (the D2L rcode is publish-time wiring — the CL-0044 class). MECHANISM: at the button seam, right after the trigger-marker test, an `engagement quiz button` item ships `form` with `href` + `label` and ONE Designer/Developer To Do note (cv2-note) carrying the writer's link and any other words of the tail. Env ENGQUIZ_OFF gives the legacy div.

trigger_marker._doc:
The writer's `[trigger engagement]` / `[engagement trigger]` / `[to trigger engagement]` is a CONDITION MARKER, not a button: the KB reads it as the dropbox-trigger signal on the activity (constraint 43, 05B, 01F) and the human build carries no engagement markup at all. The Tag_Lexicon folds those aliases into `engagement quiz button` (the KB's `engagement_quiz_button` = the real external quiz link button, `[engagement quiz button]`), so without this the generic seam would ship a PHANTOM `
Go to your journal
` (the label-less tag falling to journal_label_default). An `engagement quiz button` item whose bracket text ENDS in one of `aliases` and carries no black text emits nothing (the same reading of the marker as elsewhere); a bracket carrying other words (`[insert text box for student response – engagement trigger]`) surfaces them as ONE diagnostic red flag (cv2-note) so nothing the writer wrote is lost. `[engagement quiz button]` itself is untouched. Env ENGMARKER_OFF turns it off.
trigger_marker.words_flag: Writer's engagement-trigger marker carried extra words: {bracket}

kb_form._doc: KB 01F's tag table: `audio_button` → `<div class="audioButton" audioName="">` (05A 'Audio Button (compact)' the same); the human's audioButton is always text-less. So a free-body [audio button] ships that div — no `button` class (the green-button style), no visible label; `audioName` stays empty (the recording's file name is not in the Writers Template — the developer names it). The writer's own label words (`Tell audio`, `/ j /`, `need audio here`, `Audiovisual Request Template FUN06 Pronunciation.docx`) and a hyperlink the writer put on the tag are recording descriptors / instructions for the developer: they ride along as ONE red Writers Note right after the div (`note`, kind `note_kind`); a bare tag ships the div alone. Env AUDIOBTNKB_OFF uses `form` (`div.button.audioButton` + the label).

audio button._label_default_note:
A bare [audio button] with no writer label ships an EMPTY label, never the journal default — the human's audioButton is always text-less (`
`; the audioName is not derivable). This matters for hyperlinked tags too (BLL140/150/160/170). Remove the key to fall back to buttons.journal_label_default.

dropbox_orange_house_style._note_house_style: The human renders a dropbox button as ORANGE <div class="buttonD"> in some modules and GREEN <div class="button"> in others. It is NOT a per-button call-to-action rule: the SAME label 'Upload to dropbox' is often green AND often orange. The colour is a PER-MODULE HOUSE STYLE (almost always one colour per module) that tracks the module CODE PREFIX (subject family): Blended Literacy (BLL) = orange (other subjects AGH/ANZH/CED/ENG/MX/... = green). buttonD is used ONLY for dropbox text, so the rule fires ONLY when BOTH hold: the resolved plain [button] label matches label_match ('dropbox', case-insensitive) AND the module-code prefix is in module_prefixes. Engine: ContentConverter.#element button branch swaps button.form -> button_dropbox.form. Applied to all BLL modules (a few BLL modules the human kept green or mixed — BLL171/240, BLL246/252/254 — get orange). The <a href=...rcode=TCS-NNNNNN> dropbox link wrapper is a per-module D2L id absent from the WT+Media List (non-derivable) — only the COLOUR is matched. Env DROPBOXD_OFF makes every dropbox button green.

journal_default_guard._doc: A bracket the normaliser keys as `button` whose words are a writer INSTRUCTION ('[Please embed the video with a play button and image]', '[Check button] [Reset button]', '[Insert links/buttons to the 2 tiles as per the following]') gets no label and would fall to journal_label_default: a blank-href 'Go to your journal' button + a To Do to wire it — a journal button the writer never asked for (a journal button is never invented). Enabled: at the button seam — after the journal forms and the download rule, before the external-destination step — when the label is still journal_label_default, there is no URL, and the bracket's words (brackets and * removed) match neither bare_match (a bare button tag: '[Button]', '[Add button]', '[Button link]', '[Blue button]' — the writer asked for a button; the default stays, as AGH1003's human build ships 'Go to journal' there) nor keep_match (a journal request) — bare_match is a PREFIX: a bracket that OPENS as a button request ('[Button - click here - link to come]', '[Insert button to website]', '[Create check button]') keeps the button (as PHE1003's human build does), only a sentence that mentions a button further in is an instruction — the writer's words ship as their Writers Note (NotesAndComments.redFlag kind 'cs', the form every other instruction bracket takes) and no button is emitted. env JDEFGUARD_OFF.

go_journal.label: Go to your journal

journal_variants._doc:
Standardise the journal buttons the writer asked for; never invent one. label_match / raw_match catch only a label that folds to exactly 'go to (your|the) journal'. The writer also types 'Learning journal.', 'Go to learning journal.', '[Button – go to learning journal]', '[Button for Journal]', '[insert go to journal button]', '[Button] [Go to journal]', a label split over the red-text seam ('[button] Go to' + 'journal', '[button] G' + 'o to journal'), and whole instructions ('Complete activity 3A in your learning journal.', 'Journal. Complete Activity 4E Reflection.', '[Button] Journal' + 'Go to your journal and complete activity 4a.'). Every such button ships go_journal's own

Go to your journal

; a sentence label keeps its sentence as a

BEFORE the heading (the human's order: AGH1005 '

Complete activity 3A in your learning journal.

' then the journal element), with a leading label stripped ('Journal. ' / 'Go to journal. ' — sentence_lead). Guards: never with a URL (a linked button keeps its link); download / upload / dropbox / .docx labels excluded (their own buttons); a black tail after a non-journal in-tag label belongs to a later tag and is never folded in. Engine: Utils.GoJournalVariant, called for FREE buttons only — ContentConverter's button branch and the walk of #goJournalTail (a button after a widget, still inside its activity box). The bundle side (InteractiveScanner.#isGoJournalButton's section break, #goJournalTail's member branch, InteractiveBuilder's member skips) deliberately keeps go_journal's exact patterns: widening the scanner's test would change which items a speech bubble keeps (TEDC401 bubbles would fall back to hand-off boxes), so a variant button is released from a bundle exactly as the exact form is and rendered by the button branch. The human build is era-mixed (green button or h4); the green-button pages are a NAMED OVERRIDE (the h4 form is the current convention). KB constraint 1 ('never modify writer wording') is overridden for these button labels only; the sentence is never lost. A journal element is never added where the writer typed no [Button]. Env JOURNALVAR_OFF uses go_journal's exact match only.

go_journal._doc_member_branch_yields_to_builder: The other end of the accordion's go-to-journal contract (interactive_builders.accordion.panel_delimiters.go_journal_member). #goJournalTail's MEMBER branch ships this heading for any bundle whose member walk captured a go-to-journal [button]; the accordion BUILDER skips that member as panel content and emits the heading itself after the widget, so for a bundle that built, the member branch would emit a second identical heading. When the builder has emitted one it sets bundle._goJournalEmitted and this flag makes the member branch stand down — 'emit exactly once, wherever the item is reached'. A bundle that did NOT build never sets the flag, so every hand-off box is unaffected. Env ACCGOJOURNAL_OFF turns off the builder side and with it this one, since the flag is then never set.
go_journal._doc_absorb_suppresses_own_render: NO DOUBLE EMIT. absorb_into_activity pulls a go-to-journal [button] that sits after a bundle-owned activity's widget INSIDE the still-open box and marks the item _consumed — but the main loop has no general _consumed guard for a TAG item, only the positional 'skip the items immediately after me' idiom, which cannot reach this button because the widget's own unconsumed end tag ([end click and drop]) sits in between. Without this the button would also render on its own turn, giving a SECOND identical h4 in a bare row underneath the closed box (as in SCCH302_3_0, CEDO102_0_0, ENGC102_3_0). With this flag on, the absorb additionally marks the item _goJournalAbsorbed and the main loop skips it outright (skipping the ITEM, not just its emission, so no empty row/col is left behind). Every other go-journal site is untouched BY CONSTRUCTION (the flag only ever fires on an item this absorb itself claimed). Env GOJOURNALDUP_OFF allows the duplicate; GOJOURNAL_OFF turns off the whole go_journal rule.
go_journal._doc:
A [button] whose EXPLICIT label folds to 'go to (your) journal' (or the alias-typed [go to journal]/[journal button] span — raw_match is anchored to the WHOLE folded span so a longer prose span can never false-fire; an alias span's real trailing prose is kept as body text after the heading, never stripped) ships the design team's templated

Go to your journal

INSIDE the open activity box, never a green
(as in SCCH302-03 activity 3D). The human build is ERA-MIXED (h4.goJournal and
Go to journal, mixed within most subjects, no group discriminator); the design team names the h4 as its CURRENT convention, so this is a FORWARD-LOOKING overrides-gold rule (captured in Subject_Global_Parameters._universal_conventions.go_journal_h4; pages where the human used the button are intentional named deltas). A button that carries/absorbs a URL keeps the button behaviour (the h4 has no href); an EMPTY [button] whose label came only from journal_label_default is NOT retagged (bare buttons are also the source of the human's editorial downloadButtons). absorb_into_activity: a go-to-journal button sitting directly after a bundle-owned activity's widget is pulled INSIDE the still-open box before it closes (the mtkQuizBundleTail placement class). Env GOJOURNAL_OFF gives the plain green button.

download_journal.scaffold: Download journal
download_journal.note: The module journal document still needs to be created — the Download journal button on this page links to docs/{code} Journal.docx.
download_journal._doc: The writer's [button to download journal with standard instructions] (as in SCCH302-02 activity 2B) ships the design team's templated download scaffold byte-verbatim from the developer's specification: the docs/{CODE} Journal.docx anchor + downloadButton + the empty hint + hintDropContent(oneDrive) divs, plus ONE red+bold Designer/Developer To Do note that the journal document itself must be created. The writer's own label text is consumed (it IS the button's label, replaced by the templated 'Download journal'). The discriminator (download+journal+standard instructions, or the 'button to download journal' head) deliberately EXCLUDES the other download-journal bracket forms ([download journal], ENGS302's [Download learning journal button] etc), which keep their own routes (button_download among them). Env DLJOURNAL_OFF uses the button_download route (raw bracket text as the label).

external_button._doc:
AN [embed] OF AN EXTERNAL WEB PAGE IS THE KB'S externalButton, NEVER A BARE IFRAME. The [embed link] / [link to PDF of: …] / [Embed audio] / [Please embed these slides …] route would wrap any non-video URL in `div.ratio.ratio-16x9 > iframe`, a form the human never uses for these: it either drops the URL (kindergartenworksheets / twinkl / tahurangi worksheet and PDF pages the developer re-sourced or dropped) or keeps it as a LINK (a button / externalButton or a plain ). KB 05D: an external destination is `
Go to website
` (constraint 75's default label) — the buttons.external_destination form, label and internal-host list, reused here; a URL on an internal host (Google Docs / Drive / SharePoint, whose embed genuinely frames) keeps the iframe; a video host never reaches this branch (it takes the videoSection above). OFF (env EMBEDBTN_OFF) = the bare iframe.

unbundled_marker._doc: An INTERACTIVE-class tag that reaches the converter unbundled (the ANZH / HIS writers' `[Interactive] Please present the following profiles … as flip-cards…` request tag) would ship only the diagnostic `Interactive [interactive] reached the converter unbundled — … report this case.`, and the writer's words would reach no output. A request with ≥ min_words words joins the widget it introduces — the next bundle within `lookahead` items, past plain black lines only (ANZH203 6.0: its flip-card hand-off entry, or a note after it once built) — else it ships as the Writers Note in the diagnostic's place. A bare marker keeps the diagnostic.

capture_free_request._doc: The hand-off file is the channel for the writer's widget requests, and it is made complete. A widget capture's tag items (opener or member) carry the writer's red free text outside their brackets — `[Interactive] Please create a Venn diagram as shown above.`, `[interactive tool] flip cards – image of pumpkin on top – flip with information on other side.` The raw hand-off entry lists only the MEMBER source blocks, so without this an opener's words would never reach <CODE>_interactives.txt, and a BUILT widget (no entry) would drop them. ContentConverter.#captureFree takes each tag item with ≥ min_words words outside its brackets (URLs removed; instruction fragments — already notes — skip_tag_words and the template placeholders skipped): an UN-BUILT widget's entry (ManifestBuilder, raw and faithful modes) leads its Content with each one its lines do not already carry; a BUILT widget shows each one its output does not carry as a red Writers Note AFTER the widget. Env CAPFREEREQ_OFF.

answer_key._doc_mark_kinds: Only a YELLOW highlight gets the glyph — exactly what the parser ticks (js/formatter.js prefixes a run with ✅ when its highlight is 'yellow'); the extractor records each highlight mark's colour for this (Input_Doc_Rules.answer_marks.occurrence_index, side-channel only). Another colour stays unticked (PWY1001's partly-highlighted 'Shows' is not yellow and the parser never ticks it). The answer-GREEN kind is left unmarked: green can mark the OPTIONS themselves (as on OSAI101), so a tick there would tell the developer the wrong answer.
answer_key._doc: The hand-off box and {CODE}_interactives.txt KEEP the answer marks. In an UN-BUILT hand-off box of a quiz-engine type (types) and in that bundle's {CODE}_interactives.txt entry: (1) the writer's answer marks — the yellow highlighter / answer-green the extractor carries on the answer-mark side-channel (block.marks, block.cellMarks) — get the parser's own correct-answer glyph BEFORE the marked phrase (the _parsed.txt convention, '✅b. When two things are very different from each other.'), placed by the mark's occurrence index (Input_Doc_Rules.answer_marks.occurrence_index — ARFUN04 3N has 'Contrast' twice on one line); (2) the red answer words the writer typed inside the question (BLL244 2D 'What game are Zack and Kev playing…', True / False, 'B) Allan') — red members the classifier calls 'noise', which the box would otherwise drop (rendering only their black tail, or nothing) — are rendered with the glyph before them; a red fragment with no letter or digit (red_answer_skip — a stray ']') is skipped, and a label / media note (red_answer_plain — 'Answers:', '(image)', 'Associated media') is rendered plain. The worklist already shows the red words (it prints the whole source paragraph); it gains the glyph on both. Built widgets (the dropDown builds, the built multiChoiceQuiz) are untouched — this is the hand-off only. Env ANSWERKEY_OFF turns off the box, the worklist and the extractor's occurrence index together.

embedded_member_text._note: A tag member whose words ride its OWN bracket line ('[audio] while, whale, whirl, whole, whine', '[image] angry person', '[button] Go to journal') is CONTENT for the un-built hand-off box: the empty-bundle / empty-box guards count it and the member dump renders the raw bracket line, so such boxes are never suppressed with the words lost from the page (as in BLL150 / BLL166 audio word lists, ENGC101 4.0's five [image] faces). Only members whose primary directive is listed here (content ELEMENTs and INLINE links — never an INTERACTIVE invocation, whose bracket text is its own spec and lives in the .txt) and whose span is a TAG (an instruction-class member already surfaces as the note before the box). Env MEMBERTEXT_OFF turns off both guards and the dump.

interactive_placeholder._instructions_before_note: A writer instruction EMBEDDED inside an un-built interactive moves to JUST BEFORE the dashed box rather than rendering nested in the middle of it (as with OSAI201-01 1B's sketcher CS notes). Set false (or env NOTEBEFORE_OFF) to place it inside the box. Notes already AFTER an element are left where they are.
interactive_placeholder.block_open: <div class="cv2-interactive" data-cv2-index="{index}" style="border: 3px dashed #d9480f; background: #fff4e6; padding: 16px; margin: 16px 0">
interactive_placeholder.block_open_scroll: <div class="cv2-interactive" data-cv2-index="{index}" style="border: 3px dashed #d9480f; background: #fff4e6; padding: 16px; margin: 16px 0; overflow-x: auto">

scroll_x._note: The inline-mode un-built box has overflow-x: auto, so a wide raw member dump (multi-column tables especially) scrolls horizontally INSIDE the dashed frame instead of overflowing/breaking the page layout; the scrollbar appears exactly and only when content overflows the width. The scrollbar lives on the OUTER box (block_open_scroll), NOT member_dump_open — the dump div has no border, so scrolling the outer box keeps the dashed frame fixed while the content scrolls within it. Env INTSCROLLX_OFF (or enabled:false) uses block_open.
