interactive_placeholder.block_banner: ⚙ INTERACTIVE (un-built) #{index}: {type}{modifierLabel} — Activity {activityId} — see {manifestFile}
interactive_placeholder.inline_form: ⚙ {type} #{index}: {payload}
rules: The container is deliberately NOT an MTK style — visually and structurally distinct, easy to find (class cv2-interactive, data-cv2-index pairs it with its manifest entry).

Inside: the activity heading, the readable dump of captured members (tables as real , free text as

), writer instructions as red flags.
NEVER any comment that hints at correct answers. Answer-carrying members appear only as captured visible data awaiting development — placeholders never ship live.
Inline interactives (info trigger, hover definition …) use inline_form woven into the paragraph so the sentence still reads.

manifest_unbuilt_only._note: {CODE}_interactives.txt is the HAND-OFF WORKLIST: an interactive the converter already BUILT into the generated HTML is not work, so its entry is OMITTED and the per-entry list numbers over the un-built only. The summary header KEEPS both counts (useful telemetry) with its NOTE lines worded to match; the per-entry 'Status:' line is DROPPED when this is on (every listed entry is un-built by construction). Env MANIFESTALL_OFF (or enabled:false) lists every entry.

manifest_faithful_content._note: The 'Content:' block of {CODE}_interactives.txt must reproduce the writer's authored lines EXACTLY, so the developer knows precisely what belongs in the widget. Each member's blackAfter alone would DROP the red-highlighted words (the very adjectives the activity teaches — 'big, blue'/'stripey'/'cold'/'curious'/'excited', ENGC101-02) and STRIP the bracketed [Speech bubble] tags, leaving gap-riddled fragments ('There are two'/'fish and lots of'/'fish.'). ON: ManifestBuilder renders Content from the members' UNIQUE SOURCE BLOCKS (deduped, reading order), cleaning ONLY the 🔴[RED TEXT] sentinels + ** markers via #clean — so brackets + red words + full sentences survive. The txt is a developer-only working file (never ships). Env MANIFESTFAITHFUL_OFF (or enabled:false) uses the blackAfter capture. When manifest_raw_verbatim below is ON, the raw renderer replaces this entry body; this is the fallback when raw is OFF.

manifest_raw_verbatim._note: For the UN-BUILT interactives, {CODE}_interactives.txt carries the RAW parsed content VERBATIM, so the developer building the widget by hand sees exactly what the writer authored, unprocessed (the faithful mode still cleans sentinels / ** / whitespace and renders tables in a separate 'Data' section). ON: each un-built entry keeps only its MINIMAL header (INTERACTIVE N of M, the extract REFERENCE CODE + hint when in extract mode, File, Placeholder marker, Activity, Type) and then a single 'Content:' block that walks the member SOURCE BLOCKS in reading order (deduped by block identity) and prints each block's raw text EXACTLY — sentinels, [tags], ** and all — with a captured TABLE rendered INLINE at its position as the ┌─── TABLE ───/│ cell ║ cell/└─── END TABLE ─── ASCII box (which is literally the table block's own raw serialised text). The Modifier / Tier / Data Pattern / Position / Activity Heading / Writer Instructions / Associated Media / Red Flags sections are DROPPED from the raw un-built entry (type + anchor + raw content only). BUILT entries are already omitted by manifest_unbuilt_only, so this only affects the hand-off worklist. The txt is a developer-only working file (never ships). Env MANIFESTRAW_OFF (or enabled:false) uses the faithful/processed form.

handoff_tables.manifest_heading: UN-BUILT BILINGUAL TABLES — {count} (the writer's table is kept raw in its hand-off box on the page; no widget tag captured it, so it is not among the interactives above)
handoff_tables._doc: The hand-off file is the developer's channel and lists every box left to build. A bilingual-section table the converter cannot unfold or build (a word bank, an audio-item list, a section bundle kept raw, the widget a content table names inline) is shown in a `cv2-interactive bilingual-unbuilt` box; each such box carries a reference code (data-cv2-ref, ref_template: the module code, the page's document-order index, T + a module-wide count) and gets its own entry after the interactives in {CODE}_interactives.txt — the page file, the reference, the kind, and the table's rows in the corpus form with the writer's link addresses written in. The box's visible content is unchanged; the Page Stitcher reads only cv2-int-ref markers. Env HANDOFFTABLE_OFF.

manifest_link_targets._note: THE WRITER'S HYPERLINKS IN THE HAND-OFF. A captured block's raw text carries each hyperlink's visible words but not its address — the extractor keeps the addresses in block.links, one entry per Word run. The raw Content writes every link in the content-source form of KB 01C (`__link text__ [LINK: https://…]`), so the developer building the widget has each video, picture source and web page the writer linked. The runs of one link (the same address, separated only by whitespace or * / _ markers) are one span; a link whose words are themselves a web address is already visible and is left as it is (KB 01C: a bare URL is a media reference); a link whose words cannot be found in the block is written on its own line after the block (unplaced_form), so no address is lost. Applies to the raw-verbatim Content only (manifest_raw_verbatim). Env HANDOFFLINK_OFF (or enabled:false) gives the words alone.
manifest_link_targets._page_note: THE HAND-OFF TABLE KEEPS ITS LINKS. A table dumped raw into a hand-off box on the page (an un-built widget's table, the Bilingual builder's unbuilt rows — which have no worklist entry, so the box is the developer's only copy) writes each of the writer's hyperlinks after its own words in the cell that holds them, as page_form — the image, audio or document the writer linked («[Item 23][Audio] i haere ahau ki te whare … [LINK: …sharepoint…]») stays with the developer instead of being dropped. A link whose words are themselves an address stays as it is; one whose words are in no cell is skipped. The free body is untouched (it weaves its own links). Env page_env.

extract._note: The INTERACTIVE HAND-OFF mode. When ConversionRun.interactiveMode === 'extract' (uniform across the whole run like imageMode), an UN-BUILT interactive is NOT rendered on the page: the dashed box above is replaced by a unique REFERENCE CODE marking its exact spot, and the captured content is handed off via {CODE}_interactives.txt (ManifestBuilder) headed by the SAME code. interactiveMode 'inline' never reads this block. SCOPE: un-built placeholder interactives only — built widgets stay rendered; the bilingual-unbuilt content-table placeholders are not extracted. See default_mode for the run default; set enabled:false here to turn the mode off.
extract._default_mode_note: The hand-off is the DEFAULT for every run: both entries resolve interactiveMode from THIS key via ConversionRun.DefaultInteractiveMode (shared code — entry parity). 'extract' + collapse.enabled:true = the default (reference-code marker box + the raw content rendered COLLAPSED inside it, expandable). Env INTCOLLAPSE_OFF (or default_mode:'inline' + collapse.enabled:false) gives inline dashed boxes by default, with the bare-marker extract only under INTEXTRACT_ON.

collapse._note: The COLLAPSIBLE hand-off box, the default rendering for every un-built interactive: the loud rainbow reference-code marker keeps its exact search-by-code contract (class cv2-int-ref + data-cv2-index/data-cv2-ref + the {label} text), carries the class cv2-interactive on the SAME wrapper (so every placeholder exclusion — structural comparison, the leak scan, the EmojiStrip/LinkTextDisplay verbatim-zone walks — applies to the whole box), and CONTAINS the raw captured content (the exact inline-mode rendering: retained writer notes + the dashed box) inside a container that is COLLAPSED by default and expands/collapses with an animated (CSS grid-template-rows transition) click on the ▼/▲ arrow at the right end of the marker row. The Page Stitcher replaces the whole balanced cv2-int-ref element by data-cv2-ref, so the hidden raw content is swapped out together with the marker when the finished widget is stitched in. Env INTCOLLAPSE_OFF (or enabled:false here, with default_mode:'inline') turns it off.
collapse.wrapper_open: <div class="cv2-interactive cv2-int-ref" data-cv2-index="{index}" data-cv2-ref="{id}" style="border: 8px solid transparent; border-image: repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, #e03131 0 14px, #f08c00 14px 28px, #ffd43b 28px 42px, #2f9e44 42px 56px, #1971c2 56px 70px, #9c36b5 70px 84px) 8; background: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, #fff9db 0 28px, #ffe3e3 28px 56px); padding: 18px 22px; margin: 24px 0">
collapse.label_row: {label}▼
collapse.content_open: <div class="cv2-int-raw" style="display: grid; grid-template-rows: 0fr; transition: grid-template-rows 0.35s ease"><div style="min-height: 0; overflow: hidden"><div style="padding-top: 14px">
collapse.manifest_banner: MODE: HAND-OFF (default) — each un-built interactive renders as its REFERENCE CODE box on the page, with the raw captured content present but COLLAPSED inside it (click the arrow at the right end of the box to expand/collapse it). The REFERENCE CODE shown at the top of each block below is the SAME code live in the named File. Search the code (e.g. CODE-INT-NN-SS-type) in that File to drop the finished widget into place — replacing the whole reference box replaces the hidden raw content with it.

extract.marker: {label}
extract.marker_loud: {label}
extract._marker_loud_note: The hand-off spot must be UNMISSABLE, so marker_loud deliberately CLASHES with any module: thick rainbow repeating-gradient border, warm striped background, big centred magenta monospace label. STYLE ONLY — class cv2-int-ref, data-cv2-index/data-cv2-ref and the {label} text are the search-by-code contract and are IDENTICAL to marker. Env INTLOUD_OFF (or marker_loud_enabled:false) uses the calm blue marker.
extract.manifest_banner: MODE: EXTRACT (Phase-1 hand-off) — un-built interactives are NOT rendered on the page; each carries the REFERENCE CODE shown at the top of its block below, which marks its exact position in the named File. Search the code (e.g. CODE-INT-NN-SS-type) in that File to drop the finished widget into place.
extract.manifest_heading_hint: ↳ search this exact code in {file} to place the finished interactive
rules: The marker is a distinct class (cv2-int-ref) — NOT cv2-interactive — so it is visually/programmatically separable from the inline-mode placeholder and easy to style/grep.
id_format keys the code to module + page (NN matches the {code}-{NN}.html filename) + a per-page running number (seq, 1-based, document order over the extracted boxes) — so every code is unique.

Only un-built boxes (real captured content) are extracted; empty-marker and instruction-only bundles keep their inline-mode rendering (red flag / retained note), so no documented writer instruction is lost from the page.

The REFERENCE CODE is plain + hyphenated, with INT after the module code and the FIRST widget type only: ref_format {code}-INT-{NN}-{seq}-{type}, label_format {ref}. ContentConverter builds type from bundle.type alone (no + extraTypes repeats). The SAME {label} flows into the page marker AND the .txt header (the search-by-code contract), and the id attribute data-cv2-ref stays the bare id ({code}-{NN}-{seq}). Extract mode only (the default inline output is unaffected).

_interactive_builders_README: INTERACTIVE BUILDERS  — the data half of the 'easy widgets' auto-build.
WHAT THIS BLOCK IS:
Each key below is the name of an interactive WIDGET the converter knows
how to BUILD for real (not just dump as an orange placeholder). The value is
the exact HTML the finished widget should be made of, with {curly} slots the
engine fills from the captured Writers-Template data.
WHO READS IT:
app/js/InteractiveBuilder.js. For every captured interactive it looks up
interactive_builders[<type>]. If a template is here AND enabled, it builds
the widget. If the type is missing, disabled, or the data does not fit the
shape cleanly, the builder backs off and the orange placeholder is shown
instead — so a half-understood interactive is NEVER shipped wrong.
HOW TO EDIT (no JavaScript needed for wording / class / attribute changes):
• To change a widget's markup, edit its open / row / close strings here.
• To TURN A WIDGET OFF (go back to placeholder), set its enabled to false.
• {front} {back} etc. are the only moving parts — keep them spelled exactly.
• Whitespace/newlines inside the strings are cosmetic; the HTML formatter
re-indents the page afterwards, so write them however reads clearest.
HOW TO ADD A WHOLE NEW WIDGET (one data entry + one small code case):
1. Add a new key here with its open/row/close template (copy hintSlider).
2. Add a matching `case "<type>":` in InteractiveBuilder.js that maps the
captured table/members into the slots. That file explains exactly how.
Everything else (placeholder fallback, manifest, logging) is automatic.
SERIES-ANCHOR NOTE: widget MARKUP is corpus-wide and lives here. If one
subject/series ever needs a different shape for the SAME widget, that
belongs in the per-series anchor profile (see PHASE1_PART2_SPEC.md §A),
not as a code branch — same rule as every other style decision.

_tag_words_note._covering_doc: An EXISTING note only counts as already carrying the tag line's words when it has at least covering_note_min_words words: a bare asset note ('[Image]' → 'image') is contained in almost any instruction, so it would suppress the writer's whole request ('Can these please be created to look like postcards … an audio button to hear the greeting', SSOG103-2.0). Env covering_env = the plain containment test.
_tag_words_note.note: The words a writer types on a widget tag's OWN line ('[flip card] Please present each word on a flip card so that…', '[drag and drop] answers are placed in the correct columns, please place outside the box', '[carousel] Click on the slide to see examples of…') are not read by the builders, which take the tag as the invocation only, so on a built widget they would be lost. They are mostly developer instructions (the human rarely keeps them as learner text), so they are neither guessed into learner prose nor a reason to decline the build: they become the red Writers Note after the widget (the instruction-member class — bundle.instructions, emitted by #interactivePlaceholder), unless the build's own visible text already carries them or a note already says them (min_words 5: the 3–4-word residues a broken bracket leaves — 'of with captions', 'insert icon for' — are the tag's own vocabulary, not a note); red runs are already notes and are not doubled. InteractiveBuilder.#tagWordsNote, after every build. TAGWORDSNOTE_OFF=1 = the words are dropped.

_widget_links._doc_exclude: A picture / stock / developer-asset target (a picture's source page, a Drive / SharePoint / D2L asset, a Google image or search result, a media file) is the writer's pointer for the developer — the human rarely links these inside or beside widgets — so it is never woven as a learner link.
_widget_links._doc: KB constraint 75 ('inline → anchor') FOR BUILT WIDGETS. ContentConverter.#interactivePlaceholder hands the widget builders renderInline / renderBlock callbacks; the hover-definition stitch is deliberately off inside widgets, and without this every writer inline link inside a built widget — or in the prose the members rule renders around it — would lose its href (AGH1009-7.0's 'Yara N-Sensor' beside a carousel). On: the callbacks weave the bundle's OWN hyperlinks (every opener / member item's and captured table's block.links; the free-body weave — exact phrase, first occurrence per line, never inside an <a>); the hover stitch stays off. Env WIDGETLINKS_OFF turns it off.

_members_rule.note_consumption: consumption "read" = the EXACT rule: for the duration of the type dispatch every memberItem is a Proxy that records a read of its content (content_keys) and bundle.tables records its reads (InteractiveBuilder.#trackMembers); a member the builder READ is consumed, full stop; an unread member is classified by the members rule with the text-presence test demoted to a guard, a reference title (reference_title_pattern) skipped, an unread [image] member rendered through the page's own image emitter (image_member_render), unread prose rendered before / after the widget, anything else declining the build. This catches prose members a builder never reads (e.g. the flipCard table paths read bundle.tables alone), which the human keeps as free body. consumption "text" (or absent) = the text-presence test alone (see note), kept for comparison.
_members_rule.note:
THE GENERIC MEMBERS RULE at the one seam every builder passes through (InteractiveBuilder.Build → #withMembers; dragAndDrop excluded — it has its own rule): a built widget REPLACES the whole captured bundle and each builder reads only the members it understands, so anything else the scanner swallowed would vanish from the page without a trace (the card table's first-row instruction sentence, a trailing paragraph, the caption under [modal] + [image] / [video], the Go to journal line) — the human keeps such text as ordinary

. The text-presence reading: consumed = the built html's visible text + alt/title + the instruction notes; a member is consumed when its words are there (a short member whole, a longer one by >= consumed_ratio of its shingle-word shingles; a table by its sentence rows; a media line by its URL / video id; a media tag's own words are its reference title — never prose — and a go-to-journal [button] member is the caller's #goJournalTail business); an UN-CONSUMED prose member (a black paragraph, a [body] / bracket-less line, the invocation tag's own words, an ignored sentence row at a consumed table's top / bottom) renders through the free-body block emitter BEFORE the widget when it precedes the first consumed member and AFTER it when it follows the last; prose BETWEEN consumed members longer than between_short_words (a short line beside a modal's own video — '2. Watch the video.' — is a bounded loss the widget carries), a developer-cue line, a heading, a media member whose URL is not in the build, any other tag, a table the build ignored → with decline_on_unrenderable the build DECLINES and the hand-off box keeps every member (never half-build). A text-presence test alone cannot know what a builder consumed (a media URL a builder legitimately transformed, a title a builder drops by its own rule, a same-type sub-tag's words), which is why consumption "read" (note_consumption) records the builder's actual reads and decline_on_unrenderable is false. The widget's own markup is never edited. WIDGETMEMBERS_OFF=1 turns the rule off.

hint._note: The HINT ELEMENT. hint and hintSlider are DIFFERENT elements: hintSlider = div.hintSlider > hintRow > infoContainer > frontInfo|backInfo; hint = a title + a span.hint trigger + a sibling div.hintDropContent. Without a hint key Build would return null at its missing-template guard BEFORE dispatch, so the writer's Need-help tip would never build. The emitted form is the human's most common one in the authoring modules (the SSOG span[style]+b and SSCI104 title-inside-the-drop minorities are not followed). Requires a tagged TITLE and real BODY, so an instruction masquerading as a title declines. Env HINTELEM_OFF.

mtk_quiz._doc:
Change Ledger CL-0038. Any [MTKquiz]-family marker (any modifiers; the span-level retag in Tag_Lexicon._meta.mtk_quiz_retag does the matching) ends in the canonical button `
Go to quiz
` — href intentionally BLANK, the developer wires the D2L quicklink at publish time (the human's populated quickLink hrefs ARE that publish-time wiring, the CL-0044 class; the href divergence from the gold is INTENTIONAL) — plus ONE Designer/Developer To Do note (kind 'todo', red_flag.todo_form, class cv2-note) carrying the writer's raw quiz spec so the modifier prose ('supports engagement, audio, video, file sharing', 'should go to teacher dropbox' — which does NOT attach a dropbox wrapper) is never silently stripped. The retag makes the marker an ELEMENT, so it never opens a capturing bundle. ADJACENT WRITER BUTTON ABSORB (the human ships ONE button per quiz): a writer-typed quiz button in the marker's window — a [button] item labelled per button_label_pattern ('Go to quiz.'/'Quiz' — ARFUN02/ARFUN04/TEFUN02/TEFUN06-08) or a standalone [Go to quiz]-span bundle per marker_span_pattern (HPRE301) — is UPGRADED to the canonical anchored form and the marker's own button suppressed (its To Do note still emits). The window walks window_back/window_forward non-blank items, stopping at another mtk item, an [Activity] opener, or a section/page/closer boundary, so it can never leak across activities; a [go to quiz] span OUTSIDE any mtk window is untouched. A marker-claimed thin bundle (no content members) emits the button INSTEAD of its placeholder box; a fat one keeps its box (content never lost). Where the human build has no button (SCFUN01, MXFUN02, SSOG103, SSOG301, EXPFUN07) the ledger rule outranks it (named CHANGE-LEDGER OVERRIDE deltas). See omit_quiz_content for what the box holds. Env MTKQUIZ_OFF turns off the family.
mtk_quiz.todo_note: Create this quiz in MTK and wire the button's D2L quicklink (the href is intentionally blank). Writer's quiz spec: {spec}

omit_quiz_content._doc: KB constraint 65 / CL-0082, the designer's locked decision: an [MTKquiz] activity box holds ONLY (1) its title, (2) the writer's student instructions, (3) the Designer/Developer To Do note, (4) the 'Go to quiz' button — in that order — and the quiz's own content (questions, options, [correct]/[answer] marks, answer keys, option tables, the in-page quiz widget the writer also described, the quiz's own in-D2L title + intro) is omitted SILENTLY: no Red Flag, no comment, no trace (the one sanctioned undisclosed omission, constraint 1(b); the material stays in the Writers Template, the designer's source in MTK DEV). This supersedes CL-0038's 'writer quiz content stays rendered'. MECHANISM: the marker's emit is DEFERRED — after the marker, a short INSTRUCTION RUN is kept (a [Body]-family item or non-question prose, up to instruction_max_items; a heading only when the marker is a title-less [Activity] opener, ARFUN02 1A); a bracketed answer-mark span (answer_mark_pattern — '[Answers: B, A, B, C]', '[CS … answers …]', '[correct]') is dropped without ending the run (ARFUN04 4D keeps its instruction); anything else (a question line per question_pattern, an option, a table, a bundle trigger, a button, a heading once the box has content, a container/boundary tag) ENDS the run: the note + button flush inside the still-open box and the SILENCE starts — every content item is skipped until the quiz block ends: the box's close (explicit [end …] or the heading auto-close — ARFUN04 2E's next [H3]), any CONTAINER_CLOSE, the next [Activity] opener, a page/section boundary, the next marker, or — with no box open — a rendered heading <= container_auto_close.rendered_heading_max / any CONTAINER_OPEN (SSOG301's [H2] ends it at once). A bundle whose trigger item is silenced is marked emitted and never renders. PATH 2a: a quiz-type bundle (quiz_bundle_types) that carries the marker as its opening span or a member builds the SHELL instead of the widget: members before the marker rendered as content (TEFUN03's [Body] instruction), the post-marker instruction run, then note + button (the whole widget IS the quiz: ARFUN03 1A, ARFUN04 1H, TEFUN03/06 1A in the human build). A marker captured by a NON-quiz container bundle (accordion ENG1004/1005, speechBubble TEDC401, unclassified HPRE203 p1 / MXFU402) is NOT in scope. The writer's own quiz button the pre-pass claimed (_mtkQuizAnchor / _mtkQuizBtn) renders NOTHING under this flag — the button is the box's LAST child and the marker's emit always carries it. A box-less marker (SCFUN01, TEFUN07, MXFUN02, EXBP901, SSOG301) gets no synthesised numbered box and no default 'Quiz' <h3>. Env MTKQUIZOMIT_OFF keeps the quiz content rendered.
omit_quiz_content.todo_note: create this quiz in MTK DEV and orgunit link it to this module, then insert its D2L quicklink URL into the "Go to quiz" button href below. Writer's quiz spec: {spec}

interactive_builders._principle: PRINCIPLE (the two-layer anchor comparison). Every builder here builds the widget the WRITER's tag specifies. The human developer's finished widget is the reference ONLY where the writer's tag corresponds to the human's element (Decision-Framework B). Where the human editorially SUBSTITUTED a different element (e.g. writer [flip card] -> human accordion; writer [carousel] left as static images), that substitution is NON-derivable (Decision-Framework A1): build the WRITER's tagged widget anyway and judge it on the widget's own correctness, NOT on its likeness to the human's substitution. A structural difference from a human substitution is the expected cost, not a regression. Never half-build: build cleanly or keep the honest placeholder.

doc_button_text_fence._doc_exempt: Exempt from the learner text: a member tag matching media_tag_pattern (a picture / video / audio / embed label, a [button] / [link] label — BLLR201-5.0's genuine document button keeps its 'Go to journal'), a writer instruction, and the INVOCATION tag's own line (the tag-words note surfaces it as the red Writers Note — OSOH201-3.0).
doc_button_text_fence._doc: A CONTENT-CARRYING BUNDLE IS NOT A LINK BUTTON, whatever the content (not only a heading member). The single-document button path (exactly one URL → one anchored button) drops every other member, and the members rule counts a member consumed once it was READ, so without this fence a modal set with real text (PWY1009-2.2's modals, TEFUN03-0.0's 'AI is a tool' paragraphs, HIS1005-3.0's source text + questions, MXFL401-4.0's KiwiSaver modal, BLL240-0.0's activity modals) would become a single button to the one URL it holds — a stock photo, a source link, a website. A member carrying learner text (>= min_words words; not a [image] / [video] / [audio] / [embed] label, not a writer instruction, not the button's own label) sends the bundle on to the trigger + TKmodal set composer (or its honest box). Env MODALBTNTEXT_OFF turns it off.

modal_sets._note_additions: Five additions, each on its own env toggle. closer_pattern: a modal member whose bracket says close/end is a CLOSER and never opens a pop-out (otherwise [Close Modal] opens an empty set and sinks the whole widget — MODALCLOSER_OFF). stray_marker_tags: a content-less marker belonging to a NEIGHBOURING activity ([Tab 2], [trigger engagement]) is skipped like a [button] instead of bailing the walk — lossless, as these sit at the very end of their bundle and carry no text (MODALSTRAY_OFF; mostly BLL). prose_tags: an [external link] carrying a URL is pop-out CONTENT, not a foreign tag (MODALMEMVOCAB_OFF). opener_leading_numberless: in a NUMBERED bundle a leading text-less numberless marker is the widget's own opener, not pop-out 0 — otherwise it creates a trigger-less first set that sinks the build (EXPFUN04/05; MODALOPENER_OFF). bold_lead_label: a numbered set with no label takes the BOLD LEAD of its first line, the bold-lead rule used by the other builders (MODALBOLDLEAD_OFF; CEDT208's four tapa cloths). media_tiles: the writer's lead table of [Insert media item N] references supplies the numbered sets' TRIGGER PICTURES from the Media List the run already parses — EXPFUN04's items 4/5/6 resolve to iStock-1156854907 / iStock-155353286 / iStock-1371047758, the three filenames its human developer used, and the emit is the human's own row of tile columns followed by the pop-outs. EVERY cell must resolve or none does, so a strip is never half pictures and half words (MODALTILES_OFF).
modal_sets._note: The general TKmodal set composer, tried LAST after the image-pair form and the single-document button, so those builds are unaffected. Emits the corpus convention (div.button.TKmodalButton + its sibling div.TKmodal) from four delimiters: numbered [Modal N …] sub-tags, the SAME-BLOCK label line, a captured TABLE (one row = one modal), and the tag's own text. The text trigger is the human's DOMINANT modal form. min_modals 1 (a lone modal is the human's most common case); label_max_words 9 follows the human's text triggers (almost all ≤ 6 words, none over 9), so a longer writer line is not a trigger and the set declines rather than putting a paragraph on a button. A strict label/modal alternation keeps a multiple-choice quiz from becoming a row of buttons. Env MODALSETS_OFF.

modal.note: A [modal] whose captured content is a SINGLE document/PDF URL is the human's external-resource BUTTON (as in OSBY201-02). The button WORDING is editorial (the WT gives only the URL), so {label} is a derived short writer link-phrase or default_label; the STRUCTURE (the <a><div.button>) is the derivable match. CONSERVATIVE (never half-build): builds ONLY on exactly one URL with no data table / rich members — anything richer keeps the orange placeholder. Env MODALBTN_OFF.

image_pairs.note: Build the WRITER'S modal, not the human's flipCard substitution (the _principle rule). Repeating '[modal][image] <iStock URL>' + [body]/black content pairs (OSOH501-01's six ergonomics modals) build the corpus TKmodal convention: img.TKmodalButton trigger directly followed by its div.TKmodal (the CEDK401/ENGI301 sibling-pair form). size is editorial (WT gives none) -> the human's most common size, default_size M. NEVER half-builds: non-image modal member, no/non-iStock URL, trigger caption residue, red text, table/nested/foreign member, content before the first trigger, or an EMPTY pair (the BLL image-enlarge dialect) all decline to the single-document path / placeholder. Other dialects (EXPFUN tile-modals, MXDI '[Modal N Image]', BLL image-enlarge with no body) are not built here. Env MODALIMG_OFF.

letter_grid_bingo._doc:
THE LETTER-GRID BINGO: the BLL family's `[Self check] Click on the lower case letter ‘s’.` + a TABLE of single letters with the CORRECT cells typed in red (BLL110 / 113 / 120 / 130 / 140 / 150 / 154 / 160 / 170 — each bundle usually holding the lower-case and the capital grid, the writer's `[Add an audio that when they click/hover on the letter it says the name of the letter…]` ELEMENT tag and the `**Alphabet Audio** [LINK]` line). The human builds the KB's BINGO (03E COMP_04): `div.bingo.col-12 > div.bingoContainer[grid=N] > div.number[value=correct] > p` + the `row > activityButton reset-btn / activityButton hidden check-btn` row — grid 12 cells → 4, 9 → 3, 16 → 4; the wrapper `bingo col-12`; the button row; no h4 card title; the cell usually `p.sassoonI-text` (often with a `span.audioTrigger` — the developer's snipped alphabet audio, NOT emitted here: the package cannot supply the asset, so the writer's audio request and the link ride as the red Writers Note after the widget). Tried BEFORE the question-list form; fires only when EVERY table in the bundle is a letter grid (every non-empty cell ≤ max_cell_chars letters / digits once the red markers and bold marks are stripped; ≥ min_cells cells), every extra type is selfCheck itself (the second grid), and each table follows its own `[Self check]` invocation whose black text is the lead; per table → `lead` + the bingo: the cells row-major from the writer's table, value="correct" on the RED cells or, when the writer marked none, on the cells equal to the letter quoted in the lead (`correct_from`; neither → decline, never half-built); `grid` from the cell count (grid_by_cells, else grid_default); the cell class by module-code prefix (cell_class_by_prefix — the BLL family's Sassoon Infant; plain

= the KB form elsewhere). The box takes `.interactive` through interactive_widget_types (bingo is listed). Env BINGO_OFF keeps the hand-off box.

letter_grid_bingo._doc_writefont: KB CL-0109, constraint 93: the writing font is `writeFont` (Playwrite NZ Basic); the sassoon classes are legacy — valid on the server, never emitted in a new build. So the BLL cell class is `writeFont`, the design team's default, rather than the older human build's `sassoonI-text`. The BLL bingo pages (BLL110–BLL170 `_0_0`) are a NAMED KB OVERRIDE of their gold (§1b; _meta.gold_override_policy). env WRITEFONT_OFF uses the legacy map below.

fib._doc: THE DRAG-AND-DROP FILL-IN-THE-BLANK FORM (KB 03B 'FIB Layout'), built only where the writer marked the answer: the writer's `[Drag and drop]` + sentences whose answers are typed RED inside the black text ('Correct answers are in red'). The typing reading (InteractiveBuilder.#typing — its lines, answer segments, answer-key and reject guards, min_answers, max_answer_words) is reused and rendered as the FIB form: each red answer an inline `<span class="drop" option="n">`, the answers the drags in the same order (the widget script shuffles), the 03B button row. Tried after the standard / images / column forms; needs ≥ 2 such lines, no table, no media. Env DDFIB_OFF.

remainder._doc: THE FIB FORM'S REMAINDER: three more writer shapes inside its own family. marker_tag_pattern: the writer's `[correct answer]` tag after each red word (BLL247) is the answer marker, not a foreign tag — skipped, and a word typed inside the marker's own red run ('weather [correct answer]') is that line's answer. button_label_pattern: a trailing `[button] Check answers` / Reset / Undo is the KB button row the build already emits (TWHK907; TWHA906 labels its button "Answers" — the KB row's Check answers covers it). symbol_answer_pattern: a red `<` / `>` / `≤` / `≥` / `=` is the answer (MXEO301 3F / 6A — 'Greater than or less than?'); the red-word reader otherwise skips a word with no letter or digit. trailing_prose: answer-less paragraphs the capture ran on into AFTER the questions (MXEO301 6A's following [body] paragraph) render as prose after the widget; a question after them still declines. headless_first_row_declines: when the FIRST sentence alone opens on its blank, its head was left outside the capture (BLL247 "The bus" — the scanner keeps black text right after the opener out of the bundle) — decline rather than ship a headless sentence (so BLL247 stays a hand-off box; the marker reading serves the rest of the family). answer_trailing_punct: the sentence's full stop / comma typed inside the red word ('publishers.' — TWHA906) stays in the sentence after the blank; the drag is the word (the human's own drags). Fib mode only — the typing quiz is unchanged. Env DDFIBREST_OFF turns these off.

red_answer_column._doc: THE RED ANSWER COLUMN: the writer types a matching table's ANSWER column red (`• Sarah spent $12 … ║ «3x = 12»` MXEO301 5.1; a four-column table = two pair sets, `3² ║ «3 × 3» ║ 3^6 ║ «3 × 3 × …»` MXEO301 1.0); the standard form's red guard refuses these, but the human builds the standard matching layout (the prompts the questions, the red answers the drags, the right-hand pairs after the left). InteractiveBuilder.#ddRedAnswerPairs: every row of every column pair empty or a black prompt beside a red-only answer; a black first row over them = the label header (dropped); a URL / writer [tag] declines; strip_bullet drops a prompt's leading list mark (the human's form). max_width 4. Seen in MXFL, MXEO, MXDI, ENGR, BLL, MXDB. Env DDREDANS_OFF.

label_row._doc: THE LABEL ROW of the standard pair table: the writer's FIRST row is a red column-label row (`Question ║ Answer`, `Word ║ [correct]`, `Clause [static] ║ Description`, `║ Correct answer - can we jumble them up though please`) over red-free pairs, which the standard form's red guard would refuse. When that row's text carries a matching-role cue (role_pattern) and no category cue (category_pattern — a heading marker `[H4] Benefits ║ [H4] Risks`, `[static heading]` / `[column heading]`, a `sort` / `category` / `group` word: the human builds those as a COLUMN sort, e.g. OSSM501) and no URL, it is the header: dropped; a real-word red run in it (label_max_words, the #ddIsNote test) rides along as the red Writers Note after the widget. Env DDLABELROW_OFF.
label_row._guards_doc: Under a dropped label row only (every standard-form build is untouched): a drawn blank in a label (blank_pattern — BLL266 'My brother ____ played …', the human's FIB) and a table whose every label equals its answer (decline_identity — BLLR201–203 'cartoonist ║ cartoonist') keep the hand-off box. category_pattern also reads the UNBRACKETED 'Static Heading:' (OSAI201 2.0 — the human's column sort).

standard_decline_opener._doc: The standard pair reading takes any 2-column table as [label | answer]; when the writer's OPENER says the items go INTO coloured squares / zones / categories / groups / columns, the table is the drop TARGETS of a category sort, not the pairs — HPFUN101 1A: '[Interactive] Drag and drop, drop the statements into the relevant coloured square' over a 2×2 table of four zones (Blue / Green / Yellow / Red, each with its feelings), the statements typed after it; the pair reading would build nonsense pairs from the zone cells. The standard form declines (the hand-off box keeps the writer's content); the images and column forms are not affected. Tested on the bundle's red TAG items only (the span that names the widget is the first member when an activity box owns the opener), never the black body text. Env DDSORTOPENER_OFF.

button_row.note: KB 03B 'Standard Layout': every dragAndDrop ends with the activityButton row (Reset / Undo hidden / Check answers hidden), as the human's standard drag-and-drops almost always do. Applied to EVERY built standard dragAndDrop (the text form and the images form alike): the widget closes dragContainer / ddContainer / row (close_inner), emits html, then closes the dragAndDrop div (close_outer). Env DDBUTTONS_OFF uses the plain `close` string (no button row).

members.note:
THE MEMBERS RULE for every built dragAndDrop (the text form, the image form, the column form): a built widget REPLACES the whole captured bundle and the forms only read the TABLE, so every other member the scanner swallowed — the writer's sentence before the table, the 'Go to journal' line after it, a [button], a [body] paragraph, a cloze passage — would silently vanish (the human keeps such prose as

: AGH1001 2.0, AGH1005 6.0, TEFUN06, TWHK902, ENGC301, CEDR203, OSGM101). Walked over the members in order: the table = the widget; a black paragraph renders in place through the free-body paragraph emitter (render_black), before or after the widget as the writer placed it; a [body] tag with words is a paragraph (body_tag_as_prose); an instruction-class tag is already the red Writers Note (skipped); a [button] whose label is one of the 03B button row's own (button_row_labels — SSOG301's [insert button] Undo / Check Answer / Reset) is satisfied by the row the build emits; the words riding the invocation tag's OWN line (PHE1005 2.0 '[activity - drag and drop] Match the Māori with the English…' = the human's

) render as a paragraph BEFORE the widget (tag_words_as_prose — the safe content-preserving form; the activity's h3 is the title-level mechanism's business); a [body] or tag-line text opening with a developer cue (note_cue_pattern — OSGM101 '[body] CS: scramble the saying') is a note, not learner prose → decline; ANYTHING ELSE — a [button] with another label, [answer], [audio], [image], [activity], a nested widget — cannot be rendered from inside the widget seam, so the build is DECLINED and the hand-off box keeps every member (never half-build). DDMEMBERS_OFF=1 turns the rule off (members are silently replaced).
