<div class="dragAndDrop images" layout="standard">
<div class="row">
<div class="col-7 questionContainer">
images.note: The writer's IMAGE-PAIR table — one 2-column table whose every data row pairs ONE image URL with ONE plain-text word / sentence, `image | word` (BLL112, BLL122, BLL161, BLL125, BLL220, BLL224, BLL230, BLL210, ENFUN02, MXFUN03, CHFUN05, TEFUN08, BLL244, ENGJ102) or `word | image` (BLL146, BLL130, BLL233, CEDO105, ENFUN04, ENGS201, BLL266) — builds the KB 03B 'Standard Layout — With images' form: `<div class="dragAndDrop images" layout="standard">`, the TEXT side is ALWAYS the fixed question side (col-7 questionContainer, one .question per row) and the IMAGES are the draggable items (col-5 ddContainer: dropContainer with a .drop per row, dragContainer with a .drag holding the image per row, option = the 1-based row index = the answer key) — 03B's placement rule ('images in the questionContainer stretch vertically and make the interactive unusably tall'), whichever way round the writer typed the columns; margB0 on the drag images (03B); the KB button row follows (button_row). The image: an iStock id → filename_istock, any other host → the URL-slug placeholder (#accImageFilename); rendered in the run's image mode through the FinishImg rider (the URL is passed, so the alt is the verified acks title, else the URL-slug title — the human's BLL146 alt IS the iStock title); the image-mode templates carry no loading=lazy and the lazy_free_hosts post-pass strips any the rider adds inside dragAndDrop (constraint 83). Tried ONLY where the text form returned null (it bails on any URL). header_row_skip: a first row with no URL in either cell is a column-label / instruction row ('Image | Sentence', '**Kupu** |', '| Correct answer - can we jumble them up though please', '| [correct answers]') — dropped; its red instruction rides along as the standard red Writers Note after the widget (bundle.instructions). image_tag_pattern: a red run in the IMAGE cell matching it is the writer's own [image] tag; any other red there ('Arrow added to image', 'Please crop a little so …') is a developer asset note — surfaced the same way, the build proceeds. NEVER HALF-BUILDS (null → the hand-off box): a second table, an extraType, a media item harvested out of the table, a ragged row, a row without exactly one image cell + one text cell, the image column changing sides, ANY red run in the TEXT cell (an answer word inside a sentence = a FIB shape — BLL226 / BLL232 / BLL243 / BLL215 / BLL231; `[correct]` — BLL253 / 254 / 256; a red-bracketed audio-word — BLL272 / 273 / 274 / 276; `[Body]` — CEDK102 / SSOG105), an empty label, a URL in the text cell, a repeated label (an ambiguous match), prose riding along with the image, fewer than min_rows rows. The image COLUMN-SORT shape is not built here. The KB's optional autoCheck / noShuffle / noBG modifiers are the developer's editorial choice (no writer signal) — not emitted. The human's own substitutions (BLL112 / ENFUN04 build a noBG column form; BLL146 is the exact KB form) are A1 — the writer's tag is the target. Env DDIMAGES_OFF turns off the whole form (DRAGDROP_OFF turns off the type).

marked._doc: THE MARKED CATEGORY SORT: a header cell whose red run is a heading marker (header_marker_pattern — `[H4] Benefits ║ [H4] Risks` OSSM501, `AI can [static heading]` OSAI201) is read as its black label, a fully-red short header cell (red_label — `Short vowel ║ Long vowel` BLL270) as its label; a data cell of red text only (black separators allowed) as its item(s) (`scooter ║ science` under `/sk/ sound ║ /s/ sound` — BLL250, the human's 2-column ddColumn sort); a half-red table (red and black items) declines. A table so marked (a marked header, or every item red) may be min_columns (2) wide — an unmarked 2-column table stays the standard pair reader's. Env DDCOLMARK_OFF.
marked._echo_consumed_doc: Under a marked sort only: a black bundle line that merely repeats a drag item (the writer's `* I share your perspective.` list above the table — CEDT501 6.1; the gold shows the instruction line only) is consumed by #ddWithMembers, not rendered as a paragraph.

column.note:
The writer's CLEAN CATEGORY-SORT table — one table of 3+ columns whose first row is a row of plain category labels (Past | Present | Future, ai | ay | a_e, Noun | Verb | Adjective) and whose data cells are the items that belong under each column (a ' / ' or bullet list in a cell = several items) — builds the KB 03B 'Column Layout': a row.dropContainer with one ddColumn per category (

heading

+ one drop option=c per item in that column, c = the 1-based column index = the answer key), a row.dragContainer whose FIRST ddColumn holds every drag option=c in column order, padded with EMPTY ddColumns to the drop-column count (03B: 'Empty ddColumn pads to match drop column count', as the human mostly does), then the button_row. No blanks attribute, no autoCheck / noBG / hoverBoxes (the developer's editorial modifiers — no writer signal). Tried ONLY where the text form and the image form both returned null. NEVER HALF-BUILDS (null = the hand-off box): a second table, an extraType, a harvested media item, width < min_columns, fewer than min_rows rows, a header cell that is empty / red / a URL / a [tag] / matches header_reject_pattern (a blank run = a FIB, an image word = the image column-sort) / longer than header_max_words (MXFU402's question headers = a match), any data cell that is red / a URL / a [tag], items in fewer than 2 columns (a pooled cell = no answer key), fewer than min_items items, a repeated item (an ambiguous key); the bundle's OTHER members are the shared members rule's business (interactive_builders.dragAndDrop.members). The human mostly builds these tables as the column form. DDCOLUMN_OFF=1 turns it off.

dragAndDrop.note:
dragAndDrop NARROW N:N TEXT-MATCHING form, layout=standard. Input is one 2-column data table [label | answer]; row order is the answer key. Builds the human's questionContainer (one .question per label) + ddContainer (a .drop per row + a .drag per row, option = 1-based row index), answers as

text. CONSERVATIVE: the human's LAYOUT choice (standard/column/FIB/scatter) and image-form alt text are NON-DERIVABLE editorial (NOT in the WT — bundle.modifier is the writer's freeform remainder, not layout=), so this fires ONLY on the safest sub-shape and keeps the placeholder otherwise — bail unless exactly one table, width 2, >= min_rows rows, every answer DISTINCT plain text (a repeated answer = categorisation, not matching -> bail), and no media / URL / red / extraType. layout defaults to standard. Env DRAGDROP_OFF.

glossary.note:
A [glossary] interactive is a flat list of 'Term – Meaning' lines (en/em-dash or spaced hyphen separated), as in OSAI201-01. InteractiveBuilder.#glossary parses each captured black line via split_pattern (term = before the first dash, meaning = after) and builds the human's Term/Meaning table:

Glossary

+ with a 'Term'|'Meaning' header (tr.title-g) and one row per entry. The outer row>col-md-8 wrapper is supplied by the body emitter, so only the inner div.glossary (which carries the wavy-border CSS) is built here. Declines (placeholder) if fewer than min_rows dash lines are found. The boundary bank terminates the glossary at the next heading so a following [H3] is not swallowed.

face_marker_strip._doc: KB constraint 5, never render a [tag] as visible text. The table-form builder (#hintSliderTable) reads each cell through #cellText, which strips the writer's red style but keeps the marker words, so a writer who typed the face marker at the head of each cell — `[Hintslider front] Start with a suitable greeting.` | `[Hintslider back] e.g., Guten Tag…` (GENO901-7.3) or `[hint slider 1] Employee` | `[hint slider text 1] The person who…` (PWY1009-1.1) — would show the marker as face text. The human's faces are the bare text (GENO901_0_7, PWY1009_1_0). A leading bracket matching pattern is removed from each face. Env HINTFACEMARK_OFF keeps the markers.

labelled_pairs._note: The LABELLED-PAIR slider: a general composer run LAST, so the other slider forms are unaffected. ONE rule (a row is a FRONT then a BACK) covers every writer dialect: the front riding the opener, a [back]/[body] tag, a labelled red span, halves named in the bracket, a black bullet. min_rows 1 because many human sliders are single-row. Trailing over-captured prose renders AFTER the widget so building never loses the writer's words. Env HINTPAIR_OFF.

_comment: hintSlider — a list of click-to-reveal rows. Captured as ONE 2-column table:
column 1 = the visible hint (front), column 2 = the reveal (back).
A leading 'hint | slide' (or 'front | back') header row is auto-skipped.
Human reference: 01-Finalized_Modules_/OSAI201 (hintCssFile="standard").
hintSlider._header_note: A first table row is treated as a column-label header (and dropped) when it is the writer's red instruction text, OR when every cell is one of these label words. Add words here if a writer uses different column labels.

panel_bullet_list._doc:
THE PANEL'S BULLETS ARE A LIST: the strict text-only and image accordion paths (InteractiveBuilder.#accordionTextOnly / #accordionWithImages) render each panel body line as its own

, so without this the writer's `• …` bullets would show the glyph in a paragraph (BLL116 2.0 `

• Where do you think Sant and Nat are playing?

`) where the human lists them (`accContent > ul > li`). A run of consecutive `•` lines is ONE
    of
  • s (glyph dropped); other lines keep their

    ; a panel with no bullet is unchanged. The rich / panel-delimiter paths already list bullets through the page renderer. Env ACCBULLETLIST_OFF.

bullet_bold_lead._doc: The bold-lead panel dialect (`**Heading:** body` lines) extended to the writer's bulleted form — `• **Weed suppression** – If there are plants growing…` under `[Interactive: accordion under bold headings]` (AGH1009 6.0): an optional leading bullet character and a spaced en / em dash (or hyphen) as the separator, the dash dropped from the panel body. Every other D4 rule is unchanged (every member a black text line, ≥ min_bold_panels leads, every panel non-empty, head ≤ head_max_words). Env ACCBULLETLEAD_OFF uses the colon-only, line-opening pattern.

marker_table._doc: The writer lays the accordion out in a TABLE and types their OWN panel markers inside the cells — `[Accordion N]` / `[Hn]` (a title) and `[Accordion N text]` / `[drop down text N]` / `[Body]` / `[Dropdown information]` (a body) — in four layouts: alternating title / text rows (PWY1009, CEDK102), a row of titles over a row of texts paired by column (PWY1008), a title cell beside its body cell (PWY1009-3.3, XMES101), one whole panel per cell (TEDC401, MXEX301 `[Accordion] 1 **Title** / [Body] …`). The D2 reading (first cell = heading) refuses every one; the human builds the accordion from exactly those markers (PWY1009, PWY1008, CEDK102, TEDC401, MXEX301, PWYWHA1). InteractiveBuilder.#accMarkerTablePanels, tried LAST in #accResolvePanels (D5, after D1–D4 decline), so every accordion D1–D4 builds is unaffected. head_pattern / bare_head_pattern (the MXEX301 `[Accordion]` + a red `1`) / heading_pattern name a TITLE marker (group 1 = its number, the last group = a title typed inside the marker's own red span); body_pattern a BODY marker (its number must agree with its title's); image_pattern an image (its URL → the panel image by the image-name rule; no URL → an asset-request red note); closer_pattern the stray `]` / `)` span that closes an `[Image: iStock: … ]`; note_pattern a developer cue (`Dev team please add:`, `[CS note: …]`) and any unbracketed red sentence of instruction_min_words+ words (SSOG103's `Could the Coin images please be muddled up …`) → a red note after the widget; words typed INSIDE a body marker's red span (`[Body text] Can this be placed onto the scroll please.`) → a note too. The writer's flip-card slip `[Accordion 8 front]` / `[Accordion 6 back]` (PWY1009) reads as title / body. ANY other red span (a hover trigger, an `[Alert]`, a `[table]`, a speech-bubble spec) keeps the box. A panel still without text (a title and perhaps its picture — PWY1007) waits for its body in a later cell of the row or the cell below. min_panels_numbered: one panel stands on the writer's own numbered marker (the D1 rule); an [Hn]-only table needs min_panels. label_row_keywords: a first row of column labels (`Images | Instructions`) — or a wholly red one (CHFUN01 `Heading [h4] | Content [body]`) — is peeled first; with no marker in the rest, the ordinary D2 reading is tried on it. min_panels: at least two panels. Env ACCMARKTABLE_OFF turns it off.

panel_delimiters._note: The PANEL DELIMITER VOCABULARY, tried LAST after the strict paths and both modes of the rich fallback, so it is strictly additive. Panels resolve from an ordered vocabulary, each derivation matching the human build: D1 [accordion N] widened to the word/ordinal spellings, a heading-less panel taking its head from its own first [H2]-[H6]; D2 a captured TABLE, ONE ROW = ONE PANEL (head = a short first cell, else the content cell's BOLD LEAD); D3 a repeating same-level heading; D4 repeating BOLD-LEAD black lines. min_panels 1 for the explicit D1 (many human accordions have one panel) but 2 for the inferred D2/D3/D4, so one table row is never guessed into an accordion. Env ACCPANELS_OFF.

title_members._note:
The BUILDER half of member_rule.title_panel_member (the scanner half, in the Boundary Bank, captures the markers instead of terminating on them): a member matching `pattern` — the writer's numbered '[title N]', including the '[tilte N]' misspelling, which resolves to NO tag and would otherwise be filed as a noise NOTE with the panel heading lost — OPENS A PANEL whose heading is the tag's black tail, bold stripped (the human ships the whole tail as the accHead h4, so head_max_words is generous at 20; a longer tail falls back to its bold lead per the D1 discipline). opener_tail_as_lead: the BARE unnumbered opener's tail ('Click on the tab to see examples.') is the accordion's LEAD — the human's own

above the widget — never a bogus first panel; when the writer typed the phrase inside the red span, the bracket-stripped residual is the same lead. media_table_parts: an in-panel MEDIA TABLE ([video]/[image] cell + URL, optional [caption]) becomes the panel's own videoSection/img + caption

— the human nests them INSIDE accContent — instead of a kept table whose raw media cell the leak guard would rightly decline. EVERY behaviour here is fenced to bundles that actually carry a numbered title member (a form only CHFUN05 uses), so no other build moves. Env toggle: ACCTITLEPANEL_OFF (independent of the scanner's ACCTITLEMEM_OFF).

member_vocabulary._note: THE ACCORDION'S OWN MEMBER VOCABULARY, supplied through the SAME caller-scoped `delims` mechanism tabs, flipCard and clickDrop use — so every other caller is unaffected BY CONSTRUCTION and each family here reverses on its own data key. [body], [video] and [image] members are already placed inside a panel; the member tags that would otherwise stop the walk are buttons, data markers, external links, shape markers, tables and embeds. prose_tags: an [external link]/[website]/[Link], a [Caption]/[label …]/[Insert toolbox item] data marker and an [embed]/[pdf] carrying black content render as panel prose (renderBlock links a bare URL, so the writer's link survives as a link); carrying NONE they surface as a red Writers Note rather than being silently skipped (text_tags_note_when_empty — the never-silently-dropped rule; false for every other caller, so tabs and clickDrop cannot move). note_tags: a bare [table]/[Insert Table] is an asset request for a table, and a [purple coloured box] shape marker is a design instruction — both are notes, never content. head_tags: a [heading] is a sub-heading at head_level. defer_pattern: a mid-sentence hover marker ([definition: horizontal axis] + the rest of the sentence in its trailing text, ENGJ301-4.0) STILL DECLINES — rendering only the trailing text would drop the defined term out of the writer's sentence, and weaving it is the render stitch, which is deliberately switched off inside a widget. Accordions still left un-built are mostly blocked by another widget's invocation (a gathering case, not a builder one) or a non-journal button. Env ACCMEMBER_OFF.

go_journal_member._note: THE GO-TO-JOURNAL BUTTON. The writer ends the accordion with '[Button] Go to journal' / '[Go to Journal]'. THE SCANNER FENCE IS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE: button_tail_terminates excludes a go-to-journal button because releasing it into the body stream produces a duplicate button (HIS1006-12.0), so this rule changes nothing about CAPTURE — the button stays a member and the widget's boundary is untouched. Instead the member is SKIPPED as panel content (the human almost never puts a button inside a panel) and the accordion emits go_journal's own templated <h4 class="goJournal"> AFTER the widget, which is where the human puts it. This covers bundles with no owning activity too (where #goJournalTail's member branch never runs), so the button is never lost. The double-emit is prevented at the other end: the builder sets bundle._goJournalEmitted and #goJournalTail's member branch stands down (buttons.go_journal.member_branch_yields_to_builder). label_match/raw_match are READ FROM buttons.go_journal, never copied, so this rule and go_journal can never drift apart (the #isGoJournalButton discipline). Env ACCGOJOURNAL_OFF.

lead_before_first_panel._note: CONTENT BEFORE THE FIRST PANEL IS THE ACCORDION'S OWN LEAD (XDLS904, XDLS903, CEDT501, ENG1005, ENG1007, ENGI405, XDLS905, XGF9001). Attaching it to the first panel would put it in the wrong place, so D1 would decline; instead, as the clickDrop reading does, the material renders ABOVE the widget in the writer's own place: the lead parts are returned separately, rendered through the same renderBlock/asset machinery as a panel body, and emitted before <div class="accordion">. Nothing is invented and nothing is lost. GUARDED: only TEXT, IMG, VIDEO, EMBED and HEAD parts may lead (a table or a nested widget before the first panel still declines, since those are the shapes where the writer's intent is genuinely unclear), and a lead that renders to nothing is dropped. Env ACCLEADIN_OFF.

_comment: accordion — a stack of click-to-open panels, each a heading + a revealed body.
IMPORTANT: an accordion is built from MEMBERS, not a data table. In the Writers
Template the writer types one [accordion N] tag per panel; the text AFTER the tag
on the same line is that panel's HEADING, and the paragraph(s) beneath it are the
panel BODY. The converter groups them into panels in document order.

heading ->

...

body ->
one

per paragraph
One <div class=accordion> wraps every (accHead + accContent) pair, in order.
BUILT ONLY when every panel is plain heading + body text. The WHOLE accordion
falls back to the orange placeholder (never half-built) if the bundle is richer
than that — any other member ([image]/[video]/[button]/a data table), a panel
missing its heading or its body, or red writer-instruction text inside a panel.

{content} receives one

...

per body paragraph (so multi-paragraph panels
render faithfully); {head} is the panel heading text.
Human reference (verbatim shape): 01-Finalized_Modules_/OSBY301/OSBY301-01.html (5 panels).
accordion._image_note:
Image-bearing accordion panels (OSGM501-02): the panel image renders FIRST inside accContent (img.img-fluid, iStock id -> images/iStock-.jpg, Mode P/D, alt non-derivable -> alt=''), then the body

(s). A trailing [body] paragraph after the last panel renders as free body after the accordion (trailing_body). Built via InteractiveBuilder.#accordionWithImages; plain-text accordions are unchanged (#accordionTextOnly).

_comment: IMAGE-ARRANGEMENT LAYOUT MARKER (as in SCCH302's mixtures accordion): a red
span the lexicon resolves to [image] only EMBEDDED in prose ('[2 images next to
each other]', '[insert images side by side]'), with NO media URL of its own and
NO trailing black content. It is a writer LAYOUT INSTRUCTION about the images
that follow, not an image element — the accordion walks SKIP it as build content
and a successful build surfaces its text as the standard red note after the
widget (the instruction-member class; never silently stripped, never a
build-breaker). Without this rule both accordion walks would decline the whole
widget at this member. Env ACCIMGMARK_OFF makes the marker decline the build.
image_layout_marker.pattern: (?=[\s\S]*\bimages?\b)(?=[\s\S]*\b(?:side by side|next to each other|beside each other)\b)

head_from_first_line._note: HEADING-LESS PANEL RECOVERY. A large writer family numbers the panels but puts NO text on the tag itself: '[accordion 1]' alone on its line, then the panel's own first line ('US 29302 (Version 3)') and the rest of the body under it. Under the rich fallback's 'each panel needs a heading' rule every accordion authored that way would become a developer hand-off box. When the writer has used the accordion tag, an accordion is generated whatever the human build shows (the human may have changed the interactive after liaising with the writer — the Decision Framework's A1 branch), so this build is judged on the accordion's own correctness and the writer's tag, not on matching the human's substitution (the Decision Framework's precedence rule). THE RULE: a panel with no heading takes it from its OWN first text line, and that line is REMOVED from the body so it is never shown twice. Guarded — the donor part must be TEXT (never an image/video/nested part), must have at least one more line after the heading (a single-line part IS the body, not a title), the line must be at most max_words long and carry no red writer instruction, and a panel left with no body still declines. env ACCNOTBL_OFF turns it off (the whole accordion falls back to the hand-off box).

_comment: The RICH-accordion FALLBACK. The two strict paths above (#accordionTextOnly /
#accordionWithImages) decline the WHOLE accordion the moment a panel body is
richer than heading + iStock image + plain paragraphs. The human, however,
routinely builds panels that ALSO carry a [video] (YouTube), a BULLET list, and
occasionally a NESTED shapeHover (OSAI501-03 'When AI is not appropriate'). This
fallback fires ONLY when the strict paths returned null, so every accordion the
strict paths build is unaffected. It groups members into panels exactly like
#accordionWithImages, then renders each panel body in document order:
[image]->img (iStock, reusing #assetImage), [video]->the shared video.youtube
embed, black/[body] text->renderBlock (the converter's own #renderBlackText so
bullets become <ul><li> identically to the rest of the page), a NESTED
sub-bundle marker->renderNested (the converter's honest cv2-interactive
placeholder). Conservative — still NULL (whole accordion -> placeholder, never
half-built) on: a data table, a non-iStock image, a video with no resolvable id,
a panel with no heading or no rendered body, red writer-instruction text, or a
member it cannot place. env ACCRICH_OFF.
rich_panels.nested_placeholder_note: The nested sub-bundle is rendered via the converter's renderNested callback (#interactivePlaceholder), so it carries class=cv2-interactive and gets its own data-cv2-index + manifest entry.
rich_panels._note_panel_members: sub_headings — a panel's own [H2]-[H6] renders faithfully inside accContent (OSOH501-01 panel 4's [H5] Manaaki/Tika/Whanaungatanga); skip_instruction_members — a writer CS/Dev note inside a panel does not decline the build (it surfaces as the standard red cv2-note after the built widget via bundle.instructions); skip_list_marker_lines — a docx numbered-list artifact line ('1.') renders nothing; nested_built_wrap — a nested sub-bundle that BUILT for real (the READYSAFE tabs) wraps in the human's in-panel row. env ACCRICH2_OFF turns off all four.

_note: A captured data TABLE inside an accordion panel is ordinary panel CONTENT, and the human
ships it exactly that way (byte reference EXPFUN02_0.0's 'Success Criteria Phase Two' panel —

lead

then the kept table). The rich panel walk renders it through the converter's OWN
kept-table emitter (renderTable = TablesAndGrids.contentTable), so a panel table is identical
to any free-body table on the page — the same seam the rich TABS pane uses. Without it
#accordionRich and #accordionTextOnly would decline the whole widget at their catch-all, and
#accordionWithImages would SILENTLY DROP it (a table item carries no .text, so it would fall
through the blank-line guard and the accordion would build with the writer's table missing).
This rule applies to panels that have a HEADING. BARE-OPENER bundles where the writer gave no
panel heading at all and the table's own ROWS are the panels are a different builder (the
accordion sibling of tabs' rich_panes.table_panes): their panel headings are frequently
editorial and absent from the Writers Template (ENFUN04's human build invents 'Step
one/two/three'), so no heading is invented here.
NEVER HALF-BUILDS: no renderTable callback, no open panel, or an emitter returning nothing
all keep the honest hand-off box. env ACCTABLE_OFF turns off the whole rule.

rich._dangling_bracket_note: THE CLOSING BRACKET OUTSIDE THE COLOURED TEXT. Word lets a writer colour part of a line red and leave the rest black; TEDC402 typed two bubbles as '[speech bubble [/RED TEXT]🔴]' (the ']' beyond the colour boundary) and ENGI202's whole thought-bubble table hangs on the same '[Thought bubble ' span. The bubble's own bracket reader (#sbBrackets) demands a complete pair inside the span, so without this the invocation would fall to a designer note (TagNormaliser.Parse tolerates exactly this dangling form for classification, but the bubble builder does its own bracket reading). When true, a bracket that opens inside a red span and never closes is accepted as a marker; the orphan ']' left in the following black text is stripped by #sbRestText's STRAYLEAD rule. Env SBDANGLE_OFF.
rich._decline_note_patterns_note: THE QUIZ-FEEDBACK FENCE. A rich bundle carrying the writer's '[Auto feedback: …]' span (whole, or Word-split into 'Auto' + 'feedback:' pieces) is a TASK with a bubble beside it, never bubble content: TEDC402-6.0's 'Choose the format…' bubble would swallow the Pathway A/B task paragraphs plus their auto-feedback, and the human ships the bubble ALONE with the task as the activity's own body. Never half-build — the bundle keeps its honest hand-off box. Reversal rides SBFOREIGNTBL_OFF (the foreign-table walk-break is what makes these bundles reachable).
rich._tile_bubble_note:
[tile N] IS A BUBBLE. OSGM201-2.0 writes '[speech bubble with hover] Have six tiles surround the image three on each side.' then '[tile 1]'…'[tile 6]', each a bold line + bullets; the human's finished page shows each [tile N] IS a bubble (the bold line its first paragraph, the bullets the second). [tile N] resolves to the SUBTAG `shape n`, which the member reading does not otherwise recognise, so without this mapping every tile-carrying bundle declines. The invocation's own text is the writer's layout instruction and is demoted to the standard red Writers Note (§6). NAMED CAVEAT: the human packs all six balloons into ONE row's single column and joins each tile's bullets with
; PageForge uses its one-row-per-bubble convention (the human's usual form) with a
    body — every word right and in order, the arrangement differs. Kept OUT of tag_roles so it reverses independently. Env SBTILE_OFF.

multi_avatar._note: A bubble may carry MORE THAN ONE character picture. The writer lays out '[image] german-shepherd ║ [image] fun-bulldog ║ [speech bubble] Online bullying can be against the law!' in ONE table row (OSBY401-4.0, OSBY501-4.0), and both dogs belong to the one bubble. The human gives the arrangement: OSBY401_4.0 ships `row speechBubble > col-md-3 paddingR{img} + col-md-3 paddingL{img} + col-md-6 paddingL{bubble}` — the two pictures as consecutive columns in the bubble's own row, an ordinary shape in the human build. SCOPED TO IMAGES THAT ARRIVE BEFORE THE BUBBLE (the `pendingImgs` accumulation): an image arriving when the open bubble ALREADY has one still declines, which keeps SSCI104 out — its extra pictures are PROPS the writer asks Creative Services to composite into the character illustration ('Can Rocko be holding a calendar', 'Kiri dangling a pocket watch'), and the human answered that by hand-cutting one source illustration into rocko.jpg and kiri.jpg, neither of them derivable from the Writers Template. Emits one `image_col` per picture in document order, then the text column. Env SBAVATARS_OFF.

cast_row._note:
A group of character pictures with NO bubble of its own is a CAST ROW — the writer's row of characters beneath the bubble that introduces them. ENGR101-1.0 and -7.0 are the shape: one `[speech bubble]` cell ('Kia ora! We are the Te Kura News Team…') in table row 1, then FIVE `[image]` cells in table row 2. The human builds exactly this: ENGR101_01.0 ships the text-only bubble (`col-md-12 col-12 > bubble-basic no-hover bubble-top`) and then a PLAIN `
` of five `
` — the pictures OUTSIDE the bubble row, which is what this template reproduces. FENCED: `min_images` 2 means a bubble-less group holding exactly ONE picture still takes the trailing-image fold onto the last bubble. Env SBCASTROW_OFF.

mislabelled_media_image._note: A `[video]`/`[audio]` marker whose ONLY web address is a nameable iStock STILL image, and which carries no video host at all, is the writer mislabelling a picture — so it is read as an IMAGE instead of ending the widget. OSOH501-4.0: a 3x3 grid of four complete speech bubbles in which ONE middle cell is labelled `[video]` and holds https://www.istockphoto.com/photo/super-cow-3d-illustration-… . SELF-FENCING BY CONSTRUCTION: a decline_tags marker always ends the widget, so every bundle containing one would otherwise decline. A marker carrying a real YouTube/Vimeo address, or no address the iStock namer recognises, is untouched. Env SBVIDEOMISLABEL_OFF.

rich._note: The RICH GENERAL COMPOSER, run LAST so the four other branches keep their populations (a fallback cannot break what already works). Flattens members AND every table cell into an ordered stream of PARTS and emits ONE `row speechBubble` per bubble, in the human's most common forms (one bubble per row; avatar rows layout=speech, mostly bubble-right; image-less col-12 + bubble-basic bubble-top). Never half-builds: a foreign element with its own content, a captured non-bubble table, an un-nameable image, or a bubble with no text all decline. Env SBRICH_OFF.

_comment: speechBubble — a character image beside a STATIC speech/thought bubble of text.
CAPTURED AS: exactly ONE 1x2 table (one row, two cells) PLUS exactly one image URL in
the bundle's media. One cell is the writer's [image] tag + its iStock URL; the other is
the [speech bubble] tag + the bubble text. The cell ORDER decides which side the bubble is:
text cell first, image cell second  ->  bubble-LEFT  (text on the left, image on the right)
image cell first, text cell second  ->  bubble-RIGHT (image on the left, text on the right)
BUILT ONLY for the clean, single, STATIC (no-hover) bubble. The WHOLE widget falls back to
the orange placeholder (never half-built) the moment the capture is richer than that: a
'layout'/conversation modifier, 2+ images or 2+ rows/columns, a video URL instead of an
image, a non-iStock image we cannot name, a 'flipside'/front-back reveal, or ANY extra red
developer-instruction text in either cell (e.g. a 'CS: ...' note). Those stay visible flags,
faithful to the source — we never guess.
IMAGE honours the run's image Mode P/D exactly like every other image: Mode P shows a
placeholder + the commented-out real reference; Mode D emits the real . The iStock id
(the digits after 'gm' in the URL) becomes images/iStock-<id>.jpg, mirroring Emit_Templates.image.
Human reference (verbatim shape): 01-Finalized_Modules_/OSAI201/OSAI201-01.html (Aria, bubble-left).
TO RESTYLE (col widths, classes, the layout attribute) edit the strings below — no code change.
{text} = the bubble text; {image} = the rendered image; {layout} = layout_attr; {filename}/{label} = image slots.
speechBubble.image_only_media_note: The bubble TEXT may carry its OWN hyperlinks ([LINK: mailto:…]/[LINK: https://…]) which #harvestMedia collects into bundle.media alongside the one iStock image (as in OSAH501-03). Count the iStock IMAGES (the entries #istockFilename names) and require EXACTLY ONE; still bail on a video or a 2nd image. The non-image link URLs are the bubble's own links (the Lawdog Netsafe bullets). env SBLINKMEDIA_OFF uses the strict media.length===1 guard.

multi_wrapper._note:
THE WRAPPER-DIV RULE. WHENEVER the builder emits MORE THAN ONE

of bubble text (the ' / ' multi-paragraph path) OR a bulleted block (build_list), the human wraps the WHOLE text run in an EXTRA

nested inside a 'bubble-basic no-hover bubble-{side}' element (NOT the single-

'bubble-{side} no-hover'). {text} is the COMPLETE block run: '

..

..

' for the multi-paragraph path, or the '

../

    ..' block for the bulleted path. The human's genuinely multi-

    bubbles all use bubble-basic AND a wrapper — e.g. OSAH501-01/02/03, OSAI501-01/02, OSGM101/401, OSBY201-02, OSOH501. Single-

    bubbles are UNCHANGED (the rule is '>1

    '; the single-

    shape varies in the corpus and is left alone). The wrapper

    is required for correct CSS rendering of multi-line bubbles. Env SBWRAP_OFF uses the single 'bubble-{side} no-hover' + direct-

    / text_{side}_block form.
multi_wrapper._col_note: Keeps the builder's existing 'col-md-9 col-sm-8' bubble col (the human col width varies — col-md-8 col-6, col-md-9 col-sm-8, … — a pre-existing editorial variation NOT in scope here). Only the bubble-basic class + wrapper <div> are added.

speechBubble._build_list_note:
A BULLETED bubble ('intro / • item / • item / closing', as in OSBY201-02) is built as a

/

    structure (the human renders the list), not a placeholder. #bubbleBody groups the writer's '•'-led ' / ' parts into a
      and the rest into

      ; the text_*_block template (no outer

      ) wraps it so the

        isn't nested in a

        . CONSERVATIVE: only the clean ' / '-separated bullet form — a hard newline or a numbered list still keeps the placeholder. Env SBLIST_OFF.
speechBubble._filename_note: Mirrors Emit_Templates.image.filename_rules.istock so the bubble image stays editable in one place; the id is the run of 6-10 digits after 'gm' in the iStock URL.

no_table_image._note:
THE NO-TABLE AVATAR+BUBBLE FORM (the IMAGE-LESS form lives in text_only below). The static speechBubble branch only recognises the writer's TABLE dialect (exactly one 1x2 table, image cell + text cell). A large family of writers instead types the whole thing as ONE PARAGRAPH: '[Image] avatar Tina smiling [LINK: https://…gm…] [speech bubble] RHS '. That has no table, so without this form the bubble would fall to the developer hand-off box while its avatar rendered loose above it. The scanner's same_block_image_absorb (Interactive_Boundary_ChildTag_Bank._meta.member_rule) recovers the paragraph-mate [image]; this template block is the shape the branch emits. The human builds an avatar+bubble row for every one of these (TEDC401/TEDC402/SSCI104); its dominant column pair is 'col-md-2 offset-md-0 col-12 paddingR' | 'col-md-6 col-6' with class 'bubble-basic no-hover bubble-{side}' inside 'row speechBubble' and a single

. SIDE comes from the writer's ORDER exactly as the table branch derives it from cell order — image first => the image column leads and the bubble is bubble-right, as the human almost always does (the rare lefts are editorial one-offs). The writer's own side WORD is deliberately NOT read: it is rarely present and it is WRONG where it disagrees (TEDC401 says 'RHS' where the human ships bubble-left). env SBNOTBL_OFF turns off the whole form.

placeholder_character.todo: add this speech bubble's character picture in place of the grey 'Character' placeholder — the Writers Template names none, and the Online Safety / TEDC bubbles carry their character (Chris's D13-9).
placeholder_character._doc: In the OS* and TEDC* families only (the Online Safety / TEDC bubbles carry their character), a TEXT-ONLY bubble (no image, no table, no media) whose writer named NO picture — no picture word (picture_named_re) on its own tag line, where the tag-words note would carry 'avatar Tina … iStock' — takes the avatar form (the narrow builder's col-3 image column + col-md-9 col-sm-8 bubble-right) with the KB 04C placeholder image (never imageCentral), and ONE red Designer/Developer To Do follows the bubble group. Env SBPLACEHOLDER_OFF keeps the plain text-only form.

text_only._note:
THE TEXT-ONLY BUBBLE(S). A bubble the writer authors with NO character image and NO table ('[insert thought bubble] Where do we find stories? [insert thought bubble] Why are stories important?', ENGS404-00) is built, since all basic interactives the writer tags are built (the A1 writer's-tag branch). The human library itself uses the text-only bubble form often, and layout="thought" exists precisely for the thought wording (XDLS901 the reference). Emit shape = the human's most common form (col-12; bubble-basic no-hover bubble-top — the side/colour scatter is editorial C, this class string is the one data knob). One row per INTERACTIVE invocation member (the same-type merged '[thought bubble] … [thought bubble] …' paragraph ships one bubble each); >1

takes the wrapper

; layout follows the writer's own word via thought_re. Never-half-build guards in InteractiveBuilder.#speechBubbleTextOnly. env SBTEXT_OFF turns off the whole branch.

conversation._note: CONVERSATION layout: the writer authors '[speech bubble] Conversation layout' + alternating Prompt/AI-response BLACK lines (each line a turn). The human renders div.row.speechBubble > col-md-12 > alternating div.bubble-right.no-hover (the user/prompt turn) / div.bubble-left.secondary.no-hover (the AI response). InteractiveBuilder.#speechBubbleConversation builds it from the bundle's black members: STRICT alternation starting RIGHT (matches the human's turn-taking; OSAI401-01 conv #1 Prompt1/resp/Prompt2/resp/Prompt3/resp and conv #2 Prompt4 + 'Click to see its response'), with a content override (a line starting with a response_prefix forces left, a prompt_prefix forces right). Conservative: builds ONLY when the bundle is a clean black-line conversation (modifier mentions 'conversation' OR >=min_turns lines start Prompt/AI response) with NO table and NO face/reveal members; anything richer keeps the placeholder. Used in ENGC401, ENGS401, OSAI401, OSBY301, OSBY401.

speechBubble._droppable_span_note: Red spans in a bubble cell whose content STARTS WITH one of these (at a word boundary) are DROPPED before the build, keeping the surrounding learner text — so a clean bubble is not blocked by a developer's 'CS: …' manual-edit instruction (OSAI201 #1 'CS: can a cross be put through the brain image') or a 'flipside:' reveal LABEL (OSAI201 #8 — the bubble text after it is the second part, rendered via the ' / ' multi-paragraph path). The widget's own [image]/[speech bubble] tag span is kept; any OTHER unrecognised 2nd red span still bails (conservative). Read by InteractiveBuilder.#stripDevSpans.
speechBubble._paragraph_note:
The writer's ' / ' inside a bubble is a PARAGRAPH break when every part is sentence/paragraph-like — at least paragraph_min_words words AND containing ending punctuation (.!?); then the parts render as multiple

(OSAI501-02 #7's GenAI bubble). A ' / ' list of SHORT labels (or any bulleted/numbered bubble — OSBY301's kaitiakitanga list) is left as the honest placeholder. Lower this only if a genuine multi-paragraph bubble has unusually short paragraphs.

cell_face_split._note: T0, ONE CARD PER CELL with the faces marked INSIDE it: each cell is a whole card (ENGR102-3.0 '[H4] ai / [Image] Paint / [Body] paint / Back Try reading these words…', XGF9004-17.0 '[Front] … / [Back] …', CEDW501-5.0 '**Physical impacts** / [Reverse] …'). EVERY non-empty cell must split into a non-empty front and a non-empty back, so a table where only some cells carry a marker is a different shape and keeps its box. The marker may be a red span, a plain bracket, or the bare word, and may carry structural CO-TAGS ('[Back] [H3]') which are dropped. Env FLIPCELLFACES_OFF.

bold_lead_faces._note: The BOLD-LEAD front/back split, modelled byte-for-byte on TWHK901-0.0's human build: the bold opening phrase becomes the front <h5> with its colon dropped, and the WHOLE caption stays on the back unchanged. Fires ONLY when every resolved card has an EMPTY front and a bold-lead back, which is what makes it safe — a table where only some rows have a bold lead is a different shape and keeps its box (as in TWHK901, AGH1006, AGH1009, CEDK101). Env FLIPBOLDLEAD_OFF.

header_roles._note: A first row whose every non-empty cell NAMES a role ('Image | Title | Explanation', CEDO102-0.0) maps the remaining rows: one card per row, the Image cell the front picture, the Title cell the front heading and the Explanation cell the back. repeat_title_on_back follows CEDO102's own human build, which repeats the title as the back's heading. A role name must be the WHOLE cell, so a real card row can never be mistaken for a header. Also DROPS a role header the composer would otherwise read as a card (TWHK901's 'Images | Captions'). Env FLIPHEADROW_OFF.

general_cards._note: The general CARD composer, tried LAST so the other flipCard forms are unaffected. Cards resolve from an ordered delimiter vocabulary: T1 face-marker ROWS that repeat; T1b a face-marker COLUMN; T1c per-cell face markers riding with the content; T2 a TWO-ROW table with no markers, one card per COLUMN; T3 N x 2 rows; M1/M2 [Flip Card N] / [front]/[back] tags with a TEXT-ONLY front allowed; M3 face LABEL WORDS; M4 a bare MEDIA SERIES. A COMPLETED BACK ENDS A CARD, and content arriving while the FRONT is open is FRONT content. Text-only cards are common in the human library (a front is often a HEADING alone or a PARAGRAPH alone), so an image is never required; min_cards 1 for an explicit delimiter but 2 for an inferred one; NO length cap on a front (the human's fronts sometimes run past ten words); a label is NEVER invented. Env FLIPCARDS_OFF.

_comment: flipCard — a grid of cards, each a FRONT that flips to reveal a BACK.
CAPTURED AS: one 2-column table — column 1 is every card's FRONT, column 2 its BACK.
A leading column-label row (e.g. 'Image for one side | Text for flipped side', 'Front | Back')
is dropped (it matches the header keywords below, or is the writer's red instruction text).
Each CELL is rendered to one of two things:
• an IMAGE — when the cell carries an image reference (an iStock/.jpg URL, a [LINK: ...] to a
photo, or an [image] tag). It is emitted exactly like every other image, honouring Mode P/D
(Mode P = placeholder + commented real reference; Mode D = the real ).
• plain TEXT — the cell's black learner text (the writer's red label tags like [Front of card]/
[H4]/[Body] never reach the page). The writer's ' / ' (a slash with spaces) is the writer's

line-break and becomes
; **bold**/*italic* render normally.
BUILT ONLY when every cell is cleanly one of those two. The WHOLE widget falls back to the orange
placeholder (never half-built) if a TEXT cell still carries red developer-instruction text (a 'CS:'
note or an instruction we cannot safely drop — e.g. ENGI202's [Front of flip card] labelled cards),
if a cell is empty, has bullets, or the capture is wider than two columns / more than one table.
Human reference: 01-Finalized_Modules_/CEDO202 (text|image) and ENGJ302 (image|text).
{front}/{back} = the rendered cell; {text}/{filename}/{label} = the slots. Edit the strings to restyle.
flipCard._front_back_multirow_note: The MULTI-ROW alternating Front/Back flipCard (as in OSAH501-03). The writer lays the cards out as a [Flip card image] table: a Front|Back|Front|Back header over MULTIPLE data rows, each row holding width/2 cards (column-pairs col 2i = front, col 2i+1 = back). Each FRONT = '[body] **title** / [image] url' (image-front), each BACK = '[body] / Law: X / lead-in: / • a / • b' (a rich text + bullet list a flip back CAN hold). The human editorially rebuilt this as an accordion, but THAT choice is NON-DERIVABLE (Decision Framework A — no link from the writer's [Flip card image] tag), so the WRITER'S flipCard is built. Generalises the single-data-row form (#flipCardAlternating) to N data rows + a bulleted/rich back (#flipBackRich). InteractiveBuilder.#flipCardMultiRow strips the per-cell structural markup (#stripStructuralTags: [body]/[front]/[back]/[H#], red-wrapped or literal — [image] kept for image detection), then reuses #flipImageFront + #flipBackRich; emits tpl.card_image_front cards. Conservative (never half-build → orange placeholder): a clean Front/Back header (#looksLikeFlipHeader), >=2 data rows, every row width-wide, every card builds cleanly (a surviving CS note / empty cell / missing image|title fails the whole widget). Scoped width>=4 even, so the 2-col form (CEDO102/MXDB302/TRR114/XMES201) and the single-row form are untouched. Building it also removes the placeholder's literal-[tag] leak. Env FLIPMULTIROW_OFF gives the orange placeholder.

text_guard._doc_notes:
note_rows_after: a SPANNING NOTE ROW (exactly one non-empty all-black cell in a table at least two cards wide — the writer's closing sentence under the cards, AGH1006-2.0 'The graft support material can be removed once the graft is healed …') is not a card: the guard skips it, and when the build leaves it out it is emitted as a

after the cards (the members rule's placement) instead of vanishing.
text_guard._doc_roots:
Three causes of lost / garbled card text, under the same flag and env: header_black_label — #looksLikeFlipHeader reads a column LABEL from the cell's own short black words (<= header_max_words) whenever the row carries learner text, so a card row whose keyword only sits in the writer's red tags ('[Front] [Image: iStock: …] url / Retail | [Back] Providing good customer service …', PWY1002-3.1; CEDO502-5.0) is not dropped as the header (a row of picture labels alone keeps the plain reading); face_column_pairs — the composer's T1b face-label column reads EVERY consecutive front / back row pair (OSAI101-2.0 stacks two, so the second pair's cards are kept); br_after_inline — #flipCell renders each ' / ' line through the inline renderer BEFORE joining them with
(the renderer escapes markup, so a
joined first would show as a visible '<br>', as it would on ENGJ302-3.0).
text_guard._doc: THE BUILT FLIP CARD NEVER DROPS THE WRITER'S WORDS (e.g. CEDO502-5.0: a 2 x 2 table of whole-card cells that could be read as a header row + two picture-only cells — one card with eight sentences lost, where the human builds four). Every learner PART of the captured table (a cell split at ' / ' and line breaks; red spans, [tags], [LINK:] and URLs removed; >= min_words words) must be in the build's visible text; a part carrying a picture reference is the picture's label and a first row of short (<= header_max_words) keyword labels is the column header — both exempt. A lossy DIALECT build falls through to the general card composer; a lossy COMPOSER build keeps the hand-off box (never half-build). Env FLIPTEXTGUARD_OFF turns the guard off.

flipCard._transposed_note:
The TRANSPOSED multi-column form (as in OSBY201-02): a 2-ROW table whose COLUMNS are the cards (row 0 = the fronts '[front] / label / [image] url', row 1 = the backs '[back] / text'). Builds N image-front (placeholder image +

label

) / text-back cards via #flipCardTransposed, reusing #flipImageFront/#flipBack with the leading [front]/[back] face directive stripped. CONSERVATIVE (never half-build): exactly 2 rows, width>=2 (the 2-col front|back-per-row form is untouched), row 0 ALL fronts + row 1 ALL backs (either order), every card builds cleanly. Env FLIPTRANS_OFF.
flipCard._alternating_note:
The 'Flip card image' VARIANT (the alternating multi-column form, OSAI/OSBY/OSGM/OSOH/XGF/ENFUN/ENGI): a header row of Front|Back|Front|Back… labels over a SINGLE data row of 2N columns, each column-PAIR a card. Front cell is RICH ('Step N: title / [image] / url' → +

title

, image first); back cell is '/'-split paragraphs (**bold** kept). Conservative (never half-build → orange placeholder): built only when the header is a clean alternating Front/Back label set (#looksLikeFlipHeader), there are exactly 2 rows (header + data), every FRONT carries BOTH an image part AND a heading-text part, and no non-image red instruction survives in any cell. The 2-column front|back-per-row form is UNCHANGED (CEDO102/MXDB302/TRR114/XMES201). The OSAI201 two-

'Step N:'/title split is a NON-DERIVABLE editorial choice left as a single

. Env FLIPALT_OFF.

card_col_by_count._doc: THE FLIP-CARD COLUMN WIDTH FOLLOWS THE CARD COUNT: in the human build a 4-card group's cards are mostly `col-md-6 col-12 paddingLR`, and a 2-card group's likewise; 3 cards and 5+ cards are col-md-4 (the template default). A 1-card group is usually col-md-12 in the human build but is not listed (too few cases). `#flipCardsByCount` swaps `default` for the by_count class in each finished card at the four tpl.card join sites; the image-front card_image_front family is untouched. OFF = every card col-md-4.
card_col_by_count._exclude_doc: Per subject (module_meta.subject; the subject-less modules are the empty string): the gold's 4-card form is a TIE in 1-10 English (col-md-6 10 / col-md-3 9) and col-md-3-led in ConnectED (4 / 3) and NCEA1 (2 / 1); its 2-card form is col-md-4 in NCEA1 (2 / 2) and a tie in the subject-less TEDC modules (col-md-6 4 / col-md-4 3). Those keep the template default.

flipCard._member_image_cards_note: MEMBER-CAPTURED image-front cards: the writer authors NO table — instead [Flip Card N] then [Front][H4] title + [image] url + [back] text per card (OSAI501-03 'Brainstorm ideas / Summarise tricky concepts / Explore different perspectives / Improve grammar and structure'). The human builds a 2-wide IMAGE-FRONT grid: row.flipCardsContainer > col-md-6 col-sm-6 col-12 paddingLR > flipCard noBG > (front flipImage = img + h4) + (back = p). InteractiveBuilder.#flipCardMembers reuses #flipImageFront (img + h4 title) + #flipBack (p); fires ONLY when the bundle has no table AND every card has a clean image-front (image + title) + a back (else null → keep the placeholder, never half-build). The TABLE forms are untouched (tables.length guard). Env FLIPMEMBER_OFF gives the placeholder.

general_panes._note: The general PANE composer, tried LAST so the other tabs forms are unaffected, and deliberately NOT registry-gated (the registry is not what limits these builds; the writer's tag is the target, per the A1 ruling). Panes resolve from an ordered delimiter vocabulary: D1 [Tab N] tags; D2 a table read COLUMN-major (header row = labels, plus a role-labelled first column, and a peeled leading single-cell TITLE row); D3 a table read ROW-major or a one-row table one pane per CELL; D4 a repeating same-level heading run. Following the human build: min_panes 2 because a ONE-pane tab group never occurs; labels are short (almost always ≤ 6 words), so the cap stays 6; labels ship PLAIN. Guards: a wholly-red label row, duplicate labels, an orphan leading '/'. Env TABPANES_OFF.
general_panes._note_dupehead: A sub-heading repeating the panel's OWN title is a duplicate, not content (the accordion's `panel_delimiters.drop_duplicate_head`, env ACCDUPEHEAD_OFF, implemented in #accResolvePanels). Recorded here only as a pointer; the flag lives on the accordion. Otherwise a panel's entire body can be its own title repeated (as in XDLS501-2.0), which the human never ships; its look-alikes carry a button or an audioImage grid a text-only test cannot see.
general_panes._note_rules: The rules below each handle a writer shape that #tabsPanes would otherwise decline, and each follows a page whose human build ships the same labels. In the human build labels are short (never more than 7 words) and plain, a pane often holds a picture (and sometimes a video), and there are no one-pane groups.

marker_bracket._note: A [Tab N] BRACKET RIDING ON ANOTHER TAG. Writers put the pane marker in the SAME red span as the thing that opens the pane: '[Tab 1] [H3] Read about it' (XGF9006-6.0), '[Tab 1] [H2] Building the basics' (XGF9003-0.0), '[Tab 1 - Maori] [Video 1]' (CEDW101-0.0). The span's PRIMARY tag is then h3/h2/video, so a delimiter test that only looks when the primary is already 'tab n' would never see it. As with clickDrop's delimiter_multi_bracket, every bracket of the span is offered to the pattern in turn; the result matches the human build (XGF9006, XGF9003, most of CEDW101). The member's own content then becomes that pane's first content, so nothing is displaced.
marker_bracket._note_deny: A NAME IS NOT A TAG WORD. HPFUN301-0.0 writes '[Tab 1 - H3] How to stay confident' — the 'H3' is the writer telling the designer the HEADING LEVEL to use, not the tab's name; read as the label it would give three tabs all called 'H3'. When the captured label is a structural tag word the marker is treated as having no label, and the pane takes its name from its own first sub-heading.

cell_inner_tags._note: A TABLE CELL CARRIES ITS OWN NAMING MARKER. The writer lays the whole set out as one table and tags each cell from the inside: '[Tab 1] Video / [insert video] …' (XMES103-3.0), '[H3] **File systems, folders and metadata**' over '[Body] …' (TEDC402-4.0), '[tab title: Level 1] …' (TEDC401-4.0) — the clickDrop T0 reading applied to tabs; the result matches the human build (XMES103, TEDC402). A column whose header cell names no pane AND whose content cells are empty is not a pane and is dropped (TEDC402's [RHS] avatar column, which the human also omits); a column that names a pane but has nothing behind it declines the whole build, per never-half-build.

marker_row._note: A WHOLLY-RED ROW IS EITHER A ROLE ROW OR THE LABEL ROW. A wholly-red row is normally refused, because a flipCard table is laid out as entirely-red [front]/[drop] rows over the card faces — but OSAI201-3.0 IS that shape and its human developer built TABS from it, taking the four labels from the row BENEATH the 'front' marker row. So: a wholly-red row whose cells reduce to a ROLE WORD names the row beneath it (label row, then content rows); a wholly-red row whose cells reduce to real, distinct, short TEXT is the label row itself (TEDC401-1.0's 'Tab 1: Step 1'). Anything else still declines. Both match the human build (OSAI201, TEDC401-1.0).

label_prefix_strip._note: THE 'Tab N' PREFIX ON A LABEL CELL. The writer numbers the label so its order cannot be mistaken — 'Tab 1: Step 1' — and the human ships 'Step 1'. The separator is OPTIONAL because the writer often leaves it out: OSSC401-3.0 writes a red '[Tab 1]' marker then black 'Ari's story', which would otherwise concatenate into the label 'Tab 1 Ari's story' while the human ships 'Ari's story'. A bare 'Tab 1' with nothing after it never matches, so a label cannot be emptied.

opener_label._note: THE OPENER REPEATS AND CARRIES THE LABEL. PHE1007-1.0 writes '[Tabs – tab one] Skeletal muscle', '[Tabs – tab two] Smooth muscle', '[Tabs – tab three] Cardiac muscle'. The opener tag is skipped as carrying no content of its own, so the label would go with it. When the OPENER tag repeats with an ordinal or number in its bracket AND its own trailing text, each occurrence opens a pane named by that text (as the human build does).

lead_before_first_pane._note: CONTENT BEFORE THE FIRST DELIMITER IS THE WIDGET'S OWN LEAD, rendered above the tabs in the writer's place rather than disqualifying the whole reading — the same rule clickDrop and the accordion use. Otherwise the table reading, which demands that EVERY other part be plain text, would refuse the widget outright when a single [H3] rides along with the table (as in TEDC401-1.0). Only a heading or plain text may lead; anything richer still means the walk swept a section in.

_comment: tabs — a strip of clickable tab headings, each revealing its own content pane.
CAPTURED AS MEMBERS (not a table), exactly like accordion: a [tabs] opener, then one [Tab N] tag
per tab whose TRAILING text is that tab's HEADING (e.g. [Tab 1] Mat 1), followed by the tab's body
paragraph(s). An optional [Tabs end here] closer is ignored.

heading ->
    one
  • ...
    • per tab

body ->
one
per tab (one

per paragraph)
BUILT ONLY when every tab is a plain HEADING + body TEXT. The whole widget falls back to the orange
placeholder (never half-built) if the bundle is richer than that: a tab whose content is a DATA TABLE
(e.g. BLL233's letter tables) or an image/nested widget, a tab missing its heading, or red writer-
instruction text inside a tab. Those richer tabs stay honest placeholders.
Human reference: 01-Finalized_Modules_/ENGJ301 (text panes); BLL233 shows the table-pane case we skip.

{head} = the tab heading; {content} = one

...

per body paragraph.
LIST-OPENER form: some writers author the [tabs] widget NOT as [Tab N] tags
but as a flat '• Term – description' bullet list (HES1003 tikanga principles: Whanaungatanga,
Aroha, Mana, Tiaki, Wairua, Rongo). When the bundle has NO [Tab N] member, list_opener builds one
tab per top-level bullet: nav label = the Term (text before the first en/em-dash), pane = the
description after it. CONSERVATIVE: every line must be a clean top-level '• Term – desc' bullet
(>= min_tabs of them, the Term <= max_label_words long, no nested/indented sub-bullet, no media,
table, extra widget type or red writer-instruction) — otherwise the whole widget stays the honest
orange placeholder (never half-built). The human REWRITES each pane's prose editorially, so only
the tab STRUCTURE + the derivable Term labels are reproduced; the pane text is the writer's own.
RICH [Tab N] panes (the rich-accordion sibling). The strict [Tab N] path declines the whole widget the
moment a pane is richer than heading + plain text. The human, however, builds [Tab N] panes holding an
iStock IMAGE (HPFUN401/OSAI501), a kept data TABLE (the BLL letter mats — BLL232/233/236/245), and text
with a bold lead. #tabsRich fires ONLY when the strict path declined AND the GOLD-CHOICE REGISTRY row
below says the human builds TABS for a clean [Tab N] bundle in this subject|template group — the SAME WT
form is built by the human as an ACCORDION on OSAI|9-10 (OSAI401) + OSBY|NCEA (OSBY501), so those groups
have NO row and keep the honest placeholder. NEVER half-builds: a red instruction, an extraTypes merge,
an unlabelled tab, a non-iStock image, a caption riding an image cell, an unresolvable video, or any
member it cannot place (buttons/external links — HES1005/XLP06) falls back to the placeholder. LABEL
RULE: a [Tab N]'s first blackAfter line is the label — the whole SHORT line (<= max_label_words), or the
**bold lead** of a long line (label = the lead, the whole line stays as the pane's first paragraph —
HPFUN401's human form). env TABRICH_OFF.
THE GOLD-CHOICE ROWS: subject|template groups where the human builds TABBED NAV from a clean
[Tab N] bundle. series = per-module override. ANTI-ROWS (the human builds an ACCORDION from the
same form — never add): OSAI|9-10, OSBY|NCEA. XLP|combo is MIXED -> no row. HPFUN902
(HPFUN|combo, an accordion in the human build) is fenced by the clean-label guard: its [Tab N]s
carry no label line. SSEA| = SSEA203 (writer: '[tabs] or accordion if that suits better' — the
human chose tabs).
The HEADING-DELIMITED tabs form. A [tabs] bundle with NO [Tab N] members whose panes the writer
delimits with SAME-LEVEL [H2]-[H6] section headings (PHE1005 '[activity interactive - tabs] …' +
[H3] 'What is hauora?' + [body] …; MXFL401 '[tabs] headings: rates; insurance; …' + [H3] sections).
One pane per heading; the label is the heading's first blackAfter line (the rich_panes label rules:
short line, ** stripped). Members render via the SAME rich_panes machinery (#tabsRichPart).
Registry-gated per-FORM (registry below, from the human build): the heading form's own row set —
NEVER the [Tab N] rows above. NEVER half-builds: an instruction/noise member, mixed heading levels,
a long heading before min_panes complete, red text, a url-less image mid-widget, an unresolvable
video, a button/link/nested widget — all return null (usually the orange placeholder). TWO
section-break rules from the human build: (1) a LONG same-level heading (> max_label_words, no clean
label) AFTER >= min_panes complete panes is the writer's NEXT SECTION (MXFL401 '**But how did
Alan…**' — the human renders it OUTSIDE the widget) -> the widget closes, the heading + its following
plain text render AFTER via trailing_body; (2) a URL-LESS [image] member once the panes are complete
(PHE1005 '[insert item 3]' — a media-list reference, the human ships the img AFTER the widget) ->
rendered after the widget via the renderImage hook (the NORMAL body-path Mode P/D emitter —
MediaBuilder.image conventions). dedup_identical_panes: an EXACT duplicate pane (same folded label
+ same folded content — a writer copy-paste, MXFL401 'Power' ×2; the human ships it once) is
dropped. env TABHEAD_OFF turns off the whole form.
heading_panes.hover_marker_continuation_note: A data-marker member whose folded span is a hover/rollover definition ([hover over definition: see], PHE1005) is the writer's INLINE trigger mid-paragraph — its blackAfter is the paragraph's continuation and merges into the pending text (the marker itself is consumed; the definition is not woven here). Any OTHER data marker ([caption]/[item N]) declines the build.

_comment: THE GOLD-CHOICE ROWS for the HEADING form: PHE|NCEA (PHE1005, PHE1003), MXFL|9-10 (MXFL401),
PES|NCEA (PES1008) — the human builds tabs from this form there. NO-ROW groups: XGF|combo MIXED
(XGF9003 tabs but XGF9004 none, XGF9006 partial), AGH|NCEA partial (AGH1006 — its tab group is
TABLE-driven, the table form's territory). PES1008 + PHE1003 carry rows but may still decline on
the guards (url-less mid-widget images / instruction members).
The TABLE-SOURCED form: the writer authors the whole tab set as ONE table straight after the
[tabs] invocation — the HEADER ROW carries the tab labels ('**Bias**|**Outliers**|**Assumptions**',
red 'Tab 1: Step 1' / 'Level 1' title cells), and each COLUMN's content cell(s) carry that pane's
body (TEDC402's human build: nav Bias/Outliers/Assumptions, each pane the column's paragraphs +
bullet lists). Registry-gated per FORM — the rows below are the TABLE form's own gold choices:
TEDC| (the human mostly builds tabs) → row; ENFUN|combo MIXED → NO row (ENFUN05/08 are the
counter-example modules); PES|NCEA's clean candidates hide EMBEDDED images in empty table rows
(the media-list-image class) → no row; XLP|combo's bundle trails a [shape n] widget invocation → no
row. NEVER half-builds — declines keep the placeholder: a lead member before the table (TEDC401
1.0), ≠1 table (over-capture: TEDC402 3.0 input/memory + its drag-drop spec table), a ragged/1-row
table (XMES103 cell-as-pane sub-form), a dirty header cell (the [RHS]+[Image] avatar COLUMN —
TEDC402 4.0), a RED content cell (the writer's OWN other-widget spec — TEDC402 6.0's 5x4 dataset
table is built by the human as clickDrop buttons: the guard agrees), an EMPTY content cell (an
embedded image the docx cell extractor cannot see — PES1004's graphs), a trailing button ([Button:
go to journal] → the human's h4.goJournal) / link / marker / widget / second table. TRAILING
allowed: an [image] member → rendered AFTER via the renderImage hook (the heading-form rule;
TEDC402's avatar — the bubble TEXT is scanner-absorbed into its own speechBubble bundle and builds
separately) + that image's own instruction reference (pose + iStock catalogue line) → a retained
CS note (cv2-note); plain black sentences → trailing_body. env TABTABLE_OFF.
The TITLE-ROW column-form sub-form (as in CEDT501). Some subjects author a COLUMN tab table
with a leading single-cell [H*] TITLE row above the [tab N] label row, and a label cell shaped
'label / (sub-description)'. The human builds tabs and floats the title as a heading before the
nav + the sub-description as the pane's lead line. A subject listed here may build via
#tabsTablePanes even without a table_panes.registry 'tabs' verdict, but ONLY when the exact
signature is present (single-cell [H*] row 0 + >=2 [tab N] cells in row 1); SSCI104/TEDC401/
XMES103 are other sub-forms and do NOT match. Env TABTITLEROW_OFF. Non-derivable editorial
differences (C): the human relocates the title into the PRECEDING text row at an editorial <h4>
(page relevel gives h3) and italicises the parenthetical lead — the build ships the derivable
structure.
THE GOLD-CHOICE ROWS for the TABLE form. TEDC| covers TEDC401+TEDC402 (Digital Technologies,
phase-blank template) — the human builds tabs from the clean header-label tables; TEDC401's
bundles may still decline on the guards (lead members / trailing buttons / red matrix cells).
NO-ROW groups: ENFUN|combo (MIXED, the counter-example set), PES|NCEA (embedded-image rows),
XLP|combo (trailing widget), XMES|1-3 (1-row cell-as-pane sub-form), and single modules in
AGH/CEDO/CEDT/MXFU/OSAI/OSOH/OSSC/SSCI where the human build has no tabs or only partial ones.

row_panes._comment:
The ROW-per-tab TABLE form — the column-form sibling (as in OSOH501-01 READYSAFE): a [tabs] bundle capturing ONE table where each ROW's label cell carries [tab N] (label = the cell's remaining text, ** stripped) and the OTHER cell is the pane ([image] URL / [H4] heading / [body] text segments, slash-separated). Only a few modules author it (OSOH501, OSOH201, CEDT501) and the human builds a tabs nav on all of them — subjects gates it to those prefixes (the gold-choice discipline). Panes ship img +

+

in segment order (the human's OSOH501-01 pane shape). NEVER half-builds: !=1 table, a lead member,

members.note: The table-slides carousel builds from the TABLES alone, so without this every other member of the bundle would be dropped — the writer's paragraph before the table, the caption / [body] after it — text the human keeps. A black paragraph or a [body] with words before the first table renders through the free-body block emitter BEFORE the carousel and one after the last table AFTER it (the OSGM501-01 trailing-caption precedent, lists intact); blank lines and instruction-class tags are skipped; a paragraph opening with a developer cue (note_cue_pattern) declines; ANY other member — a heading, an image / video / other tag, words between the slide tables, a table beyond the slides — cannot be rendered from inside the widget seam, so the build DECLINES and the hand-off box keeps every member (never half-build). CARMEMBERS_OFF=1 = the other members are silently dropped.

table_slides.heading: {text}
table_slides._note: THE TABLE-SLIDE FALLBACK, tried LAST in #carousel so every dialect above is unaffected. ONE DATA ROW IS ONE SLIDE (the human's own rule); a single-row table is one slide per CELL (the media-table form); a leading header/label row is dropped. A cell becomes ordered PARTS through the rich walk's vocabulary, so a table-authored carousel and a member-authored one render identically. min_slides 2 follows the human build (a 1-slide carousel is almost unheard of). NEVER HALF-BUILDS: no parts, a red developer instruction, too few/many slides, no real content, or a finished carousel still showing a bracketed tag (leak_guard). See also dangling_marker_repair + leak_pattern_dangling. Env CARTABLE_OFF.

story_shell.todo_template: Build this carousel from the pages of the story{title}{set} — one slide per page (the human's form: images/<story title>/<story title>-01.jpg, -02.jpg …); source: {url}
story_shell._doc: The writer asks for a decodable / School Journal STORY to be paged through as a carousel — `[carousel]` + `[embed book 1] Are we able to embed just the story … into a carousel so it's like turning the pages` + `The story ‘Zac hid from Dad’ can be found - (in Set 5)` + the story's PDF link (BLL152 / BLL211 / … the BLL1 / BLL2 phonics families). The human builds `div.row.carousel > viewer > item.image > img` × the story's pages, cut from the PDF by hand (BLL152-2.0) — the page count is nowhere in the WT, so the SLIDES are not derivable, but the SHELL is: the ordinary-text path (elements.embed_story_carousel) emits exactly that shell for an `[embed story]` line, and a member captured inside a carousel bundle would never reach it. ON (#carouselStoryShell, dispatched AFTER #carouselRich and before the table-slide last resort, so every other carousel build is unaffected): with no table and no merged type, the members from the opener on are walked — a tag whose first bracket matches reference_pattern (and not exclude_pattern) is a story REFERENCE; once one is seen, a tag with no primary tag whose words match run_line_pattern (≤ run_line_max_words words) and a black line of ≤ run_black_max_words words (the link, `(in Set 5)`, `……`) belong to it; the reference run ends at the first other member. It emits the story shell (the carousel's own open / close + elements.embed_story_carousel's item and placeholder image) and a `Designer/Developer To Do:` note (todo_template: the story title from title_pattern, the set from set_pattern, the source link — the run's own URL, else the bundle's first non-video media link; NO link → the box is kept). The reference tags' own words (the writer's request) become the Writers Note after the widget (≥ request_min_words). AFTER the run: a black line or a `[body]` renders after the shell through the free-body emitter (the discussion questions), an instruction-class tag is skipped (already the Writers Note), anything else → null (the hand-off box keeps every member). Env CARSTORY_OFF.

same_type_merge._note: 'carousel + carousel' in a bundle's extraTypes is only the un-built placeholder LABEL, not a genuinely mixed widget (as with the accordion and tabs self-merge). Env CARSAMETYPE_OFF.

carousel._meta: Carousel auto-build (conservative). TWO clean forms: (1) homogeneous VIDEO carousel — every slide a YouTube video (item_video); (2) image+caption TABLE carousel — a 2-column table pairing a derivable image-URL cell with a [body] caption cell (item_image). InteractiveBuilder.#carousel keeps the placeholder the moment the data is richer/ambiguous: a non-YouTube video, a mixed/text slide, <min_slides slides, a 3+-column or irregular table, an image cell with no derivable istock id, or red developer-instruction text. Structure uses the dominant form below; the human's exact item/videoSection/col classes VARY by series (item vs item.video/item.image, videoSection icon vs plain, col-12 vs col-md-12 viewer), so what matters is the CONTENT (video IDs / image ids + captions). {embed} fills from Emit_Templates.video.youtube; {image} honours image Mode P/D like every other image; the iStock id (digits after 'gm' in the URL) → images/iStock-<id>.jpg. A leading single-cell [Title] row and an 'Images | Text' column-label row are dropped; a trailing non-slide [body] paragraph after the table renders as free body (trailing_body). Human reference: 01-Finalized_Modules_/OSGM501/OSGM501-01.html. Empty-image / member-text / mixed carousels stay honest placeholders.

item_video_with_caption._doc: A CAROUSEL VIDEO SLIDE WITH A CAPTION IS `item video`: the human's video-carrying carousel slides that also hold a carousel-caption block almost always carry the class `item video`, across the families. A video-ONLY slide has no consistent human form and stays `item`; a slide with a heading or a bare paragraph stays `item`. In #carRenderSlides, when the slide's chunks hold a videoSection AND the caption block was opened, `from` is swapped for `to` in the finished item. The media-caption-table builder keeps its own item_video_caption template. OFF = plain `item`.

carousel._image_slides_note:
The MEMBER-based image-slide carousel (the OSAI201-03 scenario form): a [carousel] opener then per slide a [heading]/[story heading] + an [image] + a [black] body. Builds one item_image_heading per slide —

heading

+ the Mode-P/D image + a carousel-caption whose

s are the body split on newlines (each via renderInline, so **Scenario:**/**Caution:** render as ). #carouselImageSlides; conservative — a slide missing its image or body, a non-iStock image, or any surviving red instruction → null (the orange placeholder, never half-build). The video and image-caption-TABLE forms are separate. The human's editorial caption styling (un-bolding 'Scenario:', bolding the whole 'Caution:' line, dropping the ⚠️) is NON-DERIVABLE and rendered here via the standard inline convention. Env CARIMG_OFF.

rotate_banner._meta: ROLLING/ROTATING BANNER (as in BLL117-02). A [rolling banner]/[rotating banner]/[banner] folds to a carousel bundle (widget_type_taxonomy rotateBanner->carousel) but the HUMAN builds a looping image STRIP (div.rotateBanner > div.bannerContainer > div.bannerItem*N > img), NOT a slideshow viewer. InteractiveBuilder.#rotateBanner builds it when bundle.variant === 'rotateBanner' from the single captured URL table: ONE bannerItem per non-empty cell, traversed COLUMN-MAJOR (the human source order). Each image is the standard Mode-P/D placeholder (the iStock id in the cell URL -> images/iStock-<id>.jpg, shown as a placehold.co placeholder + the commented real ref — the actual asset is dropped in by the developer post-conversion, exactly like every other image). CONSERVATIVE never-half-build: a non-iStock / unresolvable cell, no table, or <min_items resolvable images -> null (keeps the honest placeholder). alt is left empty (placeholder); the human's alt is the editorial Media-List description. Human ref: 01-Finalized_Modules_/BLL117/BLL117-03.html (Activity 2E). Env ROTBANNER_OFF.

carousel.rich_slides_accordion_sibling_note: see interactive_builders.accordion.rich_panels.head_from_first_line — the accordion half of the same rule (build the writer's tagged widget).

member_vocabulary._note: The member vocabulary the rich slide walk reads. A non-iStock image takes the url-SLUG placeholder; an image with no url, or an unembeddable video/[embed], is an ASSET REQUEST — skipped and surfaced as the standard red Writers Note (never a silent drop, never an invented filename); [Caption] resolves to the CANONICAL tag 'data marker'; [audio] is slide content; a REPEATED [carousel] once a slide holds content is a SLIDE MARKER. Env CARMEMBER_OFF.

rich_slides.heading: {text}

_note: VIDEO URL RECOVERY. The dominant dialect is the BLL phonics video list — the writer puts the
video's TITLE on the [video] tag and the bare URL on the FOLLOWING line, but colours that line
RED, so it reaches the builder as a tag member with no primary rather than the plain `black`
line the video_tail_url lookahead reads. Without this the URL is never found, the video resolves
no id, and the WHOLE carousel falls back to a hand-off box.
follow_any_member: the recovery walks forward up to follow_window members of ANY type,
skipping blank filler, and takes the first line that IS a video URL (a line with prose
of its own is not a reference line and stops the walk). It stops at the first member
carrying a real primary tag, so a URL belonging to a different element can never be
stolen, and at a table/nested member. Reachable ONLY for a [video] with no URL of its
own, so the rule is strictly ADDITIVE and cannot change a carousel that builds without it.
other_hosts: a URL the YouTube-id regex cannot read does not decline the whole carousel.
A YouTube SHORTS url ships the media_table.shorts_embed 1x1 form (as the human does)
and any other embeddable url ships video.generic_iframe — mirroring exactly what the
free-body media emitter (MediaBuilder.media) does for the same URL, so a video
inside a carousel and the same video in the body render by one convention.
drop_bare_url_lines: a slide line that is NOTHING BUT a bare video URL is that video's
REFERENCE, not learner prose — the human never ships a bare URL as a carousel caption, the
same convention MediaBuilder applies on the body path (stripMediaResidue). Without it every
URL line the tail lookahead did not claim would render as a visible link paragraph on the slide.
deny_extensions keeps the recovery from adopting a PDF/document/image/audio link as a
'video' (the [embed story] decodable-PDF family is a DIFFERENT class — see story_shell).
env CARVIDEO_OFF turns off both halves; CARVIDTAIL_OFF turns off the whole tail
lookahead including its black-line form.

media_series._note: The MEDIA-SERIES refinements (as in ENGS404). media_opens_slide (env CARMEDSLIDE_OFF): in a bundle with NO [Slide N] markers, each image/video member OPENS its own slide — the writer's back-to-back media list is one slide per item ('[image 1]..[image 4]' = 4 slides; 2 [video]s = 2 slides, rather than piling into ONE slide and failing min_slides); a heading/prose-opened slide still receives its FIRST media item, so the heading+image dialect is unchanged. video_tail_url (env CARVIDTAIL_OFF): a [video]/[insert video] member with no URL of its own takes it from the immediately-following black link/title line (the title-anchored link class inside a widget); the line is consumed as that video's reference. Pairs with the scanner's member_rule.media_series_break (env CARSERIES_OFF), which stops the run's capture at the first following non-media element.

go_journal_member._note: The accordion's go-to-journal rule applied to the carousel. The scanner's member_rule.button_tail_terminates deliberately EXCLUDES a go-to-journal button (go_journal owns it, and releasing it produces a duplicate button), so it stays a captured member, and the member walk would otherwise decline on it as an unrecognised piece. It is SKIPPED as slide content and the shared go_journal <h4 class="goJournal"> is emitted after the widget, via the SAME #accGoJournalHtml helper and the SAME #accIsGoJournal predicate the accordion uses, so the two can never drift apart. The human almost never puts a button inside a carousel's viewer, so a trailing button belongs after the widget. `bundle._goJournalEmitted` stops the go_journal member branch shipping a second identical heading. Env CARGOJOURNAL_OFF.

slide_label._note: THE NUMBERED SLIDE LABEL. Two writer dialects that are one rule underneath: the label rides the widget's OWN invocation ('[Carousel] Slide 1' … 'Slide 3', SSEA203-1.0/2.0) or it is a red span the normaliser resolved to NO structural tag ('Image 1: ', HPFUN102/HPFUN202-0.0; 'Picture 1: dormant trees during winter', AGH1001-4.0). Neither reaches a delimiter otherwise: the invocation branch (invocation_opens_slide) only opens a slide when one is ALREADY open, so a bundle whose every image is an asset request would never open its first; and a no-primary span is read as prose, so a whole run would pile into ONE slide and fail min_slides. The label itself is CHROME — the human captions no slide 'Slide 1' — and whatever follows it on the line is that slide's content (a media url becomes the picture or the embed, the rest becomes the caption), so nothing the writer typed is lost. SCOPED BY CONSTRUCTION to members with no primary tag plus the widget's own invocation: TWHA906-0.0 writes 'Slide 2: [body text]' on a real [body] ELEMENT and is invisible to the rule, so its build is unaffected.
