NEVER HALF-BUILDS: a rising number series is required (a lone label or a repeated 'Slide 1' is not a series), and any slide a label opened that resolves to NOTHING declines the whole build — MXEO201-5.0's 'Slide 2:' is a bare link to an external resource page we cannot embed and carries no words of its own. A caption-only slide (no /

rich_slides._note: THE RICH SLIDE FALLBACK, the carousel's sibling of the rich_panels accordion fallback. If the writer has specified a carousel, a carousel is generated (the Decision Framework's A1 branch): the human developer's finished page may show an accordion or plain body instead, but that substitution follows unrecorded feedback after the first version was handed over, so it is NOT the target; the writer's tag is. So the build is judged on the carousel's own correctness and the writer's tag (the Decision Framework's precedence rule). The other branches each recognise ONE authoring dialect — a captured image/caption TABLE, image slides that ALL carry both an image and a caption, or a member run of BARE video URLs — and decline wholesale on anything else. This fallback runs LAST (every carousel those branches build is unaffected) and composes slides in document order from whatever the writer actually supplied: a [Slide N] marker or a heading opens a slide, and a slide may hold any mix of heading, iStock image, YouTube video and prose. NEVER HALF-BUILDS — it returns null (keeping the honest hand-off box) on a captured data table, an extra merged widget type, a nested sub-bundle, red writer-instruction text inside slide content, a non-derivable image or video URL, a member tag it does not recognise, an empty slide, or fewer than min_slides / more than max_slides slides. env CARNOTBL_OFF turns it off.

carousel._note_caption_title:
caption_title_bold — the human's slide-title FORM splits by group: the listed subject prefixes ship the title as the caption's first

title

line (form B, as in OSOH) while the default stays the OSAI

-above-img form (A). item_image_caption — the pre-rendered-caption item shell used by form B and by a slide whose heading the writer forgot (OSOH501-02 slide 4; the human's title there is not in the WT — C, the slide ships body-only). env CARCAP_OFF uses the single h4 form.

media_table._note: The media-TABLE slideshow build (as in CHFUN01, 'MAKE INTO CAROUSEL!'): a carousel bundle whose single captured table passes the scanner's media-cell test builds one slide per cell in cell order — [image] cells via the standard Mode P/D asset machinery (no caption div unless the cell carries one), [video] cells via the shared video.youtube embed (a /shorts/ URL takes the youtubeShort 1x1 form, as the CHFUN human builds always do) + a carousel-caption from the cell's [caption] text. Never half-builds: an unresolvable cell (no URL / no nameable image / unknown host) keeps the hand-off box. Slides ship PLAIN videoSection (no icon) — the CHFUN family is not an icon group. Env toggle: CARMEDTBL_OFF.

media_caption_table._note:
THE MEDIA|CAPTION TABLE dialect — the writer authors the slideshow as ONE table whose every DATA ROW pairs a MEDIA cell ([video]/[image] red tag + URL) with a PROSE cell carrying the slide's title and copy, the writer's ' / ' separating each rendered paragraph ('**Tech support** / Scammers often make... / **Example:** A pop-up...'). media_table owns the all-media-cell form and DECLINES this one (the prose cell fails its media-cell test); #carouselImageTable owns the image|caption form. This branch is therefore VIDEO-SCOPED (require_video) so the image-only tables stay with their own builder. The human's video slides with a heading mostly use an h5 title and put the TEXT FIRST — i.e.
title

copy

* {media}
, byte-matching the OSSC401 and ENGS401 human builds. Title = the leading wholly-BOLD segment (the writer's own emphasis); a row whose prose cell has no bold lead ships copy-only. NEVER HALF-BUILDS: a row without exactly one resolvable media cell + one prose cell, an un-nameable image, an unknown video host, or fewer than min_rows rows keeps the hand-off box. The video form appears in ENGS401, HPFUN302, OSSC401. Env toggle: CARMEDCAP_OFF.
media_caption_table.title: {text}

general_items._note: The general ITEM composer, tried LAST so the other clickDrop forms are unaffected. Items resolve from an ordered delimiter vocabulary: D1 labelled [click drop N] tags over the full member vocabulary; D2 a captured TABLE read five ways (T0 self-delimited CELLS, T1 a face-marker COLUMN, T2/T3 a peeled header then N x 2 rows, T4 one item per COLUMN, T5 one item per CELL); D3 a repeating same-level HEADING run. Two general rules carry it: content before the first button is the widget's own LEAD prose, rendered above the widget in the writer's place rather than thrown away, and a run of media immediately before a delimiter belongs to the item it opens. Following the human build: min_items 1 for an explicit delimiter (a one-item clickDrop is its most common form) but min_inferred_items 2; label_max_words 8 (the human's labels are almost always ≤ 3 words and virtually never over 8); a label is NEVER invented, a bare URL is never a label, and a panel with no visible text is a half-build. Env CLICKDROPS_OFF.

scrap_release._doc_release_more: Env CDSCRAPREL2_OFF: (c) release_marker_pattern — a scrap whose marker is the writer's choice-board form `[Click Drop Activity N with (image) embedded image]` (XDLS903–906) releases its otherwise-refused members: XDLS906-3.0 typed `[Activity] **3E**` BEFORE its `Judge` button, so the button's scrap captured 3E's own `[H2]` / `[body]` (the bare `[Click Drop Activity N]` of XDLS908, a different human form, never matches); (d) owned_anchor_counts — when the ordinary anchor count falls short, an `[Activity]` anchor consumed by its activity's OWN widget (that bundle's activityOwner — XDLS905-4.0's modal owns `4A`, XDLS904-5.0's `5E`) counts as a panel: the box still renders with its id. Both only where the row would otherwise decline.
scrap_release._doc: The tile prepass builds the Learning-Support choice board on most XDLS902–906 lesson pages and declines the whole row when a tile scrap holds a member it does not recognise. Two of those members are not tile content at all: (a) a writer's STRAY numberless, nameless marker (`[click drop image]` typed again after `[Activity] **5B**`, XDLS906-5.0) opens a scrap that captures the activity's OWN `[H4]` / `[body]` lines — with stray_marker_members the scrap's otherwise-refused members are RELEASED back to the page (they render where the writer put them, in the activity); (b) an inline marker of a release_inline_tags type riding the same paragraph as a heading the prepass already releases (XDLS906-3.0's `[H2] Should we use less artificial [hover definition] fake light?`) is released with it. Only a member that would have declined the row is released, so every row that builds without it is unaffected. Env CDSCRAPREL_OFF.

first_panel_row._doc: THE FIRST PANEL TAKES THE ROW FORM. The human's first tile panel on every choice page is <div class="row clickDropContent noBorder"><div class="col-12 col-md-8"><div class="activity dropbox" number="2A"> — the clickDropContent token on the section ROW (the JS's first .clickDropContent shows open, noBorder), the box without it; the later panels keep the token on the box (XDLS902-906; XDLS902 lessons 2-7 carry every panel in the row form — the module's own extension, not followed). In ContentConverter.#cdTilePair the first panel id's box keeps its own class and the section row wrapping it (row_open + col_open_pattern, nothing else between) takes row_class_open; any other shape keeps the prefix form. OFF = the prefix on every panel.

panel_no_inner_row._doc:
THE PANEL HOLDS ITS CONTENT DIRECTLY. The tile-grid PANEL anchor ([Activity] **2A** on a qualifying choice page, tagged _tilePanelId by the pre-pass) would open through the standard activity_wrapper.open, giving every panel an inner row > col-12; the human's
holds its

/

/ video DIRECTLY (XDLS902 / 903 / 904 / 905 / 906 / 909). ON: ActivitiesBuilder.activityOpen emits activity_wrapper.open_bare and pushes close_bare for a panel anchor on the standard (non-supervisor-note) path; the tile pairing post-pass reads only the opening tag, so the clickDropContent prefix lands unchanged. OFF (env CDPANELROW_OFF or enabled:false) = the inner row form.

tile_grid.tile: {label}
tile_grid._note:
THE XDLS ACTIVITY-CHOOSER TILE GRID. The writer authors a page as a run of one-name click-drop SCRAPS ([Click Drop x 6] header + [Click Drop N] Label, or [Click Drop Activity NX with embedded image] Label + a URL-less LS-library icon reference) whose panels are the ordinary [Activity]-opened boxes further down the page. The human ships one TILE ROW (row > col-md-8 col-12 choicePage choiceHeightMatch > div.choice.clickDrop.dropBox.col-md-4.col-6 per tile, iconType = camelCase of the writer's own label — the human's near-universal form — label = the writer's words verbatim) and pairs the Nth tile with the Nth clickDropContent panel BY POSITION (the site JS contract; the human RENUMBERS writer id typos positionally, as on XDLS902 pages 4/5, so id lookup is NOT the pairing rule). NO is emitted (the human's own XDLS909 no-img tile form; the LS-library photo paths are hand-placed, case-inconsistent — ../images vs ../Images on ONE page — and never in the WT; the writer's icon reference is FULFILLED by the iconType div). FENCES: every clickDrop bundle on the page must be a clean scrap (click-drop members + URL-less image refs + releasable trailing headings ONLY — XDLS908/911/912's content-carrying bundles decline the page), named tiles >= min_tiles, numbered evidence (an x-N header or >= min_numbered numbered markers — TEFUN06/HES1006's bare repeats decline), a tile label is never an id-shaped reference ('4B'), and the page must carry >= as many bare-id-tail [Activity] anchors as tiles (XDLS909's short scrap runs + BLLR201's slideshow panels decline — never a tile without a panel). Scraps that stole a NEIGHBOUR's [Activity]/heading as owner-lead (the backward lookback on XDLS902 tiles 4-6) are RELEASED back to the body flow. Env CDTILES_OFF (whole feature), CDTILEID_OFF (the anchor bare-id-tail -> number= repair alone, scoped to paired anchors because the human ITSELF ships

4A

id-titles on XTAS101/XLP01/XMES203/TEDC402 — a blanket repair would diverge), CDTILEPAIR_OFF (the clickDropContent postpass alone).

_comment: clickDrop — a row of click-to-reveal BUTTONS, each revealing its own content panel.
MEMBER-based (like accordion/tabs): the writer types one [click drop N] tag per item; the
text AFTER the tag is the button LABEL, and the [body] paragraph(s) beneath it are that
item's revealed CONTENT. The converter groups them in document order.
The human renders, inside a <div class=row>, ALL the buttons FIRST then ALL the content

panels (paired by position):
label
... then

body

... . The per-row GROUPING the human uses
(e.g. OSGM501-02's 6 items as 2 rows of 3) is a NON-DERIVABLE layout choice, so we emit ONE
row of all buttons + all contents — functionally identical (the JS pairs button[i] -> content[i]).
BUILT ONLY for clean label+body items. Falls back to the placeholder (never half-built)
the moment a member is richer — an [image]/[video]/[button]/[heading]/data table inside the
widget, an item missing its label or body, or red writer-instruction text.

{label} = the button text; {content} = one

...

per body paragraph.
list_content routes each item's revealed CONTENT through the standard black-text renderer
(ListsAndRuns.renderBlackText), so a writer's Word bullets become real <ul><li> lists instead

of literal '

• ...

' paragraphs — the human never keeps '

•' bullets inside
clickDropContent (as in SCCH302, HES1007, HES1005, ENGR202). Env toggle: CDLIST_OFF (the

one-

-per-paragraph form).
Human reference: 01-Finalized_Modules_/OSGM501/OSGM501-03.html.

no_row_wrapper._doc: THE CLICKDROP BUTTONS SIT DIRECTLY IN THE COLUMN: in the human build a clickDrop button group's parent is a column (the page's col-md-8 or the activity box's col-12), almost never an inner div.row, in every subject. When enabled, both clickDrop emit sites drop `open` / `close` (the tile grid and the conversation reveal bubble keep their own wrappers). OFF = the buttons inside the `open` row.

_note: IMAGES IN THE REVEAL CONTENT. The human puts images in clickDrop reveal content routinely
(about a third of its clickDropContent blocks contain an ), so an [image] member does not
decline the widget. Each item keeps an ORDERED part list and the image renders in the writer's
own position as the standard Mode P/D asset (the same image_mode_* templates every other widget
uses). An item with NO image has exactly one body part holding the whole joined body.
THE EMPTY MARKER (the most common case): an [image] member with NO url and NO text — a
media-list REFERENCE the developer fills in later, with no asset to render (mostly the
XDLS903-906 family, whose human reveal panels carry the writer's headings and prose and NO
image at all). Such a marker is SKIPPED (renders nothing), exactly like the accordion's
image-arrangement layout marker.
NEVER HALF-BUILDS: a non-iStock / underivable image, a caption riding along with the
URL, or an image before any button still declines the whole widget.
env CDIMAGE_OFF turns the rule off (an [image] member declines the build).

_comment: shapeHover — a ring/row of clickable image 'shapes', each revealing its own text panel.
The writer types [shape hover] then a repeating group per shape (as in OSAI501-02):
[shape n][H#] TITLE  +  [body] HOVER-TEXT  +  [image] iStock-URL. The scanner captures
these as members (heading carries the 'shape n' subtag). The human builds:
<div class=shapeHover layout=clockwise>

one
(img +

title

) per shape

one

body

per shape
layout is always 'clockwise' in the human build; the h4 colour var tracks the module template
phase (OSAI->NCEA). BUILT ONLY when every shape has a title + a resolvable iStock image + a body;
declines (keeps the honest placeholder, never half-builds) on a table, a nested widget, a
non-iStock image, red instruction text, or fewer than 2 shapes. Human reference:
01-Finalized_Modules_/OSAI501/OSAI501-02.html. Env SHAPEHOVER_OFF.
multiChoiceQuiz — the MULTIPLE-CHOICE QUIZ.
THE DERIVATION, proven against the human's own page: the writer marks the right answer
with a bracket that FOLLOWS the option it marks. CEDO202-0.0 shows it unambiguously
because that writer marks the WRONG ones too — '1. 24 hours.' [Incorrect] '1. 365 days.'
[Correct] — and the human puts value="correct" on '365 days (one year).', on 'The
invisible line on which the earth spins.' and on 'Two (northern and southern).', all three
exactly where this rule puts them. SCCH301 ('a. Solid. [correct]') and XGF9004 agree.
THE FENCE THAT MATTERS: BLL264's writer types the checkbox FIRST ('☐ [correct]
everyday spoken language'), so under this rule its marked option would be the empty
checkbox glyph. A marked option that is empty or checkbox-only DECLINES the build —
an answer is never guessed onto the wrong option.
THE OUTPUT SHAPE is the human's own. 'autoCheck' is on only about half of the human's
groups, so it is not taken from a plurality — it is derived from the WRITER's own opener
words (autocheck_words, as for dropDown); the question column token is a genuine tie
(col-12 vs col), so the more common col-12 ships. mcqOptions / mcqOption are the human's
consistent classes. A correct option carries value="correct"; the others carry no value
attribute at all (the human almost never uses 'incorrect', so it is not emitted).
Env MCQ_OFF.

yellow_ticks._doc: 'Trust yellow ✅ ticks, with strict checks.' The writer's YELLOW highlight (the block.marks side-channel; the parser's ✅) marks the correct option even when the writer never announced it — CEDW501 5B `a. ✅A group of people you live with during lockdown.` (the human's CEDW501_5.0 mcqOption value="correct" is on exactly that option). Used only where the bundle has NO [correct] / [incorrect] mark of the writer's own, and ONLY when: (a) every question has exactly one ticked OPTION (options counted, never highlighted runs — OSAI101's one green run over a whole list is the trap); (b) the item right above the opener is not the writer's D2L-quiz button (d2l_button_pattern — TEFUN01 / 03 / 04, ENGR202: the human builds only the quiz-link button there); (c) nothing in the bundle or above it says there are no correct answers (no_answers_pattern — as in OSAI101). colours = the trusted highlight colours (green is NOT trusted). Env MCQYELLOW_OFF.
yellow_ticks._d2l_note: The writer's D2L-quiz button right above the opener: `[Button] Go to quiz` (TEFUN01 / 03, ENGR202) and `[Button] Quiz` (TEFUN04 — its gold builds no multiChoiceQuiz, 0 / 0) — any writer [Button] whose label names a quiz.
yellow_ticks._answer_key_note: A highlighted ANSWER-KEY line — `✅Correct Answer: B` (ARFUN04, whose option letters run b–e while its gold reads B as the 2nd option) — is never an option and never a tick; with it set aside the question has no ticked option and guard (a) declines (the key's letter is not guessed).

typing._doc:
THE TYPING QUIZ, shape 1: THE WRITER'S RED ANSWER ON THE QUESTION LINE. Built only where the writer marked the answer (never invent an answer): many typing bundles carry no answer at all and stay hand-offs, and the highlights are mostly the GREEN highlighter, unannounced, which is not trusted. The red answer on the question line — inline (BLL244 '[red]What[/red] game are Zack and Kev playing…'), at the line's end (FRFUN08 'Je vais à le cinéma. Answer: [red]au'), or alone on the next paragraph — usually equals the human's own answer= value. THE FORM is KB 03D's text-only typing quiz (level 1): div.typing layout=standardNoBorder > div.typingContainer > one div.row per question line holding its

with an at each red answer; then the reset / checkAnswer hidden / showAnswer hidden row (KEPT with autoCheck — 03D). autoCheck from the WRITER's own words (the multiChoiceQuiz list). THE BUILD, never half: members grouped by source paragraph; a red 'noise' member is an answer by Utils.AnswerKeyRedWord (a stray ']' skipped, a label rendered as text); an answer-only paragraph joins the line above; the answer-less paragraphs BEFORE the first question are the lead (rendered before the widget); an answer-less paragraph after it, a red INSTRUCTION inside a question line (MXDB302 types its question 'Rectangle 10cm by 2cm' in red), a table, a merged bundle or any other tag → decline and the honest hand-off box stays. A Word auto-number (the extractor writes '1. ' on every numbered-list paragraph) is stripped; a writer's typed number is kept. An 'answer' that is an answer-key label ('Answer: 15%', 'ANSWER: 125.68') or a question ('weekday?') declines (answer_reject_pattern). Env TYPING_OFF.
typing.input: <input class="form-control" type="text" answer="{answer}" placeholder="Type here" caseSensitive="false" />
typing.buttons:
Reset
Check
Show

table_form._doc: THE TYPING QUIZ'S TABLE FORM, built only where the writer marked the answer (the red-answer reading): one captured table whose RED runs are the writer's answers ('Answers are in red') — `[Type and check]` + `| 6 + 3 x 2 | 🔴12🔴 |` or a grid `| 673 | 🔴670🔴 | 🔴700🔴 |` — builds the human's `div.typing layout="standard"` > `div.table-responsive` > the writer's table, each red run an input (answer=), black text kept, a first row of bold labels a <th> row, a red 'Question | Answer' label row dropped (MXFUN01's tables). Declines to the hand-off box on media, on deny_pattern in the writer's words (another widget, images to recreate, words outside the table), on an all-red body row (letter tiles), on an answer over max_answer_words / answer_reject_pattern, below min_answers. A selfCheck-typed bundle (the alias word 'check' folds `[Type and check]` to selfCheck) is read only when its own opener says type / typing (selfcheck_opener_pattern). Env TYPTABLE_OFF.
table_form._tag_answer_note: A red cell that is a TAG word — GEWHA / PWY1002's layout tables (`Body`, `Table`, `Typing self check`, `[MTK Quiz Questionnaire] [engagement trigger]`, `select option Y/N`) — means the table describes a layout, not a quiz: the whole table declines. Any answer still bracketed after the single-bracket unwrap declines too, and so does a built table that would still show a writer bracket (MXFU202's `[image] 117 - 71.jpg` cells).
table_form._alt_split_note: The writer's alternative answers in one red run — `23.30 or 23.3` (MXFU202) — become the KB 03D multiple-answer form answer="a||b" when there are 2–3 alternatives of ≤ 3 words each.
table_form._label_answer_note: A red run that is a LABEL — `correct` beside the black answer (BLLR203), `(Question 1)` (SSCI205), `Example` — means red is not the answer in that table: the whole table declines to the hand-off box.

_comment: dropDown — a select-the-answer quiz.
THE FAMILY FENCE (`opener_pattern` / `opener_deny_pattern`). Tag_Lexicon aliases
`dropbox`/`drop box` onto this same widget type, but a DROPBOX is the file-upload
area where a student submits a photo, a video or an audio recording — not a
dropdown at all. Most captured bundles of this type are dropboxes; the human ships
`class="activity dropbox"` (an activity MODIFIER) for those and `div.dropDown` for a
genuine dropdown. The builder therefore fires only where the writer's own opener names
a dropdown, so every dropbox bundle is untouched BY CONSTRUCTION. Re-cutting the lexicon
alias would move many bundles' capture and hand-off labels, so it is not done here.
THE ANSWER SIGNAL. The writer marks the correct option either by colouring it RED
or with an explicit [correct] tag placed immediately before it. Both reduce to a
MARK at a character position, so one derivation serves both. A dropdown whose
answer is not marked at all is NEVER guessed — it keeps its hand-off box.
OUTPUT SHAPE — the human library's form: answer="N" 1-based (almost always; a few

multi-select);

always, almost always reading 'Select one'; 2-4
options usually (so min_options 2, and ≤10 covers virtually all); the container is
div.dropQuiz or div.dropQuiz autoCheck whose first child is div.row or, in the paragraph
form, div.dropParaContainer; the question wrapper is a bare div.dropQuestion (the most
common — the Bootstrap width variants are editorial and are not reproduced).

column_answer_fold._doc: The D3 (b) COLUMN form reads the first row as the red column HEAD whenever its answer cell is red; when EVERY answer cell is red and the first row's answer is one of the answers beneath it (MXDI202 10A 'Sorting measurements': Weight / Length … length), that row is a question — without this it would be dropped — and with options distinct only by exact spelling, the writer's lower-case `length` would become a third, duplicate option. With the flag on: the first row stays a question when its answer recurs below (case-insensitive), and the option set is distinct ignoring case (the first spelling kept; answers index by the folded key). Env DDCOLFOLD_OFF.

yellow_ticks._doc: 'Trust yellow ✅ ticks, with strict checks' (as for multiChoiceQuiz). The colour_marks path opens only when the writer ANNOUNCES the marks; unannounced, the writer's YELLOW highlight alone (never green) also opens it, ONLY when (b) the item right above the opener is not the writer's D2L-quiz button (d2l_button_pattern — the human builds only the quiz link there) and (c) nothing in the bundle says there are no correct answers (no_answers_pattern — OSAI101); (a) exactly one marked OPTION per question is every mark reading's own rule (#ddMarkAnswer returns 0 on 0 or 2+ hits and the bundle declines). A bundle with no yellow mark is unaffected. An answer is never invented. Env DDYELLOW_OFF.

upload_box._doc:
THE UPLOAD BOX. A bundle the family fence refuses because the writer's opener names a DROPBOX (the student upload area) builds the human's own upload button instead of a red flag or a hand-off box: `
Upload to dropbox
` + ONE Designer/Developer To Do note carrying the writer's own bracket words. The human build uses this button widely — label 'Upload to dropbox', class `button` outside BLL and `buttonD` inside BLL (the dropbox house style, read from buttons.dropbox_orange_house_style so the two rules cannot drift) — and many of its own buttons carry the EMPTY href we ship (the unwired pre-publish form; the populated ones carry a per-module D2L rcode that is in NO Writers Template — the CL-0044 class, an INTENTIONAL divergence). FENCES: an 'alert dropbox' opener is a REVEAL box, not an upload area (opener_exclude_pattern — CEDT101, whose human build drops them); a MERGED capture (extraTypes) is the gathering class; a captured table, media, or another widget's member keeps the honest hand-off box. Captured black/[body] text is RELEASED around the button in the writer's own order (renderBlock — bullets become real lists; see release_split); a no-primary red span's own text joins the note spec, never learner content. Modules whose human build ships NO upload button (BLL155, BLL266, ENGI400, ENGJ302, ENGJ403, HPRE301, SSEA203, SSOG103, TEDC401, TEDC402, TRR304, XMES201) are forward-looking NAMED divergences. Env DBXBUTTON_OFF turns every upload-box bundle back into its red flag / hand-off box.

release_split._note_order: The human keeps the dropbox button as the activity box's LAST content child (KB constraint 43: an activity that ENDS in the button), and puts text the writer typed AFTER the marker after the button (XDLS901 'Ka pai! You can now arrange…'); text typed before it (XTAS101 1G's '3. Upload some pictures … here.[insert dropbox link]') stays before it. THE RULE: the scanner keeps memberItems in document order (backward absorptions unshift), so the scan splits the released text at the LAST dropbox bracket member (a same-type merge holds two brackets and ONE button) — text captured before it renders before the button, the bracket's own trailing text and later members after it. Env toggle DBXORDER_OFF puts the button first, then all released text.

upload_box.todo_note: Wire this button's D2L dropbox quicklink (the href is intentionally blank — the per-module rcode is in no Writers Template). Writer: {spec}

dropDown._note_cells: cell_parens — the D1 paragraph reading applied to a table CELL, one question per cell, emitting the SAME paragraph form the human ships for exactly these tables (MXFL302_05.1, BLL275_1_0, BLLR201_2_0 match it cell for cell). cell_correct_pattern names the explicit [correct]-family bracket inside a cell; note it has NO leading \b, because the writers type [Q1Correct] and \b does not fire between a digit and a letter. thousands_guard — a comma with digits IMMEDIATELY on both sides is a thousands separator, not an option break ('(1,400 km, 1,500 km)' is two options, not four); the discriminator is the absent space, so a real option break written ', ' is untouched. env DDCELLPARENS_OFF / DDNUMCOMMA_OFF.

colour_marks._doc: THE THIRD ANSWER-MARK SOURCE: a writer marks the correct option with a yellow HIGHLIGHTER or GREEN text (00b050), and says so in their own words — the extractor's answer_marks side-channel carries the marks, and this block lets the dropDown readings consume them ALONGSIDE red and [correct], through the same derivation (a mark reduces to a range/text matched against the options). THE FENCE IS THE WRITER'S OWN ANNOUNCEMENT, per BUNDLE: the opener bracket or a member line must say so ('Correct answers highlighted' — SCCH301 puts it in all three openers; 'Correct answers in green' — OSAH401's standalone green line, OSSM401's and OSOH401's openers; the announce wording selects the mark KIND, so a green-announced quiz never reads a stray yellow guidance highlight). The announcement is essential: without it a highlight is editorial (TRR109 highlights whole paragraphs; ENFUN02/ENGC201 mark answers but never say so) and green can be the OPTIONS themselves (OSAI101 — reading it as an answer would ship a WRONG quiz) or a label (CEDT104 'Lyrics:'). A standalone member line that IS the announcement (word-limited) is consumed like the opener's own wording (the configuration-wording class). FOUR consumption sites, all-or-nothing per bundle: (S1) block marks become ranges in the rebuilt paragraph stream, so the D1 parens reading fires (ENGJ301-6.0 — the human's own paragraph form, answer-for-answer); (S2) optlist_head_pattern — the '[answer options: …]' option-tag + question-line pairs (SCCH301-3.0); (S3) the D3 grid variant where every body cell is an options-bracket + a marked option (SCCH301-2.0 — here the marks, not the identical option-list strings, give each question its answer); (S4) lettered option lines in table columns/cells ('A. Human Rights Act 1993' — OSAH401-3.0 column form, OSSM401-4.0 cell form with a row image, OSOH401-2.0 one-cell-of-options form). Not covered: the numbered-gap + options-TABLE form (ENFUN09, OSAI501); a bundle whose announcement sits on a DIFFERENT bundle (OSSM401-3.0 — the per-bundle fence is the safety); announced quizzes of OTHER widget types (OSBY501/OSAH501/OSOH501/BLL223/ANZH304 self-check/mcq/clicking-order). env DDMARKS_OFF turns off every consumption site (the extractor channel is ANSMARK_OFF).

sequential_ranges._doc: #ddRebuild places each colour mark after the previous one (falling back to the first occurrence when none follows), since marks arrive in document order. Placing every mark at the FIRST occurrence of its text would break two groups with the same ticked option in one sentence — MXDB302 8A Q5 `(0, 1, ✅2, 3) decimal places so there need to be (0, 1, ✅2, 3)` would put both marks on the first group and leave the second as plain prose. Env DDMARKSEQ_OFF.

html_class_cohorts._note_learning_support: KB constraint 89 / CL-0089, a locked admin decision: a module whose CODE begins with X is a learning-support module and ships `learningSupport` appended to the <html> class list on every page (class="notranslate learningSupport"), never replacing notranslate and never altering template= (constraint 21); a non-X module never receives it. The test is the code, not the reference files (06_TEMPLATE_RECOGNITION §4.4). A CSS hook (a larger font from the stylesheet) — the converter writes no font CSS. Each rule here is a code-prefix cohort; SkeletonBuilder appends add_class to the filled html_open tag's class list for every rule whose prefix matches run.moduleCode. The human build carries it on only some X pages (it predates the rule); the KB outranks it. Env toggle HTMLCOHORT_OFF turns it off.

widgets._quiz_doc: The remainder of c38: the quiz types KB 03A lists as autoCheck-capable take the class ONLY — the quiz builders emit no Undo / Check row in either form (their own writer-worded autoCheck form is the root class alone), and the typing quiz keeps its reset / checkAnswer / showAnswer buttons (KB 03D). Env TPLAUTOQUIZ_OFF turns off the quiz part.

template_autocheck._doc: KB constraint 38 / 03A 'autoCheck Auto-Application': on the three dedicated templates (ECH / 1-3 / 4-6) `autoCheck` MUST be applied to every interactive that supports it, the Undo / Check buttons dropped exactly as the component's 'With autoCheck' example shows (KB 03B dragAndDrop: `class="dragAndDrop autoCheck …"` and the button row reduced to Reset; the free-form area layout never takes it). SkeletonBuilder.BuildPage runs this over the page body once the <html template> (templates) / level (levels) is resolved: every listed widget root without autoCheck gains the class and loses its own drop_buttons. The human build's older pages often lack it (they predate the rule). The quiz types are in widgets._quiz_doc. Env TPLAUTOCHECK_OFF turns it off.

level_attr_map._rule: Any other registry value renders as level="{value}".

template_attr_map._rule: template_phase registry value → template attribute, normalised via this map. Compound phase bands (e.g. '9-10/NCEA') map to the single template the human ships: the iDoc host (idoc_scripts.js) loads the stylesheet by this attribute, so an unmapped compound value renders the page UNSTYLED. '9-10/NCEA' → 'NCEA' is grounded on the human gold for all 3 modules carrying it (CEDK501, ENGS401, OSAH501).

template_phase_presets._doc: THE TEMPLATE-ATTRIBUTE PRESET RULE: the <html template="…"> attribute follows the preset module-LEVEL rule (code level digit 1→1-3, 2→4-6, 3→7-8, 4→9-10, 5→NCEA) and this rule SUPERSEDES sibling inheritance for THIS attribute only — ENGJ403 would otherwise inherit template="4-6" from series sibling ENGJ402, whose own human value is itself wrong (the human ENGJ403 ships 9-10). Everything else (menu conventions, groupKey, page model, chips…) keeps the sibling-emulation rule: rules.template_phase is NOT changed, only the emitted attribute. 'subjects' lists the families that consistently follow the preset in the human build, plus ENGJ (a known inherited-error chain); families whose code digit is NOT a curriculum level (BLL phonics series, HPFUN/fundamentals combo, the OS short-course numbering, XMES, MXEO, CEDK, OSGM, OSOH, OSSC) are EXCLUDED; 4-digit NCEA codes and FUN 2-digit codes never match code_pattern; a resolved 'combo' value is preserved (a combined-cohort template decision, not a level band — protects ENGJ201). Named preset-over-gold differences: ENGJ301/302 4-6→7-8, ENGJ402 4-6→9-10, ENGS401 NCEA→9-10, CEDR401 7-8→9-10, MXFU201 7-8→4-6 (within-family deviants of the same inherited/incorrect class). Env TPLPRESET_OFF uses the pure sibling value.

unknown_subject_digit_fallback._doc: A subject NOT in the subjects preset list (a brand-new subject, as SCCH302 was) that resolves NO template_phase at all would ship an EMPTY template attribute — the iDoc host loads the stylesheet by this attribute, so the page would render unstyled. When phaseForAttr is empty AND the code matches code_pattern AND its subject is unknown, the code's own level digit supplies the band via by_level_digit (SCCH302 → 3 → '7-8', the developer-confirmed value). PURE FALLBACK by construction: any module with a resolved template_phase — including every digit-is-not-a-level family (BLL/HPFUN/…), which all resolve real values — is untouched; a code not matching code_pattern (FUN-shaped, 4-digit) is left to the later rules because the FUN families' template values are MIXED in the human build and this rule refuses to guess. prefix_overrides + cohort_overrides still outrank it. Env toggle: TPLFALLBACK_OFF.

prefix_overrides._doc: EXPLICIT CODE-PREFIX TEMPLATE OVERRIDES — the design team's exception list for families whose code digit is NOT a curriculum level. A module whose code starts with a key here gets that template attribute UNCONDITIONALLY (outranks sibling inheritance AND the by_level_digit preset; preserve_values does not apply — an explicit prefix rule is absolute). LONGEST matching prefix wins; a null value means 'explicitly NO override' (a guard entry). THE BLL200 EXCEPTION: all BLL2xx modules are actually PHASE 1 → template="1-3", NOT the "4-6" their series digit or a mis-built sibling would suggest (the human BLL250/261/264/265/275 carry the corrected value). BLLR2xx modules ARE phase 2 and keep "4-6": the BLLR guard entry is belt-and-braces ("BLLR201" cannot startsWith "BLL2" anyway — 4th char R vs 2 — but the 'BLLR is NOT BLL' startswith trap earns the explicit fence). Env TPLPREFIX_OFF turns off all prefix overrides (independent of TPLPRESET_OFF).

cohort_overrides._doc: THE LANGUAGES COMBO RULE (Change Ledger CL-0033): every page of a Languages-cohort module ships template="combo" on <html> (the sub-type still comes from the <body> class). The prefixes are doc-14 §14.1's six languages × FUN + non-FUN code forms (data/Subject_Global_Parameters.json family '14.1 Languages P1-4' scope.cohort_prefixes — listed here VERBATIM so the engine never reads SGP at runtime; SGP stays inert, master_enabled:false), plus the code forms actually in circulation, CHFUN and JPNFUN (the Languages Audiovisual Package; JPNFUN05 is the designer's language-05 structural reference); doc-14's draft spellings CHIFUN/JAPFUN stay in the list for safety, and the list stays EXPLICIT full prefixes (no 2-letter shortenings). UNCONDITIONAL within the cohort: outranks sibling inheritance AND the by_level_digit preset (preserve_values does not apply — absolute-override semantics); applied AFTER prefix_overrides (no key overlap exists; no non-Languages code starts CHI/FRE/SAM/GER/JAP/SPA). Kept SEPARATE from prefix_overrides so each fix reverses independently (§2): LANGCOMBO_OFF turns off Languages alone, TPLPREFIX_OFF turns off BLL2 alone. Without it a new Languages code would ship an EMPTY attribute (no registry row, no sibling). Env LANGCOMBO_OFF.
cohort_overrides._prefix_note: Includes "FRNO": doc-14 §14.1 names the languages in three letters (FRE = French), but the module codes actually in circulation use a two-letter language + two-letter strand form (FRNO901 IS French). This stays an EXPLICIT prefix list rather than a two-letter pattern ON PURPOSE: FR/CH/SA/GE/JA/SP collide with no current subject prefix but would silently capture a future GEOG/CHEM-style subject. New real language code forms are added HERE as they appear; anything not listed falls to last_resort_default instead, which is the safe direction.

template_phase_presets._doc_last_resort_default: A brand-new subject (as FRNO901 was) can have no registry row, no human sibling, and a code digit that is not a curriculum level, so code_pattern never matches and unknown_subject_digit_fallback declines to guess. The template attribute would then ship EMPTY, and the iDoc host loads the page stylesheet BY that attribute: the page would render unstyled. THE RULE: after every other template rule has had its say (sibling inheritance → by_level_digit preset → unknown_subject_digit_fallback → prefix_overrides → cohort_overrides), a still-empty attribute takes `value` — a LAST RESORT, never a preference, and by construction unreachable for any module that resolved anything at all. VALUE = "combo": the combined-cohort template is designed to serve mixed levels so it degrades gracefully for an unknown module, it is the doc-14 answer for the Languages cohort this rule most often backstops, and it is one of the most common values in the human library ("1-3" is commoner but is a junior band — a poor guess for an unknown senior module). A default holds only until the developer builds the first proof, which then becomes the templated reference PageForge inherits from — so the run also carries a loud warn-level note naming the module and the assumed value. Env TPLDEFAULT_OFF leaves the attribute empty.

skeleton.head:
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8" />
<meta content="IE=edge" http-equiv="X-UA-Compatible" />
<meta content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" name="viewport" />
<title>{title}</title>
{idocScript}
</head>
skeleton.idoc_host_rule: ALWAYS tekura — the registry value is policy-fixed; tekuradev was a data artefact. Registry value 'none' = module ships without the iDoc script line.

title_patterns.note: The human's form varies ('OSAH401 0.0', 'ANZH205_1.0', 'ANZH301 Big City Lights'); the reference shell sets the default. {lesson} renders as the decimal page id, e.g. '1.0'.

mtk_titles._note_title_source: The MTK / Te Reo Rangatira title source; KB 07A 'Sections to EXTRACT' (the metadata table → module code + title; the [TITLE BAR] row; the per-page [H1] TRR1XX … | … repetition), 07C/07D rule 7 (titles Māori first, English second on every page; a lesson page carries its own title else the module titles), constraint 79. The TRR1xx docx leaves its [TITLE BAR] rows EMPTY and has no Module Name row: the module title rides in the Module Code cell ('TRR108: Ngā Orokati Tuarua – Final Consonants', 'TRR102 – Ngā Oropuare Aa') and the English half, where the writer gave one, in the per-page '[H1] TRR102 The vowels: Aa | Ngā Oropuare: Aa' repetition. Without this rule TRR overview pages would get no title, a stray body heading (Finished!, Karakia Whakakapi) would become a lesson title — the first-heading harvest has no [Activity] tag to stop at on an MTK page — and PNR102/104 lessons would get a single title where the human has the pair (the registry h1_count cap). THE RULE, scoped to modules whose resolved body class matches body_class: (A) DocxExtractor keeps the Module Code cell's remainder after the code token as metadata.moduleCodeTitle; (B) when the [TITLE BAR] and Module Name gave no title, PageAssembler takes the first repetition_tags item anywhere in the item stream whose text carries a pipe (code stripped, halves in payload order), else the cell remainder (pipe → pair; ONE spaced dash with a macron on exactly one side → pair; else one title); (C) the overview emits the Māori-looking title (macron, or the Māori alphabet) first; (D) a lesson page with no own title emits BOTH module titles, Māori first, exempt from the h1_count cap; (E) the page-title harvest accepts only harvest_heading_tags. The human build: every TRR overview carries the pair Māori-first; lessons repeat the module pair where the writer gave no lesson title. Env toggle MTKTITLES_OFF turns off all five.

module_code_value_map._rule: null = omit the #module-code element entirely. 'free-text:"Module' style registry values put their literal after the colon into {freeText}. {lesson} is the decimal page id ('1.0', overview '0.0'); {lessonPadded} is zero-padded ('01').

module_code_literal_guard._doc: The style-anchor registry's free-text overview chip is mined from ONE group member's human build; when that chip is the member's OWN MODULE CODE the literal would leak to every sibling (XFUN01 would show XFUN02, MXFUN02/03 → MXFUN01, ENGFUN02 → ENGFUN03, XLP01-05 → XPL06, XWHA01 → XWHA02). A literal matching code_pattern is the convention 'the module's full code' → render run.moduleCode instead. Genuine free-text ('Module', 'Lesson 5') untouched. Every shown human chip is the module's own code (ENGFUN02, XWHA01/02, XFUN02, MXFUN01); XFUN01's human chip is commented OUT (content XFUN01); the XLP family's human builds swap XLP→XPL systematically = non-derivable editorial (the guard fixes the digits, the letters stay LP). #header-scoped. Env CHIPLIT_OFF.

family_title_default._doc: When a FUNDAMENTALS overview page renders NO title h1 (the writer left the [Title] payload EMPTY and no title was derivable), fall back to the SUBJECT-FAMILY display name — the 'empty [Title] -> family default' rule the human developer follows (HPFUN902's WT [Title] is empty and 'Health & Physical Education Fundamentals' appears NOWHERE in the WT; it is the HPFUN subject-family name the human fills in, also on HPFUN301/401/903). The map is scoped to HPFUN only, the one family whose empty-title fallback is the family name: HPFUN203's human title 'Maintaining Friendships' is module-specific and NOT in its WT (non-derivable, C — this rule gives it the family name, a defensible generic fallback); ARFUN01's title IS in its WT as '[Insert title H1: ...]' (a one-off, out of scope); SSFUN02's is non-derivable (C). Fires ONLY when titles is empty (a filled [Title] like HPFUN101 'About me' is untouched). #header-scoped. Env FAMILYTITLE_OFF.

te_reo_detect._refinements_note: english_stopwords — short English words that pass Māori phonotactics ('One-to-one' → CEDT501 lesson 7 must not split; a hyphenated token is never Māori by the alphabet path either); a multi-sentence lesson title is never a soft pair (XMES101 lesson 2); pair_half_casing — a pair split from an ALL-CAPS title is sentence-cased per half (HES1005 'KAITIAKITANGA – BE A KAITIAKI') and a half never starts lowercase; english_slot_by_language — the <title> element and a lesson page's module-title fallback take the ENGLISH half of a Māori-first pair (CEDK501 'Kia Mahitahi – Idea to Action' → <title>CEDK501 Idea to Action</title>, lesson fallback 'Idea to Action'), the overview h1 order untouched.
te_reo_detect._doc: Which half of a separated title is Te Reo: a macron (āēīōū) OR the MĀORI ALPHABET + PHONOTACTICS (Utils.LooksMaori: every word's letters from a e i o u h k m n p r t w with g only inside ng, every word vowel-final, no consonant clusters except ng / wh, a lone word ≥ min_letters_single_word letters). Read by ContentConverter.#oneHalfTeReo (the guard every overview bilingual splitter shares — dash, slash / colon, punct-pair) and by SkeletonBuilder.#lessonPair's soft separators. The human splits a non-pipe pair into two h1 when exactly one half is Māori; the phonotactic test rejects the short English words the alphabet test alone would take as Māori ('Time – Quarter Past', 'Our home: Planet Earth'). OFF = the macron-only guard.

lesson_bilingual_pair._note_soft_split: After the unconditional pipe, a lesson's own title splits on the FIRST soft separator that occurs exactly once and leaves exactly ONE half reading as Te Reo (header.te_reo_detect — Utils.LooksMaori); 'Ngā Whare - Housing' (ANZH104 lesson 2, two h1 in the human build) splits, 'Time – Quarter Past' (MXFL103, one h1) does not. Env REODETECT_OFF disables the soft path.

english_first._doc: English first in Standard modules. Outside the MTK reoTranslate modules (whose 07D rule 7 — Māori first — is untouched above) a lesson's own bilingual title pair ships the ENGLISH half first and the Te Reo half second: when exactly one half reads as Te Reo it goes second; when both or neither do, the writer's order stands and the page is recorded. reo_detect: a macron decides first; when neither or both halves carry one, 'alphabet' lets the #looksMaori test decide (letters only from the Māori alphabet — Rapa Nui / Whakawhanaungatanga / He kupu whakakapi read as Te Reo, Easter Island / Learning to relate… do not; One | Tahi both read as Te Reo → as written). Where the human kept Te Reo first (ANZH105_1_0, HIS1006_9_0) that is a NAMED override. The KB is silent for Standard (a KB delta, 00G c79 / 01A). Env ENGFIRST_OFF turns it off.

lesson_bilingual_pair._note_lesson_pair: KB constraint 79: 'a second <h1><span> appears only where the writer gave THAT lesson its own bilingual name, and is then the LESSON's English + Te Reo pair, split by the same TITLE BAR parsing rule'; 01A 'YEARS 9-10 and NCEA lesson pages'; 07D MTK skeleton rule 7 'Titles in <h1><span> — Māori first, English second'. A lesson page whose OWN title (page.pageTitle — the [LESSON n] / [H1] / [H2] source) is a pipe-joined bilingual pair would otherwise ship ONE <h1><span> with the pipe inside, and the module code in front where the writer typed it ('TRR102 The vowels: Aa | Ngā Oropuare: Aa'). The human ships TWO spans on these pages; the reoTranslate modules (TRR, PNR) put Te Reo FIRST although the writer types English | Te Reo; the Standard-template modules keep payload order (the overview splitter's own rule); human lesson pages never carry the module code. THE RULE: strip a leading module code (+ dash/colon), split on the first separator, trim both halves; in a module whose resolved body class matches reo_first_when_body_class the Te Reo half (the macron-bearing half; when neither or both carry a macron, the reo_fallback half) goes first, otherwise payload order; both spans are emitted, exempt from the registry h1_count cap, and the module-level Te Reo title is NOT pushed beside them (constraint 79). Known differences: MXFL101 / TEDC402 / PNR101's human builds repeat the MODULE pair on lesson pages (the c79 anti-pattern — the KB outranks); TRR112/113's human builds reword the English half (editorial). Env toggle LESSONPAIR_OFF gives the single joined span.

lesson_title_h1._doc: CL-0042 (the OSSC pair). For the subject code prefixes in 'subjects' (the OSSC short-course family), a LESSON page ships EXACTLY ONE title h1 — its own lesson title (the pre-activity harvest, 'Lesson N:' prefix stripped) — at EVERY level: the module's Te Reo title is never pushed as a second lesson h1, even where the registry's mined h1_count asks for 2 (OSSC3 lesson h1_count IS 2, mined from the OSSC301 human build, which repeats 'Ngā Tāware' on every lesson — the human build PREDATES the rule; that divergence is an intentional override, see Subject_Global_Parameters._universal_conventions.cl0042_ossc_lesson_h1). A guarantee rather than a live change: no OSSC module derives a Te Reo title at present (OSSC301's [TITLE BAR] '*OSSC301 Scams* ✅*Ngā Tāware*' never splits — the ✅ boundary is dropped upstream), so this protects OSSC should a future title-split rule start deriving one. The overview page + the #module-code chip h1 are untouched (overview te-reo goes through the titleBar branch, not this one). Env OSSCH1_OFF pushes the Te Reo title as a second h1.

lesson_te_reo_suppress._doc: A LESSON page whose registry h1_count asks for 2 pushes the module's Te Reo title as a second h1 — but ONLY when the lesson has NO distinct title of its own (i.e. its title falls back to / fold-equals the module English title, the XMES102/103 human form where the module pair repeats on every lesson). When the lesson carries a DISTINCT own title (fold-differs from the module English title), the module Te Reo h1 is SUPPRESSED — the human form on distinct-title lessons (XMES101, CEDT207, CEDT301 ship ONE h1, the lesson's own; as the developer confirmed for SCCH302). Known exception: XMES103-01's writer left the placeholder 'Add lesson title' as the lesson title — it counts as distinct, so its Te Reo drops where the human ships the module pair. Composes with (never replaces) the lesson_title_h1 OSSC gate. Env toggle: LESSONTEREO_OFF (the unconditional push).

title_casing._doc: The KB's title-casing rule (01A_TEMPLATE_LEVELS_CORE 'Title casing — normalise a MULTI-WORD ALL-CAPS title' / 10_CORPUS_VALIDATED_SCAFFOLDING §1 / constraint 1's permitted normalisations). A writer's multi-word ALL-CAPS header title (`DREAM IT, PLAN IT, DO IT`, `TE TIRITI O WAITANGI`) renders in SENTENCE CASE — the first letter capitalised, the rest lowercase, macrons kept, a token carrying a digit (`(US7121)`) left as a code; a SINGLE all-caps token (`STOMP`) is left as written (proper noun / acronym); a title already in sentence / title / mixed case is never touched. Finished header titles are never all-caps (the only all-caps ones in the human build are unreplaced placeholders). Sentence-casing cannot restore proper-noun capitals, so ONE red flag (cv2-note) quoting the original follows every normalised title — the KB's proper-noun caution applied to all of them, because the converter cannot tell `Castle Bravo` from `castle bravo`. Applied at SkeletonBuilder's header title fill (the plain and lowercase-span templates; the BLL phonics template has its own mechanism and is untouched). Env TITLECASE_OFF turns it off.
title_casing.red_flag: The writer's title is ALL CAPS ("{original}") — rendered in sentence case per the KB's title-casing rule; restore any proper-noun or acronym capitals the writer intended.

title_rules: h1_count drives how many title h1s appear (the #module-code h1 is NOT counted).
Overview: the [TITLE BAR] payload splits on '|' into English | Te Reo titles → one h1 each (count 2). Count 1 = English only; count 3 = an extra subtitle line when the writer provided one, else flag.
Lesson: the lesson's own title from [LESSON n] {title} (corpus practice); falls back to the module title when the writer gave none.
header.tooltip_rule: menu_button_tooltip yes → attribute present; no/none → absent.

lang_boundary_split._guards_doc: tail_upper_first: the Te Reo half opens with a capital (CHI1005 'Daily routine Ngā mahi o ia rā' — 'routine' is Māori-lettered but lower-case); max_tail_ratio: a Māori NAME inside an English title runs far longer than its head ('Exploring Te Ika a Māui', ENGS101 — the gold keeps it one title), so a tail over 3x the head's word count never splits.
lang_boundary_split._doc: The LAST fallback of the title-bar split chain (after the case split): an English run then a Māori run with no separator ('Online Bullying Whakaweti ā-ipurangi', 'Scams Ngā Tāware', 'Social Media Pāhopori' — the writer set the Te Reo apart only by highlighting it) splits before the longest tail of all-Māori-lettered words (no b c d f j l q s v x y z) that carries a macron, the head holding a non-Māori letter; then the two-language guard. The human ships the pair as two h1 spans (KB c79's bilingual pair; 06 / 07D). ContentConverter.#bilingualLangSplit. Env TITLELANGSPLIT_OFF turns it off.

title_split.rule: The [TITLE BAR] payload yields the header h1 titles. Chain: (1) strip a leading module-code token (writers often prepend it — OSAI201's payload starts 'OSAI …'); (2) split English|Te Reo on a pipe; else (3) on a line break; else (4) on a run of 2+ spaces (the OSAI201 separator); else (5) the BILINGUAL PARALLEL-PUNCT split below; else one title.
title_split.evidence:
Gold OSAI201-00: payload 'OSAI AI Digital Citizenship Kirirarautanga Matihiko AI' →

AI Digital Citizenship

+

Kirirarautanga Matihiko AI

.
title_split.placeholder_titles_note: A title-bar half equal to one of these (folded) is a writer PLACEHOLDER, not a real title — e.g. 'Te Reo' (literally 'the language') means 'Te Reo translation goes here'. The real translation is NOT in the WT (the human fills it in), so the converter drops the placeholder and emits a red flag instead of shipping it as an <h1> (XGF9001: WT 'My Inner Compass | Te Reo'; the human's title 'Te Takinga o taku wairua').

placeholder_title_rule.note: A writer who never replaces the template's italic 'MODULE TITLE TE REO' (or 'MODULE TITLE') placeholder has NOT provided that title — the real one is not in the WT, so it must NOT be shipped as an <h1>. extra_placeholders extends placeholder_titles (folded compare); a half matching ANY is DROPPED. all_placeholder_uses_course: when EVERY title-bar half is a placeholder, do NOT restore it — fall back to the front-matter Course as the SINGLE English title and emit NO Te Reo (matching the human, who ships only what's real; e.g. OSBY101/201, CEDO202, CEDR201/301/302, CEDT201-204). For a MIXED bar (one real + one placeholder, e.g. OSGM501 'GAMING SAFELY | MODULE TITLE TE REO', also OSOH101/501, TEFUN02/05, XGF9001/9006, XLP05), the real half is kept as the English title and the dropped-placeholder flag stops PageAssembler from mis-promoting it to the Te Reo slot. The strings 'module title te reo'/'module title'/'te reo' are unambiguous template boilerplate — no real module is titled that, so the discriminator cannot touch a genuine bilingual title. Env TITLEPH_OFF uses the plain ['te reo'] list with no Course fallback.

title_split.bilingual_marker_split_slash_rule: The single-char soft separators live in ONE ordered DATA list (char_separators) that the ONE splitter #bilingualCharSplit iterates — the FIRST that occurs exactly once and yields a macron-guarded bilingual pair wins. So a slash-separated bilingual [TITLE BAR] ('Responding to Texts / Te whakautu i ngā kuputuhi', as in ENGS401) splits into the two <h1> the human builds, and adding a future single-char title separator is a DATA edit here. Each entry: sep + its data on/off flag + its env A/B toggle + optional bail_other_sep (colon keeps its 'any other separator ⇒ not mine' bail; slash deliberately does NOT set it, so ENGI201 'Connections – … / Nga Hononga – …' with internal spaced dashes still splits on the top-level slash). Slash is ordered first (outranks colon). The shared macron guard #bilingualTwoLangGuard keeps a title the human builds as one <h1> in one piece. Known limit: a Te Reo half written without macrons (SSFUN06 'Ethical Citizenship / Matatika Kirirarau', MXDB301) stays a single title — the same guard limitation the dash/colon/case splitters share. Env TITLESLASH_OFF turns off SLASH only; BILINGUALMARK_OFF turns off colon+case.
title_split.strip_boundary_separators_rule: When a writer types BOTH a soft separator AND a hard one — 'Visual Literacy /  Mātau Reo Ataata' (slash + TWO spaces, as in SSFUN05/08) — the engine's hard-separator branch (pipe/newline/2-space) splits FIRST, leaving the soft separator ORPHANED on a half boundary ('Visual Literacy /'). After the split, each half has any leading/trailing char in this string (plus surrounding whitespace) trimmed. The human never keeps a title <h1> span that starts or ends with a separator char, so a boundary orphan is never legitimate. Scoped to '/' ONLY. The orphan-dash form (XDLS909 'Living In Aotearoa –', BLL246 phonics) and the trailing-colon form (PES1001 'Column Addition:', XLP02 '*:', XDLS909 'Activity 10B:') have different causes (a different separator / a heading mis-captured as a title) and are NOT handled here; add a char to this string only once its form is understood. The edge regex trims ONLY a leading/trailing separator (never one internal to a half), so it also cleans a SINGLE-title orphan (ENGI401 'A Moment in Time /', whose Te Reo half is an unfilled placeholder) while never disturbing a single-language title's intentional internal punctuation ('TV / Radio' keeps its slash). Env TITLESEPTRIM_OFF turns it off.
title_split.bilingual_marker_split_rule: Two more bilingual [TITLE BAR] boundaries the dash/punct splitters miss, BOTH behind the SAME macron guard (EXACTLY one half carries āēīōū, neither half placeholder boilerplate) so they cannot fire on a single-language or already-handled title. (a) COLON: a single ':' boundary — CEDO501 'TE WHAI MŌNI: YOUR MONEY', TWHK903 'Digital Citizenship: Tāurungi Matihiko'. (b) CASE-TRANSITION: an ALL-CAPS English half glued to a non-caps Te Reo half when the writer's ✅/emoji boundary is dropped upstream (DocxExtractor) and collapses to one space — OSAH301 'ONLINE ABUSE AND HARASSMENT Tūkinotanga ā-ipurangi…'; the maximal ALL-CAPS word prefix is the English, the non-caps remainder the Te Reo. The all-caps English half is then corrected by #normaliseTitleCase. Both run AFTER punct/dash in the chain, so they only see what those rejected. Env BILINGUALMARK_OFF gives one combined title.
title_split.bilingual_dash_split_rule: Step (6, after the punct split): when the payload has NO pipe / line-break / 2+space separator AND NO slash, split it on a SINGLE spaced dash ( – / — / - ) into TWO titles iff there is EXACTLY ONE such dash, BOTH halves are non-empty, EXACTLY ONE half carries a Te Reo macron (āēīōū), and NEITHER half contains template-placeholder boilerplate (module title / insert / awaiting / translation). The WT preserves order, and the human emits the halves in payload order (Te-Reo-first here, English-first for the pipe-split OSAI201), so parts[0]→english slot, parts[1]→teReo slot reproduces the human ordering — as in CEDT501 'Kia Māia – Stand Up, Speak Out' and ENGR201 'The Inside Scoop – He Rangahau Pūrongo'. ENGI201 (slash + multiple dashes) and XGF9003 (pipe) are excluded by the no-slash/no-pipe guard; XMES201 ('…MODULE TITLE TE REO: Aku mokai – …') by the placeholder-boilerplate guard. This overrides the non_derivable_note's 'do not split on dash' for this tightly-guarded single-dash + macron + no-other-separator case ONLY; the other two-title forms (slash/colon/bilingual-knowledge) remain non-derivable. Env DASHTITLE_OFF gives one combined title.
title_split.bilingual_punct_split_rule: Step (5): when the payload has NO pipe / line-break / 2+space separator, split it into TWO titles iff it is two phrases each ending in the SAME sentence-terminal punctuation (! !, . ., or ? ?) AND exactly ONE half carries a Te Reo macron (āēīōū) — the English!/Te-Reo! pattern. As in ENGS301 'PICTURE THIS! WHAKAAHUATIA TĒNEI!' and ENGC202 'Ready, Set, Instruct! Takatū, Whakaritea, Tohutohu!'; no single-language title matches both guards. Set false to disable.
title_split.non_derivable_note: The macron-guarded splitters cover every DERIVABLE separator present in the raw payload: pipe/line-break/2-space (unconditional), spaced-dash, colon + case-transition, and slash. What REMAINS non-derivable is a two-title module whose payload carries NO separator signal AND fails the macron guard — chiefly MACRON-LESS Te Reo (SSFUN06 'Ethical Citizenship / Matatika Kirirarau', MXDB301), where 'this half is Te Reo' cannot be told from the payload alone without a Te-Reo lexicon. The converter keeps those as one title — do not guess. Casing stays the sentence-case default: the human's Title-Case rendering of an all-caps WT title is editorial and not derivable.

lone_title_maori_guard.note:
The Course-backup lone-title→Te Reo promotion (PageAssembler) is for a lone [TITLE BAR] title that differs from the front-matter Course and is itself Te Reo (OSAI301 'Kirirarautanga matihiko AI'). It must not fire when the lone title is the ENGLISH module title and the Course is a broader subject: ENGC102 WT '*KEEPING IT REAL*' + Course 'Communication' would otherwise ship

Communication

+ 'Keeping it real' in the Te Reo slot; ENGS302 would put the Māori Course 'Te Ara Hou' in the ENGLISH slot. GUARD: promote to Te Reo ONLY when the lone title is actually Te Reo — Te Reo Māori uses only a e h i k m n o p r t u w (+ macrons; ng/wh digraphs) and NEVER the letters in non_maori_letters, so a lone title carrying any of those is English and stays the English title with NO invented Te Reo ('only ship what's real'; the real Te Reo e.g. 'Kia mau ki te pono' is not in the WT). OSAI301 still promotes (Māori → Te Reo, English from Course); English lone titles stay English, as the human keeps them. Env LONETITLE_OFF always promotes.

module_prefix_split.note: The BLL phonics [TITLE BAR] payload is 'Module N - <letter teams>' (e.g. 'Module 2 - oe, ow, ir, ur, ...', as in BLL232). The human SPLITS it: the leading 'Module N <sep>' prefix is stripped from the title h1 (so the title is just the letter-team remainder, wrapped in <span style="text-transform:lowercase;"> so the phonics render lowercase, not Title-Cased by the site CSS), and the OVERVIEW #module-code chip becomes 'Module {moduleNumber}'. Only BLL title bars carry this prefix (the discriminator is self-scoping), and the human always strips it and lowercases the tail. The chip number tracks the MODULE CODE's last digit, NOT the writer's title-bar prefix — where they differ (BLL142/147/154) the writer typo'd the prefix and the human used the code, so chip_from_code derives 'Module {last-digit-of-moduleCode}'. The human's own exceptions (BLL166's copy-paste 'Module 2', and BLL176/177/252 showing the full code instead of 'Module N') are NON-DERIVABLE editorial deviations. All of this is in #header. The strip is gated here (ContentConverter); the flag run.modulePrefix drives the chip + lowercase span in SkeletonBuilder. pattern group 1 = the title remainder. Env MODPREFIX_OFF (or enabled:false) turns off the whole behaviour (no strip → flag stays false → generic 'Module' chip + un-split, un-lowercased title).

phonics_overview_split.note: The BLL phonics OVERVIEW (parent) [TITLE BAR] payload is 'LEARNING/TEACHING THE SOUNDS – <letter teams>' (e.g. 'LEARNING THE SOUNDS – y, long vowels, silent e', as in BLL210) — the PARENT form, distinct from the lesson 'Module N - ...' of module_prefix_split. The human de-capitalises the lead ('Learning the sounds', which the CSS capitalize then renders 'Learning The Sounds') and wraps ONLY the post-dash letter-teams in <span style="text-transform:lowercase;"> so they render lowercase ('y, long vowels, silent e'), rather than the writer's ALL-CAPS lead verbatim and CSS-Title-Cased letter-teams ('Y, Long Vowels'). #normaliseTitleCase de-caps a WHOLLY-all-caps title (ENGC102 'KEEPING IT REAL' → 'Keeping it real') but SKIPS this one because the lowercase phonics tail makes the string not wholly upper. So this is a dedicated split: group 1 = the all-caps lead (de-capped via #normaliseTitleCase), group 2 = the separator, group 3 = the letter-teams (lowercase span). titleBar.phonicsLead/Sep/Tail drive title_h1_phonics in SkeletonBuilder; a phonics OVERVIEW whose #module-code chip is the bare non-numeric 'Module' literal (no module_prefix_split prefix) shows the MODULE CODE instead (as the human does on BLL170/210/220/230/240; BLL110-160 keep their own chip). The pattern is self-scoping (only the BLL phonics title phrase matches). All #header. Env PHONICSTITLE_OFF (or enabled:false) gives the un-split ALL-CAPS title + bare 'Module' chip. The writer's word (LEARNING vs TEACHING) is kept faithfully — the human's editorial TEACHING→Learning swap (BLL110/120) is non-derivable and not followed.

title_instruction._doc: KB c79 + constraint 1. A WT with NO [TITLE BAR] whose writer typed the title as an instruction in the front matter — '[Insert title H1: What the arts have in common]' (ARFUN01, after the '[ARFUN01]' code span) — gives the module its title, so the header is not left without an h1: ModuleResolver reads the trimmed front matter's red paragraphs against this pattern into run.metadata.titleInstruction, and PageAssembler takes it as run.englishTitle when no title was derived (after the 'Module Name' step, before the Course backup). Env TITLEINSTR_OFF.

title_bar_pair._doc: KB 01A (the header carries the dual title; the module's Te Reo title replaces the reference one) + KB 10 §5 / 01B (the overview's U / K / D and LI / SC are the module menu) + constraint 1. THE SECOND [TITLE BAR] IS THE TE REO TITLE, NOT THE MENU BOUNDARY: when the page opener is a title-bar tag and the first non-blank item after it is ANOTHER title-bar tag whose payload passes this block's Māori-letters test (non_maori_letters, max_words) while the opener's payload does not, the second tag is the module's Te Reo title — consumed into titleBar.teReo (the human's second header <h1><span>) and skipped by the overview's intro-marker search (the first MID-document title-bar alias). Otherwise that search would take it as the menu/body boundary: with nothing before it, the menu would ship blank + the KB 10 §5 flag and the Te Reo title would ship as a body <h4>. With the pair consumed the content-based overview fallback (menu.overview_section_labels) routes the section headings to the menu. Two leading [TITLE BAR] lines occur in the EXPlore Interest-Project pair (EXBP901, EXIP901). Env TBPAIR_OFF.

te_reo_line.note: A Māori-language BLACK line directly following the [TITLE BAR] payload IS the module's Te Reo title (AGH1006 'Te whakatō tipu kākāriki: Te whakahaere hātepe ahumāra' — the human splits the colon pair into TWO h1s; AGH1005 same shape). Fires ONLY when the payload itself produced a single (English) title, the line is the FIRST non-empty item after the title bar, passes the Māori-alphabet letters test (never mtkFlag) and is title-sized (max_words). The line is CONSUMED (it stops rendering as body/menu text). pair_split: exactly one colon with both halves non-empty → two h1 lines (titleBar.teReoLines), the human AGH1006 form; else the whole line is one Te Reo h1. Env TEREOLINE_OFF.

marker_glue_split.note: The writer left the template's boilerplate prompt GLUED inside the [TITLE BAR] payload and typed the real Te Reo after it (XMES103 'My Family – Who I live with MODULE TITLE TE REO: Taku Whānau'; the human ships two h1: 'My Family – Who I live with' + 'Taku Whānau'). The whole-PART placeholder filter only drops a marker that is its OWN part (pipe/2-space separated, e.g. OSGM501 'GAMING SAFELY | MODULE TITLE TE REO'); a marker glued MID/SUFFIX to real text never reaches it and would LEAK. This rule EXPLODES each split part at its glued boilerplate marker (dropping the marker), reusing the standard English|Te-Reo assignment (the two-h1 shape). GUARDS (both required): (a) the whole payload must NOT START with a marker — a payload leading with the marker is Te-Reo-first (CEDT104 'MODULE TITLE: Waiata I te Neke | Waiata in Motion') where English-first cannot be guaranteed, so it is left as it is (the human itself editorially reorders it); (b) a part that is WHOLLY a marker is LEFT to the placeholder filter, so its droppedPlaceholder flag + red flag are unchanged. The markers are extra_placeholders (multi-word boilerplate); the bare 'te reo' from placeholder_titles is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED — it is a real Te Reo word inside genuine titles (CEDW201 'Ko te reo atawhai me te reo manaaki'). Markers are matched longest-first so 'module title te reo' wins over its substring 'module title'. Seen in CEDK102, TWHA901-905, XLP01, XMES101/102/103/201/202; no real title carries the boilerplate (TWHK907/OSOH501's human builds ship it as a junk h1, which this rule drops). Env TITLEMARKSPLIT_OFF.

split_payload_join.note: The writer authored ONE bilingual title line but SPLIT it across spans, so the black-preferred payload rule sees only half: (a) pipe_lead_black — the embedded RED title + a black payload STARTING with '|' ([TITLE BAR] 'Whakaaro Auaha' + '| Thinking creatively', TEFUN03) → payload = embedded + black; (b) pipe_sibling — a no-primary red instruction/noise span DIRECTLY after the title bar whose text starts with '|' ('| Tangata Whenua Pūrākau', ANZH101) → absorbed into the payload + consumed. The joined payload then splits on the pipe like any normal bilingual title. When a JOINED payload yields exactly 2 parts with exactly ONE Māori-lettered half, the English half is assigned first (as the human ships it; scoped to joined payloads only — the dash/char split paths keep payload order, as CEDW501's human build has Te Reo first there). ANZH401's pipe-half is placeholder boilerplate and is dropped by the placeholder list. pipe_sibling also covers the DANGLING-pipe arm: the black payload ENDS with '|' and the adjacent span is the other half ('ONLINE @HOME |' + red 'Ngā whakahaeretanga ā-ipurangi i te kāinga', OSOH301) — the span's text AND its blackAfter are absorbed (MXFL104's bare red '|' separator span carries the Te Reo half in its OWN blackAfter, a mid-paragraph red span; the human ships both languages as h1s and no body line). Env TITLESPANJOIN_OFF.

menu_empty_heading_rule.rule: A preconfigured menu/section heading with NO content before the next heading (or the menu end) is OMITTED — human developers almost never render an empty scaffolding heading ('What do I need to get started?' is nearly always filled when kept; Connections/Assessment/Planning your time are never empty). Applies to ALL menu archetypes.

inline_links._doc: KB constraint 75 ('inline → anchor') IN THE MODULE MENU. MenuBuilder's text buffers render through ListsAndRuns.renderBlackText, which without the items' hyperlinks would lose every writer inline link in a menu pane. The human keeps some of these (the NCEA standard pages in the Standards / Information tabs — AGH1009, COM1002, HIS1004, MXS1004, PES1001–1004 / 1008; XDLS909, XTAS102) and drops others (D2L cross-module links, glossary / vocabulary documents — NAMED overrides of c75). On: each buffer (the section / tab builder and #writerTabPane) carries its items' block.links into the free-body weave (exact phrase, first occurrence per line, never inside an existing <a>). Env MENULINKS_OFF turns it off.

menu.rule: menu_type registry value picks the shell. Overview pre-body headings route into the menu per tab_map (the CONSUMED outcome — they emit no body element). menu_type 'none' = no menu button and no menu content div at all.
menu._strip_italic_all_doc: GENERAL menu-item italic strip. The human strips <i>/<em> from module-menu items almost always (Standard and Inquiry alike), while in body/activity/table it is mixed (editorial) and in acks it always KEEPS them — a clean role rule. The WT wraps menu learning-intentions/curriculum/descriptions in *italics*; the human menu carries none. ContentConverter.#buildMenu strips text-italic from ALL panes (tab1/tab2/content/left/right) via #stripTextItalic (removes <i>/<em>, keeps inner text; a Font-Awesome icon <i class="fa…"> is never touched), generalising the ENG/banner curriculum-pane strips. EXCLUDES reo/bilingual modules (#isReoModule: TRR/PNR prefix / reoTranslate body_class / mtkFlag): there the human KEEPS italic on BOTH panes — the reo line AND its English translation (TRR108 'He kaingākaunui…' + 'Mokopuna care about…', TRR301). Env MENUITALIC_OFF limits the strip to the ENG/banner family panes.
menu._none_family_fallthrough_doc: A Menu_Scaffold_Registry GROUP with NO evidence for the requested scope (e.g. a fundamentals family whose `overview` has no data) but whose OTHER scope is an explicit 'none' is a MENU-LESS family: the human ships no module-menu at all. Without this, #menuTypeFor would fall the empty scope through to the generic Style-Anchor default and FABRICATE a menu the human never built (TEFUN: lesson 'none', overview empty → a menu on the .phases overview the human leaves menu-less). The rule returns 'none' for that scope. Tight by construction — only fires when the SIBLING scope is an explicit 'none', so menu-BEARING fundamentals (ENFUN/HPFUN/MXFUN/XFUN lesson 'simplified') are untouched. Env MENUNONE_OFF uses the generic fallthrough.

repeat_lists._doc: Three more modules whose human build repeats the module-overview menu on its lesson pages: on these modules a lesson page whose own menu would be EMPTY (the writer gave the lesson no overview) carries the overview's built menu, exactly as the lists above. It is NOT a rule — ENGJ201's gold copies the overview too and is not listed (its lessons keep their own intentions). A named override of KB 01B l.316 / l.337 and KB 10 l.63 for these three only. Each entry of repeat_lists is one hand-kept list with its own env toggle (here MENUREPEAT3_OFF).

lesson_repeats_overview._doc_hand_kept_12: Twelve more modules whose human build repeats the module-overview menu on its lesson pages join the hand-kept list (repeat_modules): on these modules a lesson page whose own menu would be EMPTY carries the overview's menu, exactly as the modules above. It is NOT a rule: other modules with empty lesson menus do not repeat the overview, and a future module needs a human call. A NAMED override of KB 01B l.223 / KB 10 l.63, FOR THESE TWELVE ONLY. Env MENUREPEAT12_OFF drops this list alone (the modules list keeps repeating).
lesson_repeats_overview._doc: LESSON-MENU REPEAT. A small set of modules repeat the OVERVIEW curriculum (Understand/Know/Do) menu VERBATIM on every lesson page's #module-menu-content (MXFL201_1.0 ≡ _0.0). For a FLAGGED module, ContentConverter stashes the overview's built menu (run.overviewMenu) and reuses it wherever a lesson menu would be EMPTY. PER-MODULE by necessity, non-derivable: MXFL201 repeats but MXFL204 — SAME subject×phase, SAME 'simplified' lesson menu-type, indistinguishable WT inputs — does NOT (its lesson menus are empty); the discriminator is the human's per-module editorial choice, and no convert-time signal predicts it. Tight: only the listed modules fire, and only where the lesson menu is ALREADY empty (never overrides a populated lesson menu, never fires on a menu_type 'none' page). Env MENUREPEAT_OFF turns it off.

lesson_content_in_menu._doc: LESSON LEARNING-INTENTIONS → MENU (as in OSAH501-03). On a lesson page the [Lesson Overview] section's content IS the page menu: the intro line PLUS the [Lesson content] sub-region ('We are learning:' / 'I can:' lists). Ending the lesson menu AT the [Lesson content] marker would send only the intro to #module-menu-content and leak the WALT/I-can block into #body. With this flag the [Lesson content] marker OPENS a menu sub-region instead of closing the menu: the menu runs from [Lesson Overview] to the first heading / title-bar (whether or not [Lesson content] is present), and the bare [Lesson content] marker item is skipped. The human routes WALT/I-can to the menu almost always; its few body exceptions (XGF9001) are menu-LESS pages (no #module-menu-content), which this rule — extending only an EXISTING lesson menu — never touches. Guard: if extending past [Lesson content] finds NO heading, fall back to ending at the marker (never an empty menu). Env LESSONINTENT_OFF ends the menu at the marker.

lesson_overview_bare_lead.note: The BRACKET-LESS red 'Lesson overview' lead (EXIP901/EXBP901/ENGS302): the writer types the words as red TEXT with no square brackets, so no [Lesson Overview] tag resolves (TagNormaliser: class=noise, primary=null) and overviewIdx is never found — without this the lesson menu never fires and the whole WALT/intentions run stays in #body, while the human routes it to #module-menu-content on EVERY such page (the writer even leaves the note 'In banner (as consistent with other products)'). The phrase never occurs in black text, so a RED-span-only predicate cannot over-fire by construction; every bracketed [Lesson Overview] resolves primary and is untouched. With this flag, when NO bracketed tag exists on the page, a red noise/instruction span whose ENTIRE folded text matches `pattern` is accepted as the overview MARKER (position only — the span itself renders nothing either way). All downstream machinery (lesson_content_in_menu, the section-stop, named-heading promotion) is marker-relative and reused unchanged. Env BARELEAD_OFF uses tag-only detection.

label_headings._doc: THE MARKED LESSON OVERVIEW'S LABEL-HEADED SECTIONS. The lesson menu region ends at the first heading after `[Lesson Overview]`; MXEX101 writes the block AS headed sections — `[H2] Understand` + `In this lesson you will:` + bullet, `[H2] Know` + `This lesson will:` + bullet, `[H2] Do` + `You will show your understanding by…` + bullets, then `[Lesson content]` — so without this the region would be empty, the menu blank and the sections in the body. The human's menu is the whole block (heading + lead + list per section). When the item after the marker is a heading, `[Lesson content]` follows, and EVERY heading in between is a menu-LABEL heading (`pattern`), the region runs to `[Lesson content]` and those headings are menu content. A lesson TITLE heading after an empty block (MXDI201, CEDO501 …) never matches `pattern`, and a label heading over a widget (XGF9006's accordion) keeps its form (the widget ends the section). KB 01B + constraint 1. Env LOLABELHEAD_OFF.

lesson_overview_block_whole._doc_menu_types: The SIMPLIFIED lesson menu only. A TABBED lesson menu (HES1005 lessons 6 / 7) repeats the module overview's Understand / Know / Do + Standards tabs when the lesson has no menu items of its own (the hand-kept repeater form): an own-line sentence there would replace the whole repeat with one line, so tabbed menus are not covered.

title_like.lead_pattern: ^(?:we are learning|in this lesson|this lesson|throughout this lesson|lesson\s+\d+|you will|[aā]konga will)
title_like._doc: A TITLE-LIKE own line — no sentence ending, at most max_words words, not a lead — is NOT menu content: it is the lesson's own title (the gold's <h1> on CEDW501 x6 and MXDI201_1; HIS1004 x3 the gold drops it), a c79 lesson-title source recorded as a follow-up; it stays as before.

own_text._doc: (A) The writer's SENTENCE typed on the `[Lesson Overview]` marker's OWN line (`[Lesson Overview] This lesson is based on the picture book *A place for Zero* …`) is the block's first line: it joins the lesson menu as a plain line exactly as the same sentence typed on the NEXT line does, so the text is never lost.

lead_sentence._doc: KB 01B + constraint 1 (as with own_text). The FIRST non-blank item after an EMPTY [Lesson Overview] marker — a body / sub-head tag or a black paragraph — whose text opens «In this lesson / This lesson / Throughout this lesson» is lesson-menu content: the same sentence typed on the marker's OWN line is already the block's first line (own_text). It is a member of open_end's scan, and body_ends_section does not stop the section at it (the '[Body]' stop is for scene-setting runs — 'Welcome to lesson six…' — none a lead).
