MXFL203 lesson 1 ('[Lesson Overview]' + '[body text] In this lesson you will learn about the history of A&P shows …' + '[Activity 1A]') would otherwise show the sentence in the body under a blank menu. The human puts these [Body]-tagged sentences in the menu on the simplified lesson menus (MXFL203 1.0, XDLS901 4.0) and in the body on the Fundamentals single pages (SSFUN02 / SSFUN05 — not a simplified lesson menu, so out of scope by menu_types). Env LOLEADSENT_OFF.

open_end._doc_keep_if_body_empty: When nothing with learner content follows the block on the page (the writer typed `[end page]` straight after it — XLP02 lesson 3, the gold merges that page into its lesson), the page keeps its old form: moving the block would ship an EMPTY page body (a §1h CRITICAL). That split is the page-split lane's class, recorded as a follow-up.
open_end._doc: (B) A marked block with no heading, title bar or `[Lesson content]` after it anywhere on the page would leave the menu region's end at -1, so the whole block (We are learning / I can + their lists) would fall to the body under an empty, flagged menu. The block is therefore bounded by its own shape: from the marker, the run of WALT / SC members — blank lines, lead lines (the lesson_overview_implicit lead_pattern, lead_max_words), list lines, list tags, writer instructions / noise, and body / sub-head / h3-h5 tags whose every line is a lead or a list line — up to the first item that is none of these (the implicit block's member test; the marker itself is the evidence, so no lead count is required).

lesson_overview_block_whole._doc: THE MARKED [Lesson Overview] BLOCK REACHES THE LESSON MENU WHOLE. KB 01B ('Lesson pages: Overview content comes from [Lesson Overview]') + constraint 1 (no writer text is dropped) — authority level 1. Two cases: (A) own_text — the writer's sentence on the marker's own line (the human keeps it in the menu on MXDI201, HIS1003, GEO1005, MXFL203; where it shows it as the lesson h1 instead — CEDW501, MXDI201_1, HIS1004_6 — that is a NAMED override: the KB makes the block's content menu content); (B) open_end — a block with no end marker after it (XLP04, ENGS404, SPA1004, XLP02, ENGC403, XMES102, PES1005, PES1007, MXDI201). Env LOWHOLE_OFF turns off both; LOOWNTEXT_OFF / LOOPENEND_OFF each alone.

lesson_overview_implicit._doc_alias_words: 'over view' — the writer's spaced spelling (MXFL204 lesson 10's '[over view] Now you will follow the PPDAC cycle …'), which Tag_Lexicon _meta.toggled_aliases resolves to the title bar with the fragment 'over view'; inert while SPELLVAR_OFF leaves the bracket unresolved.
lesson_overview_implicit.lead_pattern: ^(we are learning|learning intentions?|you will show|how will i know|i can\b|success criteria|wh[aā]inga ako|paearu angitu)

lead_extra._doc:
«I AM LEARNING:» OPENS THE LESSON'S WALT BLOCK. ENGC206's writer types each lesson's block under the [overview] alias as 'Learning Intentions / I am learning: / • … / Success Criteria / I can: / • …'; the block test takes lead + list lines, so without 'I am learning:' as a lead the block would break there (one lead, no list) and the lesson menu would be blank with the WALT text in the body; the human renders the KB 01B canonical labels (
We are learning:
/
I can:
). 'I am learning' is a rarer WALT lead than 'we are learning' / 'I can' (ENGC206, TWHA902, TWHK902, TWHR905). KB 01B (the lesson menu is the WALT / SC block, canonical labels whatever the writer's wording): the pattern joins lead_pattern wherever #partitionItems reads it. Env IAMLEARN_OFF.

lead_heading_members._doc: A WALT / SC lead typed as a TOP-LEVEL heading — `[H2] We are learning about:` / `[H2] You will show your understanding by:` (CBI1008 lessons 1 / 2 / 5; PES1004) — is found as the lead (isLead accepts any h1-h6) but would be refused as a block MEMBER (isMember accepts only body / sub head / h3 / h4 / h5), so the block would never form: the lesson menu would be EMPTY and the WALT / success lists would land in the body as <h3>s, where the human's menu holds them (<h5> + <ul>). tags = the extra heading tags a member may be when its own text is a lead line and every line after it is a lead or a list line (the h3-h5 rule unchanged).

walt_sentence._doc:
THE UNMARKED 'WE ARE LEARNING' SENTENCE IS THE LESSON MENU. The implicit path takes an unmarked WALT / SC block only when it opens with a short LEAD line (≤ lead_max_words) followed by list lines, so a lesson whose writer typed the intention as one prose sentence — `[A box] We are learning about the three sectors of production. You will show your understanding by describing each sector …` (COM1005 / COM1006), a black `We are learning to explain how tectonic processes …` line before its `You will show your understanding by:` list (GEO1005 4) — would keep the sentence in the BODY under a blank, flagged menu. The human's placement splits by the sentence's OPENING WORDS, not its carrier — 'We are learning …' is always in its MENU, 'In this lesson / section, you / we …' always in its BODY (the writer's alert boxes and [Body] runs — ANZH401 / 404, SSCI205, SSOG103 / 105, ENGC403 …), so `pattern` names only the first. On such a page, after paths (a) / (b) find nothing, the opening items are walked (`opening()`, plus an EMPTY orphan sub-tag such as COM1005 lesson 1's `[A fancy looking box]` — `skip_empty_directives`); when the first real item is a black line or a `carrier_tags` tag (never a container) whose first line matches `pattern` and runs past lead_max_words, it is the lesson's menu block — with the implicit block directly after it when one follows (GEO1005's SC lead + list). It joins the menu as plain writer text (the form an inline 'We are learning about X.' line takes — CBI1004's marked block renders it as the menu

), split into its own line before `split_before` (the SC half, 'You will show your understanding by …'). KB 01B 'Lesson Pages — Simplified Module Menu' + constraint 1. Env WALTSENT_OFF.

reach_past._doc: THE LESSON'S WALT BLOCK REACHED PAST A FEW OPENING LINES. Path (b) takes a lead + list block only when every item before it is an opening item, so a lesson that opens with a black `LESSON 6` label (MXS1004 6–9), a `[Body]` intro sentence (FRNO901 2), a malformed marker line (GEO1006 1), a mis-read lesson tag (PES1004 4 `[PHO1011 lesson 5.1-5.3]`), a navigation prompt (XDLS902 2) or the writer's `[Alert solid] Blue box` (CBI1009 3 / 4) before its `We are learning:` block would show the block in the body under a blank, flagged menu. The first valid block past such lines is always within the first few items, and the human's MENU holds it (exceptions: MXS1004 7, whose human menu repeats another lesson's text, and XDLS902 2, whose human menu is different edited text). When (a)–(c) find nothing, the first `reach_items` items are walked: opening items pass, up to `max_skipped` LIGHT items (a black line, or a tag of `skip_tags`, or an unresolved / instruction / noise span) are passed over, and the FIRST lead reached is taken only when its first line matches `walt_pattern` and it forms a valid block — an SC-first block (ENGC206 2, JPN1004 7) is left, since half a block would move. KB 01B (the human's menu holds a WALT / SC lead almost always). Env WALTREACH_OFF.

explicit_marker._doc: KB 01B. AN EMPTY EXPLICIT [LESSON OVERVIEW] FOLLOWED BY A HEADING REACHES PAST TO ITS WALT BLOCK: CBI1009 lesson 1 types '[Lesson Overview]' + '[H2] Salts' + '[Body] …' + '[Alert solid] Blue box' + '[H4] We are learning about/to …' + bullets + '[H4] You will show your understanding by …' + bullets. The explicit region ends at the first heading, so its section would be empty and the menu blank, while lessons 2–4 type the same WALT box with no marker and reach_past (the implicit path — it requires NO marker) takes it. When the marker is EMPTY and its next non-blank item is a head_tags heading, path (d) alone runs from the item after the marker (paths (a)–(c) and (e) stay off); a found WALT block becomes the menu set and the marker stays the marker. Env WALTREACHX_OFF.

table_block._doc:
THE WALT / SC BLOCK TYPED IN A TABLE UNDER THE LESSON'S [Overview] ALIAS. The TEDC family writes each lesson's intentions as `[Overview]` then a layout TABLE — one cell `[H3] Learning Intentions / [Body] We are learning: / • to … / …`, one `[H3] How will I know I have learned it? / [Body] I can: / • …` (or both in one cell); path (a) finds the alias but its block test stops at the table, so without this the menu would be blank and the table would sit in the body. Only TEDC401 lessons 1–6 + TEDC402 lesson 1 have this shape, and the human's menu holds the text as KB 01B's simplified form (`
We are learning:
` / `
I can:
` over the lists). When the alias's first non-blank follower is a table whose cell lines (paragraphs joined by ` / ` or newlines, red markers and bracket tags stripped) hold a WALT lead line and a list line, the table is the menu block: its lines join the menu as plain writer text in document order, a line that is only a section LABEL (`label_pattern`) dropped — KB 01B: no separate section title above the h5. Env WALTTABLE_OFF.
table_block.label_pattern: ^(?:learning intentions?|success criteria|how will i know(?: if)? i(?: have|'ve| ve) learn(?:ed|t) it\??)$

alias_own_text._doc: THE [OVERVIEW] ALIAS'S OWN-LINE SENTENCE REACHES THE LESSON MENU. `[overview]` resolves to the `title bar` canonical (fragment `overview`); path (a) above takes the alias only when it is EMPTY, so an alias carrying the writer's own sentence (`[overview] Throughout this lesson you will learn about calendars. …` — MXFL203 lesson 2; also MXDI202, MXFL204, MXFU202) would become the page's title-bar payload and be discarded (the lesson h1 comes from the first heading) — the sentence would appear on no page. KB 01B ('Lesson pages: Overview content comes from [Lesson Overview]' — the alias IS that marker) + constraint 1 (writer text is never dropped): authority level 1; where the human puts the text in the body or drops it, that is a NAMED override — the same rule own_text applies to the [Lesson Overview] marker's own line. When a LESSON page with a menu (menu_types) found no marker and no implicit block, an alias among the opening items (max_scan_items) that carries its own text — the black text after it, else its red remainder — becomes the menu marker and that text the menu's first line; the region after it is the ordinary one (to the first heading / title bar, section-stopped at a structural tag or `[Body]`). A title-like own line (own_text.title_like) is left as it is. Env ALIASOWN_OFF.

lesson_overview_implicit._doc: The module-menu chrome region; KB 01B 'Lesson Pages — Simplified Module Menu': the lesson page's menu IS its WALT / SC block, canonical labels whatever the writer's wording. In the human build a WALT / SC lead sits in the lesson MENU almost always, including where the writer marked it `[Overview]` (TEDC402, ENGC206, CEDT501), typed it bare after `[Lesson content]` + the lesson heading (FRNO901) or bare after an `[H1] LESSON …` title (PES1004). On a LESSON page with a menu and NO [Lesson Overview] marker (nor the bare red lead): (a) an `[Overview]` title-bar alias among the opening items is the overview marker (consumed — it is never the page title); else (b) the first WALT / SC lead item (a black line, or a body / heading tag whose text starts with lead_pattern) reached through opening items only (blank lines, instructions, the title bar / lesson heading, `[Lesson content]`, an empty body tag — opening_tags) starts the block, which the section-stop then bounds (text and menu-safe tags to the first structural item or heading). MenuBuilder's simplified lesson menu renders it exactly as the marked form (the lead → the canonical <h5>, bullets → the list). The TEDC401 / TEDC402 form whose block sits inside a layout TABLE under the alias is table_block. Env LESSONWALT_OFF uses the marker-only route.

menu._note_section_content:
Module-menu section content is NOT forced to `
  • ` items. The human's menu sections are mostly lists, but at the LINE level (where such a rule would operate) a bold-labelled menu line is usually a `

    ` in the human build, and the converter's list share already matches the human's closely; a per-line list rule would overshoot and turn the writer's own prose — which the human keeps as prose — into list items.

first_page_source._doc: A LESSON THAT OPENS AT N.1 STILL PASSES ITS MENU TO ITS CONTINUATION PAGES. A lesson's menu is stored from its N.0 page (or the folded source); a lesson whose first page is N.1 — PWY1009's dotted «Lesson 1.1 …» headings, kept verbatim (KB 01D / c79) — would never store one, so its continuation pages (1.2 / 1.3 / 2.2 / 3.2 / 3.3) would ship the empty menu shell where the human repeats the lesson's menu on every page. KB 01B (a lesson page's simplified menu is its lesson's overview block): when no source is stored yet for the lesson, its FIRST page that has a menu is the source, whatever its part number; later pages inherit exactly as before. Env CONTFIRST_OFF.

lesson_continuation_inherits._note_exclude: The CEDO family is excluded: its human continuation pages leave the menu EMPTY (CEDO501, CEDO502), so the whole prefix is excluded (the `exclude_code_prefixes` pattern). The only other human-empty continuation page is BLL240_1_1, one of the dual-build human directories.
lesson_continuation_inherits._doc: THE LESSON CONTINUATION PAGE INHERITS ITS LESSON'S MENU. A writer who splits one lesson across pages writes `[Lesson 3.0] Tools – show and not tell` and then `[Lesson 3.1] Show and not tell continued`; the lesson's `[Lesson Overview]` block sits at the lesson's START, so the simplified menu is built on the first page and every continuation page would otherwise ship the empty shell. KB 01B ('Lesson Pages — Simplified Module Menu') makes a lesson page's menu that LESSON's overview block, and a continuation page is part of the same lesson. When a page's lessonLabel matches `label_pattern` with a non-zero fraction and its own menu items are empty, the items captured on that lesson's first page are re-used (shallow copies, so no per-page state is shared) and MenuBuilder renders them exactly as it did there. The human mostly repeats the lesson's menu on continuation pages (CEDT501, HIS1005, HIS1008, CEDW501, HIS1007, XTAS103, BLLR202, ENGS404, MXFL101, XMES202). NOT to be confused with the REPEATED MODULE OVERVIEW menu (the module's whole Understand / Know / Do block on every lesson page): that one is a pre-KB house convention the Writers Template cannot decide and KB 01B does not endorse — a named override, not built here (see lesson_repeats_overview for the hand-kept list). Env CONTMENU_OFF turns it off.

walt_alert.lead_pattern: ^(?:in this lesson,? you|we are learning|you will|this lesson)
walt_alert._doc: An alert / important box INSIDE a lesson's `[Lesson Overview]` block whose own text opens with a learning-intentions lead (lead_pattern: 'In this lesson you are reviewing your understanding of the UNDHR…' — HIS1003 / HIS1004's `[Lesson Overview] ` → `[Alert box] <sentence>` → `[Lesson content]`) is the lesson MENU's content, not a body callout: KB 01B / 01E make the lesson page's menu that lesson's own `[Lesson Overview]` block, and the human places such an alert's sentence in the menu (MXFL203's `coloured box` is a named exception), while every OTHER alert in such a block (CED's `[alert.top]` printable resources — the reason this section-stop ends at an alert — RHS asides, …) stays in the body or is dropped, never the menu. ON: such an alert is menu-safe in section A (the LO intro run) and joins the menu as a plain black-text item — its sentence as the human's `<p>`, no alert wrapper. Every other alert still ends the section. Env LOWALTALERT_OFF turns it off.

body_ends_section._doc: THE LESSON MENU ENDS AT THE WRITER'S `[Body]`. Inside a lesson's overview block the writer sometimes types a `[Body]`-tagged run — 'Welcome to lesson six. We are learning how to keep our wairua safe…', 'In this lesson you will learn about the properties of 2D shapes…' (XDLS903 / 904 / 906 / 908, MXEO202, ENGC403, GEO1005, XDLS901). The section-stop lists `body` among its menu-safe tags, so without this those runs would ride into #module-menu-content; the human places them in the BODY almost always. None of these runs is itself the WALT / SC lead line, so this can never decapitate a menu block. With this flag on, a tag listed in `tags` is NOT menu-safe: it ends the section-stop's run, and everything from it onward is ordinary body. Only the SECTION-STOP path consults this (the marked `[Lesson Overview]` form); the implicit block builds its own index set and is untouched. Env MENUBODY_OFF turns it off.

lesson_menu_section_stop.note: SECTION-STOP lesson-menu capture, coupled with the PAGE-ROLE-AWARE Menu_Scaffold_Registry (derive_menu_type.cjs; MENUREG_OFF). The lesson_content_in_menu region (LO → first heading) would absorb everything in between, but the CED NCEA family writes [Lesson Overview] → [alert.top] printable-resources + [Button]s → [Lesson content] → WALT → [H2], and the human keeps the alert/buttons in #body with only the WALT in the menu (CEDO501 1.0–6.0). With this flag the menu absorbs two CONTIGUOUS TEXT sections — the [Lesson Overview] intro run + the [Lesson content] section — each running only over black text and menu_section_safe_tags; ANY other tag (alert, button, image, interactive, heading) ends its section and stays body. Pages whose whole region is pure text are unaffected by construction. Env MENUSTOP_OFF uses the plain range.

XFUN|combo.sc_heading: How will I know if I've learned it?

EXPFUN|combo._note: The EXPFUN overview's human menu on EXPFUN02–05: two col-md-6 columns, h4>span labels ('Learning intentions', 'How will I know if I’ve learned it?'), the bullets verbatim. Reached through label_headings (the family types its labels as [H2] headings).
EXPFUN|combo.sc_heading: How will I know if I’ve learned it?

FRFUN|combo._note: KB 10 §5; §1d exception 1, a family dialect. The FRFUN Languages Fundamentals (FRFUN06 / 07 / 08) type `[Overview]` + `[Body] We are learning:` + bullets + `[Body] I can:` + bullets in three orders around their intro paragraphs and [Video]; the human routes ONLY that block to the module menu (the intro stays in the body). block_capture takes the block alone (fundamentals_overview_li.block_capture); the form follows the page's Menu_Scaffold_Registry type — simplified: FRFUN08's one col-md-8 column, the leads as <h5>; tabs: FRFUN06 / 07's pane form (two columns, h4>span labels, <h5> leads) in the tabs shell's first pane. The human's per-level (Novice | Emergent) wording is not in the Writers Template (class C). Env FUNBLOCK_OFF.

tabs.sc_heading: How will I know I have learned it?

block_capture._doc:
THE WALT / I-CAN BLOCK ALONE. The fundamentals capture routes the WHOLE [Overview] region (to the first structural tag) to the menu; for a registry row with block_capture: true the capture instead takes the WALT lead line (walt_match, lead_max_words) + the bullet lines right after it + the SC lead line that follows them (sc_match) + its bullets, anywhere on the overview page after the alias (an intro [Body] run or a [Video] before or after the block stays in the body), and consumes the alias (the human ships no Overview h3). A row's by_menu_type picks the form for the page's menu type: cols (1 → one column holding both leads; 2 → the LI | SC columns), lead_tag (the lead line as that heading, not a

), li_heading / sc_heading (optional generated labels), in_tabs (render inside the tabs shell's first pane). Env FUNBLOCK_OFF (the row declines).

label_headings._doc: THE LABELLED LI / SC LISTS. The fundamentals capture needs a WALT lead LINE and an SC lead LINE in the [Overview] region, and ends the region at the first structural tag; the EXPFUN family (EXPFUN02–05) types the two LABELS as headings — `[H2] Whāinga Ako | Learning Intentions` + `• We are learning …` bullets, `[H2] Paearu Angitu | How will I know if I’ve learned it?` + `• I can …` bullets — so without this the region would end at the first [H2], nothing would be captured and the overview menu would be blank. A heading of `tags` inside the region whose text matches `li_pattern` / `sc_pattern` is a region MEMBER and that side's LEAD; at compose time it switches the column and renders nothing itself (the registry's generated heading replaces it — the human's h4 label), and a column opened by a label heading keeps its lines verbatim (no lead-colon normalisation — its first line is a bullet, not a lead). The registry row still decides who fires (EXPFUN|combo). Env FUNLIHEAD_OFF.
label_headings.sc_pattern: (?:^|\|\s*)(?:how will i know\b.*|success criteria|paearu angitu)\s*:?\s*$|^paearu angitu\b

fundamentals_overview_li.note:
The Fundamentals header-menu LI/SC population (as in HPFUN903). The fundamentals front-matter [Overview] — a MID-doc title-bar alias whose variant word folds to an alias_words entry — marks the module's WALT/I-can block ('We are learning:' + bullets, 'I can:' + bullets). The human routes that block into #module-menu-content as the standard two-col LI/SC form with GENERATED labels (never in the WT — the only WT occurrence of 'Learning Intentions' is inside the template instruction), rather than a #body 'Overview' section beside a menu holding only the code line. CAPTURE (ContentConverter.#partitionItems): when the overview page's menu/body boundary alias matches alias_words AND the textish forward region (black text + menu_section_safe_tags + non-structural red, stopping at the first structural tag) contains BOTH a WALT lead (walt_match) and an SC lead (sc_match) — lead = a non-bullet line of <= lead_max_words — AND a registry row exists for the module's subject|template_phase group, the region routes to the MENU, the alias is CONSUMED (no

Overview

The Pathways writers type the overview menu's tabs as bare markers — `[Tab 1]

info_tab_omission._doc: Numbered constraint 67, universal: the tabbed overview menu includes 'only the tabs the Writers Template supplies content for (omission rule: absent content → remove BOTH the <li> and its .tab-pane; never synthesise placeholder content)'. The standards / LI promotions drop an Information tab they EMPTIED; this also covers an Information tab that was empty to begin with. On a page whose type is in page_types and whose menu is tabbed, a blank tab 2 (no text, image, iframe or table; no held tab-2 columns) sets dropTab2 — the nav <li> and the pane both go; the FRFUN in_tabs form the same. The human's own empty Information tab (ENGS401) and its non-canonical 'Information' tab holding the LI / SC or Knowledge (HIS1001, MXDB102, MXDI101–103, MXFL103, TEDC401 / 402) are NAMED overrides. Lesson pages are out of scope. Env INFOTABOMIT_OFF.

It covers what the MenuBuilder checks above cannot reach: a LESSON page's Information tab beside the lesson's own intentions (the human's form is one Overview tab), and a menu with no content at all (MenuBuilder returns early, so the shell would show two empty tabs; the first tab stays, holding the KB 10 §5 designer flag). It runs after the lesson-menu repeat copy, so a copied overview menu renders exactly as on the overview. Env BLANKTAB_OFF.

empty_lesson_menu_flag._doc: KB 10_CORPUS_VALIDATED_SCAFFOLDING.md §5 l.63, authority level 1: 'When the source has no such wording and no reference supplies it, you cannot invent it: build the empty #module-menu-content shell the skeleton requires and raise a visible red flag telling the designer the lesson-menu copy needs to be supplied.' (The hand-kept lesson_repeats_overview modules are the exception: their lesson menus copy the overview's.) A LESSON page whose simplified / simplified_bare menu is empty carries this To Do inside the shell, rather than shipping a blank menu with no flag. The cv2-note family is excluded from structural comparison. Env EMPTYMENUFLAG_OFF.
empty_lesson_menu_flag.text: Lesson menu: the Writers Template has no learning intentions / success criteria for this lesson — supply the lesson-menu copy (KB 10 §5).

extend.overview_text: Module menu: no overview copy was captured for the module menu — supply the module-menu copy (KB 10 §5).
extend._doc: The KB 10 §5 designer flag also covers a blank OVERVIEW module menu (e.g. ARFUN01–05, MXFUN02 / 03, XWHA01 simplified; SSFUN05 / 08, HIS1001, ART1004 tabs) and a blank TABBED lesson menu (SSCI104 1–5, SSEA203, GER1002 1), not only a blank simplified lesson menu: when every menu pane is blank (the pane-1 content, tab 2, the two-column and extra tabs), the overview carries `overview_text`, a tabbed lesson page the base `text`. The human menu text of these modules is in no Writers Template line, so the flag is the KB's own answer. Env EMPTYMENUFLAG2_OFF (EMPTYMENUFLAG_OFF turns off both).

simplified_bare_series._doc: 'A named Maths-series house style.' THE MX BARE LESSON MENU: on the LESSON pages of the MXFU (Standard MXFU2xx–4xx, not MXFUN), MXEX, MXDB3 and MXDI3 series the human always leaves the lesson menu BARE — #module-menu-content > h5 + ul, no row > col-md-8 col-12 wrapper. KB 01B l.296–301 says the lesson menu content goes inside the row > col-md-8 wrapper; the bare form is a SERIES CONVENTION for these four series (a series-scoped override of 01B, for the KB 10 §3 'series conventions — preserve' sub-table). A page whose menu resolves to the `simplified` shell renders the `simplified_bare` shell instead when the module code matches one of code_patterns and the page is a lesson page (the overview keeps its own menu). Every other module, every overview and every non-simplified menu is unaffected. It does NOT fill the empty MX lesson menus (no WT [Lesson Overview]) or build the missing MXEX201 / 202 menus. Env MXBAREMENU_OFF.

tab2_moved_guard._doc: THE INFORMATION TAB IS NEVER DROPPED WHILE IT HOLDS THE MOVED LEARNING INTENTIONS. A `curric_split` pane-1 registry row MOVES the overview's LI / SC runs to tab 2 and, when tab 2 has no native text, composes them as `tab2Cols` (the two-column Information form); the three empty-Information-tab drops — `_drop_empty_tab2`, `kb_canonical.drop_empty_tab2`, `kb_canonical.standards.drop_empty_tab2` — test `out.tab2`, so once the tab's native section (MXFL401's `Aromatawai | Assessment for Learning`) is promoted to its own tab, the Information tab would be dropped with the moved LI / SC inside it and the writer's text would appear on no page. Constraint 1 + KB c67's omission rule as written ('absent content → remove both the li and the pane' — the pane is not absent): each drop also requires no `tab2Cols` content. Env T2KEEP_OFF.

extra_tabs._doc: EXTRA MODULE-MENU TABS (as in AGH1001-0.0's [Module menu tab rules]). The human promotes SOME overview-menu sections to their OWN nav tabs (AGH1001: Overview | Information | Connections | Assessment for Learning) where a two-tab shell would put them in the Information pane as <h5> subsections. The ASSESSMENT section ([H2] Aromatawai | Assessment for Learning) is usually promoted — the tab LABEL mostly the house-style literal 'Standards' (the WT never contains that word; 'Assessment for Learning' / 'Assessment' are group-level minorities); the CONNECTIONS section ([H2] Hononga | Connections) is promoted only in a few families (AGH/XDLS/XTAS) and stays an Information <h5> everywhere else. Promotion + label are REGISTRY-gated per subject|phase group (a group's consistent choice, label ties deferring to the corpus label — AGH|NCEA's Standards-vs-AfL split has NO WT discriminator on byte-similar WT sections, so the corpus 'Standards' ships and the AfL pages are named deviations). Pane form = the human's dominant: row > col-md-8 col-12; the assessment pane KEEPS the section heading as an ENGLISH-reduced <h5> (the reo half drops), the connections pane DROPS it (the nav label replaces it). A promoted tab that ends up with NO content is dropped (never ship an empty pane). No registry row / lesson page / reo module / EXTRATABS_OFF => the h5-in-Information form. Env EXTRATABS_OFF.

curriculum_tabs._doc: The new-era Science curriculum sections (Knowledge / Practices) are their OWN nav tabs in the human build (SCCH301: Overview | Knowledge | Practices — NO Information tab; the reference for SCCH302), but the tab_map routes those headings to tab 1, where the tab2-only promotion never sees them. THREE row/section-scoped extensions, all turned off by env XTABCURRIC_OFF: (1) a section whose sections entry carries any_bucket:true is checked for promotion from ANY routed bucket, not just tab2 (sections without the key behave as before); (2) a sections entry may carry its own heading_element (the SCCH form is <h4><span>, the assessment default stays <h5>); (3) a registry row carrying _drop_empty_tab2:true drops the shell's Information nav item + empty pane when every section promoted away and no tab-2 content remains (row-scoped — every other tabs menu keeps its Information tab via the {tab2Nav}/{tab2Pane} shell slots' defaults).

kb_canonical._doc: KB constraint 67 / CL-0040, Universal; KB 10 §2: whenever the overview menu IS tabbed its composition follows the canonical content-driven set Overview → Knowledge → Practices → Information → Standards. Under the KB the Knowledge / Practices sections are ALWAYS their own nav tabs in the tabbed archetype, not only where a registry row names them: a module whose registry row does not name the section takes the canonical label from `labels`, but only for a heading whose folded text matches `heading_pattern` (the section heading itself — never a heading that merely CONTAINS the word, e.g. 'Learning intentions – Cultural knowledge'). `drop_empty_tab2` applies the KB omission rule (absent content → remove BOTH the <li> and the pane; never synthesise) to the Information tab those promotions empty. `exclude_subjects` = the subject letter prefixes the KB's own reconciliation leaves on their archetype: BLL (see readmit for BLL2xx) and WJFUN (the tile-page dialect, whose K / P headings never reach the menu walk). Env KPTABS_OFF limits this to registry rows.

readmit._doc: 'Their own tabs (the rulebook's set).' In the TABBED BLL2xx overview menus (BLL243, 247, 250, 251, 253, 255, 257, 261–266, 271–276) Knowledge and Practices each get their own nav tab in the KB c67 order (Overview → Knowledge → Practices → Information → Standards, 01B l.39) and the Information tab the promotions empty is removed (01B l.117 — drop_empty_tab2). A module whose code matches code_pattern is readmitted from exclude_subjects (BLL1xx is not decided and stays excluded); the flat (untabbed) BLL2xx menus are untouched by construction (the rule acts only in the tabbed archetype). The human's other forms — Information tabs (BLL251 / 255 / 257 / 263 / 264 / 266 / 275), BLL265's hybrid and BLL250's combined tab — are NAMED overrides. Env BLLKPTABS_OFF keeps BLL excluded.

standards._doc: KB constraint 67 / CL-0040 + 01B 'THE FIVE CANONICAL PANELS'. In the TABBED overview archetype the writer's assessment section (`[H2] Aromatawai | Assessment for Learning`, routed to tab 2) is the canonical Standards/Assessment tab — 01B: 'For the last tab, use Standards (the dominant corpus label) unless the uploaded reference clearly uses Assessment; the internal heading is "Assessment for Learning" either way' — even where menu.extra_tabs.registry has no row for the module's subject|phase (e.g. newer NCEA families). A registry row still decides its own label (MXEX|9-10 / SSOG|7-8 / XMES|4-6 = Assessment). drop_empty_tab2 = the c67 omission rule for the Information tab the promotion empties (the PWY human builds are Overview > Standards). exclude_subjects keeps a subject on its registry-only behaviour.

Row = a subject|phase group whose human pages consistently promote the section; value = the tab LABEL. groups keyed like tabs_pane1_two_col.registry (subject letters | resolved template_phase); series = per-module overrides, only for deviants (none listed).

tab_map._rule: Folded heading text → which tab pane and which element it becomes. Headings reaching the menu that match nothing are placed in tab 1 AND red-flagged (surface, never absorb). 'knowledge' + 'practices' are the new-era Science curriculum block (SCCH302); 'knowledge' also routes to tab 1 via the 'know' substring, and the explicit entries stop a spurious no-tab-rule red flag on 'Practices'.

tab_map.consume_note: A menu heading that IS the pane's own label is CONSUMED, as the human almost always does. Matching is folded substring-of-label.
tab_map._longest_match_doc: SPECIFICITY routing: the tab whose matched entry is LONGEST wins (rather than 'in tab 2 and not in tab 1 → tab 2, else tab 1'). This stops the bare 'do'/'know' substring pollution: 'What DO I need to get started?' contains tab1's 'do', which would strand the whole get-started section in tab 1 even though tab2's own longer entry matches exactly (the human puts it in tab 2). env TABROUTE_OFF uses the plain substring rule.

menu.overview_section_labels_note: Folded heading texts that identify an OVERVIEW MENU section. Used by ContentConverter.#partitionItems as a CONTENT-BASED fallback when a combined-doc overview has NO boundary marker ([MODULE INTRODUCTION] / mid-doc title-bar alias / in-page [End page]) — e.g. ENGJ302. A heading-led block whose heading matches one of these is routed into #module-menu-content; everything else stays in #body. 'Folded' = diacritics stripped + lowercased, so 'Whāinga Ako' matches 'whainga ako'. Add new section-heading wordings here (data edit, no code).

overview_section_labels_word_start._doc: In the content-based overview fallback (no [MODULE INTRODUCTION]) `matchesLabel` could accept a heading that CONTAINS an overview_section_labels entry as an inner or trailing word (`f.includes(' ' + l + ' ')`, `f.endsWith(' ' + l)`), so the SINGLE-WORD labels 'do' / 'know' / 'understand' would open a menu section on every question heading — CEDO204's `Why do birds build nests?` … `How do spiders build webs?`, TWHK901's `Reflect: What can you do …`, CEDR302's `What do I know?` — text the human keeps in its BODY. A label of fewer than min_words_for_inner words matches only at the START of the heading (whole, `l + ' '`, the colon forms); the multi-word labels ('how will i know', 'what do i need to get started', 'we are learning', 'i can' …) keep the inner / trailing tests, because writers embed them mid-heading ('Paearu Angitu | How will I know …'). Env MENUWORD_OFF allows inner / trailing matches for every label.

overview_section_labels_colon._inquiry_only_note: overview_section_labels_word_start tests every label against a punctuation-free fold, so `Understand:` / `Know:` / `Do:` match everywhere regardless of this flag (this matches the human build on ANZH104, XGF9004 and the TABS overviews ART1006 / HIS1007 / MXDI101 / MXEO201 / MXFL103); this flag only governs the literal colon forms on the raw fold. true = only for a page the Inquiry family claims (menu.two_col_li.inquiry_family); set false to apply everywhere.
overview_section_labels_colon._doc: In the content-based overview fallback (no [MODULE INTRODUCTION], no mid-document title-bar alias) a section label the writer typed with a trailing colon ('Understand:', 'Know:', 'Do:' — CEDT101 / 104 / 207 / 208 / 301 / 404, the ConnectED Inquiry form) matches overview_section_labels; the plain test needs a following space and would leave the curriculum block in the body while the human's menu carries it. Shares its toggle with the word-start rule.

overview_section_labels: what do i need to get started

inquiry_tab_ends_overview_menu._doc: On a SINGLE-FILE inquiry LANDING (TWHA901/903/906) the overview page holds BOTH the learning-design menu sections (Learning Intentions / Success Criteria / Planning / Connections / Assessment) AND the inquiry PANELS ([Tab 1: Introduction], [Tab 2], …). The CONTENT-BASED overview menu partition (menu.overview_section_labels) walks the items setting inMenu=true on a menu-label heading; the LAST menu section's inMenu=true would then SWALLOW the following [Tab 1]/[Tab 2] openers into #module-menu-content (they are not headings, so nothing flips inMenu off) until the first non-menu inquiry heading ([H3] Agency) — so [Tab 1]/[Tab 2] would never reach #body or get a panel sentinel, collapsing Introduction+Agency(+Resilience) into one panel. RULE: an inquiry [Tab N] opener ENDS the overview menu region (pastFirstTab) — the panels are always body content, so once the first tab-family opener is seen the rest of the page is body and is never routed to the menu. SCOPED to the overviewMenuIdx content-fallback path (introIdx<0 && isOverview && menu!=='none'); a module with NO [Tab N] opener is unaffected (the flag only fires where a tab-family tag exists, which is inquiry-only). Env INQMENU_OFF.

menu.simplified_lesson_rule: On lesson pages the [Lesson Overview] section's content (intro line + 'We are learning'/'I can' lists) fills {menuContent} — h5 for the list lead-ins, plain p/ul for the rest.

pane1_col_by_phase._note: Most-common tab-pane-1 column per phase (corpus 12/06/26: 1-3 md-8×22, 4-6 md-6×11, 7-8 md-12×18, 9-10 md-12/md-8 tie→md-12, NCEA md-6×32, combo md-6×15). Dev-variant; dominant wins.

banner_family._note:
The eng_family OVERVIEW menu transforms applied to the BLL/BANNER family (convention banner_h4_span:true, non-eng, so NOT selected by eng_family: BLL|1-3, ENGC|7-8, ENGC|9-10, ConnectED|1-3; as in BLL211-00). reduce_bilingual: a piped 'reo | english' LI/SC heading in the RIGHT column reduces to the English half (Whāinga Ako | Learning Intentions -> Learning Intentions), mirroring the bold-line path + eng_family. strip_italics: drop / from BOTH panes (the WT wraps WALT/I-can + curriculum prose in *italics*; human menus carry none). skip_named_promotion: keep 'We are learning:'/'I can:' as

lead-ins (the named-heading promotion does not run on this menu). banner_from_h1: render the top banner from the module [H1] section label reduced to English (Tirohanga Whānui | Overview -> Overview) via banner_template, rather than a 'Learning Intentions' literal that appears NOWHERE in the inputs. The banner WORD is editorially non-derivable — the human's choice (Overview / Bilingual / Learning Intentions / none) is MIXED at every grouping (subject, subject×phase, series, template); 'Overview' is the FAITHFUL rendering of the invariant WT [H1], not a structural guess; the human's era-driven deviations are non-derivable and not followed. Env BANNERMENU_OFF turns off the whole block.
banner_family._banner_max_words_note: banner_from_h1 only accepts a SHORT title (≤ this many words after the bilingual reduce). Guards against an [H1] that is 'Overview: <intro prose>' (CEDK101 and other Inquiry-family banner modules whose section label carries the module intro) — a long label is NOT a banner, so bail to the hardcoded default rather than dumping a paragraph into the h4.

two_col_li._curriculum_split_all_doc:
The curriculum SPLIT (the '**Label:** prose' Understand/Know/Do form → a label heading + the prose as a separate

) for EVERY two_col_li family, not just eng_family (as in CEDO102-00). Outside eng_family the curriculum would otherwise be pushed as a heading with the prose ABSORBED into the heading text (no separate content node), so the content-less headings would be removed by #dropEmptyHeadings and the LEFT column would be EMPTY. The split makes each label heading carry a following

so it survives. Uses the family's OWN left_heading template (the banner family's h5+span; eng_family keeps its curriculum_heading+#curriculumLevel path). Italics are stripped from the recovered LEFT pane to match the human's plain curriculum prose. The exact heading LEVEL (h3/h4/h5) and the banner's presence VARY editorially WITHIN families (e.g. BLL mostly h5, some h4; mostly with a banner) and are NOT cleanly derivable per-module — left at the family template default (a recovered node with a level near-miss is far better than a missing column). Env CURRICSPLIT_OFF limits the split to eng_family.
two_col_li.bold_label_note: Writers often mark the module LI/SC labels as BOLD lines (**Whāinga Ako | Learning Intentions**) rather than [H] tags — the menu builder treats a standalone bold line matching left_match/right_match as that column heading, using the ENGLISH part of a piped reo|english label (human BLL155-0.0 shows plain-English h5s).

The XOTP activity-table adapter's menu. The XOTP reader modules have NO overview page; every lesson page carries the same two-column menu in the human build: `col-md-6 col-sm-12 > div.item` left + right, the left pane `

Overview

` + its paragraph then Understand / Know / Do as `h3>I can:` label (lesson_label_form) stands (the human's `

` is a named override); the human's `

    ` for the I-can items is editorial bullets (plain paragraphs in the docx) — not followed. OFF (ITEMMENU_OFF, or ACTTABLEADAPT_OFF which refuses the module) = the BLL banner two_col_li form.

inquiry_family.empty_left_note: Writers Note: the curriculum Understand / Know / Do statements for this module go in this column — they are not in the Writers Template (the human developer writes them from the curriculum).
inquiry_family._doc:
KB 06 §3.4 (level 1): an INQUIRY module's overview menu is a two-column layout — left column `

Understand / Know / Do

` headings, right column `
Learning intentions
` + `
How will I know if I've learned it?
`. The NON-BLL Inquiry families' human builds follow it — TWHA / TWHK `col-md-6 paddingR | col-md-6 paddingL` with `h4>span` left + `h5` right, ConnectED paddingR | paddingL with `h4>span` left (some with a banner row above), EXPlore paddingR | paddingL with `h4>span` both sides — where the mined conventions would otherwise give the BLL banner shell (ConnectED 4-6 / 7-8), a single `col-md-8` column (TWHA: no overview convention in Html_Convention_Registry → 'flat') or NO menu (CEDW101 / CEDW201 / CEDR204, a no-evidence menu value). The BLL Inquiry PARENTS are excluded (exclude_subjects): their own human form IS the banner form (BLL110 / BLL120 are the family's outliers). The family: (a) an Inquiry-template overview (the module index's template_type — a module the index does not know keeps the plain path) outside the excluded subjects forces the two_col_li archetype (TWHA's flat → two columns), disables the banner family and the banner, and renders through the two_col_inquiry shell with these heading templates; (b) menuTypeFor's 'none' verdict for such a page becomes none_becomes ('simplified') so the button and the menu emit. The `
` labels ('We are learning:') in the right column (lesson_label_form) stay (the human's `

` lead-in is a named override). OFF (INQFAMILY_OFF — not INQMENU_OFF, which is inquiry_tab_ends_overview_menu's own toggle) turns it off.

eng_family._note: The OFFSET two_col family (as in ENGC102-00), selected when the resolved convention banner_h4_span is FALSE (ENG*/MX*/ANZH/SSOG/CEDO/CEDT/EXPFUN/XGF). The BLL banner family (banner_h4_span true) is separate. Keeps Understand/Know/Do (the curriculum [H2] '**Label:** *prose*' would otherwise have its prose absorbed into the heading text, so three text-only headings would be removed by dropEmptyHeadings). The menu lives in #header. Env MENUCURRIC_OFF turns off the whole block (the BLL-shaped two_col_li output).
eng_family._subjects_note: The OFFSET two_col treatment applies to the families whose human build uses the bare 'col-md-6 offset-md-0 col-12' shell with the simple Understand/Know/Do curriculum. EXCLUDED (different shells): MXFL/MXEX/ARFUN/XWHA (div.item carousel wrapper + plain col), ENGR/XFUN (offset+padding), CEDO/CEDT/EXPFUN/ENGFUN/XGF (col-md-6 col-12 paddingR), ANZH (mixed offset/paddingR). A module qualifies only when convention.banner_h4_span is false AND its subject is in this list.
eng_family._column_note:
Column split = curriculum-left / everything-else-right (the human's majority + the BLL convention; Learning-Intentions usually sits RIGHT with WILF, e.g. ENGS101). LEFT = curriculum (Understand/Know/Do, split into heading +

); RIGHT = Learning-Intentions/WALT + How-will-I-know/WILF + I-can/Success-Criteria. (ENGC102 balances LI to the left — editorial, not derivable — so its LI sits right under this rule; the curriculum column is still recovered.)
eng_family._split_note:
A curriculum (left_match) heading whose source is '**Label:** prose' splits into Label + the prose as a following

(the colon after the bold label is dropped). When the writer put the prose in a SEPARATE paragraph (BLL/ENGS form) rest is empty and the next black item supplies the

— both forms unify.
eng_family._reduce_note: LI/SC right-column headings reduce a piped 'reo | english' label to the ENGLISH half (Whāinga Ako | Learning Intentions -> 'Learning Intentions'), as the human does. TEXT-only.
eng_family._italics_note: strip <i>/<em> from the assembled left/right panes (the WT wraps curriculum prose + WALT/I-can lists in *italics*; human menus carry none). <b> is preserved.
eng_family._promotion_note:
do NOT run the named-heading promotion on this menu — in the two_col OVERVIEW menu 'We are learning:'/'I can:' are

lead-ins under the h5 'Learning Intentions'/'How will I know' heading, NOT promoted to headings.
eng_family._level_note: curriculum (Understand/Know/Do) heading level = the human's document re-level by subject×phase (a shift of +1/+2/+3 over the writer [H2], most often +2). by_group is the per-group dominant; by_phase is the fallback for a group with no data.

menu.consume_labels_note: consume_labels apply to EVERY menu archetype — the human menus never repeat the pane/section label heading (BLL155 has no 'Tirohanga Whānui' heading).

tabs_pane1_curric_split._doc:
Split a one-line OVERVIEW tabs-menu heading '**Title:** content' into the title heading + a following

(as in ENGR202-00), so a content-glued curriculum heading is not removed by dropEmptyHeadings (the same failure the two_col curriculum split prevents, on the tabs path). MenuBuilder.#splitTitleContent; confidence = a colon-terminated bold title OR a two_col_li.left_match curriculum label OR an Overview_Menu_Heading_Lexicon entry >= min_count (env MENUHEADINGLEX_OFF ignores the lexicon); a bilingual title (top-level '|' or an all-bold trailing half) is LEFT to the bilingual reduce; an ambiguous same-line heading is KEPT WHOLE (never dropped). env TABCURRICSPLIT_OFF keeps the content-glued heading. Overview-scoped (#header).

tabs_pane1_two_col._doc:
The OVERVIEW tabs-menu pane-1 TWO-COLUMN build (as in ENGJ402). The human renders tab 1 of most tabs overview menus as a curriculum/LI-SC column layout (the one-col families OS*/TRR/PNR/CED*501/MX*|1-3 are 'single'). pane1_col_by_phase records a single column width and serves as the TABTWOCOL_OFF path + the lesson-page/unregistered fallback. registry = generated from the human build (dominant pane-1 col-FORM + partition split per subject|phase; series rows only for ncols/split deviants). split kinds: curric_li (curriculum cols + LI/SC last col), curric_split (no LI in pane 1 — captured LI/SC heads move to TAB 2, the human's home for them, AGH1001/MXDI201), li_sc (LI col + SC col, no curriculum — CEDK501), single (the one-col path). Distribution: the LAST curric run anchors the LAST curric col (u,k|d, the 6+6 dominant); a col-md-12 BAND col takes the FIRST curric run only when exactly one other curric col remains (AGH1001 u|k,d) and stays EMPTY when two remain (ANZH304/404 |u,k|d — the human ships the empty spacer div). Any OTHER col ending empty = DECLINE, fall back to the single col. Guards: overview pages only; MenuBuilder.isReoModule (TRR bilingual keeps its one-col form); no registry row / 'single' row = the single-col path. Transforms (following the human tabs families): curric heading trailing-colon strip (the human almost always strips it) + the '**Label:** prose' glue split; LI/SC piped heading reduced to its English half (the human keeps eng-first strand labels like 'Measurement | Ine' — those are NOT in li/sc vocab, untouched); LI/SC level = li_level (h5 dominant; SSFUN05/08 h4 per group); curric level = curric_level (h4 dominant). Lead-in

s ('We are learning:'/'I can:') ride as captured content — never invented. Known differences: ART1002's empty col-md-8 band; MXDB301 strand sub-heads stay h4span (other-kind); pane-2 col token variance (AGH1001 col-md-6 paddingR vs the shell's col-md-8). env TABTWOCOL_OFF turns off the whole build (partition + registry + transforms).
tabs_pane1_two_col.curriculum_match_note: curric vocab = two_col_li.left_match (reused, so the two menus share one vocabulary); li/sc below are the right_match refinement (li vs sc sub-split for the li_sc split kind).

registry._note: Generated from the human build (two-col-aware: the unit is the col-FORM + partition split, NOT the first col's width). Dominant human pane-1 shape per subject|phase; series rows only where a module's ncols/split deviates from its group.

PWY|NCEA._note: The PWY family dialect (menu.writer_tab_markers): every PWY human pane 1 is LI | SC in two columns, col-md-6 paddingR / paddingL, each under an h4 label (mostly with a span). Turned off by env WTABMARK_OFF (the row's own env).

overview_banner_h4._note: OVERVIEW BANNER (as in OSAH401-0.0). On an OVERVIEW page whose module-menu carries NO Understand/Know/Do curriculum block, the human keeps the overview [H1] section label ('Tirohanga Whanui | Overview') as an <h4><span> banner at the TOP of tab 1 (OSAH301/OSAH401/OSOH101/OSOH201/OSSC301). Everywhere else the label is consumed and dropped (isLabel, tab_map.consume_labels). The banner family (two_col_li) re-homes it via bannerLabel; this covers the tabs/simplified overviews. Only OSAH/OSOH/OSSC do this consistently; OSGM/OSBY/CED/SSFUN/XMES/TRR114 do NOT (so 'no U/K/D' alone would over-fire -> scoped by subject). TRR301 (reo) banners it too but via a bilingual <h4 reo>/<h4 eng> split on a different menu path, not covered here. curriculum_labels is the belt-and-suspenders no-U/K/D guard. env OVBANNER_OFF.

bilingual_heading_reduce._doc: GENERAL BILINGUAL MENU-HEADING REDUCE. The writer types menu subsection headings bilingually — '[H2] Whakamaheretia tō wā | Planning your time' — and most human-built menus keep only the ENGLISH half rather than the pipe intact in the tab_map <h5>/<h4> emits and the simplified lesson-menu <h5>. The choice is a per-subject-group HOUSE STYLE — most groups reduce; a coherent KEEP family (the OSAH/OSOH/OSSC/OSSM/OSAI|1-3 'Online @ home' subjects + CEDW|NCEA, ENGR|7-8, MXDI|1-3, MXFU|7-8, ANZH|9-10, TWHK|7-8) keeps the full bilingual form. Registry rows = groups that consistently reduce (generated from the human build); lookup = series override -> subject|phase group, the extra_tabs/#tabsPane1Partition shape. Applied at RENDER only (tab_map heading fill + the simplified <h5>) — never to the ROUTING fold (the tab vocabulary carries both languages) and never inside a reo module. Known exceptions inside reduce rows (the human keeps the pipe): ANZH304, ENG1005, ENGJ302, HES1004, HIS1002, MXEX401, PHE1008, XDLS903, XDLS908, XMES201, XTAS102. No row / reo / MENUH5REO_OFF => the piped form. Env MENUH5REO_OFF.

learning_tab._doc: THE 'LEARNING' SECOND TAB (MXEO102/201/202/301 + ENGS102). These modules' human overviews name the SECOND menu tab 'Learning' and home the Learning-Intentions/Success-Criteria content there (tab 1 keeps only the Understand/Know/Do curriculum) instead of the standard 'Information' label; this two-tab Overview|Learning form is exactly ENGS102 + the MXEO modules. Their human builds also DELETE the writer's planning/get-started/connections/assessment sections outright — that deletion has no WT discriminator (other human builds such as AGH keep byte-similar sections), so the converter RETAINS the writer's info content BELOW the moved LI/SC in the Learning pane (the retention principle). SSOG301's four-tab Learning INSERT (Overview|Learning|Information|Assessment) is a one-module form = C, no row. Mechanism: when the module's group has a registry row, the LI/SC runs leave pane 1 for the top of tab 2 (via the pane-1 partition when it already moves them — ENGS102's curric_split — else the run-extraction path re-emitting the headings at the pane-1 row's li_level, the human's <h5>) and the tab-2 nav label becomes 'Learning' via the shells' {tab2Label} slot (default 'Information' everywhere else). All-or-nothing per module: if the LI/SC cannot be cleanly moved (e.g. pane 1 would be left empty), neither the move nor the label ships. Env LEARNTAB_OFF.
learning_tab.label: Learning

tab2_cols._doc: INFORMATION-PANE NATIVE TWO-COLUMN (as in AGH1002: the human Information tab lays its content out in TWO columns rather than one col-md-8). The column COUNT is a per-subject|phase house style whose within-group discriminator is LI/SC PRESENCE in the pane — AGH's li-carrying pages go 2-col while its li-less pages stay 1-col; MXEO's li-carrying Learning panes stay ONE col — so the rule is registry-gated, never a global 'li present => two-col'. KIND per group from the human's dominant pattern: 'li_sc' = LI-family groups LEFT, everything else RIGHT (the MX* families, [li]|[sc]); 'balance' = the first ceil(G/2) section groups LEFT (AGH/ANZH/HIS/CEDO/ENGR/MXFU — the split POINT itself is editorial within AGH, so the grouped balance is the general form). Consecutive li/li (an LI heading + its 'We are learning to:' lead h5) merge into ONE group before counting. Fires ONLY when the pane holds >=1 li/sc-family group + >=2 groups total and no tab2Cols were already composed (the moved-LI/SC two-col and learning-tab paths win first). Not covered (editorial, no consistent form): PHE|NCEA, XDLS|combo (li-less, indistinguishable from its 1-col siblings), SSFUN (phase-labelled panes), BLL (3-col Knowledge/Practices). Registry generated from the human build. Env INFOCOLS_OFF gives the single-column pane.

writer_tab_partition._doc: WRITER-AUTHORED MENU TAB PARTITION (as in ENGJ403): the newest WT era authors the overview menu's tabs EXPLICITLY — '[please set up as two tabs …][tab 1 – please title as appropriate]' … '[close tab]' '[tab 2 – …]' … '[close tab]' before [MODULE INTRODUCTION] — and the human builds exactly that partition (ENGJ403: tab 1 = LI/SC left | Planning/Get-started/Connections/Assessment right under the 'Tirohanga Whānui | Overview' h3 banner; tab 2 = Knowledge | Practices). When the SET-UP instruction + ≥min_closers closers are present, MenuBuilder.#writerTabPartition honours the writer's own tab boundaries instead of the tab_map fold routing. CEDK101's bare [tab N] crumb list (no set-up, no closer) declines BY CONSTRUCTION. Piped bilingual headings ship WHOLE (the human keeps them); WALT/I-can leads under an LI/SC heading ship as <h5> (lead_element); pane 1 headings plain <h4>, later panes <h4><span> (the human page's own two forms); a pane with LI/SC sections splits LI/SC LEFT | rest RIGHT, otherwise balanced (the tab2_cols kinds, decided per pane). Env MENUTABPART_OFF.
writer_tab_partition.lead_pattern: ^(we are learning|what are we learning|i can|you will show|how will i know)

lesson_li_label._doc: THE LESSON-MENU 'Learning intentions' LABEL (as in ENGJ403): the human opens a lesson page's simplified menu with a GENERATED label heading (not in the WT — the lesson regions carry only the WALT/I-can lines). Registry rows generated from the human's lesson-page menus grouped by the ENGINE-resolved subject|phase (attr-map-normalised — the #extraTabRow lookup): groups that consistently use the label, lesson menu type 'simplified', h4/h5 element forms only (the h3 families MXDB|4-6 / MXFUN|combo / SSCI|7-8 use different menu machinery and are not listed). Guards: lesson pages only, non-empty composed menu, never when a 'learning intention' heading is already present (double-emission-safe). Env MENULILABEL_OFF.

default_row._doc:
THE FIRST-IN-SERIES DEFAULT LABEL ROW (as for SCCH302): a module whose registry group failed the universal-field evidence floor (run.registryDefaultsApplied — no human-built sibling exists on disk, so no group row can match) gets its lesson simplified menu opened with the MODERN label form the design team confirmed for new subjects:

Learning Intentions

(the legacy '
Learning intentions
' wording is outdated for a new subject). Fires ONLY when no registry row matched AND the run carries the first-in-series flag — every module with real human evidence is untouched BY CONSTRUCTION. Env toggle: MENUDEFAULT_OFF.
default_row.label: Learning Intentions

lesson_label_form.note:
KB constraint 23 (Universal) + 01B 'Lesson Pages — Simplified Module Menu' lines 221–246 + the overview-tab label row 196–197; KB level 1 over the human's per-series split, a NAMED override. Inside #module-menu-content on EVERY page: (a) every learning / success LABEL — a p / h3 / h4 / h6 whose folded text starts with a role lead-in (role_lexicon), is at most label_max_words long, and either ends with a colon / ellipsis or is followed by a list — ships as (this supersedes, for menus, the exact-phrase list and its 'secondary lead-in stays

' discriminator, and the eng- and banner-family skip_named_promotion); (b) the label's FORM is the KB's: trailing '...' / '…' / nothing → ':' (the human mostly uses the colon forms: 'We are learning to:', 'You will show your understanding by:'); (c) learning_to_normalise — the writer's 'We are learning to:' / 'We are learning about/to …' family becomes the KB's learning_label 'We are learning:' and, so constraint 24's 'verb form matching heading context' still holds, each item of the list that follows gains item_prefix 'to ' (unless it already starts with it) with its first letter lowercased — what the human does where it re-words (CEDO502, ENGC401 …); 'We are learning about:' is KEPT (its items would need a verb rewrite — editorial); (d) drop_titles — on a LESSON page a section TITLE (title_lexicon: 'Learning intentions', 'How will I know if I've learned it?', 'Success criteria' …) that sits IMMEDIATELY ABOVE a label is dropped (01B line 223: the h5 IS the label); a title that is the label of its own list (followed by

    ) or a two-column banner (followed by a curriculum heading) is KEPT; on the OVERVIEW page every title stays (01B's

    overview titles); (e) overview_labels — the overview tab's 'We are learning:' / 'I can:' labels are
    too (01B 196–197 / constraint 67), rather than the two_col eng-family overview

    form (a NAMED override where the human keeps

    ); (f) a SENTENCE (a role lead-in longer than label_max_words, or with no colon / ellipsis and no list after it — the constraint-70 OSSC 'Ākonga will learn …' lead-in, 'You will be able to …') is never a label and stays

    ; (g) the SUCCESS label's wording is the writer's (colon form only): 01B's year table ('I can:' years 7–10 / 'You will show your understanding by:' years 1–6) needs a year the data does not hold (the code's level digit is not a year; the human is per-MODULE consistent) — year_table {CODE: '7-10' | '1-6'} is the hook, empty until the data or KB supplies it. Env MENULABEL_OFF turns off the whole pass.

role_lexicon.learning: ^(we are learning|we're learning|we learning|what are we learning|learning intentions?|ākonga will|akonga will|ākonga can|akonga can|students will|i am learning to|walt|what am i learning|what will i learn)\b
role_lexicon.success: ^(i can|you will (?:show|demonstrate) your understanding|success criteria|how will i know|wilf|you will be able to)\b

title_lexicon: how will i know if i've learned it
how will i know i have learned it

item_prefix_guard._doc: The 'to ' prefix is the KB 01B item normalisation — 'Items under "We are learning:" should begin lowercase with "to [verb]..." form' — and presupposes a VERB: on an item that opens with a wh-word, a gerund, an article or 'about' it would write 'to why spread is an important measure …', 'to making statements …', 'to the transfer …', 'to how to …' (MXS1004, HIS1004, HIS1008, PES1007). Such an item cannot reach the to-[verb] form by a prefix, so it keeps the writer's words (constraint 1) — only the lowercase first letter (KB 01B: menu items begin lowercase) is still applied; the label normalisation is unchanged. Env TOPREFIXGUARD_OFF.

lesson_label_form._year_table_note: 01B lines 240–244: the SUCCESS label is 'I can:' for years 7–10 and 'You will show your understanding by:' for years 1–6. Fill {CODE: '7-10'} / {CODE: '1-6'} per module (the gold is per-module consistent — 6 of ~130 modules mix); an entry re-words that module's success label; no entry = the writer's own label, colon form.

value_map._rule: footer_links pattern value per page type → ordered link keys. 'none' = the footer div renders with an empty nav ul omitted (just the #footer div) — matching ConnectED practice.

kb_position_defaults._doc: KB 01B_MODULE_MENUS_FOOTER 'Footer and Acknowledgements': the footer nav differs BY PAGE POSITION — overview `next-lesson + home-nav`, middle pages all three, FINAL page `prev-lesson + home-nav` only. The Style-Anchor registry can carry the miner's NO-EVIDENCE marker (an em dash) as a `footer_links` value (often `final`; `lesson` on OSSC), and `value_map["—"]` is undefined, so without this the footer would ship with NO links (mostly on a module's last page), where the human's footer is never empty. ON: a registry footer_links value with no value_map entry falls back to the KB's value for the page position (`overview` / `lesson` / `final`); a value that IS in the map is untouched, so every module whose registry carries real evidence is unaffected. Where the human's final page keeps `next` the KB's `prev+home` is a NAMED override (§1b). Env FOOTERPOS_OFF gives the empty footer + a warn note.

by_footer_class._doc: The sub-type forms the KB names in 06_TEMPLATE_RECOGNITION §3: `fundamentals-nav` is "typically home-nav only" (as the human mostly does); `inquiry-nav` pages follow the position rule (overview next+home / lesson all three / final prev+home) except the CED inquiry SHELL pages, which keep all three and arrive through `forceLinks` (the inquiry fallback) — that value takes precedence over these defaults. Keyed by a class token of the resolved footer class.

footer.auto_chain_note: prev/next hrefs can be auto-chained to the sibling output filenames ({CODE}-NN.html) by PageAssembler so the generated bundle navigates page-to-page. This chaining is used only under FOOTEREMPTY_OFF; by default nav_links_empty applies (the links are wired at publish time).

nav_links_empty.note: Change Ledger CL-0044, constraint 71: every footer nav anchor ships href="" — prev-lesson, next-lesson, home-nav alike. The conversion NEVER computes sibling filenames into them; the links are wired at publish time in D2L. The human build agrees: its footer hrefs are almost always empty, and the populated ones carry D2L quickLink URLs (/d2l/common/dialogs/quickLink/...rcode=TCS_Dev-NNNNN) = the publish-time wiring itself (overrides_gold false). The per-position <li> composition (value_map: overview next+home / middle prev+next+home / final prev+home / CED single-file none) and the id/class/target attributes are unchanged — only the {prevHref}/{nextHref} fill is empty. The choice-page TILE links (tiles href the generated lesson files) are a DIFFERENT element and are untouched. Env FOOTEREMPTY_OFF uses sibling chaining (auto_chain_note).

gathered_links._doc: KB constraint 75 ('inline → anchor') FOR GATHERED BODY TEXT. MediaBuilder.gatherFollowing joins a tag line's text with the following black items; without the gathered items' links, the emitters rendering it (ContentConverter.#element's body default, #calloutOpen) would lose a writer link in a gathered paragraph (ANZH104-6.0 'Google Lens / Seek by iNaturalist' inside activity 6B; OSBY401's Netsafe 'online contact form' alert). On: gatherFollowing records the gathered items' block.links (the tag's own included) and both emitters weave them (the free-body weave — exact phrase, first occurrence per line, never inside an <a>). Env GATHERLINKS_OFF turns it off.

activity_lead_links._doc: KB constraint 75 ('inline → anchor') FOR THE ACTIVITY'S LEAD PROSE. A bundle-owned activity's lead (the writer's instruction block before the widget box) is buffered by ContentConverter.ConvertPage's flushLead; without links the writer's hrefs would be lost (HES1007-3.0 activity 3B's five reading-list titles, which the human links). On: ContentConverter.#leadLinks hands flushLead the owner's block links + every non-table lead item's, through the widget-link filter (the target exclusion, >= 3-character text). Env LEADLINKS_OFF turns it off.

black_leading_tag_strip_more._doc: KB constraint 5: more tags for the black-leading-tag strip, kept in their own key so they reverse on their own env — `body text`: HIS1002-7.0 `[Body Text] Governments did not…`, MXDI201-8.0 `[body text] In the next activity…`, MXS1004-8.0 `[Body text] Strength is the measure…` typed the writer's [body text] tag in BLACK. Never legitimate content. Env BLACKBODYTEXT_OFF; BLACKTAGSTRIP_OFF turns off the whole strip.

body_region._black_leading_tag_strip_note: Structural tags a writer mis-typed in BLACK text (not the red [tag] style the detector reads) would leak as literal content; #renderBlackText strips a leading one of these from each black line. 'body' is the safe, high-frequency case (OSBY201-02 '[body] A trusted adult…'). Env BLACKTAGSTRIP_OFF. Add a tag here only if it is NEVER legitimate body content.

drop_glyph_only_lines._doc:
A free-body line whose whole content is ONE punctuation glyph (a writer's stray `.` / `,`, a text-box bracket `[` / `]` left after an image, a broken equation's `+` `=` `–`, PNR102's `✔` ticks) would ship as `

.

`; the human never ships such a paragraph. In ListsAndRuns.renderBlackText's line filter, free-body text only (stitch true — the placeholder / built-widget dumps stay a faithful hand-off): a line that, with its `*` emphasis markers removed, is exactly one character that is not a letter, not a digit, not `_` and not in `keep`, is dropped before it can become a paragraph. `•` is kept for the bullet path's own empty-item rule. OFF keeps these lines.

closer_residue_strip._doc:
THE [end X] LEFTOVER. A writer CLOSER directive ([End page] / [End of important box] / [End interactive] / [End of task] / [End of alert box] / [End supervisor note] …) renders NOTHING, but in a few downstream render contexts (a black or coalesced run, a flowing quote box) it can survive into the BODY as a LONE

[tag]

, which the human never ships. #stripCloserResidue removes such a

when the bracket (a) carries the standalone word end/ends AND (b) resolves via the REAL TagNormaliser to a CONTAINER_CLOSE or PAGE_BOUNDARY directive (class 'tag'). The 'end' word-guard is the precision floor — it EXCLUDES a mis-resolved heading like [Lesson Summary] (resolves to lesson/PAGE_BOUNDARY but has no 'end' → kept) and the [next page] page-break openers; the resolver-guard EXCLUDES content (e.g. [a mini-dictionary … near the end of a book] resolves to an OPENER 'important' → kept). A bracket carrying embedded CONTENT ([Lesson 2] THE WORLD COURT) is never a LONE

so it is untouched. The general [end X] closer convention itself is handled upstream (the end/of prefix, the 'X ends' suffix and the lexicon end-* aliases resolve almost every closer); this rule only removes the leftover (e.g. ENGFUN02, HIS1002, HIS1005, HIS1006, XDLS502, XGF9004). Env ENDCLOSER_OFF keeps the lone

.

first_heading_level._note_level_dialect: level_dialect_code_prefixes: a family listed here is promoted ONLY on a page whose panels the tile-pages / level-pages pre-pass made (run._levelMenu set). WJFUN: every human tile panel opens with its title as <h2>; the promotion rides TILEPAGE_OFF, and a WJFUN panel made by the 'Phase N' path is not touched (the human has no such heading).
first_heading_level._doc: THE PANEL'S FIRST OWN HEADING IS h2: the first heading directly in an inquiryPanel's / fundamentalsPanel's own column — not inside an activity, alert, supervisor panel or widget box, and not the introduction panel — renders at `level` (2) whatever level the writer's digit + the body shift + the rank rule gave it (otherwise the panel label heading comes out h3 / h4 / h5). The human's inquiry panels mostly open with h2 (CED*, TWHA, TWHK, EXPFUN, BLL) — EXBP / EXIP are excluded; the fundamentals panels split by family: HPFUN, ARFUN, SCFUN, MXFUN and TEFUN open with h2, while ENFUN / SSFUN / CHFUN / XFUN use h3, so only the listed `fundamentals_code_prefixes` take the rule. KB 06 §3.4 / §3.3 do not name the panel title's level; KB 06 §6's `<h3>` is the general section heading — the human's own group convention decides (§1b 3). A post-pass on the finished body (PanelsBuilder.panelTitleLevelPostpass, after inquiryPanels), the activity-title pass's sibling. Env PANELH2_OFF.

fundamentals_panels._doc: Wrap the FUNDAMENTALS body into div.fundamentalsPanel phase="N" panels. The HPFUN family delimits each phase with a [New tab] marker (which would otherwise ORPHAN as a '[tab n]' RED FLAG); in fundamentals mode ContentConverter drops that flag and pushes a top-level {sentinel} at each [New tab], and #fundamentalsPanels splits the assembled body on the sentinel and wraps every non-empty segment. The FIRST segment is the introduction panel (intro_class). AUTO-SCOPED to modules that carry [New tab] (the HPFUN family); the SSFUN and XFUN families carry NO [New tab], so the pass is a NO-OP for them (see _ssfun_note and phase_text). Not generated (non-derivable): the div.phases nav's editorial short labels ('Intro'/'Feelings'), the intro phaseLink cards' editorial images/labels/col-md layout; the tab-nav CS notes are left as notes. Env FUNDPANEL_OFF gives the flat render (orphan flags and all).
fundamentals_panels._ssfun_note:
The SSFUN family delimits its phases with a `[LESSON] FUNdamental Phase N:` PAGE_BOUNDARY tag (kept in-stream in single-file mode), NOT a [New tab]. ContentConverter pushes the `lesson_sentinel` at each; #fundamentalsPanels wraps each segment as a plain fundamentalsPanel (NO introduction) with a generated `phase_heading` (`

Phase N

` — the human's heading). Env FUNDPANEL_OFF turns off both families.

phase_text._doc:
The TEFUN fundamentals family delimits each phase with a PLAIN-TEXT 'Phase N' line (no tag, as in TEFUN02). Neither the HPFUN [New tab] nor the SSFUN [LESSON] path sees it, so without this the body would never panel and the 'Phase N' lines would show as bare

Phase N

at the top of #body. In fundamentals mode, when a single page carries >= min_delimiters standalone 'Phase N' black paragraphs AND no tag-based page/phase delimiter ([New tab]/[LESSON]/[Page N]), ContentConverter consumes each 'Phase N' line into a top-level {sentinel}; #fundamentalsPanels (phase_text branch) emits the div.phases nav (one

Phase N

per delimiter), wraps the pre-phase content in div.introduction, and wraps each phase segment in div.fundamentalsPanel phase=N (NO generated heading — the human keeps the phase's own [H3] 'Plan it!'/'Present it!'). The >=2-on-page + no-tag-delimiter gate scopes this to the single-page 4-phase TEFUN01-08 family and EXCLUDES MXFUN01 (a multi-file module whose Phase 1/2/4 sit on a deep page with [Page N]/[Lesson] openers). Not generated (non-derivable): the phaseLink cards' editorial images + the editorial Te Reo title. Env FUNDPHASE_OFF gives the flat render (bare

Phase N

, no panels).

list_then_headings._doc: A FUNDAMENTALS PAGE'S 'PHASE N' LIST NAMES ITS PHASES; ITS SECTION HEADINGS OPEN THEM: ANZHFUN05 lists four bold black lines '**Phase 1**' … '**Phase 4**' under its introduction's lead, then its [H1] introduction, then EXACTLY four '[H2] Writing in history: …' sections — the human's four fundamentalsPanels (the Phase N list stays in div.introduction). The phase-text rule reads a bare 'Phase N' line as a DELIMITER (the TEFUN form); these lines are bold and form a LIST. On a single-file fundamentals page where the phase-text mode did not fire, a run of consecutive list lines (list_line_pattern) numbered 1 … k (k >= min_delimiters) followed later by exactly k top-level heading_tag items puts a phasebreak before each of those headings; the list renders as before. Env PHASELIST_OFF.

red_delimiter._doc: The ENFUN family (ENFUN01-05/07/08/09, all single-file) delimits each phase with a standalone RED 'Phase N' span (no brackets: class noise, primary null, renders NOTHING) — the red twin of the TEFUN black line — so the black-line pre-pass would not fire and the human's chrome-and-panels form (.phases nav + introduction/tiles + 4 fundamentalsPanel) would come out FLAT. Longer prose mentions ('link to phase 2 fundamental', '[MXFUN102 content - Phase 1]') stay inert under the ENTIRE-folded-text predicate; a lone span is below min_delimiters. THREE coupled acceptances, ONE toggle: (1) the ConvertPage pre-pass accepts the red span (type tag, no primary, class noise/instruction, whole folded text matching delimiter_pattern) as a phasebreak, blackAfter preserved; (2) #partitionItems routes a PRE-alias matching span to bodyItems (it renders nothing in the menu — position-only, the bare-lead class; the fundamentals menu region otherwise untouched); (3) InteractiveScanner #swallowMembers treats it as a HARD terminator (the red twin of terminators_absolute_text — otherwise a widget can swallow a span and that phase never opens). The emit path is the phase-text one (nav 'Phase N' labels + introduction holding the phaseLink tiles + plain panels = the human's ENFUN form, as for TEFUN02); the human's introduction PROSE is human-authored (in NO WT) = C, as are the per-phase [Overview]+WALT repeat blocks the human drops/merges into the menu editorially. Gate everywhere: fundamentals body_class + page_model single-file + the flag (+ >=min_delimiters page-wide for the pre-pass/partition). Env FUNPANRED_OFF turns off all three.

code_content_delimiter._doc: §1d exception 1, THE MXFUN CODE-CONTENT PHASE DIALECT. The MXFUN02 / MXFUN03 Writers Templates author ONE single-file Fundamentals module as four PHASES, each opened by a red marker of the form `[MXFUN203 Content - PHASE 2]` (the per-phase deliverable code + 'Content - PHASE N') and each REPEATING the front matter — `[Fundamental 1 code] MXFUN203`, `[Title] Measurement`, `[Fundamental content]` — before its `[Page N]` + `[Side tab N] label` sections; an `[Intro page]` / `[Front page]` … `[End page]` block before `[Page 1]` is the module introduction. The human builds the fundamentals PHASES shell: div.phases (one item per phase), div.introduction (the intro page's paragraphs + the row.phaseContainer of col-md-3 col-6 phaseLink tiles), one div.fundamentalsPanel[phase=N] per phase with its pages FLAT inside (no sub-panels, no crumbs), the side-tab labels not rendered (the h1s come from the writer's `[Lesson N title H1]`), the overview menu an empty simplified shell. Without this rule the second `[Title]` would be read as the overview's intro marker (all of Phase 1 would land in #module-menu-content), the labelled side tabs + page openers would fire the page-delimited inquiry mode (crumbs + inquiryPanels), and the \btab\b sentinel would wrap every side tab in its own fundamentalsPanel. HOW: ContentConverter.#codePhasePrepass (on page.items, before #partitionItems; fundamentals body class + single-file page model + at least one marker with N >= 2) marks every marker (N = 1 consumed — the first phase opens at the first non-intro `[Page N]` opener, which becomes the first break), the per-phase front-matter repeats after each marker (consume_repeat_tags; the page's FIRST title bar is kept as the opener) and every `[Side tab N]` (side_tab_pattern) as consumed; the overview intro-marker search skips consumed items (no menu region → the empty simplified shell); the phase-text pre-pass turns the breaks into phasebreak items and splices the consumed items out; the page-delimited / CED / heading-label / side-tab-nav inquiry modes are vetoed on a code-phase page. MXFUN01 (the same family, a bare `[PHASE N]` marker) is multi-file (page_model_exceptions) and is untouched; SCES201's `[phase N]` are moon-phase table cells inside a widget (never a tag item — a fence). Env CODEPHASE_OFF turns off the whole dialect.

bracketed_delimiter._doc: The ARFUN family (ARFUN01/02/03/05, single-file) delimits each fundamentals phase with BRACKETED red instruction spans — the third dialect after TEFUN's black 'Phase N' and ENFUN's bare red 'Phase N' — in widely varied wording, spelled numbers AND digits: openers '[Phase one content begins]'/'[Start of phase two content]' (class instruction, primary null; they would otherwise render as retained CS notes), closers '[End of Phase One]'/'[End of phase two content]' ('end other', CONTAINER_CLOSE) and '[End page and phase N content]' ('end page', PAGE_BOUNDARY — those never reach ConvertPage items). ARFUN02's phase-4 boundary is CLOSER-ONLY ('[End of phase three content]' — the writer never wrote a phase-4 opener), so closers are break candidates too, gated by closer_requires_opener: CLOSER-ONLY modules (ARFUN04 + TEFUN01/03/04/06/07/08 '[end phase N]') stay untouched — TEFUN already panels via the black dialect (unconditional closer acceptance would double-break it) and ARFUN04 (multi-file page model, a 'beginning of/begin' opener dialect) is not covered. An engagement-quiz bundle can swallow the next phase's opener (ARFUN01/03/05), so the scanner hard-terminator twin covers the OPENER pattern (closers are never consumed). Adjacent closer+opener breaks and a trailing break are harmless by construction (the phase_text emit branch trims + filters empty segments). Both patterns are ENTIRE-folded-span with optional surrounding brackets, so near-miss wording stays inert; no module carries both this and the black/red dialects. Env FUNPANBRACKET_OFF turns off all three acceptances; FUNDPHASE_OFF turns off the whole phase-text machinery.

tag_anchored_delimiter._doc:
SCFUN01 and SSFUN03 anchor the phase word to a TAG's blackAfter instead of a standalone line/span — the fourth and fifth delimiter shapes after TEFUN black, ENFUN bare-red and ARFUN bracketed: SCFUN01 '[TILE N] Phase N' (primary 'shape n' SUBTAG — the split-bracket '[TILE 1'+']' and ✅-emoji forms all self-heal to a clean parse; ONE tile the writer typed in BLACK text, '[Tile 2] Phase 2', is covered by black_line_pattern) and SSFUN03 '[Fundamental content] SSFUN03 **PHASE N**' (primary 'lesson content' SECTION_MARKER; the blackAfter carries the MODULE-CODE prefix + ** bold marks — the {code} placeholder in blackafter_pattern is replaced with the run's own module code, never hard-coded). eligible_tags maps each primary tag to its BREAK KIND — the branch whose emitted form matches the family's human build: 'shape n' → 'phase_text' (ptsent; SCFUN01's panels open with the WT's own [h2], NO generated heading — the TEFUN form) and 'lesson content' → 'lesson' (lsent; the SSFUN family form = generated

Phase N

, as in SSFUN01/02/05/06 — SSFUN03's own h5 is a within-family deviation, the family form ships). The predicate: an UNCONSUMED tag item whose primary is in eligible_tags AND whose ENTIRE cleaned blackAfter (** stripped, symbol/emoji edges stripped, whitespace folded) matches blackafter_pattern — so residual prose can never be silently dropped. EXPFUN02-05 '[Title] Phase N' is excluded structurally (title bar NOT in eligible_tags); XFUN01's [H1] delimiters carry longer text and never match; these tags are never widget-consumed, so no scanner twin is needed.
