SCFUN01's orphan [tab 1]/[tab 2] SUBTAGs in phase 4 would otherwise hit the [New tab] push and add phantom panels: the ptsent branch strips stray CV2_FUNDPANEL sentinels (the human builds that pair as real tabs, not covered here). Env FUNPANTAG_OFF turns off the whole acceptance; FUNDPHASE_OFF turns off the entire phase-text machinery.

accordion_delimiter._doc: XFUN01 authors its whole body as ONE [Accordion] widget of NINE numbered [Accordion 1..9] sections, and the human builds NO accordion — the fundamentals phases chrome instead (nav ×9 heading-labels + ONE noPhase row of 9 phaseLink tiles + 9 fundamentalsPanel, 1:1 BY NUMBER with the writer's sections; panel 8's head is the writer's [H4], so heading-counting misses it — the accordion NUMBER is the phase). These delimiters are widget INVOCATIONS the scanner consumes into bundles (the other phase dialects accept UNCONSUMED items), so the rule is FOUR coupled pieces behind this one flag: (1) InteractiveScanner SUPPRESSION — on a gated page an accordion-primary INTERACTIVE invocation never opens a bundle (numbered/bare forms left unconsumed for the pre-pass; the writer's '[link to this section of the accordion menu]' cross-link falls to the link dissolve) + the numbered/bare forms are HARD member-walk terminators (no other bundle may swallow a phase boundary); (2) the ConvertPage pre-pass — folded ^\[accordion (\d+)\]$ → ONE {type:phasebreak} (ptsent kind: panels keep their own [H3]/[H4], the TEFUN no-generated-heading form), the bare [accordion] opener + the [End accordion section] closers (bracketed CONTAINER_CLOSE + one bracket-less instruction form) → consumed no-ops, blackAfter preserved everywhere; (3) the third nav/tile dialect on the ptsent branch, driven by THIS registry row: label_mode heading (faithful first-heading nav labels — the human's 'Low tech'⊂'Low tech (no computer chip in sight)' abbreviations are editorial) + ALL-phases ONE-ROW col-md-4 col-6 tiles in a 'row phaseContainer noPhase' container with alt='Phase N' (differs from both phaseNavTiles and newTabNav; tile img = panel-first-img with intro fallback — the human's tile iStock images are in NO WT); (4) leftover handling — link_dissolve_pattern drops a '[link to … section]' cross-reference MARKER and re-exposes its blackAfter as prose (the human keeps the prose, drops/edits the links, instead of orphan-subtag red flags), black_residue_pattern drops a split-bracket black '[' leftover. THE FENCE: numbered [Accordion N] is the corpus-STANDARD accordion idiom — non-fundamentals modules build REAL accordions and are untouched BY CONSTRUCTION (no registry row), so only XFUN01 is gated; XFUN02 is fenced (no numbered accordions, multi-file, lesson-structured). Registry lookup = series → subject|template_phase via skeleton.template_attr_map. Not generated (C): the human's rearranged Hoa-ako note + 'Be my hands' in panel 5 (the WT's Accordion 9 — kept in panel 9), a video + nznasca button in NO WT, the tile iStock images. Env FUNPANACC_OFF turns off all four pieces; FUNDPHASE_OFF turns off the entire phase-text machinery.

phase_nav_tiles._doc: The phaseLink picture-tile NAV (.row.phaseContainer of N `col-md-3 col-6` > div.phaseLink[phase=N] > h3 'Phase N' + img.phaseImg) + the `.phases` nav, for the Phase-N fundamentals families (the phase_text/TEFUN branch builds the nav; the lesson/SSFUN branch gets nav + .introduction added). The human's fundamentals overview always pairs a `.phases` nav with this tile row inside `.introduction`. Keyed on the build's OWN phase set (panelSegs) so it is self-scoping — a non-fundamentals page never reaches #fundamentalsPanels. Tile LABEL 'Phase N' is derivable; the editorial tile IMAGE is not, so each phase's first content image is hoisted as a thumbnail (an image-less phase yields an h3-only tile). HPFUN ([New tab], custom tile labels + intro=phase-1) is built by new_tab_nav (below). Env PHASETILES_OFF gives the nav-less/tile-less render.

writer_tile_labels._menu_bound_note: The menu/body-boundary half of this rule (a mid-document title-bar alias INSIDE phase 1 is that phase's title, not the boundary) must never touch the fundamentals `[Overview]` alias — that alias IS the menu source for the ENFUN / HPFUN family (menu.fundamentals_overview_li, the `_funLi` capture); without this list the ENFUN overviews would lose their Learning-intentions menu. Only a plain `[Title]` / `[Introduction]` alias is bounded.
writer_tile_labels._doc: §1d exception 1, the ARFUN family dialect: THE WRITER'S PHASE-TILE LABELS. The ARFUN Writers Templates (ARFUN02 / 03 / 05 red, ARFUN04 black) follow the overview's `[Insert links to the 4 individual phases]` instruction with four `[Title: Phase one] Emoji for thumb nail 🎸` lines — the labels of the phaseLink tiles the human builds (h3 'Phase N' + an image, generated here by phaseNavTiles). They parse as title-bar aliases, so without this the first would be the overview's INTRO MARKER (the whole introduction — the welcome prose, the right-hand alert, the elements list — would land in #module-menu-content; the human's div.introduction holds it) and the rest would render as <h4>s in the menu; on ARFUN02 the first would even be the PAGE OPENER (the real `[Title: Puoro me te Oro| Music and Sound]` resolves to `audio` — see Tag_Lexicon _meta.head_section_marker_owns_payload). On a fundamentals-class page, #partitionItems marks a title-bar item whose payload (the text after 'title:') matches payload_pattern, and a black line matching black_line_pattern, as a tile label: never the opener, never the intro marker, consumed (rendered nowhere — the tiles are generated). Env PHASETILELABEL_OFF turns it off.

new_tab_nav._doc:
The .phases nav + phaseLink tile pairing for the HPFUN [New tab] branch (as in HPFUN903). The human pairs EVERY [New tab] fundamentals overview with (a) a .phases nav of one

{label}

per PANEL (intro included) and (b) a phaseLink tile grid for the CONTENT phases only (2..N — one tile per content panel; HPFUN401's missing 7th tile is its own outlier), the tiles sitting INSIDE the intro panel after its content, chunked into .row.phaseContainer rows of tiles_per_row when the count exceeds tiles_split_over (4 tiles → one row; 5 → 3+2 HPFUN301; 6 → 3+3 HPFUN903; HPFUN101's single row of 5 + HPFUN102's justify-content-center wrapper are outliers — the family form ships). LABELS: label_mode 'heading' = each panel segment's FIRST heading, English half before ' | ' — the FAITHFUL [H2] text; the human's abbreviations ('Intro', 'Wheels' vs its own tile 'Wheeling around') are editorial. Tile alt = the label (HPFUN201's form; HPFUN903's own alts are copy-paste junk from a water-safety sibling). Tile image = the phase segment's first content src, module-first-image fallback. SCOPE: a registry row must exist for the module's subject|template_phase group — HPFUN|combo (the [New tab]-branch family whose panels are sound); ARFUN04, SCFUN01 and MXFUN01 have NO row and are untouched BY CONSTRUCTION. label_mode is data per group because the families differ (HPFUN/MXFUN01/XFUN01 use section names; ENFUN/ARFUN/TEFUN/SSFUN use 'Phase N'). Env FUNNAV_OFF gives the [New tab] branch its nav-less form.

tile_pages._doc_li_run_any: A tile's FIRST We-are-learning run is its menu pane's LI / SC whatever introduces it — a label line (Year 3 Learning Intention), a red [Learning Intentions] tag, a red lead, [H3] Learning intentions + [body], a writer instruction — so the pane is not left with only the h5 (as in several WJFUN modules). Env TILELIRUN_OFF.
tile_pages._doc: THE TILE-PAGE fundamentals dialect (the WJFUN 'My Te Kura Writing' FUNdamentals family): the writer authors ONE single-file module whose lessons are TILES — `[Tile N content]` (or `[Tile N]`) opens each, `[Tile N content ENDS]` closes it; inside a tile `[H1] ` names it, `[Overview]` + `[Learning intention for tile]` (a 'We are learning:' lead + bullets) + `[Success criteria for tile]` ('I can:' + bullets) carry its menu pane, `[Lesson content]` opens the body; before the tiles the module's `[Overview]` holds the `[H3] Knowledge Year N` / `[H3] Practices Year N` bullet blocks (the menu's Overview pane, two columns), the `[Introduction content]` prose, an `[Insert links/buttons to the individual tile sections …]` tile table (rendered by the tile row, so consumed) and the `[RHS side tab navigation: for all pages/tiles]` list of `Tab N <label>` lines (the phases nav's labels, consumed). The count of distinct `[Tile N …]` markers (and the `Tab N` list) matches the human's fundamentalsPanel count (exceptions: WJFUN105's developer split one tile in two, WJFUN112's nav lists a 'Test' phase without a panel). The human form: `div.phases` nav labelled with the tab labels, `div.introduction` ending in a `row phaseContainer` of `col-md-3 col-6` phaseLink tiles (h3 label + phaseImg), one `fundamentalsPanel phase=N` per tile opening with the tile title as `<h2>`, and a tabs menu Overview + one pane per tile (ONE `col-md-8 col-12` column: `<h5>Learning Intentions</h5><p>We are learning:</p><ul>…</ul><p>I can:</p><ul>…</ul>`). Rides the level-pages machinery: the pre-pass pushes a phasebreak per tile, synthesizes the tile title as a writer heading (title_writer_level), fills run._levelMenu (PanelsBuilder.#levelPagesNav builds nav + tiles from the registry row; MenuBuilder.#levelTabs composes the panes — menu.pane_form 'single_col' puts LI + SC in one column). Registry-gated (WJFUN|1-3 / 4-6 / 7-8) + fundamentals body class + single-file; a module with fewer than min_markers distinct tile markers is left as it is. Env TILEPAGE_OFF turns off the whole dialect.
tile_pages.tile_links_pattern: ^\[insert links?\s*/\s*buttons? to the individual tile sections
tile_pages.module_pane_heading_pattern: knowledge|practices|learning intention|success criteria|how will i know
tile_pages._doc_boundaries: The dialect's three tile BOUNDARIES, counted together against min_markers: (1) a `[Tile N content]` / `[Tile N]` marker (marker_pattern — most of the family); (2) a `[LESSON N]` marker, alone or riding the title's own span (`[LESSON 1] [H1] Literary Techniques`; lesson_marker_pattern, lesson_markers — WJFUN205 / 210 / 212); (3) a top-level heading (title_tags) whose text IS one of the tile NAMES the writer listed (named_heading_openers — the opener-by-name pattern; WJFUN210 / 307). The names come from the `Tab N` side-tab list (tab_line_pattern) or the `[Tile title] / X` cells of the tile-links table (tile_title_cell_pattern; the table is recognised by its own cells, tile_cell_pattern, whatever its instruction line says). A tile's LI / SC block typed as a `[Lesson Overview]` / tile `[Overview]` + 'We are learning: … I can: …' run (no `[Learning intention for tile]` tag) splits at the SC lead (li_lead_pattern / sc_lead_pattern) into the tile's pane — the FIRST tile's block is harvested from the menu items when #partitionItems routed it there.
tile_pages.sc_lead_pattern: ^(i can\b|success criteria|how will i know|you will show)

shell_row._doc: The tile dialect's menu takes the ROW+COL tabs shell (moduleMenu › div.row › div.tabs.col-12 — `menu.shells.writer_tabs_row`) rather than the bare writer_tabs shell of the level-pages machinery: the WJFUN human build always uses ROW+COL, as the human does for almost every tabs menu. CHFUN (bare in the human build) keeps the bare shell: this block lives on tile_pages.menu only. OFF = the bare shell.

menu.sc_label_default: How will I know I have learned it?

registry._doc: series (this module's own code) beats the subject|template_phase group. Every WJFUN level shares the gold's one tile form.

level_pages._doc: The LEVEL-PAGE fundamentals dialect (as in CHFUN01). The Languages Fundamentals family authors ONE single-file module as '[PAGE N <Level>]' sections grouped by named proficiency LEVEL (Novice, Emergent, ...): each level = ONE fundamentalsPanel (its pages joined, each page's marker text becoming a section heading synthesized at title_writer_level so the ordinary relevel ranks it h3 and pushes writer [H2]s to h4 — the human's outline); the phases nav + phaseLink tiles carry the LEVEL names; each page's [Page Overview] LI/SC block aggregates BY LEVEL into the module menu's per-level tab panes (Overview tab = the module's own [Overview]-section [H3] LI/SC blocks; introduction prose stays in the body). Markers require a LEVEL WORD after the digit, so the CED/XDLS '[page N]' splits can never match. Registry-gated + single-file. Env toggle: LEVELPAGE_OFF.
level_pages._doc_level_section_marker_pattern: The JPFUN family's LEVEL SECTIONS: JPFUN02's writer marks them as '[Novice Content starts here]' … '[Novice content ends here]' '[Emergent Content starts here]' — unresolved instruction spans, not page tags — so without this the level pre-pass would not run (no .phases nav, no level panels, no level menu). For a registry row with level_sections: true (JPFUN|combo) the opener is a level marker (its level word the label; a repeated opener for an already-open level re-enters it — JPFUN02 types '[Novice Content starts here]' before its [Tabs] LI / SC block AND before its content) and the closer a structural no-op. Env LEVELSECTION_OFF.

level_menu_tabs._doc: KB 10 §5 / 01B; a §1d family dialect on the `JPFUN|combo` row. THE LEVEL MENUS TYPED AS A [TABS] BLOCK: the JPFUN writer types each level's LI / SC as '[Tabs]' + '[Tab 1] Novice Learning Intentions' / '[Tab 2] Novice Success Criteria' / '[Tab 3] Emergent Learning Intentions' / '[Tab 4] Emergent Success Criteria', each followed by 'We are learning:' / 'I can:' + bullets. The tabs widget captures the block before the level pre-pass, so without this no LI / SC would be found, #levelTabs would return null and the generic Overview | Information menu would ship. For a registry row with level_menu_tabs: true, a tabs bundle whose EVERY labelled tab matches label_pattern is read into per-level menu buckets (#levelMenuLines — the lead, the bullets), seeds each level's menu when its marker opens it, and is dropped from the body and from run.interactives (no widget, no hand-off entry). The row's menu_omit_empty_overview drops the Overview tab when the module has no LI / SC of its own (the JPFUN human build: Novice | Emergent only). Env LEVELMENUTABS_OFF.

level_pages._doc_level_first_marker_pattern: The LEVEL-FIRST form of the level-page marker — JPFUN01 / 02 write '[Novice Page 1]' / '[Emergent Page 2]' where CHFUN writes '[PAGE 1 Novice]'; read the same way (the level word is the label). Env LEVELFIRST_OFF (with the JPFUN|combo registry row).

menu.sc_label_default: How will I know I have learned it?

JPFUN|combo._doc_menu_tabs: The JPFUN level menus typed as a [Tabs] block → the level-tab menu, no Overview tab (level_pages.level_menu_tabs; env LEVELMENUTABS_OFF).
JPFUN|combo._doc: The Japanese Fundamentals level-page modules (JPFUN01 / 02) — the human form is the CHFUN one-page combo level form (.phases Novice / Emergent, col-md-6 offset-md-0 col-12 paddingR / paddingL menu columns, the phaseLink tiles); the same row. Env LEVELFIRST_OFF.

activity_box._note: A level-pages task bundle whose opener leads with an activity id + title ('1A Check your understanding', as in CHFUN01) wraps in the human's `activity interactive` box: number = {level ordinal}{next letter} (the phase ordinal set at each phasebreak — writer ids 1A/3A/4A renumber to 1A/1B/1C, the lesson-letter sequence rule), heading = the lead title. Rides LEVELPAGE_OFF (only run._levelMenu pages can enter).

level_overview._doc: §1d exception 1. THE MULTI-FILE LEVELS OVERVIEW: the FRFUN Languages Fundamentals (FRFUN06 / 07 / 08) write each level page as its own file, opened by a level-first title marker (`[Title] [H1] [Novice Page 1] Languages do not translate word for word` — also spelt `[NovicePage 1]`, `[Novice Page5]`, red-split `[ Emergent  Page  1 ]`), and every human overview carries the levels: `div.phases` (one item per level) → `div.introduction` (the overview content + a `row phaseContainer noPhase` of phaseLink tiles inside its row) → one `fundamentalsPanel` per level (h2 level name + one `button button-invert` link per level page, the page's own title). The level-pages dialect builds this for SINGLE-file modules; this block is its multi-file twin. Only a registry row saying `level_overview: "multi-file"` enters (the FRFUN row). The overview gathers the level pages from run.pages (each page's first marker: its level word + the title typed after the marker, red or black; a leading `1.` numbering and bold marks stripped); a button links the page's generated file (PageAssembler.PageFileNames — the choice-tile precedent, target _self). PageSplitter: a level marker met on the overview opens the first level page (FRFUN06's `[Novice Page 1]` follows its overview with no [End page]; the human ships it as its own file). The tile images are designer assets (no source) — the tiles ship without one and a run note lists them. Not built: the level-suffixed file names, the Emergent introduction page folded into its panel, the designer-written level intros (no source). Env LEVELOV_OFF.
level_overview.panel:
{label}

{buttons}

inquiry_tabs._doc: The INQUIRY tabbed template (BLL [Tab N]-label-list family). A firing module has a 'side tabs' instruction + a `[Tab N] <label>` crumb-label list + ≥2 EMPTY `[Tab N]` panel openers. ContentConverter captures the labels, pushes a {sentinel} at each empty opener, suppresses the instruction + the label-list, and #inquiryPanels wraps the body into `div.crumbs` (an intro crumb + one per tab) + `div.inquiryPanel` (an intro panel + one per opener). SkeletonBuilder sets the `inquiry container-fluid` body class + the `footer-nav inquiry-nav` footer when content.inquiryActive. The discriminator is conservative (side-tabs instruction REQUIRED) so the `[tabs]`-widget `[Tab N]` modules (BLL232/236, OSAI501, MXDB202, PNR, XGF, ENGJ402…) do NOT fire. Env INQUIRYTABS_OFF gives the flat render (orphan `[Tab N]` flags and all).
inquiry_tabs._footer_nav_doc: The FIXED inquiry footer nav shell (the human ships an identical home/prev/next `ul.footer-nav.inquiry-nav` on every inquiry page). SkeletonBuilder emits it for a firing CED page (content.cedInquiry) ONLY when the registry produced NO footer links (single-file CED → footer_links 'none' → empty footer) — so a BLL module that already carries registry footer links is unaffected. The hrefs render empty (single page), matching the human.

side_tab_nav._doc: THE SIDE-TAB-NAVIGATION FUNDAMENTALS DIALECT (the FRFUN family; KB 14.1 / 06 §3.3). The writer authors each lesson page as `[Side tab navigation]` + a ONE-COLUMN TABLE of the tab labels (the crumb list), then one `[Side tab navigation] <label>` per panel (the label typed black OR inside the red span) + `[Title] [H2]` + the panel's content. The lexicon reads `[Side tab navigation]` as `tab n`, so the BLL inquiry mode would fire on it — but the base walk only knows `[Tab N]`: a labelled nav tag has no N, so its label would be dropped and NO panel opened. The human form: `body.fundamentals.container-fluid.noPhase` + `div.phases` (the N labels, the first `showing`, phase 1..N) + one `div.fundamentalsPanel[phase]` per tab (the first `showing`), no module menu, the `footer-nav fundamentals-nav` footer (the HPFUN `[New tab]` form with labels). This dialect: a page with >= min_labelled labelled nav tags (nav_tag_pattern on the tag text) fires side-tab mode (the shared inquiry machinery runs): the bare nav tag + its label table are CONSUMED (label_table: every cell <= label_max_words words); each labelled nav tag opens a panel with that label (its black text, else the red text after the tag words); PanelsBuilder builds N unified crumbs + N panels (no synthetic Introduction — the writer's first tab IS it; a non-empty lead segment before the first tab is prepended to panel 1) from the `flavour` templates; SkeletonBuilder takes the flavour's body_class / footer_class and, with lesson_menu 'none', drops the module menu. In practice only FRFUN06 has the in-page shape (FRFUN07 / 08 author their side tabs as page navigation — see level_overview); enabled as a family dialect that matches its family's own human build (§1d exception 1). Env SIDETABNAV_OFF uses the BLL inquiry path.

inquiry_tabs._body_class_requires_build_doc: Couples the `inquiry` body token to an actually-built inquiry page. The registry stamps `container-fluid inquiry` as a whole-SUBJECT default (ConnectED, Blended Literacy, *WHA), so every lesson page of those subjects would inherit `inquiry`, though the human ships it ONLY on the crumbs/inquiryPanel landing and leaves every lesson page plain `container-fluid` (in the human build an inquiry body goes with an inquiry build almost without exception). SkeletonBuilder strips the `inquiry` token when the page is NOT content.inquiryActive; fundamentals/mathJax/reoTranslate untouched; a page that DOES build inquiry keeps it via the inquiryActive override. Env INQBODY_OFF uses the raw registry token.

heading_label._guards_doc: Over-fire guards. (1) `min_true_openers` (2): `_emptyOpeners` counts the `[End tab]` CONTAINER_CLOSE closers, so the EX `[Section N]`/`[New side tab]` family (EXPFUN04: 1 true opener + 7 closers) would otherwise fire and build a 1-panel page vs the human's 7 — require ≥2 TRUE openers (the real panel-split signal). (2) SINGLE-FILE scope (`run.resolvedRules.page_model !== 'multi-file'`): the heading-label landing is one page; the EX multi-file inquiry family is a DIFFERENT structure. EXIP901/EXBP901 build inquiry panels via the `_bllInquiry` side-tabs-instruction path, NOT this rule. (3) The HPFUN fundamentals family meets the firing condition but is unaffected (the fundPanelMode SUBTAG branch pushes its own FUND_SENTINEL before the inquiry sentinel, and #inquiryPanels no-ops without an INQ_SENTINEL). Firing set: TWHA901/903/904/906/TWHK903; EXPFUN06, CEDO501, ENGJ301, ENGJ302, PES1004, XGF9003 do not fire.
heading_label._doc: The TWHA/TWHK HEADING-LABEL inquiry sub-family. Unlike the BLL family (a labelled `[Tab N]` crumb-list + a 'side tabs' instruction) these carry EMPTY `[Tab N]` openers, NO labelled list, and NO 'side tabs' instruction — the crumb LABEL is each panel's FIRST heading (English part before ' | '). FIRE when `_labeledTabs === 0 AND _emptyOpeners >= min_openers`. The threshold 6 separates the templates (TWHA901, TWHK903, TWHA906, TWHA903 — the count includes the `[End tab]` CONTAINER_CLOSE closers, which do NOT open panels) from modules that must not fire (CEDO501, ENGJ301, PES1004, ENGJ302 have few such tags; XGF9003 always has `_labeledTabs>=1`). BUILD = the UNIFIED page_split form (rel="1".."N", first showing): crumb-1 is the fixed 'Introduction', crumbs 2..N are the panels' first headings; panel-1 absorbs any pre-first-tab body content (usually empty — the overview is partitioned to the menu) so nothing is lost. TWHA901's openers map 1:1 to the human's panels (headings Agency/Resilience/.../Curiosity == the human crumbs). TWHA902 fires via the labelled path; EXPFUN06 does not fire. Env HEADINGLABEL_OFF gives the flat render (orphan `[Tab N]` flags).

opener_stops_capture._doc: KB 06 lines 169 / 171. A widget's member capture (`InteractiveScanner.#swallowMembers`) stops at the bank's absolute terminators, CONTAINER_CLOSE, PAGE_BOUNDARY and h2–h5 — not at a `tab n` SUBTAG — so an un-closed bundle could run THROUGH the next panel opener and take the whole panel with it: CEDR401's `[Carousel of videos with captions]` would swallow `[Tab 5] Surprises in the data` up to `[Tab 6]`, TWHA902's flip-card / carousel bundles would swallow `[Tab 4] Body language`, `[Tab 6] Artistic expression` and `[Tab 9] Know your audience`. The consumed-opener recovery handles only a TRAILING empty opener. On a registry-known Inquiry module (`module_meta.template_type`) whose page model is single-file, a `tab n` SUBTAG item (`[Tab N]`, `[New tab]`, `[New side tab]` — never the `end tab n` closer) ends the capture of every NON-`tabs` bundle; a real `[Tabs]` widget keeps its members. (XLP06 / SSOG301 / GENO901 are Standard `[Tabs]`-widget members, out of scope by the template test.) Env INQOPENER2_OFF (shared by three related rules) turns it off.

openers_unconsumed_only._doc_labelled_body:
`labelled_body_opens` — by POSITION. The BLL branch reads EVERY digit-labelled `[Tab N] label` as a crumb-LIST entry (the label captured, nothing opened); the writer's list is the labelled run BEFORE the first true (empty, non-closer) opener, so a labelled tab that comes AFTER it is a body opener carrying its own label (TWHA902's `[Tab 4] Body language` … `[Tab 9] Know your audience`, released by opener_stops_capture). Scoped to the HEADING-LABEL family (the crumb derives from the panel's first heading), where the human opens the panel with `

label

` (TWHA902 crumb 4 + h3 'Body language'): the branch closes any open activity, pushes the sentinel and emits the label as the panel's h3. The mode tests (`_bllInquiry` / `_headingLabelOn` / `_pageDelimited`) count the LIST tabs (before the first true opener) so the released openers do not flip the family's mode. Guard: a labelled tab whose previous or next item is a `[page N]` boundary is the hybrid form's twin (BLL130 `[page 6]` + `[Tab 6] The letter b`, BLL240) and stays a label. Env INQOPENER2_OFF.
openers_unconsumed_only._doc_nodigit: `nodigit_labelled_opens` — in the BLL body branch a LABELLED tab whose bracket carries no number is an OPENER, not a crumb-list entry: `[New tab] 2` (TWHK907 — the index typed outside the bracket; a bare number is no label, the panel's heading decides) and `[New side tab] Values` (TWHR907 — the panel takes that label, inquiryLabels[<panel index>]). Read as labels with no index (inquiryLabels[n] needs a digit) they would open nothing. Same env INQCONSUMED_OFF.
openers_unconsumed_only._doc: KB 06 lines 169 / 171. Counting EVERY `tab n` item on the page would let a `[Tabs]` WIDGET's consumed `[Tab]` members (TWHR907, TWHK907) count as EMPTY panel openers, so the BLL mode would fire on a page whose real openers are labelled `[New side tab] Values` / `[New tab] 2` items with no digit — which it reads as labels with no index, opening nothing. With this flag `_tabItems` (and so `_labeledTabs` / `_emptyOpeners` / `_trueOpeners`) counts UNCONSUMED tab items only — a widget's members are the widget's; the mode does not fire on those pages and the template_fallback takes them (its tab_opener_patterns accept `[New side tab]` / `[New tab]`). Env INQCONSUMED_OFF counts every tab item.

empty_intro_folds._doc: The BLL build prepends a synthetic `Introduction` intro panel (crumb_intro + panel_intro_open, rel="intro") holding the lead segment before the first opener. On CEDK102 / CEDR204 / TWHA902 the writer's FIRST opener IS the introduction (`[TAB 1] Introduction` in the crumb list, an empty `[TAB 1]` opener at the very start), so the lead segment is EMPTY and the build would have N + 1 panels — an empty first panel — where the human has N. With this flag a lead segment with no text and no media is not a panel: the first opener's panel takes crumb 1 with the list's own label for index 1 (else intro_label) and the panels are numbered 1..N (the template_fallback's hasIntro rule). A lead segment with content keeps the intro panel. Env INQEMPTYINTRO_OFF keeps the synthetic intro.

stage_dialect._doc: KB 06 §3.4 crumbs + inquiryPanel. THE EXPLORE STAGE PAGE'S SIDE TABS ARE ITS INQUIRY PANELS: a page of a stage-dialect module (PageSplitter's page_split.stage_opener_break found >= min_labels bare 'Lesson overview:' labels and set run.metadata.stageDialect; never the overview) builds the fallback shell whatever its page model, template type or BLL mode: every opener in the writer's EX forms ('[New side tab] Intro', '[New tab] Keep track of progress', '[next tab] Peer feedback', '[Showcase tab]', '[New tab - Next steps]' — opener_patterns, beside the fallback's list) opens a panel labelled by the bracket's own words with label_strip_pattern's opener words removed (a leading 'new / next / side … tab', a trailing 'tab'), else its black tail; the lead segment is the intro panel when it holds real content (the intro_min_chars rule), labelled intro_label — the human's numbered crumbs 'Intro | Brainstorming | … | Next steps'. Without it the BLL mode would fire with EMPTY crumbs (an opener with a label is a crumb-list entry there) or not at all (every opener labelled). Env EXSIDETAB_OFF.

new_tab_opener._doc: `[New tab]

black_list._doc: 'The writer's nine Tab N lines must become the tabs, never plain text' (CEDT301, built as one tabbed Inquiry page). THE WRITER'S BLACK SIDE-TAB LIST: a side-tabs instruction (a black `Side Tabs:` line matching instruction_pattern, or a red `[Side Tabs]` tag) followed by >= list_min black lines matching line_pattern, numbered 1, 2, 3 …, is the writer's crumb list (the fallback's own capture reads only red `[Tab N] label` tags): its labels become the crumbs, the lines and a black instruction render nothing; any_heading_level lets a heading of any level that repeats a listed label open its panel (CEDT301's `[H4] Digital collage`); boundary_heading_names_panel makes a listed heading that is the FIRST heading of a panel a `[page N]` boundary opened name that panel instead of opening another. (CEDT207's list sits in the MENU partition, which this capture does not reach; MXEX201 is Standard — outside the fallback's Inquiry scope.) Env INQBLACKLIST_OFF.

template_fallback._doc: KB 06_TEMPLATE_RECOGNITION.md lines 63 / 169 / 171 — the Inquiry template's navigation IS div.crumbs → div.inquiryPanel[rel] and its body class `inquiry container-fluid`. THE INQUIRY-TEMPLATE FALLBACK SHELL, for Inquiry modules' single pages whose Writers Templates delimit their panels in dialects none of the five modes above accept: a labelled `[Tab N] label` LIST followed by labelled REPEATED openers (BLL250 / 260, CEDR101 / 401 …), labelled openers with no list (CEDR203, CEDT208, CEDW201, TWHR907's `[New side tab] Values`), the label INSIDE the red span (`[Tab 1: MODULE INTRODUCTION]`, `[Tab 2 – Scenario]`, `[Insert Right click tab – ‘The seasons’]` — CEDO201, TWHA902 / 904 / 905, CEDO202), and SECTION markers — `[LESSON N] LABEL` (CEDK401), `[LESSON N]` + an `[H2] Lesson N: label` (TWHK901 / 902, TWHT903), `[Lesson N content] label` (CEDT104), `[page N]` (CEDT102, CEDO204). FIRES ONLY when the module's Module_Structure_Index template_type is in `template_types`, the page model is single-file, NONE of the five existing modes fired, and the body holds >= min_openers panel openers. OPENERS (top level, an open activity closed first): an unconsumed `tab n` SUBTAG item that is not part of the writer's crumb LIST (the first run of >= list_min consecutive labelled tabs — consumed, its labels captured by index, never rendered); a `lesson` / `page` PAGE_BOUNDARY item carrying a digit (`[Lesson Summary]` / `[Lesson Overview]` are not openers); a `lesson content` SECTION_MARKER item ONLY when the page has fewer than 2 lesson / page boundaries (CEDT104's form — never beside `[LESSON N]`). LABELS, in order: the crumb list's entry for that panel index; the opener's own label — the black tail after the tag when it is at most label_max_words long, else the words inside the red span after strip_label_words are removed (`[Tab 2 – Scenario]` → Scenario; `[LESSON 6] A COMMUNITY INITIATIVE` → A community initiative, ALL-CAPS folded to sentence case); else the panel's FIRST heading with strip_label_prefix removed. PANELS (PanelsBuilder.inquiryPanels fallbackMode): when the lead segment before the first opener holds real content (>= intro_min_chars of text or a heading) it is the intro panel with intro_label (intro_label_by_prefix for the module's code prefix — the CED human builds say Intro) and the openers follow as panels 2..N+1; when it does not, the openers are panels 1..N and the first takes its own label or intro_label; an empty trailing segment is dropped. The built page takes the inquiry body class + footer class through content.inquiryActive (as every other mode) and the fixed home / prev / next footer shell through the forceLinks path (a single-file Inquiry page has no registry footer links of its own). Not fired: pages where another mode fires, Inquiry modules the human builds with no shell (CHWHA / GEWHA one page with no openers; ENGFUN02, XDLS901 / 903 / 909 multi-file), every non-Inquiry template. A page whose single-file WT is the empty template (CEDR201 / 301 / 302, CEDT201–204 — no openers) is unaffected. Env INQFALLBACK_OFF (or INQUIRYTABS_OFF) gives the flat page.

section_nav._doc: KB 06 §3.4. THE EXPlore "NAVIGATION WITH N SECTIONS" INQUIRY DIALECT (EXPFUN02–05). The writer declares the crumb trail in ONE instruction — `[Side Navigation with 6 sections: Learner, Communicator, Scientist, Social Scientist, Mathematician and Innovator]` or `[Tab Navigation with …]` — and opens each section with `[section N] Label` (EXPFUN02), a `TAB NAV N: Label` line (03 / 04 / 05; the first, `TAB NAV: Intro` / `TAB NAV 1: Introduction`, opens the intro panel) or a top-level [H1] / [H2] heading naming the label (EXPFUN02's last four: 'Think like a scientist' …). PanelsBuilder.detectInquirySections finds the instruction, parses the labels (split on commas / 'and'), matches every label IN ORDER to the next opener after it and fires only when all are found; the instruction and the tag / line openers are consumed, a heading opener stays as the panel's first heading; with no explicit intro opener the instruction itself opens the intro panel. inquiryPanels sectionMode: the content BEFORE the first sentinel stays outside the scaffold (the overview's learning-intention rows), then N+1 unified crumbs (intro_label + the list, the first showing) and N+1 inquiryPanels (the first showing) via the page_split templates — as the human builds all four. Guards: single-file pages, never alongside the BLL / heading-label / CED modes. Env SECTIONNAV_OFF.

page_opener_fire._doc: Widens the `_bllInquiry` firing test to the `[page N]`-DELIMITED PANEL form. The BLL mode fires when a labelled `[Tab N]` crumb-list (>=3) is followed by >=2 EMPTY `[Tab N]` panel openers. BLL140/BLL220 author the crumb-list then open panel 1 on an empty `[Tab 1]` and panels 2..N on labelled `[page N]` markers (only ONE empty opener), so they would fall between the BLL path (>=2 empty) and the heading-label path (0 labelled) and build no panels/crumbs/nav. This flag makes `_bllInquiry` ALSO true when min_labeled orphan labelled `[Tab N]` (a real crumb-list) AND min_empty empty `[Tab N]` (the lead opener) AND min_page_openers top-level `[page N]` PAGE_BOUNDARY markers (the panel delimiters) co-occur — then bll_page_split opens the `[page N]` panels and the crumbs build, no new build code. The min_page_openers>=3 requirement is the over-fire discriminator: the widget-`[Tab N]` modules (MXDB202/XGF9003/MXFL301) carry orphan labelled tabs but no top-level `[page N]`, so they never fire. BLL240 (a multi-page inquiry variant with no page-openers on the landing) is not covered. Env BLLPAGEOPENER_OFF (independent of INQUIRYTABS_OFF).

bll_page_split._doc: The BLL phonics inquiry family (as in BLL210; _bllInquiry: a labelled `[Tab N]` crumb-list + EMPTY `[Tab N]` panel openers) authors each section as a HYBRID boundary — an empty `[Tab N]` AND a `[Page N]` PAGE_BOUNDARY AND a `[H#]` label, e.g. `[Tab 4][Page 4][H2] a_e`. But SOME sections open on a `[Page N]` ALONE (no empty `[Tab N]` of their own — BLL210's Long vowels `[page 2]` + Silent e `[page 3]`), so splitting only on empty `[Tab N]` would MERGE such a section into the previous panel and shift every later crumb LABEL. RULE: in `_bllInquiry` (NOT cedInquiry — that family is mutually exclusive) a top-level `[page N]` PAGE_BOUNDARY ALSO opens a panel (closing any open activity first), DE-DUPLICATED so it never double-splits the `[Tab N][page N]` pairs: a `[page N]` is a no-op when the immediately-preceding body item is itself a tab-family opener or another page boundary (so the `[Tab 4][Page 4]` pair = ONE boundary, and a consumed-`[Tab N]`'s `[page N]` defers to the recovery). General + data-described; the firing discriminator is unchanged (still _bllInquiry), so a module with no standalone `[page N]` is unaffected. Env BLLPAGE_OFF splits on [Tab N] only.

inquiry_tabs._recover_doc: INQUIRY consumed-opener RECOVERY. The empty `[Tab N]` PANEL OPENERS that follow a widget are often SWALLOWED by that widget's scanner capture (BLL150/160/170/210 — a trailing `[Tab N]` absorbed as the last member of the activity's final `modal`; TWHA902 — a `carousel`), so the panel would never open and the inquiry page would under-build. In CONFIRMED inquiry mode (content.inquiryActive, computed post-scan so the discriminator is unchanged), a NON-`[tabs]` bundle whose TRAILING members are empty `[Tab N]` closes any open activity and pushes one panel {sentinel} per swallowed opener — restoring the boundary WITHOUT un-consuming the tag (no leak) and WITHOUT a scanner change. Real `[tabs]` widgets are skipped (their `[Tab N]` are legitimate members; ENGJ301/XGF9003 untouched). A module that does NOT fire inquiry never reaches this path, so a non-inquiry module that absorbs an empty `[Tab N]` (ENGJ402, an accordion the writer mis-tagged) is unaffected. Env INQRECOVER_OFF turns it off.

page_split._doc: The CED [Page N]-SPLIT inquiry sub-family (the ORPHAN crumb-list cut: CEDK101, CEDT404). Unlike the BLL family (panels open on EMPTY [Tab N]), these carry a PURE `[Tab N] <label>` crumb-list (EVERY tab labelled, ZERO empty openers) and split panels on in-stream `[page N]` PAGE_BOUNDARY markers (single-file mode keeps them as section breaks — these CED levels are page_model:single-file). FIRE only when ALL hold: a consecutive labelled `[Tab N]` run >=3 that EQUALS the module's total `[Tab N]` count (a pure crumb-list), 0 empty openers anywhere, >=2 in-stream `[page N]` openers, AND panels(openers+1) == crumbs(labels). The >=2-in-stream-`[page N]` requirement EXCLUDES every real `[tabs]`-widget module (they carry no in-stream `[page N]`). ContentConverter captures + suppresses the label run (CEDK101's list sits in the MENU partition, CEDT404's in the BODY — the flag suppresses both), pushes a {sentinel} at each top-level `[page N]` (closing any open activity first), and #inquiryPanels (page_split mode) wraps the body into N UNIFIED crumbs (the first tab IS the intro — NO separate 'Introduction' crumb, distinct from BLL) + N inquiryPanels (first showing). The crumb/panel index VALUE (0- vs 1-indexed) is editorial; 1-indexed here matches CEDT404 exactly and is functionally identical for CEDK101. See _consumed_crumb_list_doc for the consumed form. Env CEDPAGE_OFF gives the flat render.
page_split._consumed_crumb_list_doc: The CED page-split for the CONSUMED crumb-list cut. In CEDO102 the `[Tab N]` crumb-list is eaten by a `[tabs]` WIDGET bundle. The labels still reach #detectInquiryCed (it scans page.items, not just orphans), but (a) the plain alignment formula assumes a leading intro panel ((openers+1)==labels), while the consumed family opens the first ('Introduction') panel ON the first `[page N]` (panels==openers==labels), and (b) the consuming `[tabs]` widget would ALSO render. This flag accepts the openers==labels alignment AND, when the crumb-list is consumed, suppresses the consuming bundle so only the div.crumbs remains; #inquiryPanels drops the empty leading-intro panel (segs[0]=='' -> N sentinel panels, not N+1). SCOPED tight: CEDO102 fires (the bundle ate ONLY the crumb-list, its free `[page N]` count equals its labels). CEDW101 (stray empty `[Tab N]` -> not pure) and CEDT208/CEDW201 (panels split by a NON-`[page N]` signal) do NOT fire. Every real `[tabs]`-widget module carries no in-stream `[page N]` -> no-fire. Env CEDCONSUMED_OFF uses the orphan-only ((openers+1)==labels, no suppression) form.

c47._doc: KB constraint 47 in full, the opening duplicate body heading. On a LESSON page the FIRST RENDERED free-body heading whose text equals the header title once case, punctuation and a `Lesson N` label are ignored is DROPPED — the header already shows it and the lesson NUMBER stays in the #module-code chip (c79: the lesson's own title is the h1, never emptied). Where the human keeps the heading (SCCH301, SCPH301, HIS1001, MXEO202, XDLS903) that is a NAMED override. Refinements of the de-dup TEST: first_rendered_heading — a heading CONSUMED by the de-dup does not spend the first-heading slot (MXEO202_3_0: `[H2] *Lesson 3 Triangles*` consumed as the title repeat, then `[H3] Triangles` — the real opening heading — is still tested). ignore_punctuation — the compare keeps letters and digits only (HIS1001_7_0's curly quotes, ENGR202's italicised `*:*` that would defeat the prefix strip, PES1002's `**` markers + the writer's trailing note). skip_inside_activity — a heading inside an open activity box is the activity's own title (ENGI101 'Being Frank'): never the candidate and never spends the slot (KEPT). exclude_body_class — the Bilingual template (reoTranslate) is excluded: KB 07B governs the MTK section heading, the more specific rule wins (TRR111). The overview page keeps the plain exact de-dup (c47 is strip-only there). Authority: KB level 1 (c47, Universal). Env DEDUPC47_OFF turns it off.

title_markers._doc: c79 hygiene, upstream of the title-casing seam: a lesson page's header title never carries a writer's markdown marker (the human never ships one). PageSplitter strips every `*` from page.pageTitle at the start of the title post-pass — BEFORE the label / bare-number tests, so `**3**` reads as the bare number it is and takes the lesson's own name from its first heading — and collapses whitespace; a title left with no letter or digit (XLP02_4_0's `*:`) is emptied so the module-title fallback applies. Fires only on a title that carries a `*` (e.g. MXFU302 `**Statistics and Sports**`, PES1008 `*Heat Capacity Calculations*`, SSOG101 `* Police Officers`, MXFU201 `**3**`; a trailing writer's note such as PES1002's '*Te reo* Māori translation needed' and MXFU201_8's `8.` number are separate cases). Env TITLEMARK_OFF turns it off.

tag_prefix._doc: KB c79 title hygiene (like the black-typed-tag rule). A HEADING TAG TYPED IN BLACK INSIDE A [LESSON] TITLE IS NOT PART OF THE TITLE: MUS1004's writer typed [LESSON] and then, in black bold, '**[H1] Lesson One. What are the Essentials? Part one.**' (Two, Three alike); the [LESSON] payload is the page title, so without this the lesson h1s would show the literal '[H1] …'. The title-marker step strips a leading heading tag (pattern) from the page title before its label tests (the label strip then reads 'Lesson One.' as the lesson label, as for every other '[LESSON] Lesson N. Title'). Env TITLETAG_OFF.

embedded_heading_title._doc_bracket_remainder_yields: KB c79, the page's own title. A heading whose words are ALL inside its red span AND whose parse remainders all sit inside its own tag brackets — FRFUN07's `🔴[Title] [H1] [Emergent Page 3] Change of shape🔴`: remainders ["emergent"] (the level word of the `[Emergent Page 3]` bracket) — would name the page «emergent», because the harvest takes `blackAfter || remainders` and the embedded-title rule runs only with no remainders. A bracket's own word never names the page when the writer typed the title: the embedded red words (the same RenderText) win. Env BRACKETREM_OFF.
embedded_heading_title._doc: KB c79 / CL-0069 / CL-0076. The lesson title harvest also reads a heading whose words are typed INSIDE its red span ('🔴[H2] Missionaries and Māori🔴' — no black text, no parse remainders): its TagNormaliser.RenderText words (what the body renders for that heading) name the page, so the module title does not stand in for the lesson's own title.

lesson_title_dedup._harvest_before_activity_only_note: PageSplitter harvests a lesson page's header title from its first [H1-5] heading when the [LESSON] tag carried no title. When true, that harvest is restricted to a heading BEFORE the first [Activity] opener (a genuine lesson title) OR an explicit 'Lesson N:' heading — a heading buried AFTER an activity is widget/section content (BLL241-2 [H3] Fog, a clickDrop panel label; HIS1001 section headings), NOT the page title, so it is not used (the page keeps its bare label / module title instead of a wrong word; the human never titles these pages with such a heading). env LESSONTITLE_OFF uses the first heading anywhere.

lesson_label_titles._doc: KB constraint 79 / CL-0069/0076, the `Lesson N` LABEL sub-mechanism. A lesson page whose header title is nothing but a lesson LABEL — 'Lesson One' / 'Lesson 1' (the [LESSON] tag's own payload), 'Lesson #3 Opening Doors…' (the plain strip accepts 'Lesson 3' but not 'Lesson #3'), 'Lesson One – The Ode' (a word number), 'Lesson 5 continued' (a sub-page) — takes the lesson's OWN title, as the human does (ENGI102/202/203/301, ENGJ301/302/402, ENGC201, ANZH203, CEDT501): the first real heading (a label-only heading is skipped) with the label stripped; a label-prefixed title keeps its own words; a label-only SUB-page (N.M, M > 0) with no heading of its own inherits its parent lesson's title (CEDT501 5.1 → 'Speaking up'). The lesson-NUMBER logic (a 'Lesson N' heading's number wins) is untouched; the body de-dup then drops the body heading that now equals the title — the human's shape. Env LESSONLABEL_OFF turns it off.

lesson_name_from_heading.note: When a lesson page is opened by a '[LESSON] N' tag whose only payload is the digit (as in ENGS302-1.0), PageSplitter sets page.pageTitle to that bare NUMBER ('1'), so the header <h1><span> would show '1' instead of the lesson NAME. The post-pass that harvests the name from the first '[H2] Lesson N: Name' heading therefore also fills a pageTitle that is merely the bare lesson number (or label) — extracting the name from the first heading exactly as the empty case does (re-using PageSplitter's ^lesson N [:.\-–] strip after a leading-* strip, so italic/bold/plain + ':'/'.'/'-'/'–' variants all work). This cascades to the body de-dup: with the real name in #pageLessonTitle, the prefix-tolerant test matches and the duplicate '[H2] Lesson 1: Plot Structure' body heading is consumed. The human never titles a lesson header with a bare number. Env LESSONNAME_OFF keeps the bare-number title (and the un-de-duped body heading).

overview.note: The OVERVIEW page's first-body-heading de-dup compares the overview's first body heading against the module English title in the header (#pageEnglishTitle), exactly as a lesson page de-dups against its lesson title, so a [MODULE INTRODUCTION] [H1] that repeats the MODULE title does not show as a body <h3> (ENGC102 '[H1] Keeping it real' = the header title 'Keeping it real'). EXACT folded match only (where such a duplicate occurs the human always drops it — never an over-strip). Env OVDEDUP_OFF disables the de-dup on the overview. This relies on the lone-title guard (lone_title_maori_guard) so #pageEnglishTitle is the real title, not a Course swap (ENGC102 would otherwise have 'Communication' as its header title).

lesson_title_dedup.note: The FIRST body heading that repeats the lesson title (already promoted to the header <h1> by PageSplitter) is de-duped. When the writer wrapped that heading WHOLE in *italic* ('[H2] *Lesson 3: Be kind online*', as in OSBY201-03) the leading-'Lesson N:' strip (anchored on ^lesson) would miss it (the string starts with '*'), the prefix would survive, and the de-dup would never match 'Be kind online' in the header — leaving a DUPLICATE title in the body, which the human almost never keeps. strip_lesson_prefix makes the de-dup COMPARE tolerant of a leading 'Lesson N:' on BOTH sides (rendering of any genuinely-kept heading is unchanged). Env LESSONPFX_OFF uses the exact-match compare.

language_fonts._doc: KB constraint 92 / CL-0093 (locked admin): the language-font classes `jp-text` / `ch-text` / `pinyin` are MANDATORY on every occurrence and the conversion applies them. THE CJK HALF: every run of Chinese / Japanese text on the page is wrapped `…` / `…` (ListsAndRuns.LanguageFontWrap at the PageAssembler whole-page seam — after LinkTextDisplay, before MathReplace, the pre-acks slice only like every other text pass; the human leaves its acks CJK bare). A RUN = blocks of CJK characters (Han, kana, CJK punctuation, fullwidth forms — `cjk_chars`) joined by internal whitespace and by the ASCII brackets / slashes / stops that sit BETWEEN two CJK blocks (`internal_joiners` — the KB's `他(她)是我的(哥哥/弟弟/姐姐/妹妹`), trimmed to start and end on a CJK character, and holding at least one Han or kana character (a punctuation-only stretch is never a run). The CLASS: a run holding any kana is Japanese regardless of the module (`kana_is_japanese`); a Han-only run takes the MODULE's language from `module_language` (longest code-prefix match on run.moduleCode); a Han-only run in a module with no language entry is left bare (`han_needs_module_language` — the KB's Red-Flag half is not built: such runs are acks / video titles the human also leaves bare). Verbatim zones (`skip_zones`, opener → closer):
language_fonts._doc_joiners: The underline sentinel pair (U+E024 / U+E025 — the writer's in-sentence underline, made <u> after this pass) joins a run like a space, so an underlined word inside a Japanese / Chinese run never splits the run's span; the underline pass then keeps a <u> only where it nests cleanly.

merge_adjacent_lists._doc:
A writer's bullet run can be split into two sibling `
    `s by an item that rendered nothing (a bullet's trailing inline `[link to X]` marker, a consumed item, an image between bullets); the human almost always ships it as one list. `ListsAndRuns.MergeAdjacentLists`, a full-page post-pass at the typed-number-list seam (after TypedNumberList, before LinkTextDisplay; body only; the same verbatim zones — cv2 dumps, notes, the listed built widgets): a bare `
` followed only by whitespace and a bare `
    ` joins into one list. `ol` is deliberately NOT listed (a restart at 1 is a new numbered list, and the human does not merge them). OFF keeps the split lists.

orphan_punctuation._doc: ORPHAN PUNCTUATION. A block (p / h1–h6 / li) whose whole text is ONE sentence mark, or a mark with no wording, is what is left when an inline widget capture, a fill-in answer span, a URL line or a moved definition took the words around it — the gold never ships one. merge_pattern (a lone . , ; : ! ?): the mark joins the end of the text block that closes right before it (through a list close), so the writer's mark is kept; with no text block before it the block is removed. drop_pattern (a lone dash or bullet glyph, a bare ** run, the cell line-break marker / on its own): the block is removed, with a list it leaves empty. Verbatim zones — hand-off boxes, developer notes and comments, the built widgets on typed_number_list.verbatim_widget_classes — are never touched. Env ORPHANPUNCT_OFF.

lone_list_number._doc:
A LIST NUMBER NEVER STANDS ALONE. A bare

whose whole text is a list number («1.», «12)», optionally inside one bold / italic wrapper) is the residue of a Word-numbered paragraph whose content went elsewhere — a wholly red item lifted into a Writers Note (an answer key «1. C / 2. B», a developer instruction) or an item whose leading [body] tag opened a block of its own («1.» above «In your journal, write…»). It carries nothing for the learner and the human build never has one (KB constraint 5 — no parser residue; constraint 42 — numbered steps are

  1. , never a bare number), so the page post-pass after TypedNumberList removes it. LIVE zones only: hand-off boxes, notes and the typed_number_list verbatim widget classes keep their text.

typed_number_list._doc:
KB constraint 42 (Universal): numbered instructions / steps / sub-questions are semantic
  1. (start="N" when the run does not begin at 1), NEVER

    1. …

    manual numbering. The writer TYPES the numbers as plain text ("1. What happened…", not a Word numbered list, so LISTNEST never sees a list); the free-body path (renderBlackText) builds the
      , but widget panels render lines as

      and never see it (e.g. inside a built accordion panel). The human mostly ships such text as a list (usually

        ), the typed number stripped. MECHANISM: ListsAndRuns.TypedNumberList, a FULL-PAGE post-pass at the EmojiStrip seam (PageAssembler, after the emoji list clause, before LinkTextDisplay, body only — the acks block is never touched): a run of >= min_run consecutive bare

        elements (whitespace-only between them) whose text opens with SEQUENTIAL typed numbers (n, n+1, …; a restart ends the run) OR with the extractor's Word-numbered-list marker on every item (DocxExtractor prefixes each numbered-list paragraph with "1. " and never counts, so a Word list inside a widget panel would show as

        1. …

        1. …

        — every question numbered 1; marker_form_all_equal) becomes ONE
          (start="n" when n > 1) of
        1. s with the lead removed from the first text node. VERBATIM ZONES copied through untouched: cv2-interactive hand-off boxes, cv2-note / cv2-comment, script / style, AND every built widget subtree whose class opens with one of verbatim_widget_classes — a flipCard face keeps its typed number as the card title (TWHK901
          1. Partnership…
          ), a dragAndDrop question is a plain

          (CEDR501), a carousel caption a

          (XGF9003); accordion panels, activity boxes and free body are LIVE (BLL212 / SCCH301 / ENGR101 ship the

            ). Env TYPEDOL_OFF turns it off.

activity_dropbox_postpass._note: The `dropbox` modifier class on an activity box. A dropbox is NOT its own element — in the human build it is always a CLASS TOKEN on an ordinary activity div (`activity dropbox`, `clickDropContent activity dropbox`, `activity interactive dropbox`). The writer's own `[dropbox]` TAG does not predict it, nor does a dropDown hand-off box. WHAT DOES predict it is the writer's own BUTTON ('[3 buttons – film, camera and microphone] Upload to dropbox') inside the box's own span: this rule is usually right where it fires, though it misses many human dropbox boxes (often because the writer's one activity is split into a widget box and a body box, so the button and the number= land in different divs). A looser 'the box mentions dropbox anywhere' rule is right only about half the time and is not used. The human's choice is per activity, not a per-module house style. Env ACTDROPBOX_OFF.
activity_dropbox_postpass._note_buttond: The \bbutton\b pattern does not match the orange 'buttonD' (no word boundary before the D), and that is deliberate: in the BLL family the human's convention is a PLAIN activity around the orange buttonD upload button (almost never marked `dropbox`), while activities around the green upload button are mostly marked. So new green buttons join the class automatically, and buttonD buttons correctly stay unmarked; do not widen the pattern to buttonD.

activity_interactive_postpass._note: Post-pass that adds .interactive to a free-body activity div whose depth-balanced span contains a cv2-interactive placeholder declaring an interactive-task widget type (the set in activity_wrapper.interactive_widget_types). It covers activities whose interactive widget is a SEPARATE inner bundle (not the activity-owner bundle's own type), which the emit-time forceInt at #activityOpen misses — e.g. BLL135-01/BLL216 dragAndDrop, BLL145/BLL155 selfCheck, CEDK102/CEDO105 multiChoiceQuiz. Same human convention as the emit rule (the human usually marks such activities .interactive, e.g. CEDO102/CEDK101/CEDW101's overview class="activity interactive"). Env ACTINT_OFF turns it off.
activity_interactive_postpass.marker_format_note: the placeholder type marker 'INTERACTIVE (un-built) #N: TYPE' is a structural constant of interactive_placeholder; the DECISION CONTENT (which types count) is data here via interactive_widget_types.

family_row_per_block._doc: THE FAMILY ROW PER BLOCK, a per-group dialect (§1d exception 2: one row per family, each on the kinds it isolates). In these families the human gives each free section heading — and per family each widget / image / alert / table — a `div.row > div.col` of its own, the paragraph runs between them grouped, rather than packing heading + prose + widgets into one column. The isolated kinds per family: PWY heading, widget, image, alert, table (paragraph runs stay grouped); PHE heading, widget (images and alerts not isolated); ENO heading, widget, alert (images not); XOTPB / XOTPG headings only (their other blocks are the human's div.item grid); other families do not isolate headings. A page post-pass (ContentConverter.#familyRowPerBlock, last): in a module whose code matches a row's code_prefixes (`^PREFIX\d`), every TOP-LEVEL single-column `div.row` of the body splits so each isolated kind sits in its own row with the same column class (an image keeps its commented placeholder and a caption above / below it; a converter note travels with the block after it); rows inside activities, panels and widgets, and two-column rows, are untouched. No KB rule covers the top-level body row (05B covers an activity's inner rows). Env FAMROWBLOCK_OFF.
family_row_per_block._doc_forms: WHERE the human's lone heading sits: PWY, XOTPB and XOTPG put it in its OWN ROW (`row > col-12 col-md-8 > h`) — mode rows; PHE and ENO put it in its own `col-12` COLUMN first in a row whose next column is `col-12 col-md-8` — mode columns (the row stays one row, a column per block, the heading's column `heading_column_class`). The page's OPENING heading (the first block of the first row): XOTPB keeps it with its prose (keep_opening_heading); PWY, PHE, ENO and XOTPG mostly isolate it.

intro_heading_full_row._doc:
THE BLL INTRODUCTION HEADING'S OWN FULL-WIDTH ROW. The writer's mid-document `[Introduction]` (a title-bar alias) renders as `

Introduction

` at the head of the ordinary `col-md-8 col-12` content row; the Blended Literacy human build mostly gives that heading its own FULL-WIDTH row, `div.row > div.col-12 > h3 Introduction` alone. A page post-pass (ContentConverter.#introHeadingFullRow, just inside #pageNumberNormalise): in a module whose Module_Structure_Index subject is listed, a row whose column OPENS with the heading is split — the heading alone in `row > `, the rest in the row's own column; a heading alone in its row just changes column class. A family dialect keyed by subject (§1d exception 1). Env INTROROW_OFF.
intro_heading_full_row._exclude_series_doc: The human's form per series: the full-width row in BLL11, BLL12, BLL13, BLL14, BLL15, BLL16, BLL21, BLL22, BLL23, BLL25; the col-md-8 column in BLL17 and BLL26; BLL24 a tie — those three series keep the plain row (a per-group rule, §1d exception 2).

empty_callout_heading_box._doc: THE ALERT WHOSE TITLE IS A HEADING (form A): the writer types the callout tag alone (`[Alert]`, `[Summary alert box]`, `[Important]`) and its title on the next line under a heading tag (`[H3] Keen to learn more?` — ANZH105, BLL252, DAN1003 …), the text after it. The strict callout gathers only black text, so without this the box would be EMPTY with the 'Empty [alert]' red flag and the heading + its lines would go free in the next row. The human mostly boxes the heading and the first line after it (sometimes the second too). ContentConverter.#emptyCalloutHeadingBox (run first inside #summaryHeadingAlert): a content row holding ONLY that empty box, followed by a row whose column opens with an h2–h5, becomes one box (its own class) holding the heading + the column's following run of paragraphs / lists; the rest of the column moves to a new row (the summary-box form); the empty row and its flag go. Form B (`[Alert] [H3] …` in one span) is the co-tag rule (Tag_Lexicon activity_heading_cotag.callouts). Env CALLOUTHEADBOX_OFF.

summary_run._doc: A summary heading takes the summary box's short run (one plain paragraph, any lists, one closing paragraph after a list) instead of the block's run_rule — the human's summary box holds the recap and leaves the closing narrative free (as on SSCI205).
summary_run.pattern: ^(?:lesson summary|summary|key points|what have we learned|what have we learnt)$

empty_callout_heading_box._summary_handoff_doc: summary_handoff: true = a heading the summary_heading_alert rule matches (Lesson Summary, Key points …) keeps that rule's box and this rule drops only the empty row. Left false: this rule's own box fits the human build better on those pages (HIS, SSOG).

summary_heading_alert._doc:
THE SUMMARY HEADING'S ALERT BOX. A lesson's closing summary heading typed as a plain heading (no [Alert] before it) would render bare in the content column; the human boxes the heading and what follows it to the column's end as div.alert > div.row > div.col-12. KB 14.8 (HPE) names the 'Lesson summary alert' ([alert] → [H3] Lesson Summary → [body] Ka pai! … → [Hint Button] Need help?); KB 05B gives the 'Key points' alert its

Key points

label. The human's form per family: Lesson Summary in HIS, HPRE, SSCI, SSOG, SSEA, CEDK (XGF and TEDC keep theirs bare — not listed); Key points in PES (

); Summary in SSFUN (

; not HIS); What have we learned in BLLR (

; XGF a tie, not listed; XGF's Key questions is a bare div.alert > h4 + ul with no inner row — a different box, not listed) — a per-group rule (§1d exception 2) keyed by the module code's family prefix. A heading that is a column's direct child, outside every exclude_ancestor_pattern container, whose plain text (trailing : ? . stripped) matches a rule for the module's family opens the box; the rule's level re-levels it. The box holds what the human's holds (HIS a paragraph, PES a list, SSOG p ol p / p ul p, SSCI / SSEA a paragraph with the hint right AFTER the box, HPRE p ol / p p.hint p): one plain paragraph, any lists, one closing paragraph after a list, and the hint only where the rule says hint_inside (KB 14.8's HPE sequence); the rest of the column moves to a new row in a column of the same class. Env SUMALERT_OFF.

rules._families_doc: SSCI is NOT listed: its human build splits one module each way (SSCI205 boxes all its summaries, SSCI104 boxes none, the heading an <h4> there) — a tie with no discriminator.

summary_heading_alert._skip_doc: A summary whose column goes on to the end-of-module dropbox button is that box's content: HIS1006's last page — the gold's activity dropbox holds the Lesson summary heading, its paragraphs and the upload button (the only such page; −13.25 unguarded).

no_cross_p._doc:
The title paragraph may not CONTAIN a `

`: the lazy `

([\s\S]*?)

(\s*<[^/])` runs past a paragraph closed by `` (an alert whose only paragraph is its body, or an empty red-flag alert) into the NEXT alert, takes that alert's first paragraph, and leaves its short title a

. Promotion rules unchanged (max_title_chars, a following block tag). Built and held OFF: 7 pages / 5 modules, under the body floor on its own. Env ALERTHCROSS_OFF = the lazy match.

alert_title_heading._note:
An [alert] callout whose FIRST content line is a SHORT TITLE ('Safety message', 'Key points from today's lesson:') followed by body is rendered by the human as a HEADING inside the alert (

, as in OSAI201-03 'Safety message'), not a

. A post-pass (run AFTER re-levelling, like named_headings, so the h4 is not re-levelled) promotes the FIRST

inside a .alert to when its text is <= max_title_chars AND a following block exists (a single-block alert is body, untouched). With <=45 chars and >=2 blocks the human uses a heading far more often than a

, and the heading-first level is mostly h4, so level 4 is the default. A

->h4 tag change never alters the row/col/activity wrapper chain. Env ALERTH_OFF turns it off.

heading_relevel._supervisor_skip_note:
The supervisor-note CALLOUT (elements.supervisor note template) carries a FIXED '

Supervisor note

' label inside its super-content-button box. That label is NOT a free-body section heading, and in the re-level level POOL it would PIN the base rank at h3 — so the page's real writer [H3] section headings (digit + body_shift = h4) could not normalise back DOWN to h3 (ENGC101-02's two supervisor notes would leave 'Conversations'/'Speaking clearly'/'Listening'/'Practise…' at h4 vs the human's h3). The super-content-button box is treated like a widget subtree: its heading is excluded from BOTH the pool and the rewrite (its own fixed h3 is unchanged). Env SUPHEAD_OFF includes the supervisor-note label in the pool.
heading_relevel._activity_anchor_note: An activity-title heading is emitted at a FIXED level (h3 — the top content-section level); a free-body [H#] heading is the writer digit + body_shift (+1). So a writer [H3] SECTION heading that is a PEER of the page's activities would render one level too deep: the human renders OSAI401-01 [H3] 'Types of AI' at h3 (peer to the activity titles 'What can AI do'/'Match the AI Tool') and [H4] 'What is Generative AI…' at h4, whereas with the activity h3 in the re-level pool as the base rank they would go to h4/h5. #relevelHeadings treats activity subtrees like widget subtrees (excluded from BOTH the level POOL and the rewrite), so the free-body [H#] outline ranks from base on its own and the activity titles keep their fixed h3 — the top [H#] then aligns with the activities, matching the human's flatter hierarchy. SELF-SCOPING: the rank map only changes when an activity is the SHALLOWEST anchor (if a real free-body h3 or [H2]→h3 is present it already holds the base, so the outline is unchanged). Env RELEVELACT_OFF includes activities in the pool.
heading_relevel.note: DOCUMENT-LEVEL heading re-levelling: human developers IGNORE the writer's heading digit and re-base every page's body-heading outline to a consistent h3-top hierarchy (most human pages start their body at h3; body headings collapse to h3>h4>h5). The writer's [H?] digit is noise; the human's consistent OUTPUT convention is the signal. ContentConverter.#relevelHeadings runs a post-pass on the assembled #body: the page's DISTINCT free-body heading levels (sorted) map to base_level, base_level+1, … (clamped at max_level) — a rank normalisation. Headings INSIDE a widget subtree (skip_classes) are left untouched (protects the built widgets' own heading conventions). A rank-based mapping matches the human far better than writer+1; heading level doesn't change the wrapper chain. enabled:false or env RELEVEL_OFF turns it off.

digits_by_prefix._note_mxfun: No MXFUN row here: the MXFUN03 human build keeps every free-body [H2] at h2 (and MXFUN02's 'The equal sign' likewise), but MXFUN01's human builds (the single-file phases build and the split Standard build) follow the shift, so a prefix pin would be wrong for MXFUN01 across more pages than it would help MXFUN03 — the family is split.

digits_by_prefix_families._note_blocks: The sibling block digits_by_prefix_families_2 (env HKEEPFAM2_OFF) holds the rest of the qualifying groups; the emitter's path (c) reads every digits_by_prefix_families* block.
digits_by_prefix_families._note: The same per-digit prefix pin as digits_by_prefix, for families that table does not name, where the human keeps the writer's digit on free-body headings while the shift rule would move it: FRFUN [H2] → h2 (carried by FRFUN06; FRFUN08's human build follows the shift — the family's outlier, a NAMED exception), WJFUN [H4] → h4, ENGC [H4] → h4. CEDT [H2] is not listed (CEDT501's human build follows the shift). A per-group rule (§1d exception 2). Env HKEEPFAM_OFF turns off these rows only.

digits_by_prefix_families_3._note: THE ONE-LEVEL SHIFT UNDER A BODY [H1]: where a body [H1] sits above them, the rank rule would push the page's [H2] / [H3] TWO levels down while the human shifts them ONE: ARFUN [H2] → h3, ARFUN [H3] → h4, TWHT [H3] → h4 — a family dialect (§1d exception 1). EXPFUN [H2] is not listed (EXPFUN02 / 04 / 05 follow the rank). pin_levels pins the listed digit at digit + 1 (the level rides in the emitter's data-wd marker). Env HKEEPFAM3_OFF turns off this block only.

digits_by_prefix_families_2._note: The per-family heading-digit pin, the rest of the qualifying groups (the human keeps the digit on free-body headings where the shift rule would move it): [H2] COM, GEO; [H3] TWHK, TWHR, EXPFUN, CEDK; [H4] CEDO; [H5] OSOH. Not listed (a pin would be wrong more often than right): OSAI [H5], MXDB [H5], TRR [H3], TWHA [H3] / [H4]. Env HKEEPFAM2_OFF turns off this block only.

digits_by_prefix_families_4._note: The per-family heading-digit pin, block 3 — groups where the human KEEPS the digit: [H2] ENGC (ENGC403 / ENGC206), ANZH (the page's top heading); [H4] HIS (HIS1005 / 1006). Env HKEEPFAM4_OFF turns off this block and digits_by_prefix_families_5.

digits_by_prefix_families_5._note: The ONE-LEVEL SHIFT (pin_levels: the listed digit ships at digit + 1) for families where the rank rule would push two deep: [H2] → h3 CBI (CBI1008 under a body [H1]); [H3] → h4 ENG and [H4] → h5 ENG (ENG1004 / 1005 / 1007 overviews). XGF [H2] is not listed: its headings sit inside alert boxes (XGF9003 'Key questions'), where the pin never fires — the KB 05B alert title is h4 (exclude_classes). Also left out (no consistent human level): ENO [H2], WJFUN [H2], PES [H2], XDLS [H2]. Env HKEEPFAM4_OFF (shared with digits_by_prefix_families_4).

keep_writer_digit._pin_levels_note: The level a pinned digit ships at; a digit the map does not name pins at itself. Digit 1 pins at 2: the human ships a writer's [H1] body heading as h2 — the plain body shift with no rank — in BLL, HIS (HIS1005 / 1006 / 1007) and CEDR (CEDR204); the body never carries an h1 (the page title owns it). Not listed: ENFUN (follows the rank), EXPFUN (a tie split by module), singletons. The pinned heading still counts in the rank pool at its intermediate level.
keep_writer_digit._digit4_note: Digit 4: the human keeps a writer's [H4] at h4 in ENGJ, ENGR, OSSC and OSOH; across the corpus as a whole it is a tie, so it is not pinned globally. The shift-followers stay out (XDLS, MXDB, MXFL, MXEO, ENGI, ENGS, AGH). digits_by_prefix_env is a per-digit map (a string is still accepted for every digit; a digit missing from the map falls back to H<digit>KEEP_OFF).
keep_writer_digit._digits_by_prefix_note: A per-DIGIT prefix registry: the human keeps a writer's [H2] at h2 in these prefixes and follows the shift rule everywhere else (it keeps it in HIS, CEDR, ENGFUN, TWHA, TEFUN; follows the shift in XDLS, MXFU, SSCI, ENFUN … and PES has its own h4 dialect). An entry is a letter run (matched as the module code's whole letter run — ENG never matches ENGFUN) or a letters+digits SERIES prefix (matched as startsWith: BLL2 = the BLL2xx series — the BLL1xx parents use h3 (BLL150), while BLL210 / 220 / 230 keep h2; TWHK splits by module and is NOT listed). Within HIS and TEFUN the human keeps the digit in most modules (HIS 1002 / 1005 / 1006 / 1007 / 1008 keep, 1001 / 1003 / 1004 follow the shift; TEFUN 03–08 keep, 01 / 02 follow the shift) with no derivable discriminator inside the series — the majority ships, the minority modules are NAMED exceptions. The list IS the scope — no template gate; the exclude_classes boxes and widget / supervisor subtrees still apply in the releveller, and a pinned heading still counts in the rank pool at its intermediate level. Env H2KEEP_OFF = no digit-2 marker; the emitter owns both toggles, so H3KEEP_OFF never silences a digit-2 marker.
keep_writer_digit._exclude_prefixes_note: The letter run of the module code (ENG1004 → ENG, ENGC102 → ENGC — distinct). ENG and ARFUN follow the shift rule in the human build for free-body [H3]; CEDO and XGF are excluded because their [H3]s mostly land at h3 already and the rest are the human's own h4s, so a pin would do more harm than good. Every other prefix keeps [H3] at h3.
keep_writer_digit._pool_note: A pinned heading still COUNTS in the rank pool at its intermediate level, so the page's other headings rank exactly as they would without the pin — removing it from the pool would make the page's [H4]s rise to h3 (as on OSAI401 / MXEO201).
keep_writer_digit._note: A writer's explicit [H3] keeps its digit: the human ships it at h3 on most Standard and Fundamentals free-body sites, while the body shift + rank rule would put it at h4 under a [H2] and at h5 under a [H2] + a title [H1]. The heading emitter adds a TRANSIENT data-wd="N" marker when the digit is listed and the module's template (Module_Structure_Index.module_meta.template_type — a module the index does not know is not pinned) is listed; #relevelHeadings pins such a heading to <hN> — out of the rank pool, its close tag rewritten too — unless an exclude_classes box (the alert family: the KB 05B alert title is h4, and the human rarely uses h3 inside alerts) or a widget / supervisor subtree is open around it; inside an activity box the pin applies. The marker is stripped in every branch and never reaches the output. Inquiry and ConnectED are near-ties and not listed; Bilingual is governed by KB 07B. [H2] and [H4] do not qualify globally (see digits_by_prefix). Env H3KEEP_OFF = no marker, the standing rule.

heading_relevel._fixed_level_note:
TEMPLATED CHROME headings the converter emits at a FIXED level with a fixed class must not join the re-level pool. `

Go to your journal

` (go_journal) is the case: the human always ships it at h4, inside an activity box or standalone, but as an ordinary-looking free-body heading it would be re-ranked with the rest (coming out h3 or h5), and its presence in the pool would also displace the writer's real headings around it (as in SCCH302). A heading whose OWN class is listed here is excluded from BOTH the pool and the rewrite (the activity-anchor / supervisor-note exclusion treatment, keyed on the heading's own class rather than an ancestor div). Env FIXEDHEAD_OFF.

alert_table._side_pair_note:
The human pairs a RIGHT-positioned alert (col-md-4) in the SAME div.row as the FOLLOWING intro content's col-md-8, not in its own row (ENGS302_1.0:
{Welcome +

Under the Skin

+ watch + video}
{Vocab dump}
, then a fresh row at

Understanding the plot

). When side_pair is on and the alert is positional (a real col, not default_col), ContentConverter DEFERS the alert as a pendingSideAlert (the side_col_open/close portion — col + alert box, NO outer row); the following intro content opens a col-md-8 row and FLOWS in (its film-title heading is gathered, not broken) until a media element (the intro video/image) completes the column, then the next row break closes the row with the alert appended as its col-md-4 right sibling. The EXACT col-md-8 extent is editorial (lesson 2 pairs a different-sized section); scoped to the positional-alert-in-table form (ENGS302). Env ALERTPAIR_OFF renders the alert in its own row.
alert_table._note_alert_table:
Writers AUTHOR a side alert box as a 1x1 TABLE whose single cell leads with the positional tag '[Alert box on right hand side]' (also '[Alert box to the right]', ENGS302 lesson 2) then [H3] title + [Text] + bullets. Through #layoutTableGrid the [alert] tag would be DROPPED and the title/bullets rendered as PLAIN content in the page's default col — no alert box, no positioning. The human renders
{h3 + p + ul}
(ENGS302_1.0). ContentConverter.#alertTable intercepts a single-cell table whose lead is a POSITIONAL [alert...] tag (positional_only) BEFORE the grid, parses the position/style keywords, and renders the rest of the cell via #renderCellParts wrapped in the alert callout + col. positional_only keeps the scope to this form; plain [alert]/[alert solid]-in-table and FREE-BODY positional alerts ('[Alert box to right]') are not handled here. The pairing with the main content's col-md-8 is side_pair. Env ALERTTBL_OFF uses the plain grid.

red_part_note._doc: A ' / '-separated part of a layout-table cell that the writer typed WHOLLY in red with no [tag] the normaliser knows (a note to the developer beside the picture: `please add eyes, mouth and license plate`, `[Image like this – kombi van parked in Auckland`, ENGS202 1.0 / 3.0) renders as the writer's red note (NotesAndComments.redFlag kind cs), the free body's own form, instead of a learner paragraph (which would leak the writer's literal note). The raw cell is split on the same separator; a part count that does not match cellParts keeps the plain rendering. Also off under TABLEHOVER_OFF (the table_cell_release master toggle).

layout_table_grid._multi_row_note: MULTI-ROW panel grids. A 1-row tagged table is always a side-by-side panel set. A multi-row tagged table is gridded ONLY when EVERY non-empty cell is a tagged [tag] mini-document (the clean-panel case, e.g. XGF9003-04 food cards). A multi-row table with ANY plain cell is a DATA table (a tagged header row or first-column label + plain data rows — ENGJ402 rhyme-scheme, XGF9003-05 skill matrix) and MUST stay a <table>. WIDGET-DATA tables ([Embedded] [Flipcard]/[Item N] front/back; e.g. PNR101/102/104) are a widget-capture matter, not a grid job.
layout_table_grid.note:
LAYOUT-TABLE -> GRID: the writer lays SIDE-BY-SIDE panels in a 1-row table whose cells (║-separated) each embed a /-separated tagged MINI-DOCUMENT ([H3]+[Image]+[Body]+list, e.g. CEDO501 'Earned income | Unearned income'). The human renders a row>col grid with each cell's parts as proper

//

/

    , rather than the literal [H3]/[Image]/[Body] text in a /. ContentConverter.#contentTable, when insidePlaceholder=false (free-body content tables only — widget-placeholder tables stay raw so their captured data is visible) and the table is SINGLE-ROW (a 1-row table is never an MCQ/comparison DATA table — those have header+data rows), and a cell carries a recognised structural [tag] (structural_tags) and NO cell carries a widget-member tag (GetWidgetTypes guard — a mis-captured flipCard/carousel stays raw), renders each cell as a col via #renderCellParts (each /-part run back through the element renderer: heading->h, [image]->image emitter, body/bullets->#renderBlackText->p/ul). Col width derived from the cell COUNT (2->col-md-6, 3->col-md-4, 4->col-md-3; the human's exact paddingL/R/offset are non-derivable). Genuine data tables (no structural [tag]) keep the raw . Free-body only (placeholders untouched). enabled:false or env LTABLE_OFF turns it off.
layout_table_grid.deferred: MULTI-ROW tagged tables are not gridded — a multi-row tagged table may be a per-row panel set OR a data table with a tagged header row, and the two cannot be told apart reliably. single_row_only:true scopes this build to the unambiguous 1-row panel case.

list_nesting.drop_empty_items_note: A writer bullet whose ONLY content was a red instruction (e.g. '• Insert appropriate introductory video…', as in AGH1004-00) has its instruction lifted to a cv2-note, leaving a black '• ' that #renderBlackText would emit as an EMPTY <li> mixed into the populated 'In this module you will learn about:' list; the human never ships such strays. renderList drops an empty item ONLY when the list ALSO has >=1 real item; a list whose items are ALL empty is a deliberate blank-worksheet scaffold the human DOES ship (e.g. MXFUN03/PES1004/MXDB301) and is left intact. env EMPTYBULLET_OFF keeps the empty <li>.
list_nesting.drop_note_residue_bullet_note:
The ALL-EMPTY follow-up to drop_empty_items (as in MXDI202-00). A LONE bulleted instruction (e.g. a CS-note bullet) leaves its bullet as a SINGLE-item empty
once the instruction is lifted to the cv2-note; drop_empty_items keeps ALL-empty lists (worksheet scaffolds), so this stray would survive. ContentConverter post-pass #dropNoteResidueBullets (parity with #stripMediaResidue) removes a SINGLE empty
