immediately FOLLOWED by a cv2-note paragraph — the residue of a bulleted instruction whose text was lifted to that note; the human never ships these. A DELIBERATE lone blank bullet (not followed by a note) is untouched, a multi-blank worksheet scaffold (>=2
  • ) never matches, and the post-pass (vs an emit-time pop) is robust to consecutive bulleted instructions. env NOTEBULLET_OFF keeps the residue bullet.

asterisk_bullet._doc:
THE WRITER'S TYPED ASTERISK BULLET: a line the writer started with '* ' (asterisk + space — a manual bullet; the engine's Word list numbering always renders '• ', and the italic marker '*text*' never opens with a space) is a list item, not a paragraph; otherwise it would show as a literal

* …

— the asterisk visible, the list broken (e.g. BLL240 / 242–244 / 247 / 250–252 / 271–276, the overview menu's 'Decoding an unknown word … involves:' sub-points; ARFUN02; HIS1006; MXEO201; MXFL401). The human lists these lines: nested under the preceding '• …:' bullet (the BLL form), flat after a colon lead (ARFUN02). The rule: directly after a '•' bullet line the '* ' line nests one level deeper; after another '* ' line it takes that line's level; anywhere else it is a flat top-level item. Env STARBULLET_OFF keeps the literal

.

ol_start._doc: A CONTINUED NUMBERED LIST KEEPS ITS NUMBERS (KB constraint 42: numbered steps use <ol><li>, with start="N" for continuation across split content). A numbered run whose first item is N > 1 — Word's own number, which the extractor now writes on every numbered paragraph (list_numbering.word_count), or the writer's typed digit — opens <ol start="N">, so steps 1–2, a sentence, then step 3 shows 3, not a second 1. A run that starts at 1 is unchanged, and a bullet list promoted to numbers (ol_bold_parents) never takes a start.

list_nesting.emphasis_led_bullet_note:
A writer typed a literal bullet glyph as the list marker, but WRAPPED it in emphasis ('*•structural features…*'), PRECEDED it with stray emphasis (' *•make independent…'), or separated it with a TAB ('*•\tdescribe…') — none caught by #renderBlackText's plain ^• test, so the item would show as a

instead of a list

  • (ENGS302-00 'I know that:' + '•structural…', 'In my learning…' + '•make…'; the human ships both as
  • , like all the other bullets; also XMES102). #renderBlackText ALSO matches a bullet after a leading run of *,_ emphasis markers and, when the bullet sat inside an emphasis WRAPPER, drops the now-dangling closing marker so the content stays clean. A plain '• text' bullet flows through the unchanged path. env EMPHBULLET_OFF uses the plain ^• test (emphasis-led bullets fall back to a

    ).
list_nesting.note:
The writer's docx carries list NESTING via w:ilvl (DocxExtractor encodes it as leading 2-space indentation per level); #renderBlackText builds nested
    /
      from it instead of flattening every bullet to one level. OL-OVERRIDE: a TOP-level bullet list whose every item is BOLD and carries nested sub-points is rendered as a NUMBERED
        (the human numbers these 'category + sub-points' lists even though the docx tags them as bullets — OSAI201-02 'What did we learn?':
        1. Be specific
          • Bad prompt…
          • Good prompt…
          2. …). Conservative: top level only, every item bold AND parented, >=2 items, so a plain flat list or a non-bold list is unchanged. indent_spaces_per_level matches the extractor's encoding. env LISTNEST_OFF flattens every list to one level.

data_table_cell_tags.note:
DATA-TABLE CELL-TAG rendering. A structural [tag] inside a cell of a KEPT (one #layoutTableGrid did NOT un-table — i.e. a real DATA table, not a panel grid) would otherwise leak as literal text (' vs [H2] header -> ; ENGJ402-04 rhyme header [Body, bold] **Line** -> , the ** supplying the bold); [Body]/[Text]/[list] text -> the text (no bold); an image-ONLY cell -> the in-cell (#cellImage); a cell carrying a TEXT label AND a decorative [Image] renders the label and DROPS the image (the XGF9003 matrix header icon). ContentConverter.#renderCellInline, called per cell from #contentTable, ACTIVATES only when the cell's LEADING part is a structural [tag] in structural_tags (resolved via TagNormaliser.Parse); a cell whose leading tag is a widget member ([front]/[Card N]/[Item N]/[Tab N] -> SUBTAG, excluded) or a non-tag bracket ([tick], bracketed prose -> Parse null, excluded) returns null and is rendered LITERALLY — so a genuine data table cannot be mis-rendered. Does NOT change the keep-vs-grid decision (#layoutTableGrid). Inline / sit inside the cell, so the wrapper chain is unchanged. enabled:false or env CELLTAG_OFF turns it off.
[Body, bold] Line', ' [H2] Organisation'). The human developer renders the tag INLINE, marker stripped: [H1-6]/[Body, bold] text -> text in a DATA cell () but PLAIN text in a HEADER cell ( is already bold, so no inner is added — XGF9003-06 matrix: [H2] first-column label -> OrganisationExecutive function skillLine

phrases: you will show your understanding by
how will i know if i've learned it
what am i learning to do
named_headings.note:
NAMED LEARNING-DESIGN HEADING promotion (a positional/content convention, B-ii). The Te Kura learning-design headers (WALT 'We are learning to', WILF 'You will show your understanding by', 'Success criteria', 'Learning intentions', 'How will I know if I've learned it?') are a CLOSED, recognisable vocabulary the human developer renders as a HEADING even when the writer left them as plain untagged black text (AGH1004 'We are learning to ...' -> the human's
). A GENERIC bold-line->heading rule is not used (the same arbitrary phrase varies by developer); but the NAMED phrases follow the human's consistent OUTPUT convention. ContentConverter.#promoteNamedHeadings runs as a post-pass on the assembled #body AFTER #relevelHeadings (so the fixed level survives the rank-normaliser): a FREE-BODY

(NOT inside a widget subtree — heading_relevel.skip_classes) whose folded text EXACTLY equals a phrase (modulo tags / trailing punctuation; a leading reo|english 'Whāinga Ako |' prefix is NOT stripped so bilingual [H2]-tagged headers are untouched) becomes . The EXACT-whole-paragraph guard avoids body-sentence false positives ('we are learning about budgeting' != 'we are learning to'). The human's form is mostly h5, hence level 5. A tag/level change never alters the wrapper chain. enabled:false or env NAMEDH_OFF turns it off.

menu_lead_in_headings.note:
MENU LEAD-IN heading promotion. On lesson/overview menus the human renders the learning-intention lead-ins 'We are learning:' / 'I can:' / 'We are learning about:' as a HEADING (
), but they fold to 'we are learning' / 'i can' (NOT the named phrase 'we are learning to'), so #promoteNamedHeadings alone would leave them

. The human KEEPS them

only when they are a SECONDARY lead-in UNDER a learning-design parent heading ('Learning Intentions' h5 -> 'We are learning:'

). DISCRIMINATOR: promote UNLESS the lead-in is immediately preceded by another LD label (parent or lead-in) with NO bullet list in between — the second label of a heading+lead-in pair stays

; bullets reset the group. This agrees with the human most of the time; the main exceptions are the engFamily two_col menus that skip promotion anyway (skipMenuPromo). 'i will be able to' is EXCLUDED (the human never promotes it). Level h5 (the human's dominant form). MENU-ONLY (#promoteNamedHeadings isMenu flag; the body never promotes these); ld_labels is the guard vocabulary. Menu is #header-scoped. Env MENULEADIN_OFF turns it off; enabled:false disables it.
menu_lead_in_headings._doc_eng_family:
Complements skipMenuPromo: engFamily two_col OVERVIEW menus skip the WHOLE promotion (their 'We are learning:'/'I can:' are

lead-ins under an h5 'Learning Intentions'); this flag only fires on the NON-engFamily menus (HES/AGH/CED/PES/OSxx/...) where the lead-in is the top label of its group.
menu_lead_in_headings._doc_new_era_label:
ld_labels includes 'how will i know i have learned it' — the new-era SC-heading phrasing (no 'if', 'I have' not 'I've', as in SCCH302), without which the guard's exact-fold match would miss it and the 'I can:' lead under it would wrongly be PROMOTED to
. The human ships

I can:

under this heading (SCCH301 / SCPH301 / SSCI205 / TEDC401 / TEDC402; HPRE203 keeps
— a single deviation). Rides the MENULEADIN_OFF machinery (a vocabulary edit).

body_region.row_rule: ONE STRUCTURE PER ROW is the dominant gold-standard convention: about half of the human pages' rows hold exactly one direct child. The engine therefore gives every root-level block its own row, with one grouping exception below. Inside an open container/activity, no row breaks ever happen.

row_breaks.flow_blocks_note: ROW GROUPING: the human opens a new top-level div.row only at a HEADING, an ACTIVITY, the page-START/quote or a CALLOUT, and FLOWS everything else (media, tables, widgets, lists, body) into the current section row, rather than giving every media/table/widget its OWN row. flow_blocks=true makes media/table/widget FLOW; only heading/activity/boxed-callout (kind 'section') break a row (ContentConverter rowFor + the 'section'/'block' call-sites). emit() never opens an EMPTY row (a de-duped lesson-title heading returning [] would otherwise leave an empty row>col); and FLOWING callouts (quote/thought) flow into the section row instead of a self-contained box (the page-start quote opens the row and the intro flows in). env ROWGROUP_OFF gives one row per block.
row_breaks.group_content_note: GROUPED ROWS: text and lists FLOW into the current row; a heading starts a fresh row (the text after it flows in); a hard block (media/table/callout/widget/activity/page) takes its own row. This matches the human, where most rows hold 2+ content children (h+p+p and p+p+p dominant). Set false for one block per row (heading_keeps_next_black_run).
row_breaks.heading_note: LEGACY (used only when group_content=false): a heading keeps its immediately-following text run in the same row. Everything else — each [body] block, video, image, table, callout, button, widget — stands alone.
row_breaks.after_note: Content following a closed callout/activity/widget always starts a fresh row (verified OSAI201_0.0, OSAH401_1.0).

rules._exclude_doc: Excluded subjects (the human keeps the prose after the flipCard group in the same column): Leaving to Learn, NCEA1, 1-10 English (a tie). Kept: Online Safety, ConnectED, Mathematics, Science, and the subject-less TEDC pair.

after_built_widgets._doc: The flow_blocks rule keeps every built widget IN the section row and lets the next prose flow on after it; the human does that for every built widget but ONE — after a built flipCard group (`div.row.flipCardsContainer`) the human mostly CLOSES the column and opens a new row for the prose (the group is usually its column's LAST or only child — English, Mathematics, ConnectED, Online Safety). For every other built widget the human is evenly split, so it keeps the flow rule. A rule = class_match (a regex on the built html's open-tag class), templates (module_meta.template_type), exclude_subjects (module_meta.subject). Fires only at the INLINE widget site (a top-level widget — inside an activity box the group never closes the box). The break BEFORE the group is NOT taken (the human is split), nor the col-md-12 width. OFF = the prose flows on after the group.

choice_page_tiles._meta: The XDLS900 'Learning Support' CHOICE-PAGE TILE NAVIGATION. The WT opens a choice page with [LESSON Choice page] and (usually) a [Tab Nav Layout … Repeat on EVERY PAGE] marker + a ONE-column table of bold category names, one per learning area; the human builds a grid of icon tiles (div.choice), one per lesson, merged onto page 00. Tile links = the GENERATED lesson HTML files (the human's online MTK quickLink rcodes exist nowhere in the WT); category k maps 1:1 positionally to [LESSON k] (as in XDLS906). Labels = the writer's own table categories (XDLS906's human build uses them verbatim; the 903/904/905 human builds' partial renames are non-derivable editorial, C), falling back to the lesson TITLE when there is no table (XDLS902 — its human labels ARE the lesson titles). iconType ships EMPTY plus one Designer/Developer To Do note (the human build itself carries 'CS: review iconType' comments — icon choice is editorial). The opener occurs in XDLS902-906; the layout markers also in XDLS908. Env toggles: CHOICETILES_OFF (the tile build), TABNAVDROP_OFF (marker consumption + layout-table To Do + the sticky-layout page-boundary demotion), CHOICEMERGE_OFF (the page-00 merge).
choice_page_tiles.bare_marker_note: The bare [Tab Nav]/[Sticky Nav] repeat markers on every later page are layout REPEAT directives, not content — the human drops them (the sticky nav is a js/stickyNav.js include). Bare [Sticky Nav] parses to DROP; bare [Tab Nav] is consumed here (it would otherwise leak an 'Orphan sub-tag [tab n]' red flag on almost every XDLS90x page). Matched on the span's own folded text so a real orphaned [tab 1] sub-tag still flags. The optional trailing ']' tolerates XDLS905's '[Tab Nav]]' doubled-bracket typo (the malformed-bracket class).
choice_page_tiles.merge_note: The human merges the choice page INTO page 00 (every gold ships 00 + one page per lesson, 8 files); the writer's [End page] before [LESSON Choice page] is disregarded exactly like the AR-1 introduction-cluster rule. Verified clean on all 5 opener modules. Env CHOICEMERGE_OFF.
choice_page_tiles.link_target_note: The human's target=_blank belongs to its external quickLink form; a local generated-file link navigates in place like the footer prev/next links.
choice_page_tiles.shell: {tiles}
choice_page_tiles.tile: {label}
choice_page_tiles.icon_todo: Choice-page tiles built with an EMPTY iconType — pick an icon for each tile: {labels}. (The human-built siblings use iconCentral iconType values such as physicalHealth, nutrition, mindfulness.)
choice_page_tiles.tabnav_todo: The writer's [Tab Nav Layout] (repeat on every page) is an online tab-navigation set-up, not page content — configure the site tab nav with: {labels}.
choice_page_tiles.sticky_todo: The writer's [Sticky Nav Layout] (repeat on every page) is the sticky-nav include (js/stickyNav.js), not page content — set it up with these cross-module links: {items}.

cell_image_link_match._doc_summary: Title-anchored table-cell images resolve via the block's hyperlinks.
cell_image_link_match.note: A cell [image] with no URL in its text finds the table block's hyperlink whose folded anchor text sits inside the folded cell text (longest wins) and uses its target — the same resolution the free-body path gets from it.block.links. Env CELLIMGLINK_OFF.

container_auto_close.rule: Writers frequently omit [end alert]/[end activity]. A callout holds its following content RUN, never the rest of the page. An open container auto-closes — with a summary note, never silently — before any item listed here. An explicit [end X] always wins where present.

callout_close_before.SUPERSEDED: The engine does not read this block: callout containment is set in callouts.containment (STRICT following-run by default; SPAN only with an explicit [end X] ahead). It remains only so references to it still resolve.

activity_close_before._doc_side_by_side_headings_stay: A heading that shares its source paragraph with another heading — a side-by-side caption row ('[H3] Picture A     [H3] Picture B', XGF9003 5C) — labels the open activity's own two-column content and does not auto-close it (the human keeps the row and what follows inside the writer's box). Env SBSHEAD_OFF.
activity_close_before._title_heading_note: An activity's OWN title heading must stay INSIDE the box, never auto-close it. title_heading_tags = heading tags that are ALWAYS the activity's title (an [activity heading] is never a section break). heading_closes_only_after_content: a PLAIN section heading (H2-H5 ≤ rendered_heading_max) is the activity's title when it is the FIRST thing after the [Activity N] opener (before any content) and so stays inside; only AFTER the activity has content is such a heading a section break that closes the activity. Without this, an activity whose title is a SEPARATE heading tag right after the opener (ENGC201-01 1B: '[Activity heading H3] Creating emotion avatars', and 246 such boxes across 59 modules) auto-closed EMPTY, spilling its heading/body/list/video OUTSIDE the box. An explicit [end activity] / a new [Activity] / a section marker / a page boundary still close it as before. Read by ContentConverter.ConvertPage#autoClose.
activity_close_before._rendered_heading_max_note: 4, so a writer [H3] SECTION heading closes the activity. renderedHeading = writer-H-digit + body_shift(1), so the threshold is on the LOGICAL level: max 4 closes [H1]/[H2]/[H3] (section-level) and KEEPS [H4]/[H5] (rendered h5 > 4 — activity sub-headings 'Answers'/'Questions'/'Your Turn'/'Checklist'). With 3, a [H3] (rendered h4) would slip past, so an activity (OSBY201-03's 3B, S.A.F.E) would swallow the following [H3] 'The banter trap' + body + table until the next [Activity] tag. The first top-level heading after an activity's content is usually a writer [H3] (usually followed by a new [Activity] — a section break), while [H4] / [H5] there are sub-headings kept inside. The title protection (heading_closes_only_after_content) still keeps a [H3] activity TITLE inside. Env ACTHEAD_OFF uses rendered_heading_max_legacy (3).
activity_close_before.keeps_inside: everything content-like including images, buttons and interactive placeholders, until an explicit [end activity] or a structural break

page_split_rules._doc: General PageSplitter rules for the mid-document literal [TITLE BAR] (the AR-4 sub-document trigger) on modules that are not in reoMode (the MTK house header does not put a module in reoMode). Both stay in-page exactly like the reoPage branch (the item lands on the current page as a lesson/section title). Env MTKPAGE_OFF disables both (MTKREO_OFF also puts the MTK modules back in reoMode).
page_split_rules._single_file_doc: page_model 'single-file' also suppresses the AR-4 second-[TITLE BAR] sub-document split — the registry's 'one file regardless of page tags' promise, honoured for the title-bar boundary too. The modules this touches (ENFUN01-09 + CEDT104) then match the human's 1-file shape; no other single-file module carries >=2 literal title bars.

duplicate_opening_drop._doc: A PASTED-TWICE OPENING [TITLE BAR] + HEADING IS ONE OPENING: BLL124's writer pasted '[TITLE BAR] Module 4 - c, k, ck …' + '[H1] Tirohanga Whānui | Overview' twice; AR-4's duplicate rule keeps the identical second title bar in-page, where ContentConverter's partition would read it as the menu boundary — the overview menu would be near-empty and its content would land in the body. A same-text duplicate [TITLE BAR] whose previous non-blank item is a heading and whose next non-blank item repeats that heading is dropped together with the repeated heading. Env DUPOPEN_OFF.

empty_titlebar_inpage._doc: AN EMPTY SECOND [TITLE BAR] ON THE OPEN OVERVIEW IS NOT A TWIN DOCUMENT: MUS1006's writer typed [TITLE BAR] + the title, [MODULE INTRODUCTION] + its text, then a second, EMPTY [TITLE BAR] before '[H1] Tirohanga Whānui | Overview' and the overview sections — AR-4 would read it as a twin sub-document, so 0_0 would keep the introduction and 1_0 would ship the overview as a menu with no h1 and an empty body; the human ships one 0_0. A literal [TITLE BAR] with no payload (no black tail, no words after the bracket) arriving on the overview while it is still open (no [end page] before it) stays in-page. AR-4's twin documents carry their own title. (ENFUN09's empty repeated [TITLE BAR] follows an [End page] on a single-file page and is unaffected.) Env EMPTYTB_OFF.

lesson_titlebar_inpage._doc: A TITLE BAR THAT OPENS A FRESH LESSON PAGE IS THAT LESSON'S TITLE, NOT A SUB-DOCUMENT. GER1002's writer opens each lesson `[LESSON]` then `[Title bar] 1.0 EINE EMAIL AUS DEUTSCHLAND`; the literal mid-document [TITLE BAR] is AR-4's second-document trigger, so the [LESSON] page would stay empty and the lesson would open a new sub-document page, shifting every later page. AR-4's twin document (a reading-record set) opens after an [End page], never on a lesson page that holds only its opener; the reoMode branch likewise keeps a mid-doc title bar in-page as a lesson title. KB 01D (the [LESSON] tag opens the lesson page): a mid-document literal [TITLE BAR] arriving while the current page is a LESSON page whose items so far are only its opener tag(s) and blank lines stays in-page. Env LESSONTB_OFF.

page_split_rules._duplicate_doc: a second literal [TITLE BAR] whose folded block text EQUALS the previous title bar's is a writer copy-paste duplicate, not a twin document — keep it in-page (as in BLL124 — a verbatim duplicate 2 lines apart; the human ships one fewer file than AR-4 would). The genuine twin-sets (EXBP901/EXIP901 English|Te-Reo title pairs) have DIFFERENT payloads and keep the AR-4 split.

output_naming.page_token: {page} = the page's lessonLabel with '.' -> '_' (overview 0.0 -> 0_0; lesson N -> N_0; a sub-page or dotted writer lesson verbatim: 2.1 -> 2_1) - the site library convention the developer imports against (SCCH302_0_0.html).
output_naming.page_number_format: library form: {code}_{lesson}_{part}.html in document order; legacy (env PAGENAME_OFF): two digits, zero-padded, -00 overview, -01 ...
output_naming.decision_note: Output files use the library's underscore naming ({CODE}_{page}.html) so the developer never renames on import; env PAGENAME_OFF uses the dash form ({CODE}-NN.html).

black_number._doc: The writer's other way of typing an explicit lesson number: a BARE [LESSON] tag followed by the number in its own black text («[lesson] 4», «[LESSON] 1 New Zealanders and dates»). That whole number counts as the tag's explicit number, so an implicit page break inside lesson N whose next tag is «[LESSON] N+1» opens lesson N's continuation N.1, not lesson N+1. A dotted number (4.1) or a bare tag with no number still records none.

implicit_break_sub_page._doc: KB 01D 'Lesson Numbering: [LESSON 1] → -01, [LESSON 2] → -02 … explicit numbers preserved'. An implicit page break (content after [end page] with no [LESSON] tag and no 'Lesson N' heading) would open lesson N+1 by the running ordinal; when the writer's own [LESSON N+1] came later it would collide, PageSplitter's duplicate-label pass would relabel it N+2, and every later lesson would shift by one (e.g. CEDR501 [LESSON 2] 'Take note!' as 3.0). Inside a lesson page N (an integer number) whose writer still has an explicit [LESSON N+1] ahead, the implied page is lesson N's CONTINUATION, sub-page N.k — the human's form (CEDR501 1.1 'Roles', 2.1) — and keeps the lesson number, so the continuation rule hands it the lesson's menu. Env IMPLSUB_OFF.

page_split._doc: THE NEW-ERA WRITER LESSON NUMBERING (as in ENGJ403): the newest WT era numbers lessons ALREADY DOTTED ([Lesson 0.0]/[Lesson 1.0]/[Lesson 2.1]) and closes in-lesson TILE structures with [end tile lesson navigate back to lesson N]. Three coupled PageSplitter rules: (1) overview_zero_pattern — a [Lesson 0/0.0] while the OVERVIEW is open is the overview's own number (the module introduction), consumed, content stays on 0.0 (so the overview is not left empty; env ZEROLESSON_OFF); (2) dotted_label_verbatim — a dotted writer number is the page label VERBATIM ('2.1' not '2.1.0'; as in ENGJ403 + CEDK501/CEDO501/CEDR501/CEDT501/CEDW501/XMES202, whose human builds ship the same '2.1'-style pages; un-dotted '[Lesson 4]' keeps the '.0'; env DOTLESSON_OFF); (3) tile_closer_pattern — an 'end lesson' closer whose own text matches the tile pattern is an IN-PAGE structure closer, never a page boundary (env TILECLOSER_OFF).

stage_opener_break._doc: THE EXPLORE STAGE'S «LESSON OVERVIEW:» OPENS ITS OWN PAGE: each EXPlore stage (Explore / Plan / Do / Share It) opens with a header run — an optional '[Navigation] Navigate to <stage> …' note, the bold stage name ('**Share It | Mahia Whakaaturanga**'), the banner instruction, then the bare red 'Lesson overview:' label + its LI / SC. Where the writer typed no [End page] before the header, the stage would ride on the previous page (EXIP901's Share It on the Do-It page; EXBP901's Explore It on the module overview); the human always ships one page per stage. In a module holding at least min_labels bare labels (label_pattern; a red span with no tag of its own), PageSplitter walks back from each label over up to lead_max header items (instruction tags; a black line that is all bold, at most lead_bold_max_words words) and, at the first of them, closes a current page that holds content — the header opens the next page. The bare label occurs in EXIP901 and EXBP901 only. Env STAGEBREAK_OFF.

side_tab_end_page._doc: AN [END PAGE <TAB>] THAT NAMES THE OPEN SIDE TAB CLOSES THE TAB, NOT THE PAGE (like the tile closer): the EXPlore writer closes the Plan-It stage's Intro side tab with '[End page intro]' (EXIP901; EXBP901 '[End page Intro]'), which would otherwise split the stage in two — its lesson overview + Intro tab on one page, the rest (blank menu, no side nav) on the next. PageSplitter tracks the open side tab (a 'tab n' opener whose text matches opener_text_pattern; a closer_pattern span clears it); an 'end page' span whose own words name that tab (equal, or the tab's label starts with them) becomes an '[End of tab]' closer and the page continues — only when another tab closer / opener follows before the next PAGE_BOUNDARY or stage marker (stage_marker_patterns: the bare 'Lesson overview:', '[End of … phase …]') within lookahead items. The writer's '[End page next steps]' / '[End page Next Steps]' close a stage's LAST tab and the page, and stay page ends. Env SIDETABEND_OFF.

writer_lesson_numbers._doc_dotted_heading_verbatim: A DOTTED lesson number read from a 'Lesson N.M:' heading — the implicit-page opener's harvest and the post-pass 'heading says Lesson N' override — is the page label verbatim, as dotted_label_verbatim makes it for a [LESSON N.M] tag; appending '.0' would give 1.2.0-style labels and `_1_2_0` files (PWY1001 / 1002 / 1008 / 1009, MXEX301, MXEO301, MXDB301, MXFL302, MXFU302, BLLR203; the human always names them N.M). Env DOTHEAD_OFF.

page_split._doc_lesson_boundary_guard:
TWO PageSplitter guards on what counts as a lesson page boundary.

(1) duplicate_number_merge — THE DIVIDER-BANNER FORM. A WT house convention writes the lesson number TWICE: an all-caps banner on the divider page right after [End page] ('[LESSON 1.0]'), then the real titled opener ('[Lesson 1.0] Elements of narrative'), with ONLY the lesson-MENU region between them ([Lesson Overview] + the black We-are-learning / I-can run). The banner would open an empty file and the duplicate-label relabeller would then shift EVERY later lesson number (as in ENGS404). When a [Lesson N] marker's number equals the OPEN lesson page's number AND that page has received NO BODY content yet, the marker is merged into the open page (its title adopted if the page has none) instead of opening a new one. 'Body content' = a table or a tag whose directive is ELEMENT/INTERACTIVE/CONTAINER_OPEN/INLINE; the menu region's SECTION_MARKERs and black text do NOT count — that material belongs to the same lesson either way. The no-body rule by construction EXCLUDES pairs where the writer genuinely reused a number across real content (CEDO501, HES1005, AGH1006, HIS1007). Env LESSONDUP_OFF.

(2) instruction_guard — THE BURIED-MARKER FORM. A span becomes a lesson/page boundary merely because the word 'lesson'/'page' appears inside writer prose ('[insert lesson from ENO511 …]' → a page numbered 511; '[Designer note: Please insert old lesson from here…]'; '[Rollover for mana: … complete History fundamental lesson 7 …]'). NECESSARY CONDITION: the primary must have matched how:'embedded' (the clean_hows distinction) — boundaries that matched exact/denumbered/denumbered_head are untouchable BY CONSTRUCTION. Among embedded matches the marker is disregarded when EITHER the span is instruction-dominant by TagNormaliser.IsInstructionDominant (all tags embedded + a recognised writer-instruction cue + >= min_words of prose), OR the bracket names a FOREIGN module code (foreign_code_pattern, any position, the run's own code excluded — the cross-module 'copy that lesson' reference form: '[insert lesson from ENO511 …]', '[Copy PHO1032 lesson 8]', '[PHO1011 lesson 5.1-5.3]'), OR the text BEFORE the marker word carries a hover/rollover marker word (deny_lead_pattern — '[Rollover for mana: … complete History fundamental lesson 7 …]' is a hover trigger whose DEFINITION mentions a lesson: vocabulary, not structure). FAIL-OPEN by design: an unrecognised embedded form stays a boundary. Genuine embedded markers survive ([Lesson summary], [lesson title], [Lesson Two], [Lesson six], [Final Page], [Next Page], [New Page …], [Intro page], [ILanding page], [Page N of diary], [page ends]); the [MODULE CONTENT: PAGE n] and [Sticky Nav Layout …] forms are consumed EARLIER in the same branch and never reach this guard. DELIBERATELY NARROW: a broader leading-instruction-verb deny (insert/copy/create/from) is not used — forms like ENGI405's '[insert zones writing wheel from this page' and ART1006's '[Create two new colour boxes … page called the' sit where the human developer DID break the page. Env LESSONGUARD_OFF.

intro_page_label._doc: AN [INTRO PAGE] SPAN RIGHT AFTER [MODULE INTRODUCTION] IS THE INTRODUCTION'S LABEL, NOT A PAGE: XLP05 types '[MODULE INTRODUCTION]' then '[Intro Page] Introduction' — the span parses as a 'page' PAGE_BOUNDARY and would open a new page, so the introduction would leave the overview, every later page would shift one file along and 0_0 would ship a menu with an empty body; the human keeps the introduction on XLP05.00 and renders no 'Introduction' label. A PAGE_BOUNDARY span whose folded text matches pattern and whose previous non-blank item is the [MODULE INTRODUCTION] tag is consumed (its label with it); the page continues. (MXFUN03's [Intro Page] is the code-phase dialect's intro-page marker on a fundamentals page, not after [MODULE INTRODUCTION].) Env INTROPAGE_OFF.

label_form._doc: KB 01D Standard Page Structure: the overview page carries the module introduction; AR-1. A RED LABEL naming the introduction — `Splash Page - Intro`, typed as an unbracketed red span on the line after the overview's [End page] (EXBP901, EXIP901) — is an introduction-cluster marker: the [End page] before it is disregarded and the introduction (`[H2] Nau mai haere mai …`, the welcome, the project cycle) stays on page 0.0, the human's form; with menu_boundary the label is `_introStart`, so the overview section above it is the menu. It rides with header.title_split.te_reo_line.title_bar_pair (TBPAIR_OFF): together they keep both overviews' menus and bodies filled. Env INTROLABEL_OFF.

intro_cluster_forms._doc_menu_boundary: KB 01D Standard Page Structure. The item where AR-1 recognised the module introduction (every form above, and [supervisor note]) is marked `_introStart`; with no red [MODULE INTRODUCTION] tag and no mid-document title-bar alias, ContentConverter ends the overview's menu there, so the introduction is the page's body (as in the human build) instead of sitting in #module-menu-content (HIS1002, XFUN02, PES1005, ART1006, MXFL103 …). Env INTROMENU_OFF.
intro_cluster_forms._doc: AR-1 disregards a stray [end page] on the OVERVIEW when the next tag span is an introduction-cluster marker ([MODULE INTRODUCTION] / a mid-doc title-bar alias / [supervisor note]); four more writer forms are recognised, so the module introduction does not become its own page 1.0: the marker typed BLACK ('**[MODULE INTRODUCTION]**' — HIS1002, ART1006, PES1005, TEDC402 — black_pattern on the whole line), the marker glued to another tag ('[MODULE INTRODUCTION] [insert image]' — GEO1004, MUS1004, XFUN02 — embedded_pattern on the span's raw text), a CS / unresolved instruction tag in front of it (ENGR102 — skip_unresolved_tags: a tag with no resolved primary or of class instruction is looked past), and the heading form ('[H2] Introduction', '[H1] **INTRODUCTION**', '[H3] **MODULE INTRODUCTION**', '[H2] **Introduction:** Precipitation Reactions' — CBI1009, COM1005, COM1006, DAN1003, DAN1004, MXDI101 — heading_pattern on the h1–h3 words; 'Lesson 1: Introduction to …' never matches). In the human build page 1 is lesson 1 and the overview holds the introduction. Env INTROFORM_OFF.

title_form._doc: A NUMBERED 'N.0 TITLE' LESSON TITLE OPENS ITS LESSON PAGE: GER1002 opens lesson 1 with [LESSON] + '[Title bar] 1.0 EINE EMAIL AUS DEUTSCHLAND' and then marks lessons 2–5 ONLY by a numbered title — '[title] 2.0 SCHNELLER, HÖHER, WEITER', '[title] 3.0 WO WIR WOHNEN', a bare red '4.0' + black 'ZU HAUSE', '[title] 5.0 MEIN ZIMMER' — under one [End page], so without this lessons 1–5 would ship as ONE page; the human ships a page per lesson. A tag in tags (the title-bar family, '[title]' its alias) whose own words match pattern, or an untagged red span matching number_span_pattern with a black title after it, becomes a mid-page lesson candidate (kept in-page as the lesson's title) — it opens lesson N when N is above the lesson in effect. Env TITLENUM_OFF.

split_form._doc: KB 01D. A RED «LESSON» + A BLACK «N TITLE» OPENS LESSON N'S PAGE: CBI1008 types '[H1] Lesson' (the word alone in the red span) + the black '4 The Law of Conservation of Mass'; without this lesson 4 would ride on page 3.0. When the red free text matches word_pattern and the black text matches black_pattern, the heading is a mid-page lesson candidate for lesson N (group 1), group 2 its title; every mid-page guard is unchanged. Env SPLITLESSON_OFF.

span_number._doc: KB 01D. A «LESSON N» TYPED INSIDE THE RED HEADING SPAN OPENS ITS LESSON PAGE: '[H2] Lesson 2' + the black title 'Solubility Rules' (CBI1009), '[H2] Lesson 3' + 'The PPDAC Cycle' (MXFL202). The heading candidate reads the black text first, so the number in the red span (parse.free) would never be seen and the lesson would ride on the page before. When the black text does not open 'Lesson N', a red span whose free text is exactly 'Lesson N' (a number or number word, an optional colon) makes the heading a candidate, the black text its title; every mid-page guard is unchanged. (Most such headings already open their page — after an [end page], inside a page a [LESSON] tag opened, or on single-file / first items.) Env SPANLESSON_OFF.

black_marker_any_case._doc:
KB 01D. A BLACK UPPER-CASE [LESSON N] LINE OPENS ITS LESSON PAGE. black_pattern above is compiled without the i flag, so its bracketed alternative would only match a lower-case '[lesson N]' — GEO1006's writer types '[LESSON 2]' / '[LESSON 3]' / '[LESSON 4]' / '[LESSON 5]' in black: lessons 4 / 5 would open late at their '[H2] Lesson N …' echo, AFTER their red [Lesson Overview] (so lesson 5's LI would become lesson 4's menu and 5.0 would ship a blank one), and lessons 2 / 3 would open at the implicit break after [End of lesson] with the marker line shipped as a red 'Writers Note: [LESSON 3]'. A black line that is exactly '[LESSON N]' in ANY case is a candidate (pattern + flags; the unbracketed 'LESSON N …' form stays upper-case only); implicit_break_consume: when a black marker candidate (either form) is the first item after an [end page] (the implicit page break), the line is consumed, as it is mid-page — the page keeps the running ordinal (MXS1004's writer skips 3 and 8; the human numbers the pages in sequence, as the implicit break does). Also affects GEO1004 (a bare 'LESSON 1'

) and MXS1004 (its [LESSON 5] opens 5.0; the black echo 'LESSON 5 Measures of Central Tendency' stays a

as its other echoes do). Env toggle: BLACKLESSON_OFF.

mid_page_lesson_heading._doc_empty_page_merge: KB 01D AR-2: an EMPTY current page (not the overview) when a mid-page lesson opener fires is reused, not left behind — DAN1006's '[New page]' typed right before '[H2] Lesson Five' would otherwise leave an empty 4.1. Env MIDEMPTY_OFF.
mid_page_lesson_heading._doc: The implicit-page-break branch harvests a 'Lesson N: …' heading only right after an [end page]; a writer who opens a lesson with the heading alone ('[H1] Lesson Four: Creating movement…' DAN1004, '[H2] Lesson two: key features…' DAN1006, '[H2] Lesson 2 The Negative Powers of 10' MXDI301, '[H1] Lesson 3 Carbon Compounds' CBI1008) or with a black '[LESSON 5]' / 'LESSON 3' line (MXS1004, GEO1004 / GEO1006 — the marker typed without the red style) would have that lesson merged into the page before it; the human starts a page there. PageSplitter pre-scans candidates (an h1–h3 heading opening 'Lesson <N>' — digits or a number word — or a black line that is exactly '[LESSON N]' / an upper-case 'LESSON N …'), keeps a candidate only when min_items_after items follow before the next candidate with a DIFFERENT number or a page boundary (a lesson LIST is not openers; a '[LESSON 4]' line and its '[H2] Lesson 4 …' echo are one opener), and at run time opens page N.0 only on a lesson page (never the overview), off single-file and reoMode modules, when N is HIGHER than the lesson in effect; the black marker line is consumed. Env MIDLESSON_OFF turns it off.

page_marker_as_lesson._doc_ar2_restores_ordinal: A [PAGE] that opened a page-as-lesson (ordinal N) followed at once by a [LESSON] tag: AR-2 pops the empty [PAGE] page and restores the ordinal that page had bumped, so the [LESSON] opens lesson N — not N+1 (CEDO301 '[Page 1]' '[LESSON]' '[H1] 1.0 Hauora and You' would otherwise number its lessons 2.0 … 6.0 where the human has 1.0 …). Env AR2ORD_OFF.
page_marker_as_lesson._doc: THE WRITER'S [PAGE N] OPENS ITS OWN LESSON PAGE (as in MXFL103). PageSplitter's page-as-lesson rule (the BLL pattern) fires when the [PAGE] follows the overview or another page-as-lesson; it also fires for a [PAGE] after a lesson page opened IMPLICITLY (content after [end page] with no 'Lesson N' heading — after_implicit) or carrying the NEXT lesson's number straight after [LESSON N-1] (writer_next_number — only before any sub-page of that lesson), which would otherwise fall to the sub-page branch and ship x.1, x.2 … where the human ships lesson N. Env toggle PAGELESSON_OFF.

front_matter_fold._doc_dotted_sub_lesson: A DOTTED [LESSON N.M] of the open lesson N after a page holding only that lesson's front matter continues the page (its number + title become the sub-lesson's) — PWY1001 '[Lesson 1]' '[Lesson Overview]' … '[LESSON 1.1] Timeliness' would otherwise ship an empty 1.0 page the human build does not have. Env FRONTFOLDDOT_OFF.
front_matter_fold._doc: THE FRONT-MATTER-ONLY LESSON PAGE FOLDS FORWARD, so no page ships empty (e.g. CEDK501 4, DAN1006 4.1, MXFL103 0, MXFL204 6, MXFU301 4, PES1007 6, PWY1001 1, XLP05 0). A LESSON page (not the overview) whose items are ONLY its front matter — section markers ([Lesson Overview] / [Lesson content] / a title-bar alias), at most max_headings heading tags, writer instructions / noise, and black text that is blank or made only of WALT / SC lead or list lines (prose is content even inside the [Lesson Overview] block — SPA1004 lesson 2) — does not end at the writer's next `[end page]`, bare `[LESSON]` (no number) or `[PAGE]` marker: the content that follows continues on it, so the lesson ships as the human's one page (MXFU301 lesson 4: `[Lesson Overview]` + WALT + `[Lesson content]` + `[H2] Lesson 4: Time to play` then a bare `[LESSON]`; XLP02 lesson 3: the block then `[end page]`). A marker with its OWN, DIFFERENT lesson number still opens its page (a genuine new lesson); the same-number merge and RR-3 / AR-2 are unchanged (they count a heading or the WALT text as content, which is why these pages need this rule). The folded marker's title is adopted when the page has none. Env FRONTFOLD_OFF.

denied_note.link_tail_todo: Designer/Developer To Do: the writer's link — {text}: {url}
denied_note._doc_link_tail_todo: A black tail that is nothing but ONE hyperlink is the note's object — the lesson or page to copy in ('[insert lesson from ENO511' + «Lesson 3.0 - Show, don't tell - English 000», ENGS404; '[insert zones writing wheel from this page' + a D2L link, ENGI405) — and becomes the house To Do note (the bare_link_url_note form, with the link's words) rather than a learner-facing link.
denied_note._doc: Constraint 1, and the guard's own contract «the span is NOT dropped — its own content still renders wherever it sits»: every writer request reaches the developer. A page / lesson span this guard DENIES as a boundary stays in the page, but ContentConverter's PAGE_BOUNDARY case turns every in-stream boundary item into a bare row break, so without this the writer's note AND its black tail would vanish (HIS1001 «[Can you please make a map of Te Moananui-ā-Kiwa …]», CEDR501 «[The Instant Standard assessment task … Please attach a Te Kura cover page …]», ART1006 «[Create two new colour boxes …]», HIS1006, PES1004 …). PageSplitter records each denial's reason on the item (_boundaryDenied: 'note' — instruction-dominant, foreign code, hover lead, placement, reference (lead_pattern); 'label' — the [lesson title] / [Lesson Summary] section labels; 'docref' — a [page 21] document-page fragment); a reason listed here renders as a red Writers Note (NotesAndComments.redFlag, kind 'cs' — the §5.16 whole-span instruction form, so the template-placeholder omit still applies) with its black tail as body text. Env DENIEDNOTE_OFF.

lesson_notes._doc: Constraint 1. A WRITER'S REVISION NOTE THAT POINTS AT A LESSON IS NOT A PAGE BOUNDARY. ENGC206 is a rewrite of ENO304 and its writer left notes: '[Found in Lesson 3 of old module] Download recipe.' (an embedded 'lesson' span — the preposition lead 'Found in' before the word) would open a one-line page, and '[End - From Lesson 3 in old ENO304 module]' (an 'end lesson' closer naming the foreign module ENO304) would close it, so lesson 2 would ship as three pages (the human: one). (a) lead_tags_extra — lead_pattern above (a preposition + determiners before the marker word; its own examples include 'navigate forward to lesson 5', 'rewrite of lesson 1') also denies an embedded 'lesson' span; (b) foreign_code_close_tags — an 'end lesson' closer whose bracket names ANOTHER module's code (foreign_code_pattern, the cross-module reference) is a reference, not a boundary. Env REFLESSON_OFF.

reference_forms._doc: Constraint 1 + the WT's own [LESSON] / [End page] structure. A WRITER NOTE THAT REFERS TO A PAGE OR LESSON IS NOT A PAGE BOUNDARY (e.g. GENO901 would otherwise split far beyond its human page count). (a) lead_pattern — tested, like deny_lead_pattern, on an EMBEDDED page / lesson span's bracket text BEFORE the marker word: a preposition (+ determiners) there means the span POINTS AT a page or lesson — '[Sticky Nav Layout with the following repeat on EVERY PAGE]' (XDLS903 / 904 / 905 / 906 / 908), '[This is a complete rewrite of lesson 1 from the original module]' / '[Found in Lesson 3 of old module]' (ENGC206), '[navigate forward to lesson 5]' (ENGC403), '[insert zones writing wheel from this page' (ENGI405), '[keep colour coding on student page]' (GENO901), '[from the what of linked lesson below]' (PES1007), '[from page 4 of Niskisha is a champ]' (BLL175). Every genuine embedded marker puts the marker word first or after a label word — '[Next Page – New Page 3.1]', '[Page 2 of diary]', '[MODULE CONTENT: PAGE 1]', '[insert page break]', '[Database LESSON 2 – …]', '[PAGE 1 Novice]', '[Lesson 4.2 continued]'. (b) doc_ref_pattern — a NUMBERED span of a doc_ref_tags canonical (any match type) whose preceding non-blank item ends with a document name or URL is a page reference INTO that document: '… GENO901 Audiovisual Request Template RAP 2026.docx [page 21]'. A denied span stays in the page (the guard's deny path). Env REFMARK_OFF.

lesson_boundary_guard._doc_deny_position_pattern: A PLACEMENT NOTE is not a page boundary: an embedded page span whose folded text says where on the page something goes ('[Kōwhai Avatar – right hand side of the page]' BLLR201–203, '[Insert bookworm on right side of page …]' BLLR202 / 203, '[Create two new colour boxes to go on the side of the page …]' ART1006) names a POSITION. A denied span stays in the page (the guard's deny path). Env POSNOTE_OFF.
lesson_boundary_guard._doc_deny_marker_pattern: A SECTION LABEL is not a page boundary. (1) deny_marker_pattern, unconditional: the inline '[lesson title]' label ('[H2] *Lesson 2* [lesson title] *Heat Capacity Calculations*', PES1008) names the title of the lesson it sits in — the human keeps one page per lesson. (2) deny_short_marker_pattern: a red '[Lesson Summary]' label before the lesson's own '[H3] Lesson Summary' heading (HIS1002, MXFU402, CEDK401) is part of the lesson when the next page boundary follows within deny_short_marker_max_items items (the summary is short); when a whole run of content follows it stays a boundary — HIS1002's FIRST summary is where lesson 2 (typed with no marker of its own) begins, so denying it would merge lessons 1 + 2. A denied span stays in the page (the guard's deny path), exactly like an instruction-dominant span. Env LABELMARK_OFF.

formatter._comment:
Block-level line breaking. The emitters glue structural runs onto one line (
, ......); the human build breaks almost every mixed div/table-structural glued boundary onto its own line and keeps ONLY the empty-element one-liners glued (
, , ). HtmlFormatter.Indent splits a zero-whitespace >< boundary when BOTH tags are in `tags`, EXCEPT an open tag immediately followed by its own close (the empty-element exception). Whitespace-only between tags, never inside a text node — semantically inert. Env LINEBREAK_OFF keeps the glued form.

lazy_free_hosts._note_lazy_hosts: KB constraint 83 / CL-0083: NEVER add loading="lazy" to an image inside a moving-or-draggable interactive — lazy loading defers the image until the browser judges it near the viewport, which breaks any interactive whose images move; the KB names the rotating banner, carousel, drag and drop, click drop (incl. .clickDropContent), flip card, memory game and sketcher, in both image modes, real images and placehold.co placeholders alike; every OTHER image keeps the attribute. MediaBuilder.FinishImg adds the attribute to every image it builds and cannot know its host, so the rule lives here as a whole-document pass in HtmlFormatter.Indent, run before the line walk: a void-aware tag walk keeps an open-element stack and strips `attribute` from any whose open ancestor carries one of host_classes (the KB's own list; the inner names — drag, drop, front, back, item-level classes — sit inside their outer hosts anyway, and .clickDropContent is the click-drop panel's SIBLING, so it is listed in its own right). The human build mostly agrees inside hosts, and is era-mixed outside them, where FinishImg's rule stands. Env toggle LAZYHOST_OFF turns it off.

xhtml_voids._note_xhtml:
KB constraint 28 + 01A_TEMPLATE_LEVELS_CORE 'Void element self-closing syntax' / 'DOCTYPE casing' + the 02C checklist. The KB's output spec is a lowercase and XHTML-style self-closing void elements (, ,
). In the human build the two halves are ONE style — the lowercase-doctype pages mostly self-close ' />', the uppercase-doctype pages almost never do — so the human MAJORITY does not follow the rule; under the order of authority (§1b) the KB outranks the human build because the human build predates the rule: an INTENTIONAL OVERRIDE, structurally neutral (an HTML parser reads and as the same node). THE RULE: HtmlFormatter.Indent's final pass rewrites the doctype line to `doctype` and normalises every void open tag's tail to `close` (attribute-aware: quoted attribute values may hold '>' or '/'); idempotent on tags already in the form. Env toggle XHTMLVOID_OFF keeps the uppercase doctype and plain void tags.

reference_module._doc: The HTML Generator's REFERENCE-MODULE feature. The upload UI names the SUGGESTED reference module (advisory-only — PrecedenceResolver.SuggestReference over the library index; changes nothing), lets the person PICK a different library module (PrepareRun referenceCode -> the structural rules re-resolve as that module's), or — when no suitable module exists — UPLOAD the reference module's finished HTML pages (PrepareRun referenceHtmlFiles -> ReferenceMiner.Distil mines the Style-Anchor tracked fields, applies them live, and ships the distilled template as {code}_reference-template.json to add to the templated modules). A batch conversion passes neither option, so it is unaffected BY CONSTRUCTION. Env REFMOD_OFF turns off the overrides + the distilled output; enabled:false does the same from data.

custom_template._doc: The 'Make your own template' choice: the person picks a subject + phase + template and ReferenceMiner.PickBySpec inherits the structure from the MOST TYPICAL library module of the narrowest matching pool. THE TEMPLATE IS NEVER RELAXED (each template is a separate format — Fundamentals/Inquiry are one-page formats — so it dictates the content/lesson layout); when no module matches all three choices the pool widens by dropping phase first, then subject, always keeping the template. 'Most typical' = the pool member agreeing with the per-field majority of the Style-Anchor tracked fields on the most fields (ties → most recently built). Rides the parent enabled flag + REFMOD_OFF.

reference_module._mining_doc: Two miner rules (as used for SCCH301 → SCCH302), both data-flagged above and turned off with the whole feature by REFMOD_OFF. chip_padded_detect — a zero-padded two-digit lesson chip ('01'..'09', the SCCH301 human form) mines as 'padded-number' rather than 'decimal' (which would render '1.0'). tooltip_content_scan — the menu tooltip attribute is also read off the module-menu-content div (the human build carries it there on some pages and on the button on others — the converter emits the button form either way; this only affects the MINED yes/no).
